text: I was incredibly disappointed by this place. I have seen these as they are a chain around philadelphia and the suburbs many times and couldn't wait to try them. First off their pizzas are made in front of you and you bake them at home. Not an issue at all. I got the following 2 pizzas, Pepperoni and Mushrooms and peppers. The cost, $34 for TWO pizzas that I have to cook! I don't mind paying for good pizza, but when i finally heated them up and made them....they were bowling alley pizza at its best. Incredibly bland, and just plain. I would NOT recommend this place as the price ruins something that isn't that good to begin with. I was shocked at the price of the pizza and was hoping that my meal would be better when it was cooked but no. Not good and DEFINITLY not worth the price. For dinner I ha the Lomo Saltado which was delicious and the portion was just right. The plantain chips were spot on and where I'm from a $4 draft of Blue Moon and a $4 bottle of Fat Tire is unheard of. Their happy hour is also one of the best I've found in my travels... $1.50 domestic bottles, $2 drafts of 312 and Amber Bock, and $16 pitchers of Sangria... 1/2 price mango margaritas... Try to beat that in downtown STL! Happy Hour runs M-F from 3-6 pm and Fri-Sat 10-Close (1 AM).

text: I don't even know where to start with this place. Overall, my experience was terrible. I would like to give the place another star for the view but I don't think it even deserves credit for that. You'd be better off bringing your own picnic and eating on the beach. I don't understand why the leasers just didn't resign the owners of the Brown Pelican. That place was outstanding. I figured I'd try the new establishment of my old favorite thinking it had to be a great place. I was so wrong. First, the hostesses gave us 2 choices of where to sit since the bar area was full. Even though it was only 4:30pm, we were told we could not sit on the patio because they save it for reservations only and that we could sit in a far back corner or inside. All we wanted was a quick appetizer and to try the margaritas. So we sat inside and ordered two Blood Orange Margaritas. For $8.95 they were pretty watered down and just not worth it. I thought they would come in pretty decent sized glasses for that price but they came in tiny tumbler glasses. I'll give them points for the looks of the margaritas but when I'm ordering a drink, I am looking for quality not aesthetics. A few friends joined my boyfriend and I, and we decided to order a couple things. The waiter took forever to greet us and take our orders. He was also very unpersonable and just not pleasant at all. My boyfriend and I ordered the fried shrimp and chips, which were over cooked and too greasy. Also, the plate only came with 4 pieces with a big bowl of coleslaw and some fries. May I add that this was not an appetizer dish and definitely not worth the $12.95. I'd say skip the giant bowl of coleslaw and add some more shrimp. That's what I thought I was getting. I would have let it pass if it weren't over cooked and made my stomach do flip flops from one bite. One of my friends ordered the fish and chips and said they were overcooked and rubbery. Another ordered the salmon and french fries. She said the salmon was very good but instead of getting fries as she ordered, she got rice. When she told the waiter she ordered fries not rice he argued with her. Not smart. Also, we all asked for ranch dressing and got unfriendly "kay" remarks. The argumentative attitude was the last straw for me so I went up to the manager to complain. Now, a managers job is to make sure their guests are happy and to compensate for poor service. He did not seem to care that service was well below standard and certainly gave off the impression that he really didn't care. He interrupted me, asking me where we were sitting and said he'd switch out the server. The new waitress was ten times better but the damage was already done. Even upon leaving, the manager asked noncommittedly as he walked past me if things ended up better. Usually, I like to give places another chance but I won't be going here again. Poor service + poor management + overcooked food + overpriced menu = bad establishment. Save your money and your time by going elsewhere.
label: NEG

text: "dude, like, ya brah, that chick was so hot I was like yo down on your knees hahahahahahhaha ya brah i love you yo when we gonna hit the weights" That's like a more macho version of Sharkeez. text: This is where we buy our milk. As of this writing (June '09), a half gallon of milk is $1.19. No, that's not a typo. A buck nineteen. That's because area milk producers ship in bulk to Halo, who in turn packages it on-site. You're not paying for the extra transportation and refrigeration costs that you do at the supermarket. Plus, the milk is darned good. Halo is also a great place to grab your eggs, 1/2 and 1/2 and of course - their famous ice cream, which is also a bargain. My favorite flavors? 1) Strawberry-Heath Bar 2) Chocolate peanut butter 3) Everything else. Oh, and the CHOCOLATE MILK. Nom, nom, nom. Halo also carries a selection of Pepperidge Farm, Arnold and other brands of breads. Similar to a brand-name bakery outlet, if you've ever been to one of those. Lots of junk-food type snacks (potato chips, pretzels, cheez puffs, et. al). There are also big-time devotees to their house brands of lemonade, sweet tea, grape ade, etc. Again, I can't speak to the sugary drinks, as I don't partake. Unique to the Lawrenceville/Trenton area, it's a must-stop if you're down here. And if you live here - you should be buying your milk from Halo! Not only will you be supporting one of our best local businesses, you'll be saving a lot of money.
label: POS

text: The worst Italian food I have ever tasted!!! I'm far from Italian, but I can make a MEAN lasagna & spaghetti myself compared to this place. 1st of all, we waited 45mins patiently w/ a hungry Hubby, 2yr old, 7yr old, & myself. When we finally got seated, the waitress was very polite, but forgetful at times. Didnt drink any alcohol or sodas but the lemonade was very tart & the garlic bread was not-so-fresh...had to request for some fresh bread after my family devoured the 1st basket from starving & waiting for so long. I ordered the stuffed shells & chicken parmagiana. The salad was very tasty; however, they only have Italian dressing...no ranch or anything else. I am not a picky eater & rarely complain, but the stuffed shells & parmagiana chicken tasted HORRIBLE!! The chicken was very bland & the stuffed shells were hard & overbaked. The meranera sauce tasted like it was old or aged too long (if there's ever such a thing, lol). I could not bring myself to eat my entree. I had to send it back. I heard the lady at the table next to ours say the salmon was good, so I figured the salmon might be safe. It was actually very good! I was still very disappointed after this restaurant was referred to me by many. I felt like they got an easy $50 bucks out of me. I would have rathered gone to the olive garden or macaroni grill. If u r looking for an awesome authentic Italian cusine restaurant in Tucson, I highly recommend Contessa off of Ina Rd. The only reason we didn't go there is b/c it was out of the way from where we were going. It's pretty far from where we live but always worth the drive. Everything is freshly made & u can definite tell the difference! I'm sorry Caruso, but I don't think my family will be coming here ever again!

text: We decided to check out Wedding World during their sample sale a couple weeks back. This place looks small on the outside and is easy to pass by, but it's a lot larger from the inside of the store. The service is great, the girls really help you out and give you one-to-one service. My friend managed to narrow things down to one dress out of several choices. They have a lot of beautiful designs in a range of styles and prices, so there's something for almost every bride and budget. Prices seemed to range from about $600 to over $1500. They also have a lot of bridesmaids' dresses to choose from, in all sorts of colors available for customizing. What's nice about this shop is that you can get more than your dress here. They sell almost everything you'll need for your big day, like wedding glasses, ring pillows, flower firl baskets, guest books, banners, and those pom-pom things you put on your car. Definitely worth checking out, if you're having or planning a wedding anytime soon. It's convenient because you can cross a lot of things off your list, and there's something for every price range.

text: Being from LA, I was a little skeptical when a local recommended PM. I mean, I come from the land of Asian fusion, how good could it be? But then somebody said it was run by a Top Chef contestant so curiosity got the best of me. We started with the Peking duck spring rolls and BBQ pork bao bun (char siu bao). The spring rolls were greasy and missing something...oh yeah, the taste of duck. I'm not sure if the greasiness overpowered it but it wasn't there. It just tasted like a giant spring roll. The char siu bao was better but the filling lacked that great char siu flavor and bright red color. This one had a brown sugar color and was kind of pasty and bland. For dinner I had a couple rolls - spicy tuna (cut) and and the Godzilla (salmon, shrimp tempura, krab, cucumber). Not impressed at all. The fish was not the bright flavored, super-fresh kind that I have grown accustomed to over the years in LA. And krab with a k? C'mon, Top Chef, get the real stuff. I recommend avoiding any sushi dishes if you visit. I did try my co-worker's spaghetti pad prik pao, which is a vegetarian dish with fried tofu, cashews and basil. With a little hot sauce, this dish wasn't bad but I feel like I could have whipped this up at home on one of those nights where I just cobble something together with whatever I have in the pantry. Overall, pretty disappointing. Aside from the food, the floor was slanted, which was annoying and the a/c needed to be cranked up - it was hot and humid inside.

Their three-meat dishes, Chinese watercress with garlic, and fish dishes are all delicious, and remind me of eating in Taiwan. However, there are also the generic dishes for those less adventurous or that cannot read the Chinese menus. Also, seating is tight, it's a small, but often busy space! We've also ordered larger dishes for catering (rolls, rice, noodles, and meat dishes), and they were swift, and gave us a discount!

text: I have been using this quiet little place, three doors south of Metropolitan Bakery, since 2001, and have never been disappointed. My experience yesterday moved me to write a review. It was 3:00 p.m. and my two pairs of workhorse wingtips (the brown and the black) were in dire, dire need of heels and thorough shines. Somewhere between moving from Seattle to Philly to Seattle to Philly (2001, 2005, and 2008 respectively) my shoeshine equipment got waylaid, so these two poor bastards have gone a good year each without any love. Sad, but I have had NO TIME to take them in, until yesterday, when I remembered "hey, I wonder if that guy is still there next to the Metropolitan Bakery!" Indeed, he was, and open. Now, sadly, several of my pairs of shoes have migrated to my girlfriend's apartment in NYC, so I've been tag-teaming these shoes back and forth and needed to have them back yesterday afternoon. I also brought a third "reseve" pair along that needed a front sole--that I could wait for. So I pled my case, and he cheerfully said, "come back at 5:45." When I returned (with cash--cash only, FYI)--all three pairs were lined up, looking brand new, new vibram heels, new sole, shined. $52 for the trio. Thanks, man! I can't opine on his facility with womens' shoes, to the extent there are repair-requiring differences, but for your trusty, expensive, long-lasting wingtips--I give this my highest recommendation.

text: The following series of events took place on Saturday, November 23rd, 2010 upstairs at Bailey's. This is the first 1 star review I've given on Yelp. An employee, perhaps she was a manager or a supervisor put 2 small tables and 6 chairs on a side wall for us. While she was setting up the following words came out of her mouth "that group over there offered me $20 for you table." I guess first come first serve does not hold true at this bar. Needless to say we got the table and ignored her request for a bribe. While we waited for 4 more members of our group to show up, the same employee came by twice and uttered the words "if your group doesn't come soon I will have to take one of your tables." About ten minutes later she took 1 one of our tables and 3 of our chairs. During the course of the above events about 30 minutes passed while we were waiting. I noticed 2 servers rushing around the entire room. The table that was taken from us was given to a group of 3 whom appeared to know her. She got them drinks and food, while walking past our table a total of 5 times. She did not ask us if we needed anything. After the rest of our party showed up, we again gave them the benefit of the doubt and waited another 15 minutes before we gave up and left. Now I understand that Bailey's is a sports bar, and I also understand that Saturday was a big sports day, but you would think that a SPORTS BAR of all places would be able to handle the expected rush of so many major sporting events. My last visits to Bailey's for sporting events was quite successful. We received decent service, they've upgraded all their tvs, and they've added an HD projector. I'll chalk it up to poor management and a miscalculation of the day's events. I hate to say it, but I'll probably be back since they're one of the only bars in Nashville that show UFC events. Many others where serving St Louis style since the late 1940's and early 1950's. They also claim the square cut was because Mr. Imo was a tile cutter. That may be. But before 1964, before Imo's, most of the early St. Louis style pizza's were cut into squares because the pizza's were made rectangular. They were rectangular so they could fit a large pizza in front of each person at a table if needed. If you claim you don't like St. Louis style pizza, because you don't like Imo's. text: The best Indian food I've eaten in Philadelphia, by far. If it weren't located a bit away from the Penn campus, it would give places like New Delhi and Sitar a real run for their money. But trust me, if you want really good, authentic north Indian food then Desi Village is the place. It is simply outstanding. Indian food is rarely eaten in buffet style, its almost always ala carte and you know when you see a buffet (for example, at Indian weddings), you know its for the convenience but not the substance. Desi Village is all about the substance. They do not serve buffets, and that means all the dishes are made for you, customized if you want. The village Naan is exciting - don't be put off by its red color - its spicy and extremely tasty. The dal makhani is the best I've had in ages, as is the saag. The staff is very warm and friendly. text: I've seen multiple doctors here, including Kelli Peters, Humeera Hina, and James Kwak. I spend long and hard efforts trying to self diagnose myself whenever I'm feeling ill and I usually have some type of understanding as to what my problem is before I go to the Dr. I DO NOT however demand specific things from the doctors as I know they are the professionals, I merely suggest what I think is happening. One of the most harmful cases was this past summer, when I started getting a stiff neck, and day after day the pain for worse and worse. I read online about my symptoms and decided I may in fact have lymes disease. I decided it was time to go to Advocare and suggest to them that was the case. In a proper medical procedure, if there is any symptom that a patient has lymes disease they are issued a blo0d test and a prescription of doxycycline just in case. Humeera Hina decided I just needed a massage and some Motrin. 3 days later I called back in even more pain, and she asked to see me again. After taking my $25 co-pay and taking all the money from my insurance, she sent me away again, with a pat on the back saying everything will be fine. The symptoms kept getting worse and worse, to where it would take me 20 minutes to get out of bed. My mother took me to a local Urgent Care where they immeditaly took a blo0d test and gave me 7 days worth of doxycycline. Within days, I was feeling better. A week later, I received a call from the Urgent care in NC saying that I tested postitive to Lymes disease as well as Rocky mountain spotted fever. If I had taken "Dr" Hina's advice and waited a few more weeks I would have been dead. I left a message expressing my disappointment that I had put so much time into consigning to be stood up, and then I headed back home on the Schuylkill in continuing rush-hour traffic. text: For my 100th review, I thought it should be special. What's more special than my favorite meal, at my favorite restaurant, in one of my top 3 favorite cities. Manale's is famous for their BBQ shrimp. Are you thinking shrimp slathered with BBQ sauce? Well, you're wrong. BBQ shrimp are shrimp baked with the heads and shells on in a mix of butter, Worcestershire and a host of other spices. I guarantee you've never tasted anything this good (although Drago's char-broiled oysters run a close second) in your life. Served with perfect New Orleans French bread (paper thin, light crust, soft, airy bread on the inside) for sopping up the sauce, this is a New Orleans staple that was originated at Manale's. In addition to the BBQ shrimp, there are other reasons to visit this New Orleans establishment as well, like the oyster bar where I once challenged a 10 year old kid to eat a very large raw oyster. He did it so I had to as well, and I hate a large raw oyster (yet tiny ones are a gift to the world). Good stiff drinks in the bar as well as oysters to die for and shuckers who win contests. Seriously. When you go to the dining room, it's like stepping into another decade. It's got that old school Italian feeling. I expect to see Carlos Marcello surrounded by his people at a back table. OK, not really since I wouldn't know Carlos Marcello from Tony Soprano...but you get the idea. The waitresses are all of that older, steak house variety. You know the kind, weathered, hardened and not about to take any crap, but still wonderful, attentive and knowledgeable because they've been there since the joint opened. The Italian-inspired menu ranges across everything you can think of and all the New Orleans classics as well, but you know, in the end, it's all about the BBQ shrimp. And that might just be the best meal on earth.
label: POS

text: This place feels like it's trying to be everything to everyone - and just fails in it's attempts to do so. The Lime is a strange mix of a lounge, sports-bar, tapas restaurant and a regular Mexican restaurant. The only thing that they've got down right is their feeling of pretentiousness. We visited on a Saturday night. A large group had just cleared out, and the restaurant was a little less than half full. We had all already eaten dinner - and while we were really here for drinks and a place to sit and talk - we were also open to some snacking. At a glance, the menu looks pretty good - if a bit expensive. The beer list is decent - but our waiter clearly didn't know much about any of them. We ordered a couple of beers and a martini along with the trio of dips. The cucumber martini wasn't that good. Watered down and with an off flavor. My wife didn't even finish it. The trio of dips was decent enough. We just thought it was really odd when we were finished (out of both chips AND dip) and the waiter brought us a second bag of chips - but no extra dip. The waiter seemed really pleased with himself for this too - like he had done us some huge favor. Had we stopped there, I would have given The Lime 3 stars. But we decided that we were still a little hungry. Our friend spotted the tostones and asked the waiter how many were included. Two. He ordered two orders. He chose not to add any of the optional meats on top of them. While we waited - we discussed the fact that there were only two tostones per order. It turns out that he had mis-read the menu and thought that it was $2 per order of two. The $2 was for the optional meat. The order of two tostones is $6 each. So, $12 for four tostones. To be fair - the tostones WERE fairly large - but hardly large enough to justify $3 each. They were topped with gucamole, pico and queso - all sorts of things that tostones don't need. Never mind the optional meat. Turns out you CAN get tostones served a little more properly - in the form of their "fried plantains" which are served with black bean rice and sour cream. I assume there are only two per order there as well. While we ate, there was a DJ playing a very odd mix of hip-hop. While the general ambiance of the restaurant leaned towards being a lounge, the music was a bit high energy. The sports playing on the tv's confused the vibe even more. Pick one direction to go with the place and just focus that way.

Just watch it, because the servers are really on top of things and they'll think you're finished with it before you really are -- you'll want to get every delicious piece of crabmeat out of this! The crabcakes are equally delicious -- more crab than 'cake' in them. I've spoken with people from New England who swear that these are better than most crabcakes that they've ever ate back at home. Mmmm... you'll find the freshest seafood in the city here, and if you're looking for an upscale downtown dining experience, you can't go wrong at Oceanaire.

I ordered chips and salsa, and they brought be a basket of chips with nothing else and no explanation. Another night, they had no ground beef. On yet another, they couldn't make any of their wraps because they were out of tortillas. Service is also horrendous. They pack the audience in together like sardines and employ too few waiters. You will likely wait the better part of an hour for a meal. Drinks are the same deal. One time, I only got my drink (a soda) 10ish minutes after my meal had come. The waitstaff will periodically forget about you or misplace your order. The comedians are basically bottom of the barrel, as well. Usually there is a "hungry" local MC of middling quality, followed by a veritable rogues gallery of comedians who will pontificate about their impotence, incontinence, aversion to hygiene, and inability to keep a woman (SHOCKER). Usually, on a night's bill of 3-4 comedians, one MIGHT be kind of amusing (thus, the second star). Funny sidebar - Laff's seems to loooooove comedians who make lots of gratuitous noise in the service of imitating things like airplanes, racecars, and flushing toilets. One night, when there with my girlfriend and a couple of our friends, we were watching a particularly bad comic who seemed to dig making our ears bleed with his impressions. My friend, who had been in the restroom when he came on stage, returned to the table with a shocked look on her face and disclosed that it sounded, from the toilet, as though the club was under attack by the Luftwaffe. Sadly for her, she had confused an air raid with the comic's impression of a fart. I guess the only thing that's *kind of* good about Laff's is that it's easy to get free tickets to the shows. Just sign up with the cards on the tables and you'll get a call every other month or so with a password (I shit you not) to claim your free admittance. That said, I think I'm done with Laff's for the forseeable future.
label: NEG

text: This was my default place in Phiadelphia. Its a place where you can bring a hot date or your parents. The food is so fresh and tasty. Tare Tare- Incredible. Calamari salad- fresh, airy, and fulfilling. Lobster Mac - n Cheese- Classic. Great service. The Buzz Aldrin is always a fun drink to get in your in the mood for TANG! Its normally a great place for a Friday night to drink, but when the roof deck is open... EVEN BETTER! Its probably one of the only bars in Philly that have a roof deck. For some reason it hasn't caught on yet which I cant understand.

text: $5 dollars for a bottle of domestic beer!! $5!!!!! This is Nashville and you should be ashamed of yourself Lime! I ordered a Miller Light because the mojito you made for me was a nasty color, tasted like sweet tarts, and conatined no rum only to find out that you would try and rip me off in the "cheap" beer department also. The bar constantly smells like bleach because the glass washing thing is right in your face, and the girl bartender can't make a drink. text: Super nice new digs on the West Bank for desserts and breakfast! The new building complex is huge and gorgeous and super spacious!!! I love the fact that parking is behind the building so the experience is slow-paced and relaxed, none of that hustle and bustle! Parrot Pete's is really nice inside, great tables all spaced adequately with those Carribean-esque wicker chairs. the magazines on display are for purchase, no reading! So definitely not a Barnes and Nobles experience. The layout is a bit confusing though. When you enter, head straight and you will hit a dessert case. Turn right to purchase your icecreams/milkshakes. But more than likely you will get dessert and a cup of joe. Coffee here...$2!!! It's a good brew, although a bit watery for my tastes. Had the berry cake...it was delicious! Yellow cake w/ a whipped topping with blueberries and strawberries..it was moist and absolutely delicious - not sweet at all! love it...friend had lemon bar..it was okay. fountain drinks - $2.00!!! my gosh! they totally get you on drinks! The prices for the desserts are a bit steep - a mini wedding cake was $6.00!!! A slice of cake - $5.00!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! My goodness! Breakfast here starts @ 8.00....lunch will definitely run you at least $15! But the environment is relaxed and the workers seem to be so happy. Haven't tried foods yet, but the specialty at Parrot Pete's is the Kitchen Sink...a huge icecream sundae meant for sharing w/ lots of folks, served in a huge bowl w/ a "faucet" and "taps". ...the kids faces totally lit up - very cute..up to the point they got their sugar rush and put their mouths on everything (eww). I'd be back here for brunch..it's nice, it's clean, the workers/cooks seem genuinely happy...that's always a plus! Not sure if there is WI-FI available..but a few folks had laptops out...

text: Update to an earlier review - I'm rating primarily on the beer selection, hence the excellent rating. The Monkey has the best draft beer selection in South Jersey, bar none. They have customer cards so if you are a frequent customer you end up with free manicures and pedicures every now and then. I don't get to go that often but they know my mom and her best friend by name. I'm simply known as my mom's daughter. Everyone does a great job except the lone guy that works at this place. text: Name a restaurant where you may not get your appetizers until 2 hours after your reservation time. Survey says... Pearl - is the number one answer! The night started out on the wrong foot when our party of 4 waited over an hour to be seated, even with a reservation. We had to ask the hostess what was going on, and kept being told we were "next on the list". And then we'd see other parties being seated ahead of us. After about an hour they did comp us a round of drinks when it was clear we were getting upset, but it was a round none of us really wanted - we only took it b/c it was free and we were still waiting. I know it's restaurant week, and I know that means extra busy... but don't overbook your restaurant, don't wait til people get pissy before apologizing about the wait, and DON'T tell them they're next and then seat same-sized parties ahead of them. Don't lie to me. Then when we were finally seated, we waited nearly 30 minutes for our appetizers! A table that was sat after us even got their apps before we did. After we said something to the waitress and it was clear we weren't happy, the manager finally made his way over to us and asked what he could do to make our dining experience better. Sorry buddy, we don't want anymore drinks, we're already getting apps, entrees and dessert with restaurant week, and we've wasted 2 hours of our life that you can't give back. Note he didn't offer to take anything off of our bill. None of this was our waitress's fault (she was quite nice), and after the apps the rest of the food certainly came out quickly since they knew we were upset. The food itself was quite good too - duck spring roll was meaty and flavorful, black truffle scallops were tender, and cocoa pot de creme was thick and not too sweet. But I won't be going back since the management is so poor. Bottom line: the whole night was poorly managed by the restaurant, and we were so annoyed by the time the food arrived that we decided we won't be returning, no matter how good the food was. You may have a better experience, but I will take my business elsewhere.
label: NEG

text: Sadly this Walgreens is NOT closed. The Keystone Kops staff the pharmacy department. text: The Flying Saucer is a beer lovers dream. Hands down, they have the largest selection of beer that I have ever laid eyes on. This is definitely one of the more crowded places around Nashville, as it is usually super packed on the weekends. Regardless of the service, the flying saucer is a really awesome place for some serious beer sampling.

text: I wish my first Mo's experience was as outstanding as everyone else who has reviewed. I went there last night for dinner at 7 pm - crazy enough we were out of there by 8:15 pm. I have never felt so rushed at a nice steakhouse. Our steaks came out before our salads were finished and then, our creamed spinach plate was removed from the table with more than half left. The waiter didnt ask if we were finished with any of the sides we had left before he snatched them up. One of our steaks were burnt on the outside, but extremely pink on the inside. No medium ground for a steak that was ordered medium. I will say our mashed potatoes were delicious. And our waiter was pleasant. You really couldnt blame him... I typically am a Capital Grille fan for steak, but had decided to go to Mo's for the night when I had received a gift certificate to the restaurant. Unfortunately, at the end of our already unpleasant dining experience, they informed us that this specific location doesnt accept gift cards. You have got to be kidding me! When your restaurant has the same name and logo as what's represented on the gift card, you better accept it! Apparently it was a "new" policy. Regardless, I was extremely disappointed with the experience and food and plan to stick with a steakhouse experience I can count on at The Capital Grille.

text: It's Nashville, people. What can you expect on Broadway? Bailey's is alright, but not the greatest. I've come to Bailey's to host work events every summer and to dine as a normal patron. For our events, the food always seems to be cold when they put it out. Explain that? The cheese on the potato skins is always congealed. The artichoke dip has a thin layer of grease on top. Great when you're hungover. Not when you're trying to have a few appetizer's on a hot summer's day. Having one waitress serve drinks to approximately 40 people? Particularly large, thirsty, "I wany my booze now" men? Not the best idea. Service was slow as molasses. Now.... as a regular patron, if you want to get away from the honky tonkin', check out Bailey's to watch a variety of sporting events. The drinks are alright, a bit overpriced in my opinion. The service is not all that great as a normal patron either. The staff doesn't seem to give two hoots about you. I've waited for over 20 minutes just to have someone take our order. The food again, meh. The crowd is cool, the vibe is right, but you only get it from the patron's, not the staff. Oh yeah and it's super smokey!

text: Macy's Philadelphia is honestly a depressing store. Often I'll say something is depressing when the quality is poor, or the service sucks. Perhaps I should clarify: The Wanamaker Building is HUGE, Macy's content and inventory is minimal. When you go into the store you immediately feel dwarfed as the hundred food ceilings tower above you. To preserve the authenticity of the Wanamaker building's interior design the lights are dimly lit. Tables full of clothing are far and few between, randomly placed throughout the building. You cannot go up most of the stairwells, as anything above the second floor is empty. Worst off, as if you're in Phantom of the Opera, they play there original pipe organ, because the experience isn't dreary enough.

text: Price: very cheap. I believe 6.95 - 7.95 for a big bowl of vermicelli with pork _and_ spring rolls. Not dirt cheap, which is why (according to my father) you see more younger, American crowds than older, immigrant Asian. That's not to say these guys weren't authentic. It's just the place seems too nice to be that dive, authentic Vietnamese place we all know and love. Well, if you think that way, then you'd miss this gem. Food: Definitely authentic. Down to the nuoc mam (fish sauce) to the cha gio (spring rolls). I've had their mon cha gio thit nuong (vermicelli with spring rolls and pork). It's a very large portion but light, which is characteristic of Vietnamese food since they toss a bunch of fresh vegetables in there and don't put too much fat or batter into anything other than the deep fried appetizers. I've also had their Fukien style soup, which is two types of noodles with squid and miscellaneous things that I forgot, topped off with a deep fried shrimp. Their pork chops, definitely good too. Atmosphere: leaving the least important (for me) for last. This is a nice place. Quiet, spacious, nicely decorated in some red/cherry theme. I don't exactly remember hearing them play any Vietnamese songs, though I remember once I went there I definitely faintly heard some trance/techno song. Great place for a date or for a few friends. Though it is quiet, I would imagine a bit of rowdyness would be perfectly fine in this place.
label: POS

text: Doc's is an off-the-beaten-path bar that has done a lot with the local community to make it a friendly and fun atmosphere. One thing I like in a hometown bar is a good pool table, which is freshly felted. That, they have. It has no sags, so slow shots work fine. Doc, as the owner is called, is friendly to the patrons and does a good job to accommodate them. They also have specials for each night of the week, like all you can eat wings for 10 bucks on Tuesday, and 3 dollar Heineken on Wed. Bar food is very good. I would try the Shepherds Pie and the fish and chips is awesome, if you like that kind of thing. The crowd is sparse during the week, which can be good or bad, depends on what mood you're in. Overall, very good, if you happen to be in that area.

text: Porterhouse is located right across the street from Peddler's Village. Most people think they are a brewery, but in fact they serve Riverhorse Beer. Riverhorse has a nice assortment of beers and Porterhouse has about 6 on draught at all times. My favorite is their Irish Stout. Beer prices are reasonable (about $4 for a pint of stout) and it's a SMOKE FREE establishment (Yay!) The ambience is ok, there's a large bar area downstairs and a nice restaurant upstairs with a view of Bucks County. Food prices are mid-priced for the area. They have a nice selection of bar food. Their Buffalo Chicken sandwich covered in real blue cheese and baby spinach is the best bar sandwhich i've ever had in my life. They also have an Andouille Sausage Spring Roll appetizer that is delicious. I would discuss other menu items, but everytime that i go there I get the Buffalo Chicken Sandwich :) If you're around Peddler's Village and you want some great beer and food, I highly recommend checking this place out. Parking gets to be a pain at dinner, so be prepared to either valet park or walk from Peddler's Village.

The hanger steak was impressive and the PB&J cheesecake desert was phenomenal. Unfortunately, I have yet to see this masterpiece make another appearance on their menu. text: Heard about this company through an acquaintance of mine. I booked the 14-pass Escalade for my boyfriend's 30th surprise party. The booking process was flawless. Laura (she's no longer there) and Dominique were so patient with me and helped me with the planning process and payment schedule (they don't require it, I needed it for myself). Jill (I think she's the Director of Operations) is the sweetest person I have ever spoken to. She made sure I didn't have any questions or concern the evening of the party. Cost wise, it was great! They included 15% gratuity with the cost, but I still had to give the limo driver more, because he was just that awesome. Driver was John Burke, and he is good at what he does. He called me the morning of to go over the itinerary for evening. When he got to the house, he carried out the beer and wine and set them up in the limo. The drive was flawless and he was just so personable. Everytime we were ready to move on to our next destination, all I had to do was give him a call and seconds later he would be outside waiting for us. AND before he started driving again, he would always do a headcount to make sure we were all accounted for. Best part - one of the girls felt nauseous in the limo so I yelled up to John to let him know. He throws back a puke bucket, roll of paper towels and a rubber band to tie her hair up with - who the heck does that?! Luckily, we didn't have to utilize the puke bucket, but it's definitely good to know that he has it readily available. All-in-all, a really great experience with Secrets Limo. I will definitely give them a call again when it comes time to plan the bachelorette and wedding! And I definitely will be requesting John Burke, he's all that and MORE!

text: Visit a great sushi place without going into the city! Start with an order of the Gyoza. These little pan-fried pork dumplings are to die for. Try the Godzilla roll, the Black Jack roll, the Hot Girls roll, the Tokyo roll ... they're all delicious. For dessert, the tempura banana with ice cream is the best way to finish off a meal here. Don't forget your saki ... this place is BYOB, which only adds to the allure of this affordable, quaint, and addictive Japanese restaurant.
label: POS

text: Still an outstanding establishment. Needed to have my eyebrows waxed and re-shaped so I decided to leave it to the pros at Nadine Janet. I called around noon and was given a same-day appointment with Marla at 2:30. She really took her time on me and explained the necessary upkeep and re-shaping process really well. Waxing and tweezing were close to painless. Usually I have a small reaction to whatever lotion/gels used after waxing, but they must use a higher-quality product. No problems, even with my sensitive/fair skin. I will definitely request Marla again. Even when I come in wearing denim and a tee shirt (who gets dressed up to get their hair done?), I am always treated with respect and courtesy--like a queen. I look much younger than my age without makeup (which I wouldn't wear when I'm about to have eyebrow wasing done) and I get the same outstanding treatment as the older ladies with designer hand bags getting multiple services done. I cannot recommend this place enough! I would especially recommend Nadine Janet as a mother-daughter salon. They seem to be really kind to kids. This is a great place for a young woman's first visit to a real salon, especially if she's nervous about a major hair style change. I'm moving about 45 minutes away from this place but that won't stop my repeat business.

text: I had a great salon in Boston and asked for a rec when I moved to Philly. They said people x, y, and z at Pierre and Carlo. Well, x, y, and z have moved on and I thought that anybody might be OK if the salon was good. Not true. 2 crappy haircuts with 2 different people at 65 bucks a pop. The stylists are much more into gossiping with each other and about each other than giving you the haircut you want. Not worth the price or the snobbery. I am still in search of a good salon in Philly. Until then, I'll take trips to Boston.

text: GROSS. The lobby is very nice and kind of tricks you into thinking the rooms will be as well. Don't be fooled. There are magazine articles on the wall with write ups about the hotel, but if you check the dates, they're all from like 1999. The rooms might have been nice 10 years ago, but they aren't anymore. Also, housekeeping doesn't replenish your toiletries every day. I woke up in the morning with small bites all over my body. Disgusting, disgusting, disgusting. Never ever would I stay there again.

text: While doing some shopping in Maplewood, I got into the spirit of staying local and felt the urge to dine at Nosh. I was not disappointed! We walked in on a Friday night around 7pm and got a table right away. It filled up shortly thereafter, though I never saw a wait. This place is so cute! It's small but they have really cool small pieces of flair as the decor. The light fixtures, artwork, and bar area are nicely done. Not too much but enough to notice. We sat pretty close to the door and regretted it because it was a little colder than we preferred and also there was a piano playing there, so it was a bit loud. Not a big deal. The restaurant did get loud, but a lot of it was a group of people with "that girl" in it. Aka, the loudest, obnoxious, clap and scream at her own jokes type. Certainly not Nosh's fault. I've found one of my top 3 favorite cocktails here! Their list is very long and full of fruity stuff (and more). I ordered the hard blueberry lemonade. It was like candy! So fresh and refreshing, even in this weather. It had real, FRESH blueberries in it. I wanted more but I limited myself to one. It didn't taste like alcohol at all and I didn't care one bit! What other diners said is true, the food comes out REALLY slowly here. There is a blurb on their menu about making everything to order and taking time. Don't come here if you want it fast and ordering an appetizer is recommended if you are really hungry to start. The service was by no means inattentive. Our waiter (also the bartender) came by frequently. The manager came around to check on us too, and was very visible. I ordered the Orchard Melt and Butternut Squash Soup and my hubby ordered the Fried Egg BSRP with chips. text: Want a taste of that real southern, Cajun cooking? Not willing or able to spend a lot of money to do it, either? Then you might want to walk over to Cafe Maspero in the French Quarter to get your share. If you want a quick meal, and a lot of food--this is your place. If you are looking for atmosphere, or top-notch service, consider going elsewhere. You know that saying, 'you get what you pay for?'--that definitely applies here. Walking in, you might think the place is a little on the gritty, not so clean side; lots of old wooden tables and chairs, with that old bathroom looking tile, but do not be deceived, my friends. Once you are greeted with a smile at the door, you will then be escorted to your table (if you aren't faced with a full house) and your server, who will most probably be wearing a loose t-shirt and shorts with a pair of Converse tennis shoes, will then proceed to ask you for your drink order. (Beware, they don't offer refills on drinks other than water for some strange reason--but if you're really nice to your server, they might 'do it for you'). However, there are all kinds of (cheap) drinks for everyone, big or small. You may ask, "why would I want to go to a place that's gritty, or unclean to EAT?" Well, I'll tell you, I wasn't impressed my first time, but after trying their signature French Onion soup, (LOADED with melted gooey Swiss cheese) I was sold. If you order the fried seafood platter, you'll get enough food for two days (or two people.) Like I said, this place is low on price, and high on quantity. That can be good, considering sometimes we're paying $20 for a small piece of nothing, and we end up complaining. At Maspero, four bucks gets you the best French Onion soup in the Quarter and 11 bucks gets you more shrimp, oysters, and catfish than you could ever want. Nothing is over twenty dollars, and you will frequently see large parties dining together. (Whoever picks up that tab will be smiling). That said, if you lower your expectations for four-star service, the most immaculate decor, or spotless floors, then you will definitely enjoy all that this place has to offer. The service may be slow at times, but the food speaks for itself. If you're really hungry and in a hurry, it's the place you should try. If you really don't like it; well, put it this way, you didn't really lose much money, did you? That's a good feeling to have these days.

text: I rushed into this restaurant the last night of my Indianapolis trip after being stalked by a creepy dude in a white car for a couple of blocks. I had looked up this place on Yelp already and was determined to get me some Indian food. As I walked in, I was, first off, very surprised with how big and spacious the place was. Most Indian places I've been to around the world, their venues tend to be cozy/small. This place could comfortable accommodate a party of a few dozen people easily. I was seated promptly. I asked for Mango Lassi, samosa to start. I asked the waiter if he recommended Saag Paneer or Murg Tikka Masala as those are my usual favorites and he said Tikka Masala so I went with that and rice. He asked, no naan? And I said no thank you, initially. I just didn't think I could eat that much carbs by myself and frankly, I was expecting the portion of the Tikka Masala to be just about enough to be finished with rice alone. Well, first I get the Mango Lassi. Good, but really sweet/syrupy...good for sweet tooth, for me, it was borderline too sweet. Samosa was fresh and good, but somehow it didn't some with any dipping sauce. I made do with some sauce that came with the pappadam? that was complimentary to the table. Then came the Murk Tikka Masala... and wow, their portion is pretty big!!! I worked on it until I ate up all the rice, and there was still plenty left... So I called back the waiter, and asked a box to go and also added a new order of Paratha (sp?) after all so I have something to eat the Tikka Masala with later. The bill was not cheap, but within an affordable range. I ended up not eating the rest of the Tikka Masala until the next day in my hotel room, but it was still pretty good! Having said that, their Tikka Masala, compared to many I've tried, are also on the sweet side. It was quite tasty, but next time I travel to Indianapolis, I might try their Saag Paneer instead for a healthier alternative : )

Our sushi chef was nice enough, but it took me a solid fifteen minutes to get someone to bring me a water. Seeing as how it was my first time, we decided to forego the all you can eat and just order a couple of items. My friend got two long rolls and I got two hand rolls. My hand rolls had some nauseating sweet sauce on them that tasted like mayonaisse and sugar. I've had my fair share of interesting aiolis in my time, but this was just plain gross. My friend devoured both her long rolls, and seemed to enjoy them, but I was feeling sick so I didn't even want to try them. So, all in all, it was two years before I got brave enough to try sushi again, and now I realize it's the most amazing food on earth. text: OK - a lot of people rave about this place, but I'm not sure what the big deal is. Perhaps the white table cloths and BYOB policy? Starting off or finishing the night across the alley at the Boat House is definitely part of the overall experience - and worth a visit if you would like a pre or post dinner cocktail. My partner and I have been to Hamilton's Grill Room twice - just to be sure. Both times were forgetable experiences. Although we had attentive service, the food was served either undercooked to specifications (I hate raw tuna - no sushi for me) - or cold...well, I should correct that last statement...it came out warm, and cooled off in about 10 seconds. Might have something to do with relatively cool temperatures inside the restaurant and the fact that they don't serve their food on warmed plates.... To give you a better idea, we just ate their a couple of weeks ago - the weekend before Christmas and surpising were able to walk in without a reservation. Granted it was early (6:00 PM), but I was surprised that they were able to seat us. That was a pleasant surprise. To start, I had a nice tasting tomato-crab soup...although I would say that it was pretty lacking in actual crab. No worries - it tasted pretty good and I thought we were going to have a good meal. Next comes the entre - a ribeye steak for me. Nothing special here - pretty fatty cut of meat and rather bland tasting. Came with nicely cooked vegatables but rather wall-paper paste-like mashed potatoes. For $34 - I was pretty disappointed. Now, Hamilton Grill does have a great reputation for seafood - so I could chalk up the "OK" steak to not being one of their specialities. But, in my last visit, I ordered a tuna special that I specifically asked to be cooked medium - it came to the table raw. Pretty untouchable for me. I know that chef's in general seem to like to sear their tuna - but if you ask for it medium, it should be somewhere close to that. If I recall correctly, my partner ordered some type of shrimp, that was pretty tasty but needed to be shelled at the table. OK if you have a well lit room and good eyes - but neither was the case. It made what should have been a delicious meal quite a challenge. The waiter was kind to us that night though - comped the deserts for us, which were actually very good, but didn't quite change the overall experience. Now, I have to admit that most people I have talked with really enjoy the Hamilton Grill room. We just don't appear to be in that group.

text: Unbelievably disappointed. I had heard so much about this restaurant. We arrived as a group of 3 with a small child treating ourselves to a lunch here, as lunch is a great way to experience an expensive restaurant without paying too much. Like others, I will comment that service was unbelievably slow. We started out with an order of a dozen of their assorted oysters. After 30 minutes, they asked if we would prefer eating our entrees first or our oysters. Our entrees were ready but it would take another 10 minutes for the oysters. That was an odd thing to ask and I didn't understand why. It's an open kitchen and there were very few filled tables. 3 cooks should have been found the time to shuck at least one oyster. We opted for the entrees as we were all getting filled on our second order of bread. It took 40 minutes for them to bring a kids cup of water for my son. I ordered a salad to be doubled up to be large enough for an entree. OK and definitely not spectacular arugula salad. 98% arugula and the rest was slices of pear, walnut crumbles and cheese. For what was essentially 15 dollars, I could have gotten a great "wow I wish I knew how to make this at home" salad at many other similiarly priced restaurants in Tampa. The other two diners I was with received an overcooked Wagyu burger and an Ok grouper sandwich. Oysters came out last and although we ate it, it frightened one member in our group because they were so warm. They were only ok oysters even if they were from NewEngland and Canada. For their name they should be serving spectacular oysters. Each adult had one order of alcoholic beverage and the meal came to 100 dollars. I don't mind paying alot for a good meal but I have spent just as much having dinner at any of the other great restaurants in Tampa and left with better service and better prepared food: food that blows your mind. When you are charging these prices, you are also promising a commensurate level of food quality and trained staff. We found neither. While the service staff are always present, it feels disorganized and undertrained. On a side note, as a Mom who enjoys eating out with her two kids, I find that the Kids Menu at many restaurants is a reflection of the management and the chef's attitudes towards food. Rarely have I ever seen such JUNK on a kids Menu: Hot dog and chips, PB&J and fries, Mac N Cheese and chips, etc. for 8-10 dollars??? You may argue that the restaurants are not catering towards kids but I would argue that if you serve junk, then your belief is that people don't know any better.

text: After hearing some recent praise about Le Meritage, my family decided to give it a shot for my father's birthday. The location has been home to several restaurants in the past, so the permanence of the restaurant is a little questionable. Upon our arrival we were greeted warmly and seated. The decor of the restaurant did leave a little to be desired. The place was a little bright for my taste and the art was just plain bad. Restaurants tend not to have as much freedom in their decor when inside of a hotel, but they could have done a better job nonetheless. The wait staff was very congenial and lively, which they tend to be in New Orleans. The menu was large and inviting. The twist about Le Meritage is the fact that you can select any dish on the menu as small or large plate (appetizer or entree) this provides and excellent opportunity for foodies and indecisive people alike to try a number of different dishes. We all elected to choose three dishes and do something of individual tasting menus. Each dish is paired with wine grouping right there on the menu, so if your knowledge of wine is somewhat limited, they have done what they can to idiot proof it. I ordered the gnocchi, crab cake and lamb. Each dish was impeccably done and stood along beautifully in its own right. I am a huge gnocchi fan in general and when I travel I often seek out what claims to be the best in a given city. This gnocchi dish was a great surprise. They were firmer that what I am used to, as they have been pan seared after the water bath; but the combination of that and the delicious sauce made it a truly excellent dish. The crab cake followed this. In a word, it was one of the BEST ever. My apologies to the state of Maryland, but this is one crab cake to try. Even though it was the "small plate" this crab cake was massive and done to perfection, it was just a delight. Lastly was the lamb. The lamb (as a small plate) was essentially a rack of lamb, but done as a single piece. It was cooked perfectly, the way anyone who loves lamb should expect. The meat was a great temperature and the inside was moist and juicy. Growing up in New Orleans and being privy to such amazing cuisine, I am rarely surprised and delighted by a restaurant, but I was there. Le Meritage had a wonderful attention to detail and I only detract from the 5 stars because of the decor. (Really it should be 4.5 stars)

text: I know, I know, I say this all the time--when you rate/review something, you're making a comparison; I think "x" is amazing because I've had "y." With this in mind, once again, I'm left with a headache inducing conundrum. Do I rate the Deacon under the "dive bars with food" category, or do I rate them as a regular restaurant? I've been here a few times now, because I wanted to check on their consistency. Here's what I know: 1.) The hummus and sweet potato salsa are both excellent (and I have a firm dislike of sweet potatoes) 2.) Their salads, while not amazing, are definitely solid. Kudos to you Deac, for making your own dressings. 3.) The curly dog sandwich is definitely unique, and also delicious. The fish and chips are decent. The veggie boudin burger wasn't to my liking, but then again, I'm the guy that would order "pork" if they offered it as a side dish. However, I'm going to agree with Nowell in saying that it is refreshing to try a veggie burger that doesn't taste like every other veggie burger--the lady seemed to enjoy it. 4.) Their vegan pineapple upside down cake was toted as "so good, you won't know it's vegan." Yes, yes you can tell it's vegan. Fail. Fire your copywriter. 5.) Their jukebox is pretty amazing. Limited selection, but hey, I can't complain since they decided to kick it old school and have a flipping board showing CD cover art (they still have CDs? I kid.). It is no surprise that the last two times i've been here, I've walked in to a fairly large intoxicated woman (different times, different women) singing along to Journey. Hey, it's the Midwest--I'd be happy to be a part of your reindeer games. But seriously, they have some pretty solid jukebox listings. 6.) I love the totally incorrect latin translation for "Saint Louis" in their avatar. I find it either ironically hip, or endearingly retarded. Overall, very decent food for a very good price. This may sound unfair, but the food is too good for a bar. I can't in good faith rate it as anything less than a full blown restaurant. The place is a little more on the "divey" side than I'm used to, but hey, I'm hip. Let me just find my self-deprecating t-shirt that alludes to my 80's youth. I know it's around here somewhere. Gather round kids, because apparently it's Halloween time and I'm handing out 4 star reviews like its candy...

text: My friend a huge carnivore had been excited about going to this restaurant for years, I went along hoping for a nice fish entree since I don't eat meat but will eat fish The steak selection in the case was beautiful. I liked that the waiter took the time to come over with a tray showing all the cuts of beef available and talked about where the meat came from. Nice touch, they are really proud of the beef they serve there. We shared a stuffed mushroom drowned in hollandaise sauce as an appetizer, I ate a few bites before realizing it was LOADED with bacon, no indication of this on the menu anywhere as an ingredient, unfortunately I have a bad reaction to meat thats why I don't eat it. The fish entree was off that night, out of the five or so fish entrees on the menu they only had salmon for some reason and I hate that so I ordered some of their creamed spinach and a potato. I had to send the spinach back because yet again they had bacon in it and no indication of that on the menu. My friend ordered a steak it looked great and he seemed pleased with it. The bill was very expensive of course and I left feeling pretty unsatisfied, but as a vegetarian going to a steakhouse I can't expect much more. The poor review is because a few hours after eating there my friend became deathly ill, vomiting, shakes and other symptoms of food that has not been handled properly. As a chef I know all too well the dangers of cross contamination, food that has not been kept to temp properly, etc. Probably a freak occurrence, but it was enough to turn off my friend and I forever to that restaurant. My friend was pretty heartbroken from the experience, as a hardcore carnivore visiting Charley's is supposed to be like a "mecca for meateaters" and ours (his especially) experience was really terrible.

text: When I saw the name of this Mexican BYO my first thought was "Chinicuiles". Hildalgo is one of the States of Mexico and Chinicuiles is their favorite food item. What they did have was authentic Mexican food, no tacos, burritos or chimichangas here. After the complimentary homemade salsa and corn tortilla chips we ordered an appetizer of flautas. Flautas are like a Mexican spring roll with spicy chicken wrapped in a corn tortilla, light fried then topped with a soft Mexican cheese - very good. For dinner I ordered the Chiles Rellenos, which was made with Poblano peppers stuffed with picadillo (ground beef, cheese or potato) that is dipped in egg and lightly fried. My companion ordered one of the specials, red snapper with avocado, lightly breaded and covered in a cilantro sauce. Some other items on the menu were Queso Fundio (a cheese melt with chorizo and chips), Cohnita Pibil (prok cubes with axiote baked in banana leaves) and many other pork, chicken and beef dishes. The restaurant is owed by a Mexican couple. She waits the tables and he is the chef. The service was friendly and attentive. The dinning room was clean and neat but not posh. We brought our own beer but they will supply margarita mix if you bring the tequila. Credit cards are accepted. Total cost of the meal before tip was $43.

text: I am genuinely shocked this place only averages three stars. Here's the deal: It's a BYOB, so you are completely eliminate your alcohol bill. The appetizers: the Antipasto is a MUST. Every, single, time. The grilled, marinated artichokes and eggplant, the BRUSCHETTA is addictive...it is phenomenal. The mussels are fantastic. If you want a salad, the arugula salad is a personal favorite - a light lemon vinegarette is addictive. But, if you order the chicken with it for an entree, the portion is huge...the shrimp, the one time I did I actually got three shrimp, so don't expect to be full if you get the shrimp. My husband loves the caeser with homemade croutons. The tomato, fresh mozzarella salad is beautiful and sizable. The bread is always delicious and the olive oil is always cold pressed and delicious. The tomato bread is also addictive. The pasta entrees: the Za Za is a personal favorite, my husband's spaghetti and meatballs were delicious - I hate sweet tomato sauce and this was salty and tangy. The pesto is very good but BE WARNED - they make it with cream, but if you ask, they will leave it out. Sensitive tummys have to be aware of that. The sausage, broc rabe, and chicken is very tasty as well. All of the portions are huge, so just accept the leftovers. The protein dishes as well as very sizable and the specials are VERY fairly priced and sound decadent, so don't be scared to order then for fear of $$. The pizzas are good - on a weeknight, it's very common for us to go grab an antipasto, a pizza, bottle of wine and call it a meal. The desserts: I don't even like dessert, and I will order something on a special occasion. The service is fantastic - I literally had one bad server like five years ago, and the manager remedied it IMMEDIATELY. Saturdays can be very busy, so bring TWO bottles of wine (one for the wait, one for the meal :)). Go, enjoy, don't break the bank. In the summertime, the outside dining is lovely. For a place to have me call things "addictive" and "personal favorite" this many times, you know I'm telling the truth!

text: This is hard for me to write, as I am a hopeless rabbit lover. I know too well about the importance (it's mandatory) of seeking out a "rabbit knowledgeable" Vet. For years, I used Penn Animal Hospital in Jennersville, PA - Dr. Beck -- who was superb. But it was an 1.5 hour shlepp each way, and obviously not practical in case of an emergency. So I switched to Radnor Vet. I didn't notice anything "off" at first, but soon I experienced the following supremely uncomfortable incidences. I am a freelance graphic artist. After being an established patient and having spent a good amount of $$ on bunny care (NOT cheap) , my business was slow. On a visit, I asked Dr. Donato if I could have a break, due to my current circumstances. To my astonishment, he flat out answered "No, I've been burned." This, coming from a Vet, really surprised me?? On another occasion, ~2yrs later, after at this point spending a few thousand dollars on my bunnies in a 5-7 yr span. During an exam, I asked Dr. Donato if he would mind if I wrote a post-dated check. (It would have been maybe 1 week delayed.) He said "that's fine." Then, in the waiting room while writing my check, suddenly his Office Mgr appeared and embarrassed me in front of the whole Reception area and other patients by stating rudely and loudly, "We don't accept post-dated checks here!" I felt humiliated. It was disturbing. At that point, Dr. Donato appeared and stated that he "forgot " to relay the message to his mgr. By that time, it was too late. I had already suffered embarrassment. It was awful! My last trip there was frantically driving a much adored bunny when his kidney failure had exacerbated. He died on my chest while enroute. When my little guy was pronounced dead, I collapsed. The vet (not Donato) said, and I quote "There will be no charge. Don't worry about any bill." That was 2 yrs ago. I have not been back. Fast forward to 3 days ago. I decided to adopt another bunny thru a Rabbit Rescue. Naturally, I gave Radnor Vet as my doc. When the Rescue checked references, Radnor told them I owed a balance of $55. I was clueless about this, since I hadn't been there for 2 yrs! More importantly, I NEVER received a bill. Becuz of this info from Radnor, the Rescue denied my application! Not to mention, having spent probably a few thousand dollars on the one bun, alone, with the renal failure. In conclusion, for these reasons, I would not recommend using this hospital, unless you're dripping with money. Dr. Donato has money signs in his eyes, and little to no human compassion. The adjective "Cloak & Dagger" comes to mind, since I have found him to be disingenuous. There are many other options for good Exotic (Bunny) care out there, and thats where I will go. Just research House Rabbit Society online and select "Recommended Vets". I hope this helps someone else. I don't want to see anyone else experience this.

text: I was visiting New Orleans for the first time on business and staying in the French Quarter. Though there were tons of places to eat, the French Quarter was full of tourists and I wanted to try a local restaurant. So, I went to Yelp as usual for some ideas and tips. Chochon came up as a restaurant with great reviews. I ended up walking there, took only 15-20 minutes, and got to see some less touristy spots of New Orleans but with cool local bars and restaurants. The food was amazing. We ordered okra and alligator to start, then my colleague had the rabbit and dumpling dish while I had a yummy catfish entree. The place was packed and we didn't call ahead for reservations, definitely need to do on Fridays and weekends. We were lucky and got a couple of seats at the bar and that was good too. The bar was exposed to the restaurant but you still had a nice intimate setting. Would recommend to anyone who wants to get away from all the tourists and see where the locals hang out. Just make sure to make reservations for the weekend.

text: Watch out now if someone approaches you at a Phillies game, Flyers game or other such public event asking you to enter win a grand prize like a spring-training getaway with the Philies or a new hummer. It's probably Sundance travel working on their customer recruitment scam. Cons -The whole banana - my hackles should have been raised when my wife got the call announcing we'd won an all expenses paid cruise to the Bahamas, but would have to meet in person at Sundance Travel's KOP office at 6:30 this past Tuesday to claim our prize. Like most folks, we never win anything, so it was tempting to be optimistic about this. This prize-winning approach isn't a scam so much as it is a bait and switch to get you into their office for a hard, hard sell on 'wholesale vacations': 30 of them for a modest up front investment of $20,000 which they'll happily finance at loanshark-like rates north of 16%. Yikes! Further Internets research yields varying accounts of the quality of the actual product, which seems to swell somewhat in price and underwhelm in the vacation experience. Needless to say, we didn't bite but it took a lot of perseverance as we weathered the gauntlet of escalating, heavy hard closes. You start in the group pitch which takes an hour, then your personal sales rep escorts you to a little table in a large sales floor among other tables, reps and marks and pump-up vacation music playing. If you don't buy, the rep calls in his boss, a sales manager, who attempts to sweeten the deal and close you again with some fancy math. If you make it past him, congratulations you can claim your prize, but you have to do so at the VP of Sales office. We were lead from the table to a couch outside his office and the level of anxiety I felt literally transported me back to first-grade visits to the principal's office. One last, lame attempt to close was made by the big shot behind the desk and he signed our vouchers for the cruise. It was the toughest two hours of my whole week. In the end we did get our 'prize,' but on examination of the fine print it looks like it's not so free after all (up front booking fees and port fees will cost about $500) and may be very difficult to redeem considering all the red-taped contingencies that must be met including black out dates, advanced notice, etc. All I'd really like now is to warn others about this experience, and maybe my two hours back. Think I could redeem the voucher for that?
label: NEG

text: Olio is exactly what Santa Barbara needs. Finally a place that serves thin crust neopolitan style pizza from a wood fired oven!! The restaurant is a cozy and charming creation with a great layout, excellent bar and bustling casual ambiance. We started out with the $5 garden salad which was decent, if slightly overdressed - but overall a good salad and a great price. For our main course we split the Pizza with Anchovies, Oregano, Mozzarella, and tomato. Our only complaint with this pizza was the misuse of the Anchovy which totally overpowered the pizza. They used whole chunks of Anchovy which gave the pizza a very very fishy flavor. I don't know many people who appreciate whole anchovy chunks. A better use might be grinding the anchovy with garlic and using is as a spread so you get the nutty flavor without the fishy. All and all a great new restaurant for Santa Barbara and we look forward to returning.

text: "DO NOT GO SEE DR. MICHAEL HORWITZ" I spent $500 at Feet For Life and did exactly what they instructed in order to cure the pain in my left foot, including a cortisone shot and purchasing an extra $85 pair of Vibram FiveFingers shoes. text: I had made a date with a young lady from Northeast Philly. After looking into some local fare, I decided to go with Kellys Seafood. The reason being that any restaurant that opened in 1958 and was still in business had to be a good choice. What an awful mistake of judgement on my part! If you check out my reviews, you will notice that I always try to find the positive in every establishment. The only positive at Kellys, was the waitress, who couldn't have been nicer or more efficient. We started off with the fried calamari app. This really was not bad at all. Very light, quite a large portion for the price, and a fairly good hot sauce as well. The waitress and the fried calamari almost made me go with two stars, but the entrees were so disapointing, I couldn't check the second box. I ordered the shrimp fra diavlo over linguini. When the dish arrived there were six shrimp floating on what appeared to be an oil slick similar to the now infamous Exxon/Valdez oil spill. I really thought they had forgotten the linguini, but to my suprise, somewhere about two inches below the surface was some really over cooked, oil soaked linguini. My date had about the same luck with her linguini with clam sauce. She was able to fill a small bowl with oil before locating her linguini. The server was so nice that I didn't have the heart to send this nautical nightmare back. Any cook that could send this disaster out of his kitchen, probably would have trouble boiling water! It's a shame that a place with nice atmosphere, and great servers would present a meal like this. The last reviews on this place were over two years ago, and seemed to be positive. Hopefully, they can bring the quality back again.

text: What a disaster in a pretty box! As we pulled up in the torrential rain, I was excited to be getting somewhere where we could watch the football game between the wedding and the reception. I should have known something was up when there was no one directing traffic through the port-cochere and no one to help us with our bags. We finally got a somewhat covered spot, though the wind was blowing the rain under in sheets, and proceeded to unload our bags ourselves while still wearing our formal wedding gear. Fun times. So we waited in the lobby while Keith checked in, and then proceeded to one of the two elevators, and up to room 326. The set up of this hotel is not that user-friendly - the elevators are at one end, and you have to traipse all the way down the hall if you have a high-numbered room. If there were a fire, you'd literally have to go the full length of the hallway to the stairs... Anyway, we get to the room, and the keys don't work. Keith goes back to the front desk who advises him not to put it near a cellphone. Ok, while that will disable the keys, it doesn't do it that quickly. So as he's walking back with the "fixed" key, a woman is walking practically alongside him. He stops at 326 where the rest of us are waiting, and so does she. "I think this is my room," she said. Oh, really. Well, we tried Keith's key, and sure enough it worked, and sure enough, the woman's husband was inside. Thank goodness he was dressed! So Keith goes down to the front desk to get us an unoccupied room. We wait since we don't want to haul our luggage until we know where we're going. The man and woman came out a few minutes later to say that he'd gotten a call from the front desk and apologized saying that they thought they'd put them in 235 and that they would reduce the rate on the room. So we headed to 235 because sure enough, that's what they gave Keith. Jokingly, I said "make sure you knock a few times first" to Keith when we arrived at the door to 235. Well, good thing he did, because there was a guy asleep in his pajamas in this room, and he was none too thrilled that we'd awoken him. So at this rate, I'm livid, and so are the rest of us. We take all of our luggage down to the front desk and drop it in a pile in front of everyone else when Jimmy says "This is the most embarrassing hotel experience I've ever had!" Fortunately, that got their attention, so Keith could quietly say "yeah, that one was occupied, too. Is it really too much to ask for an unoccupied room?" Everyone cleared away from the desk. The Bellhop was so scared that he walked briskly away and left his cart, so I stole it for all our luggage. Finally we here "Ok, 220 was just cleaned, so I know it's open." So we head to 220. And yes it was open. And it was a decently nice room. The front desk called when we'd been there about 15 minutes to ask if the room was acceptable and to offer a $20 discount. Then they called again 10 minutes later to ask the same thing and offer the same discount. Clearly, there were communication issues at the front desk. When we took the shuttle to the country club for the reception, it got us there directly with no issues, and even a polite hello and goodbye from the driver. Best service we got from Normandy Farms all day. At the reception we learned that they wrong number of rooms for 2 members of the bridal party, so it wasn't just us. The bed ended up being quite comfortable, though I woke up stuffed up, indicating that the air was too dry or the place was moldy and activated my allergies. The brunch buffet was extensive and most of it was quite good, though the stuffed pancakes were not in fact stuffed with blueberries as advertised and were extra mushy as if uncooked in the middle. The salads were great, and I was impressed by the fresh oysters. So Normandy Farms, you get one star for comfy beds and one star for brunch. Service was atrocious. If you stay at NF so you're to Blue Bell Country Club (I can't imagine any other reason to stay), at least get the brunch so you don't leave with such a bitter taste in your mouth.
label: NEG

text: Although I'm not a Santa Barbara local, I'm pretty sure this is the sort of shop that is loved by locals and tourists, alike. The number of offerings - from moderately-priced bottles to hard-to-find, high-end offerings - is staggering. We happened to visit on a Thursday, too, just in time for a free wine tasting with the owners and a number of other customers. We ended up blowing off our picnic plans to spend time enjoying the tasting, where we tried a number of different varietals, all of them excellent. From what I understand, the Grotto just changed ownership, but it was as if these two guys have spent a lifetime around wine. They were incredibly knowledgeable, extremely helpful, and just generally fun to spend a Thursday evening with; it's like we were out at a bar with friends - but they were friends we had just met. They were also very helpful in terms of pointing us to other fun activities in the area. I'd highly recommend the Grotto and its owners to anyone - local or tourist - with an interest in wine. text: I'm not a huge fan of frozen yogurt, but I must say that Yogurtland really delivers where it counts (at least what is most important to me). Good selection of flavors. Good taste. Texture is not too soft. Good variety of toppings. Decent syrups. And very reasonably priced ($0.30 per ounce). This Yogurtland, located on State Street in Santa Barbara, is not much different than other Yogurtlands out there. I tried their pistachio flavor, which was good. I also tried their lychee flavor--I definitely could taste the lychee; decent but maybe not for me. They have a lot of toppings and I went with some Fruity Pebbles, Cap'n Crunch and bananas. They had a lot of other stuff you would come to expect such as other kinds of fresh fruit, candy bars, cheesecake bites, chocolate chips, and so on. They had nice big Ghirardelli syrup dispensers. I tried the caramel and it was good. I went a little bigger than I usually do and my total was in the $3 range. Usually, I'm in the $2.50 range at Yogurtland. Service was pretty quick. There was a little bit of a line, which is often the case at Yogurtland shops. It can be a little frustrating because I worry that my frozen yogurt is going to melt. Of the self-serve frozen yogurt places I've tried, I would have to put Yogurtland at the top (though I could not really tell you what makes one frozen yogurt better than another one so the affordability of Yogurtland is weighing heavily here). Cherry On Top has a lot of toppings, but their frozen yogurt is too soft. Menchies has a lot of toppings too and their frozen yogurt has a nice texture, but they are too expensive. There are other frozen yogurt places out there, but for me at least they don't seem to provide a significant advantage over Yogurtland. Parking is available on the street (though hard to find); parking is also available at a nearby lot that is free for the first 75 minutes.

text: I was in town and stayed at the Ambassador, which is right down the street from Mothers. I had been told, "Try the poboys at Mothers. They're the best."
