It's fried seafood on bread. That's it. There's no magic to it. There's gravy. There's also coleslaw of some sort (at least I think it was a vegetable). But there's no magic. Poboys are fried seafood sandwiches without a single thing to recommend them beyond saying "I tried one". The poor, unsuspecting seafood is mercilessly fried into submission. There's no taste to it beyond "crunch" and "grease". The bread, which is supposed to be unique to the poboy, tasted like generic crusty baguette. I feel I've had McFish sandwiches that tasted better than these did. Between the terrible food, the atrocious customer service, and the generally unappealing nature of the place, I can't find a single redeeming thing about the place. I know there are many people who rave about Mothers and the food in New Orleans. I guess it's just not to my taste.

text: I've been walking to Manhattan Bagel all summer with my dog. Usually to pick up a whole wheat everything bagel...I'm in and out in under 2 minutes. And if a manager treats customers poorly, I know from experience, they treat the employees the same way. I was told my dog was no longer welcome at Manhattan Bagel due to 'insurance' reasons. Fine. No problem with that. But it was the way I was told. A manager that values customers would have been kind and would have offered a solution: "Since we don't have a spot you can tie your dog up outside, we'd have no problem if you called in your order and someone would run it out to you." And then maybe she could have smiled. But no. It was a bark (ha ha), a growl, and obviously, the manager really could give a crap if I return. And I was the Four Square MAYOR!!!! Sheesh. text: There are two Esau's Diners in and around the Santa Barbara area. One 10 miles south of SB, in Carp, and this one right downtown in Santa Barbara--recently risen from the proverbial ashes. Formerly the downtown Esau's was located on lower State street . It has now, after a year's absence, moved up a few blocks, and across one to Chapala, directly across from Paseo Nuevo. In its former location Esau's was everything you expected. A diehard surfer diner, primed for big breakfasts, and thanks to the UCSB crowd, open till late at night too. Noisy, busy, rough around the edges, but always fun, fast, and satisfying. Sadly, none of that seems to ring true in its new locale up on Chapala. It's been open for at least three months now, but we could easily have mistaken our recent foray there as if it was opening night. Long lines, inept waiting list helpers, and a front of the house crew who all seemed to be on their first ever food service shift. The service wasn't so much bad, as essentially non-existent. Nobody was nasty or offensive. Just simply not there. Even when someone did show up at the table, they were still not really there. Eyes glazed over, and clearly not interested in... well anything it seemed. Since we had however waited 45 minutes to get a table, once seated (akwardly) we opted to stay and order some lunch. (Breakfast time had since well passed). A Patty Melt and a Rueben Melt, one with fries, the other with rings. Food did arrive within a somewhat reasonable timeframe, but there was no love at all. Items were clearly tossed onto the plate, and thrown off the line as fast as possible. The sandwiches were edible, the fries well cooked, and the rings unfrozen. We ate, we paid, we tipped, and we will never return. This is not the Esau's we came to know and love when we first moved to SB 7 years ago. And it pains me to now know, that that Esau's down on State street will forever be nothing more than a pleasant memory.

Perhaps, I am foolish, but I actually thought they might call me if the car required more work than the initial estimate. I actually thought that was the point of verifying contact information. Call me crazy. I got a call the next day that the car was ready to be picked up and the bill would be $300 more than they had quoted because extra work was required. Needless to say, I was not pleased and decided to talk with them when I picked up the car. When there are problems, I prefer to deal with people face to face. The strange thing is a don't think that they even understood why how they handled my situation would upset someone. Too bad. The owner explained the difference in the quote and the extra work that was required, but could not explain why he didn't call me again before doing $300 more work. I won't ever go back to this mechanic because there is no good reason not to call a customer when a bill is going to be substantially more than the estimate. He said that it was not practical to call customers every time that a part had to be added and that I would be just as upset about being called several times and nickled and dimed. No, not really. I just like to know what's been done and what it's going to cost so I can authorize it. I have never had a mechanic do work to a car without talking to me and getting it approved. Except for at Quality Care. Although they were polite in handling the problem, they did not offer me anything except removing of the part and leaving me with a car that would not run. Again, since the work was not authorized ahead of time, I consider it extremely poor service. To add insult to injury, I got behind the wheel of my repaired car after paying the bill and the check engine light was still on. Overall, I believe they are good mechanics and honest, but the manner in which they handled the quote and repair left quite a bit to be desired. text: I took some time to read the other reviews before I wrote mine, so do not think the two stars is a snap judgment. Like many others, I've been coming to Zern's my entire life. I have been bringing my son there since he was born, and my 90+ year old Aunt tells stories of when it was new and in the middle of nowhere. But Zern's has changed, and not in a good way. I've watched the cafeteria close and never be replaced by a business that has stuck for more than a season. I've seen the flea market reduced from a huge venture to a few very old retailers hawking the same products they've been selling for the last ten years. Watched as craftsmen and real vendors have been replaced by dollar store vendors, siding salesmen, roof repair hawks, and empty stalls. Even the huge army navy store closed a couple years ago. replaced by a bunch of smaller craptastic hawkers. Spring Glenn farms, the last true purveyor of true PA Dutch food closed a few years back (Allentown Market Fair has a stall). There is only one Bakery left, and they are hit or miss with what they have, and Burts Farms, the best purveyor of meat in the market, closed this week. Years ago you'd see local farmers selling fresh produce along side their wives, who sold their jams, jellies, and fresh baked goods baked fresh early that morning. Do you remember? Zern's apparently does not. Yes - there are still some glimmers of hope. Little Richards, eternally staffed by teens still serves a decent lunch. The spice shop is well stocked and fair priced, and (some) of the fruit and veggie vendors still sell decent local produce. But the decent vendors are fast fleeing, and management seems content to let the market die. Maybe they'll put in a nice Wal*Mart - wouldn't that be grand?

text: My second trip to New Orleans did not involve family, so Bourbon Street was a different experience. I went twice this trip, once drunk and once sober, and that also made a huge difference. Sober, Bourbon Street is a spectacle, but not quite as fun as when your head is swimming in hand grenades. The concept of Bourbon Street is pretty awesome - it's like a Disneyland of night-time revelry. You don't really go and sit in one place nursing a drink. You buy a hand grenade or a huge cheap beer from any random stop in the street and keep walking. Hand grenades, incidentally, are kind of nasty. They go down pretty easy, though, especially in ice-blended form. On our drunken night, somewhere far down Bourbon Street my boyfriend and I stopped to sit on some stairs. We were approached by a man who called himself Buckethead. He had a giant white plastic bucket and he offered to make up a song for us. We were hooked and he asked our names and proceeded to sing a rather racy little jingle with his head stuck deep in the bucket, which provided some wobbly acoustics. We were happy to put a few bills in the bucket when he was done. Several minutes later, another man surprised us by declaring us under arrest for public drunkenness. He turned out to be a rather hilarious civilian who talked to us for a few minutes in what amounted to a well-put-together stand-up routine. He called himself Catfish, and he earned a few bucks from us, too. If every panhandler in the world had that much of the street performer in him, we'd have a much greater distribution of wealth. We thought about entering a strip club, but the street itself was so rich with entertainment that we just stuck with drinking and walking. What a lively place.

We waited again, for at least 10 minutes for him to come back and take our drink order. Not complicated. Isn't that what a server does? Finally he came back, no personality at all. I mean, nothing. Stone wall. He took our drink order. Then, we waited another 20 minutes for him to come back with our drinks and to take our food order. The drinks weren't anything to write home about. So...we waited...again...I think we spent more time in there doing nothing than we did actually eating. Isn't that what a restaurant is? An eating experience? Still there were tons of servers, standing around, doing nothing. I guess we walked in on social hour. But, aren't these people on the clock? Because at my job, I start working the moment I walk in. Anyway... We finally got our food. Things just placed on the plate. Nothing special. My friend got a Chipotle Turkey Burger that came with nothing on it. It was a turkey burger and a bun. She had to flag him down again, to ask where the Chipotle sauce was and the onions and the avocado and spinach was. He replied, "ohhhh, you wanted a Chipotle Burger??? I didn't hear you say that". Ummmm....there is only one turkey burger on the menu. And, that is the only one. At this point, it was just bad. I didn't get my salad. Instead I got watery cole slaw aka cabbage and tiny bits of carrot slopped in a bowl. But, I just didn't want to deal with him anymore. My friend got the burger and yet again, there was no chipotle sauce, spinach, avocado...etc...Great. I mean, seriously. I work in customer service. I mean, I work for a company that is rated #1 in customer service. I get service crammed into my soul everyday. So, when I am out, all I have as an expectation is that the person (who applied and got a job working in customer service meaning, you chose this position) does at least their job. I don't need a server to be my best friend. I don't need a server to come over to the table every five minutes. Just do your job. This isn't the first time this has happened. And, friends and family have said the same thing. Instead of spending all this money making the place look pseudo-hip, spend the money on hiring staff that actually care about their jobs. Servers rely on tips to make money. That is your job. At least attempt to give a crap. I will never eat here again. Thanks.

text: I really wanted to have a good experience but alas, it wasn't so hot. We had lunch here a few weeks ago. It was the middle of the week around 2/2:30 and the place was empty. I was relieved because I always hear how busy it is on the weekends. The service was fine and so is the atmosphere/decor. I love the photos on the wall. So far so good... We ordered: The breakfast salad (aka Salad Lyonnaise) The flatbread white pizza (tomato, spinach, garlic & ricotta) Coffee Passion fruit soda "peanut butter" cookie The Salad Lyonnaise was good but not by any means one of the best I've had. Unfortunately the poached egg was way overcooked, leaving me with a solid egg yolk. This bums me out because if you're a lover of the lyonnaise salad, you know that breaking the yolk and mixing it into the salad is an integral part of dressing the salad. So without a yolk, there's wasn't as much flavor. They serve it rustic style, meaning bigger potatoes and bigger slabs of bacon, with huge hunks of fat on them as opposed to the more traditional cubed lardons. I'm not crazy about the huge hunks of fat they leave on the bacon although I appreciate the flavor they lend. I tend to lean more towards the traditional cubed and crisped lardons but hey, it's still bacon, and hey, I guess that's why they call it the breakfast salad instead of Salad Lyonnaise. Anyway, long story short; it was good but not great and certainly not one of the better ones I've had in the city. The white flat bread pizza was just...awful. Not only did it lack flavor but it was so dried out and hard as a rock. It tasted like it had sat out for hours, been heated, sat out again and the re-heated, and then served to my mother. My poor mom, I'm always excited to bring her to these places I hear great things about and she always ends up with the worst dish. Anyways, I wouldn't recommend it...at all. The passion fruit Italian soda I had was good but I probably should have ordered black cherry since I like the flavor better. Coffee was barely lukewarm. Our server was kind enough to heat it up for my mom. The decaf is not so great but the Sumatra had a good rich flavor. The Cookie: When I went to pay at the register I noticed some naughty looking cookies nearby. I spotted a big old peanut butter cookie with the mashed fork impressions in it and I immediately bought one and brought it back to the table. Christ, what a dick tease. That cookie tasted nothing like a peanut butter cookie. It tasted more like a cross between a snickerdoodle and a sugar cookie. blah. I dunno...maybe it wasn't peanut buttter flavored...? If it wasn't then it should be illegal to put those crossed fork impressions in them! I'm going to give this place a few more tries. It had to have been a fluke. But until then this cat gets 2 stars.

text: While I don't detect any difference amongst the various locations, I should say that this review is specifically about the newer location at Manchester and Rock Hill (which is not apparently in the Yelp database). Buckle your seatbelts, because this is going to be harsh. Let's establish some background first. I love BBQ. I grew up with it around every corner in Tennessee. I make it. I've been in large competitions. But....I'm not a BBQ 'snob'. I've had edible BBQ come out of a home oven before that had never so much as seen a piece of wood, much less any smoke (god forbid). So I don't require that there be a 3/4 inch smoke ring and a dark bark to put it in my mouth and force myself to swallow (that's what she said). Smoke is not an issue at Bandana's however. Plenty of that. But it's frankly just not that good. The pulled pork in particular. I think my dog might turn up his nose at it. Let's get something straight right off the bat, *pulled pork* should be *pulled*....not chopped, sliced, minced, or diced. Duh. And why the hell is their pork slightly slimy on the outside? How are they keeping this stuff heated? The sides aren't very good either for that matter. The food has so turned me off that when my sons entire baseball team decided to go there (to my chagrin), guess what I ordered? A baked potato. "Oh, you mean our loaded baked potato with pork, cheese, and sauce on it? Very good choice sir. A popular item". "Yes please. Oh, and could you hold the pork, the cheese, and the sauce?" "But, sir, that would just be a plain baked potato" "Exactly" Only pluses I can even find within me to mention would be that their spicy sauce is pretty good, and they make great iced tea. So if you're thirsty, and you have a craving for squirting sauce straight out of the bottle into your mouth then I suppose this would make a good place for you to go.

My friends all got the lobster bisque and they were raving about it. Three of us ordered steaks while one got the meatloaf. My filet mignon was cooked perfectly (med-rare) and the other two that got steaks echoed my sentiments. The friend that got the meatloaf was very pleased with his dish as well. All of the sides we ordered (we did some sharing) were delicious and fairly sizeable - which is good considering they're all a la carte and far from cheap. Dessert was the only blight of the night. text: We chose Kota for our 'regular-dinner-get togethers' last Saturday night with friends. It is one of many 'to-try' choices in my Yelp bookmarks. For a party of 8, there was no trouble getting a table as the Fox was vacant this weekend. I am sure this is a much different venue with the pre-show crowds. Nevertheless, love the location of this place and the real city-feel you get in Grand Center. Suffice it to say, having lived in the city for many years, Grand Center really has come to life. The service was aces, with a very attentive hostess, bartender and server. Again, it was a slower night. The waitress even walked us to the table pointing carefully to the short set of stairs. The decor is tasteful with carefully selected art and a huge row of colored glass and low lighting to add ambiance. Very comfortable space. Trying to describe 'New American' style of cuisine invites some laughter, but indeed it's interpretation can vary depending on the chef. Someone in our party got excited for the cajun dishes offered, another the variety of vegetarian choices. Presentation was good. We started with the calamari, ahi tuna tostadas and stuffed mushrooms for the table. Our entire group seemed pleased. The tostadas have been reviewed before, and they are that good - not the best by any means - but served on a plantain chip gave this app a good flavor. For the main course, I ordered the Voodoo Shrimp Pasta (hickory fired shrimp with squid ink fettuccini in jalapeno cream sauce, with roasted corn and poblano peppers). And it appeared every one asks the server what 'squid ink' fettuccini is; simply by the look on her face when we did the same. For the record, it is just dark-colored noodles. The flavors were great. The cream sauce brought out the bite and made the shrimp rather tasty and juicy. Good dish. We had a duck connoisseur of sorts on-hand and commented on trying that the coconut curry duck linguini was very lacking. It was the only dish that offered us an option of leftovers. The jambalaya - made with mussels - was said to be very good. Before I forget, Koda offers Delirium Tremens on tap here which is an excellent Belgian pale ale if you like yours strong. Because of it's proximity to the Fox, I am sure the mood of the restaurant changes between casual and semi-formal, depending on the night. My recommendation, to soak in the surroundings and your meal, go when there is not a show. But alas, it fits the bill for a perfect dining option where you can where your jeans and yet eat a refined, creative menu.
label: POS

text: There are more Claddagh's spreading across the midwest, but this is the original and still the best. The owners are from Ireland (Galway, if I remember correctly), and everything is extremely authentic. The codfish (fish & chips) is phenomenal. Unless you're on a gorgefest, just get the small order. Believe me, it's more than enough. Also, the mussels are some of the best I've ever had inland, and better than the majority I've had even in the northeast. Some of the other dishes aren't quite as impressive, but much of that could just be because I think they give you way too much food. I'll take a couple points off for the smoking. Indianapolis's "smoking ban" is one of the most toothless I've ever seen, as it seems that every place possible has just used the loophole of declaring part of the restaurant "over 21" and turning that into the smoking section. In a place as open as the Claddagh, the "ban" is completely worthless.

text: Chad's Steakhouse and Saloon. Bland, Boring, Tired and Expected I really enjoyed reading Courtney Colainanni's interview of Executive Chef Satchi Buber in Tucson Guide*. Unfortunately, that's all I enjoyed. Chef Buber is a proud Hungarian that grew up learning traditional recipes from his mother. Meat and spices were the focus of the nomadic people that arrived in the Hungarian region in 800 AD and it remains the main focus of Hungarian cuisine today. Unfortunately, Hungarian Cuisine doesn't seem to have had much influence on Chef Buber. Hungarians gave us hot paprika, sweet paprika, sausages and goulash. So far Chef Buber only gives us bland, boring, tired and expected. A wagon wheel and small stream by the door with a too-small sign floating above sets the tone for the tired "decorations" inside. Chad's wants to be a wild west saloon.... desperately.... but it's trying too hard and using old, worn out, faded ,stereotypical trinkets. Lighting is too harsh to be enjoyable or realistic. Back room activities were instead performed right in front of me with a tiny screen embarrasingly trying to hide it. (See photo). The "comes with it" salad arrived on a nice, chilled, pewter platter. But the mostly iceberg lettuce, carrot slivers, broccoli, and tomatos composed salad had no flavor. Even the bleu cheese crumbles they sprinkled on top were bland for bleu cheese. I ordered the rib eye because in his interview, Chef Buber said it was his most flavorful steak with great marbling. If this is his most flavorful steak then the rest of his steaks have negative flavor. While it did have great marbling and it was cooked to medium rare just as I ordered it had absolutely no flavor. None. The baked sweet potato had been baked dry and served with a plastic cup of butter and another of brown sugar. Rather disturbingly the potato had been cut to measurement and weight. I understand the need to maintain portion sizes.... but don't make it a glaring part of the presentation of my meal please. If sweet potatos are so expensive that you must do this make mashed sweet potatos so it's not so obvious. Cowboy Beans (baked beans with more onion) were oddly served in a small crock to be shared at the table. They were spiced... but seemed canned. The staff is well educated on cuts of meat. Nice job. Management is attentive and quick to fix problems but they stand by the kitchen door and stare at the patrons like anxious teachers expecting a fight on the playground. The desserts are prepackaged and oh so worn out. Cheese cake, mud pie, Death by chocolate..... yawn. ... sorry. I didn't bother. I expected an incredible, savory, craveable steak dinner from this up and coming young chef. That didn't happen. Something tells me Chef Buber is one to watch but for now he's not the one to cook. . . . *read the interview in......Tucson Guide, Winter 2008-2009, page 79. tucsonguidemagazine.com

text: We met some friends staying at the Royal Sonesta across the street. They wanted to check with their hotel concierge for recommendations. The concierge walked around from the desk, grabbed my friend's arm, and practically marched us over to Oceana Grill, which was across the street. The aggressive marketing (and what I can only assume are kickbacks to hotel staff) set a bad tone for the meal -- how good can a restaurant be if they have to try that hard? One couple in our group ordered an appetizer of fried eggplant that was tasty, although I recommend skipping the blend of ketchup and mayonnaise that they served as a sauce. (Ask if they have a marinara.) I ordered "Redfish Amer" ($18), which was pan-fried redfish smothered in a creamy crawfish sauce. I grew up on the gulf coast, where we used to catch our own redfish. I can only assume the redfish in my dinner (if it was indeed redfish) was farm-raised. At first bite, I thought it was catfish -- it tasted like the bottom of a lake! The crawfish sauce was bland almost to the point of being tasteless. It was like hollandaise with no lemon, with some chewy red bits of meat thrown in. Several people at our table ordered the "Taste of New Orleans" ($16), which was a trio of Crawfish Etoufee, Red Beans and Rice, and Jambalaya. The jambalaya had a pleasant spiciness, but the rice was a little gummy and the sausage was a little rubbery. This was the first time I've had jambalaya, and I would have to try it at a better restaurant before I passed final judgment. The etoufee was bland but passable. Is it possible that they used canned beans for the red beans and rice? I'm just not sure. On the plus side, we had a group of nine and we were seated immediately. We had some picky children eaters with us, but they had a kid's menu if you asked -- Chicken fingers or fried shrimp or fried cheese sticks (each served with fries) for $5. The mixed drinks were $6 and served in large schooners. The service, while not superb, was adequate - no complaints there. The prices, which seemed a little high at first blush, may not be too far out of line for a touristy restaurant just off Bourbon Street. Portions were large -- a couple could easily share an appetizer and one entree and fill up.

text: This place is crap. I went here for a wedding over the weekend the decor was nice however the food was/is downright terrible. Firstly we had escarole soup which was good. Next was a caesar salad which was bland and had no flavor. Next up was a trio of salmon, fillet and veal. The salmon was hard and had obviously been cooked hours ago and sitting in a sauce. The fillet was OK. And now for the big reason for the one star the veal. The veal was a nice veal, not milk fed, and had been rolled up with i believe prosciutto and cheese. I took a bite and it was OK, however i felt something on my tongue. I reached it my mouth and pulled out the longest BLACK hair you could possibly think of. I along with the rest of my table was disgusted and stopped eating. Truly a very memorable experience in deed! Next was the argument i got into at the bar. They had two bars in the main ballroom one at each opposite end of the corners of the room. I walk over and nobody is there. I proceed to chat with a friend figuring that somebody will come back. I started commenting on the fact that its now been a while with my friend and we now time it. 7 minutes go by and the bartender is not back. I see the beers lined up at the bar so i go and take one. Immediately as i take one a bartender comes running back and says, that I can't do that. I say I'm sorry but somebody hasn't been here for a while and its a wedding I'm not wasting my time in line for a beer. He proceeds to rip it out of my hand. I was not pleased and went and complained to management who stuck up for the employee. I said as a manager of a banquet facility you should have some brains and have a bar back for the bartenders if they run out of stuff they should have coverage. Its not right for him to leave the bar for periods of time like that. I will never go here again, I assure you that i will make sure all of my friends know about the hair and the lack of bartender staff. I will make sure to post this so that brides and grooms are well aware of the issues, so that they can make wedding plans accordingly. Be warned this place is deceiving, it looks nice in the outstide but on the inside where the food/service count for a wedding its downright TERRIBLE.
label: NEG

text: Well... besides the grim and debris build up on all surfaces this place has cold beer, tvs and i have heard the food is ok. I have not been strong enough to try it yet as the grease and food covered walls are a turn off for me. I would say go have a beer and watch a game. The staff is standoffish and abrupt (everyone other than the English bouncer) so bring your own company to enjoy.
label: NEG

text: I've been to this book store a couple times during visits to NO and I really like it. The owner is really a nice guy and fun to talk to. This time, he pointed me immediately to the book I was looking for, a social and economic history of the city. I can envision returning to this store every time I am in NO.

text: Food was terrible but not as bad as the service. After we waited 45 minutes for a table we asked about our table and the hostess rudely told us she never wrote our name down. We waited a few more minutes and were seated. After ordering we waited over an hour for our appetizer which was just spinach and artichoke dip. 4 tables that sat after us ate appetizers and lunch and paid before we received our appetizer. We questioned our waiter about our food, he then apologized and quickly brought out all of our food which was disgusting. The gumbo was terrible, the BBQ pork sandwich was bland, the fish steak sandwich was over cooked/dry and the pastrami poor boy was tasteless. They promised to comp us something because of the mix up and when we got the bill NOTHING they promised was removed from the bill. After I questioned the waiter on the bill he only took of the spinach and artichoke dip which was basically the best thing we had. Overall I would never go back there again!
label: NEG

text: I go there for their jalapeno tempura and their Spicy Hit Roll cooked yellowtail, eel, masago, cucumber, spicy sauce. Dont forget to get their white sake.
label: POS

text: Food is way below par, and we feel cheated, calling this an ethnic restaurant is just not fair. There was only one Pho on the menu and it lacked any flavor, it tasted like a packet Pho with a few things thrown in, although actual beef was fine if a little overdone. I had the eggplant with pork, alledgedly flavored with fish sauce, there was no fish sauce in it I had to ask for it, and the eggplant just tasted of oil. It was awful, this was not first day shambles, the point is a resteraunt has to deliver to its public and if you just dont have a chef that understands the food...even if they are Vietnamese.....our food sat for 3 minutes on the counter while the owners hugged and congratulated themselves with friends so it was pretty cold when it arrived. So its still back to trudging up Charlotte Pike or out to Murfreesboro road for real ethnic food. My husband never complains but he did first in this case. Oh well, I suppose there will be an army of people who will accept this kind of delivery and like what is on offer so they dont need us. The tables and chairs and decor were OK if you like modern cafe decor. The service was bizarre, please employ real servers!
label: NEG

text: What a horrible experience it is, shopping at this store. I am a mac user by default (I am not a loyal cultist, but there is nothing better out there). I actually enjoyed this store more when it first opened and it wasn't as impersonal. Now however it is crowded and the sales people are less than helpful. I don't think that the latter stems from the former. One thing that really bothers me here is that there seem to be service charges for everything. Want a bag to put your item in? That will be a 2.00 service charge. Would you like an indifferent Apple Store employee to put the item IN the bag? That's an extra 5.00 service charge. Worse still, when I brought my laptop in for a repair a while back, during the repair week, I got a few hard sell phone calls from the store reps trying to convince me to buy extra insurance coverage. They even tried to guilt trip me! There is no benefit--no discount, no nothing- that you get from buying your Apple products here. I use Micro Center for all my Apple needs.
label: NEG

text: My family recently stayed there for four nights. The room has 2 king-size beds, huge restroom. built on 2007 as the frontdesk said. I paid $40 /night on priceline.com for it, but actually the hotel website offered a better price, like $35. They charged extra service fee $11, but it is totally acceptable. Free Wifi. Free parking. Will stay there in our future trip.

text: The crepe/blini things here are amazing in texture and taste, superlative. That's the short story. I've been here for lunch, once, and got a chance to try both a ham and cheese crepe lunch special and thanks to a generous co-dining family member, the cabbage rolls. The ham and cheese part of the crepe was solid (for me, tastewise, but also literally in that the cheese was unmelted, phasing at least one co-diner), but the crepe itself was in fact something to write home about. The cabbage rolls were not overpoweringly savory. Just perfectly savory. Borscht came with the lunch special and was a good introduction to the tastes to come. There was more cabbage and less beet than others I've had... there seems to be a wide variety. I'll definitely be heading back on Friday to try the stroganoff.

text: This restaurant did not live up to its reputation. I went with 4 colleagues there for lunch. All of our fish dishes were drowning in butter, even the one that was supposed to be grilled and prepared more healthily. Also, the vegetable side dishes were meager and uninspiring. Our waiter, who was going to help us get through the menu and order special Creole dishes for us, just read the menu, down the specials list. There are much better restaurants in New Orleans, especially at the price point of Galatoire's.
label: NEG

text: I'm a lover of great sushi and Naked Tcopstix is defintely #1 on my list in Indy (Edging out Sakura SLIGHTLY). Not only do they have FABULOUS sushi (who can deny the delectableness of the Playboy Roll and the Spider Roll?), I am absolutely in love with their Spicy Tofu/Seafood. I AM NOT a fan of Tofu but I LOVE the Spicy Tofu. Shortly thereafter I tried the Spicy Seafood and they are SO delicious. A little pricey but worth it in my opinion.
label: POS

text: Who could have ever imagined that food served at this orange double-wide with hand-painted "Thai Food" signs (with the last few letters crammed on the plywood HA!) leaning up against the porch would be so delicious?? It is! The curries are all great. The pad thai with tofu is perfect. It has changed my wife's mind about pad thai. She has found every other pad thai uninteresting but this one is delicious! When they have mangos, the sticky rice and mango is a must order. The only downside of this funky little trailer home is that it gets pretty cold inside in the winter. If you're coming in during the colder months bring a hat, coat, and scarf. Better yet, be prepared to walk in check the thermostat and if it's under 60 in there order your food to go and head home. They have replaced the one little electric space heater on the table with a little better upright heater, but it's cold in there if you're not sitting right next to it. The deck looks like a fun place to eat in the summer. Definitely becoming a regular so I'm sure we'll be enjoying that when it warms up.
label: POS

text: Eh. Not a bad place. Prices aren't bad and they will fill up your gas tank at a really good price. They are very quick, which is awesome. My problem was that the inside of my car wasn't cleaned that well (vacuumed quickly, but the dash/window were not wiped down or anything) and when I got home I realized they hadn't cleaned the dead bugs off my front bumper, the whole reason I went to the carwash in the first place. Maybe if my car was less dirty I wouldn't have minded, but come on...I was paying you to do that! My boyfriend said afterwords that I could have told them to do it while I was there, but I didn't notice until I was already home. Oh well. Car needed a wash anyway, but I'm not really cool with paying for a car wash and still having a dirty car.
label: NEG

text: I SO wanted this place to do it for me. When I go for a salad downtown I always go to Bitter Creek. So, for a change I thought I would try the Falcon today. What an incredible disappointment. I ordered the Steakhouse salad which was topped with and incredible marinated steak. The rest of the salad was one of the worst I have ever had. On two occasions I removed pieces of lettuce from the salad that had that brown nasty part of the lettuce that you typically throw away. The lettuce was also a bit soggy as if it had spent some time in the fridge. The same with the tomatoes. The dressing sucked and I had to eat half of the salad to find it. The servers are friendly and fairly efficient and the atmosphere is better now that they moved to their new location. The beers are limited but its not a bad selection. They now have a huge outdoor seating area that catches the full sun during lunch. I guess its back to the Bitter Crotch for salads....
label: NEG

text: when i first started going here, the service was great and the food was fantastic. the last time i was here, though, was my fiance's mom's birthday dinner. we went because they heard us raving about the place. very disappointing. they upped the prices drastically (for no apparent reason). my scallops were chewy and milky. (ew.) the service was terrible. we waited forever just to get water and bread, and even longer to have our order taken. let's just say i felt bad for recommending the place.

text: My only experience with this Ted's stemmed from husband's last minute desire to eat some prime rib coupled with not wanting to dress up for and pay $100 a person at a fancy restaurant. Since Philly has no Outback, it looked like Ted's would suffice. Wrong. After waiting 15 minutes to be seated (when only three other tables in the huge restaurant were occupied), we waited another 20 minutes for a waiter (while many whizzed by our table) before I finally got up and hunted one down. I was in a burger mood, so ordered their steer burger. Husband excitedly requested medium-rare prime rib. They were out. They were also out of rare, medium and medium-well. This was at 7:00 on a Saturday night! We should have just left but, deciding to make the best of it, husband ordered strip steak instead. Long story short: overcooked burger, wet bun, overcooked super-salty steak, absent waiter, wrong check, etc. We will not go back. The only thing that saved this from a "1 star" is the fact that it might have been a good place to get reasonably priced prime rib if they had any.
label: NEG

text: This has to be good for a tourist. Because the food cannot pass for New Orleans cuisine for people that are from here. Nothing intresting that sticks out the menu. The last time I was there, I didn't know what to order.. Nothing seemed appealing. The only upside to this place is the cheesecake.
label: NEG

text: I made a few new friends at Outback. One was a small cockroach that greeted me at our table. The next was his winged kin who fell to drunk death in a pool of my rotten margarita. The sour mix tasted like it'd been wrung through a sock and mixed with tequila. Our server greeted us with a nervous over-zealousness and when the table behind us asked to speak with the manager, this was their exchange: Woman: I ordered the mixed green salad. This ain't mixed greens. Manager: Well ma'am I'm very sorry about that. This is the salad featured in the menu though. Woman: No, the salad on the menu says "mixed greens." This is iceberg. Manager: Oh. Well. Ok. Would you mind if I asked what exactly you mean by "mixed greens?" Woman: What? Manager: Um. We only have iceberg and romaine lettuce. Woman: Mixed greens is different shapes of lettuce. It's like spinach. But it ain't spinach. They proceed in a stare down contest and ultimately the manager, who is no match for her downtown sass, quivers and backs down. The broccoli that complimented my New York Strip tasted like it had been frozen for four years, the ketchup that came out of the bottle tasted fermented, and I actually refused to eat the mushrooms. If this is what Australia tastes like, you can count me out.

text: Its not bad : 3stars. It just used to be much better. Tho the ribs are still pretty solid. It must be a Penn gentrification thing, price goes up quality & quantity goes down.

text: I'm giving the new SB Ruth's Chris only 4 stars because I'm comparing it to RC on the island of Maui. That was my first taste of a RC steak and I was hooked. I remember it being the perfect experience, but maybe that's because it was Maui and my honeymoon. So needless to say RC in LaCumbre Plaza will probably never be 5 star. I had the ribeye which was huge and spectacular tasting. My wife's Filet looked amazing but I don't think I got to actually taste it. She's funny like that. Ha, Ha, real funny babe. The salmon dish looked tasty and there was a huge piece of fish. My ideal meal at RC is the Rib Eye sides of veggie and potatoes and a green salad with blue chesse. My in-laws have this thing about always ordering the cheapest glass of wine so they had the Pinot that was $16 and I had a Zin that was at least $17. Let's put it this way if you get a gift certificate to RC for $100 you better go by yourself. I would never go there if I was paying. Absolutely no atmosphere, the valet parking guy will actually just pull into a spot in the gynormous parking lot 5' away, the serves are not refined in any way, and my steak was not perfect. I would never pass up a chance to eat here as long as someone else was paying. Eating in the bar would be a great option.
label: POS

text: I love the idea that a restaurant can showcase such a simple dessert item and still be able to create original interesting flavors. Their creations were whimsical and yet delicious at the same time. This is a wonderful place to stop by with the family or by yourself and enjoy something sweet. I like how they use a buttercream based frosting instead of a royal icing. It is not too sweet.
label: POS

text: I've read a lot of positive reviews about this place but I was just not impressed. The only exciting aspect of my dining experience was drinking a very cheaply priced margarita, and hey I love margaritas, and also running into my friend while drinking said margarita. Mmm good combination. The food though was lackluster. If you are looking for inexpensive and cheap quality Mexican food (if authentic concerns you not) this is your place but honestly I'd prefer the Fresh Mex variety of Chipotle or Qdoba, which lack the same restaurant atmosphere but you choose your battle... I got excited to see a chicken mole dish on the menu, I love a rich coffee, chocolate spicy mole sauce so I figured I'd give it a go...horrible mistake. The sauce was a light brown, almost reddish and had the taste of vomit. The chicken was shredded and combined with the sauce seemed like it had been regurgitated onto my plate. The "Mexican" rice was dry and non-descript and the limp iceburg and tomato garnish didn't do much to freshen the plate. Needless to say i couldn't finish the food, and not because i was full. I didn't bother to bring home leftovers and for me that is rare. My friend ordered chicken enchiladas and didn't finish them. I didn't get too much feedback from her except that they were ok, decent. The chips and salsa were tasty however, I'll give it that but thats not usually too hard to mess up unless the chips are cold or soggy or the salsa too spicy. Perhaps other menu items were better or perhpas I'm too picky but i will not be back.
label: NEG

text: Billie's Fine Food is an old school diner hidden in Soulard just east of Broadway in the industrial section. I come here for it's satisfying breakfast, usually ordering the chicken fried steak covered in gravy with hash-browns, eggs and toast or biscuits. It's a gut buster, but it sure hits the spot! The menu also offers pancakes, biscuits & gravy, lunch items, etc. I'd give the food 3 stars, but the character of the place and the friendly service adds to the experience and gives it an additional star.
label: POS

text: A large group of us stopped in here rather late on a weekday. That might have been our first mistake but in no way were we pushing the limits of their closing time either. We just needed a place to eat that would accommodate 8 people. We sat on the balcony overlooking Bourbon. I ordered a burger. Tasted okay going down but definitely nothing special. We were starving and this place filled the void. Service was extremely rushed. Later that night the horrible stomach cramps and diarrhea began. It lasted for two days. Sorry if that's TMI but consider yourself warned!
label: NEG

text: I am sitting at the bar as I write this. They are nine days since opening and I am in heaven. 25 beers on tap and an audience of folks ranging from ten months to sixty years. I NEVER got to a place so soon after opening bc I like to see a place with their A game. Kraftwork is on their A game and have pleased me mightily. We enjoyed some of our favorite styles of beer (me: imperial stout; him: ipa). Along with the vegetable platter. The Faux Gras was so.damn.good. I also have to respect the place b/c they only have 5 or 6 liquors behind the bar and make some solid traditional mixed beverages. The staff also seems to help each other out, with all asking if we needed a refill or how our dish was (without being overbearing). I am also impressed with the cross section of diners/drinkers here. You have families, neighborhood residents, suburbanites (like me); all various ages represented, too. Oh yes, I'll be back and it makes the trek from Chester County to Fishtown worth it completely. **ps: this was drafted on Sunday, while sitting at Kraftwork, but not posted until later, mid-week**
label: POS

text: I am over Monk's and will not return. Over the years, I have visited this place hoping that service and food would improve. If anything, Monk's has gotten progressively worse over the years. Upon arrival, you are greeted by the hostess, that appears confused, and as always, offers a seat at the bar to eat your meal, as opposed to the MANY open tables around. The wait staff is inexperienced, and could care less about service. I cannot tell you how many of them ran by while my water glass remained empty. Not one offered to refill it, nor did any of them ask if everything was okay after the food was delivered. The fries are NOT what they used to be. Small, soggy, heavily salted and inconsistent. In this day and age, there are too many restaurants in this city that appreciate the business, and make you feel welcomed. This place makes you feel as if they are doing you a favor simply by seating you at one of their tables (that need to be scrubbed down, and thoroughly cleaned). My friend and I left disgusted. I hope this place either cleans up their act, or closes it's doors. There are too many other places to go to these days.. Monk's is not the one. Don't waste your money or your time.
label: NEG

text: Of all shopping malls in Edmonton, Westmount Centre is my least favorite. If I wasn't living close by, and if it wasn't for Save On and Shoppers Drug Mart which I visit often, I wouldn't come to this mall at all. Westmount Centre is undergoing the renovation process which will make it into a two-level shopping mall. For now, there is only one level, and the number of stores on this level is ridiculously small. If you are looking for a pleasant shopping experience which involves having a number of nice stores to choose from, Westmount will disappoint you. There are several apparel, footwear, jewelry and electronics stores as well as one or two hair salons and bookstores. There is also a food court where you can buy unremarkable fast food. The only two remarkable things about Westmount Centre is the movie theater which has the comfortable seating in town, and the ice ring used to attract many solo skaters and happy skating families, but recently has been replaced with Gold's gym.
label: NEG

text: Nice local pub that is independently owned and a bit different from the other northside options. Great place to drink a pint. Staff is friendly and food, though limited in options, is solid. It is loud, so be ready to raise your voice
label: POS

text: Bland, bland, bland. The portions are big, but that just means there is more blah food for you to eat. We ordered some fried stuff, which was soggy, the meditteranean chicken sandwich, which had nothing meditteranean about it, and the club, which was just another club. And a side of jambalaya, which was probably the best thing we ordered, but that's not saying much. The service was quick and friendly, though, which was nice. If you are starving and cash strapped, this is probably a good place for you, but if you can stand to walk another block or two before you eat, go somewhere else. There are too many good eats in the quarter to waste your time here.
label: NEG

text: Another adventure to Hog Heaven with some out of town guests led me to order a turkey sandwich with the white sauce....(don-dun-don!!!!). I know I was initially afraid myself, but a sample on a spoon totally flipped my mind. I think renaming the white sauce to "kickin' chicken sauce" was a bonus because white sauce makes me think Alfredo sauce. But no, it was a fantastic blend of ranch, buffalo sauce, and perfectly complemented the turkey. For four people, we had a chicken sandwich with cornbread in flapjack form (interesting option instead of a bun); a pulled pork plate with the cornbread and a side of coleslaw and mac n' cheese; a brisket sandwich on a bun; and the turkey sandwich with cheese on an onion roll that was reminiscent of the day after thanksgiving. All for $28.00! Another fantastic field trip to Hog Heaven.
label: POS

text: I see many people love their Happy Hour... wasn't lucky enough to try it.. so this review is really just for our food. Our friends took us here.. a stone's throw away from their place so we walked here on an absolutely amazingly beautiful morning. The restaurant has a nice cool atmosphere about it. We sat outside on their patio. Awesome patio, pretty big too. Oh, and they also have lil fire pits outside so I'm assuming a dinner on a nice cool night is pretty nice here, as well. Staff was super welcoming and nice. I ordered the Halibut Fish Tacos that came with a side of beans, a bit of cheese, and some chips. The boyfriend ordered the Sloppy Joe with pulled beef that came with fries. The food, while good, was just your average "American" brewhouse fare...burgers, fries, salads, dips, etc. The food was good, not amazing. My tacos were a bit dry but I will admit... I can tell their beer-battered halibut probably made for some good fish & chips. They didn't have any salsa for the chips so I just had some dry tortilla chips. The boyfriend's sloppy joe was pretty decent... definitely hearty so great for those who want a nice big meal. Overall, great place to come, hang out with friends, grab a beer, sit by the fire pits... but don't come here expecting great food.
label: NEG

text: I was truly bummed when I found out that the parent company of Davis-Kidd Booksellers filed a Chapter 11 Bankruptcy which has resulted in several locations closing..including the Nashville - Green Hills store. This location was part of one of the nation's most prosperous book-selling companies at one time and has been open for nearly 30 years. I am personally a sucker for any businesses that create an interactive element for their customers. Davis-Kidd has hosted discussions, book signings, and live music that draw both adults and kiddies. Bestsellers, newly released books, and bargains have always stocked their organized shelves and the staff kindly gives you a tour if needed. A well edited gift section and convenient Bronte Bistro round out this location and make it really tough to leave. I have spent hours here before without realizing that the time had flown by. It is sad to see this wonderful business close and if you haven't popped in before, be sure to come by to say goodbye. TIP: Store closing markdowns have already started and will continue until they vacate their space in December.
label: POS

text: I had a few friends visiting, and Bistro on the Brandywine was in a prime location to follow our visit to the Chaddsford Winery, not to mention it is BYOB. Had I known what I was getting myself into, I would have filled up on more cheese at the wine tasting!! We ordered the truffle Parmesan frites, which had good flavor but they were extremely salty. Two of us ordered the pulled pork with gnocchi, and it still gives me nightmares. It was a sloppy, salty, ugly, awful mess, not to mention they forgot to actually add the pork to BOTH of our dishes, and our server did not believe us! She finally brought us each back a bowl of pulled pork to add, after admitting we were correct, but there was no saving this dish. (The manager, however, ended up taking something off of our bill). This is the worst type of restaurant - it is all show. Bistro on the Brandywine is in an affluent area with beautiful decor, and the menu looks great on paper, which is all to distract you from noticing the sub-par food.
label: NEG

text: For the overall Cheesecake Factory experience across the country I'd give it around 4 stars. But for this specific branch I think 2 stars is too much. Just for the most pathetic service and average food. It begins with trying to put your name in (don't even think about getting a table without a wait, it doesn't happen here). Not even putting your name in, but trying to find the hostess counter behind the mad chaos of customers crowding the waiting area. It's a complete circus. Two nights ago, we decided we didn't have the patience to wait for a table and got takeout instead. What a huge annoyance. Where do you place your order?! Welcome to the Cheesecake Factory detour, 'Go that way', 'No, behind that plant', 'See that man there? Place your order with him'. It's more frustrating than trying to call up your credit card and having to speak your options to an automated service. The seventh level of hell. For my first experience with take-out from this branch, I have to say it was total crap. I got Renee's Special - half a sandwich (chicken or turkey), salad and soup for $10, and has been solid every time I've ordered it while dining in. Not only did they give me turkey when I asked for chicken, but the sandwich was disgusting. I wanted to throw it against the wall. The sandwiches I've had before looked nothing like this. I think they took some leftover bread from someone's bread basket, threw in turkey cold cuts, added a tomato, and called it a sandwich. No dressing, no mayo, no nothing. Please, I could have made this myself and it would've tasted better! And no bread with the meal. Isn't bread complimentary with take-out? All the other branches I've gotten take-out from provide bread without hesitation. There are tons of people waiting outside, sitting on the floor. I don't blame the people, I blame Cheesecake Facotry. Either you need to provide more seating for people waiting, or speed up your painful service. The food at this branch isn't that good either. Very inconsistent, versus the one in my hometown back in Cali where you can order something again and again and it'll always taste great. I want to go in there and shake the manager. The one redeeming factor is the cheesecake.
label: NEG

text: I'm not much of a review writer and I will try to make this short and sweet, but after the great experience we had at RIM on 9/12/10 and after hearing that it was receiving bad reviews, I felt the need to take a moment. First, I want to say that I know RIM is only about four months old and that ANY new business needs a little bit of time to get into the groove and fix the hiccups, so I don't doubt that someone may have had a bad experience in the first few months of the doors opening. Rarely is everything perfect shortly after opening when you have a new facility, new employees, new menu, new routines, new everything. First, we were greeted immediately and asked how we would like to be seated (we had our six year old son with us, who does eat sushi) and we sat at the bar. When I went to sit down I felt for the purse/coat hooks that some sushi places use under the bar and unfortunately there was none, BUT the manager saw me look and came right over to tell me that they were on the way. It was good to know that they were paying attention to anything their customers might want that they weren't providing. The entire time we had very attentive service, people constantly clearing our plates and filling water and asking if we needed anything else. The stools had backs and were some of the most comfortable stools I have seen for sushi (I noticed this because I have a horrible back and I dread sitting on hard, wooden stools with no back). Our chef was David, who had been working there for about five weeks and had peviously worked at another favorite of ours, Jazmine (we figured this out through the nice conversation he held with us throughout the meal). I didn't have a single bite that I didn't love. Their fish was fresh and they had some awesome rolls, including oldies and new creations. Our normal favorites are Sushi Pier 2 and Jazmine for your reference. Our son finished a little earlier than us and was getting bored and a lovely lady that was coming and going behind the bar noticed this and asked him if he wanted some ice cream, which she brought him a huge bowl of complete with edible decoration on the house. On our way out the manager checked in with us to make sure we were happy and every employee we passed thanked us and bid us a good night. The only reason we will probably not eat there much as locals is the price. We can save a little bit of money and hit another favorite spot. But this is a hotel restaurant, and we knew what we were looking at. We had a $50 gift card that we wanted to use up and this was the perfect place to use it. I'll also mention that they have a lower price for kids All You Can Eat - something I haven't seen anywhere else in town. So much for short and sweet.
label: POS

text: I'm sorry, but I'm just not impressed with these sandwiches. For $7.30 you'd think it's be a damn good lunch, but not so. I got the Beach, nothing extra added to it, on their regular french bread and a side of chips for an extra $ .99. OK, the bread was hard as a rock. The sandwich is suppose to have avacado on it. I couldn't find any, so I went to the counter and waited there while they helped 3 customers. text: "Chocolate is the substitute for love and will always be there for you" my menu told me. My inner fat kid wanted to hug the menu. The guy behind the counter told her not normally, but he'd get one for her. He came back with our drinks and actually gave her two marshmallows because they were smaller than the photo.. totally won points. The staff, or at least our server, really knows their chocolate. He seemed genuinely happy to recount his favorites and to give suggestions. They also have a Patron happy hour with $5 mixed drinks that I really need to try. text: So, my mom REALLY likes tea houses, so my sister and I took her here as our Christmas present to her. We did the high tea option on the menu (which btw you need to let them know in advance, and you must cancel within 24 hours). The high tea began with each of us choosing a pot of tea. My mother chose the white chocolate mousse, my sister ordered mango mist, and i ordered a raspberry paris bush tea. Then, we were told to go and PICK our tea cup. They brought out our tea (and brought milk in a little cow dish as well as lumps of sugar). Then, they brought our first course of scones and muffins. The scones were OK... just OK, but darn those muffins were GOOD!!! The 2nd course, we chose the type of soup we want. My mom and I had the potato soup, while my sister had the chicken mushroom noodle. BOTH of the soups were YUMMY! Course 3 was a savory torte... they called it a quiche, but i wouldn't say that as it really wasn't egg-y enough. We all had the spinach and artichoke one, but the other option was a broccoli one. This course was just okay. I wasn't so impressed with it. After this they brought our a tiered tray. The first tier was of fruit... kiwi, orange, and pineapple. (BOO!!! I LOVE MANGO AND OTHER THINGS... i thought the fruit could've been more fun). The second tier was the little snacky sandwiches-- a curried chicken salad in phyllo, cucumbers with some basil, and a tomato- bacon one. SUPER YUMMY!!!! The bottom tier was of desserts! Each of us had a chocolate covered strawberry, a little pineapple upside down cake and another crisp of some sort that tasted citrus-y. YUM!!! Finally, they brought out sherbet... which I could hardly eat because i was STUFFED! The bill itself was about 84 bucks and with tip, I spent 102. TOTALLY YUMMY THOUGH and a great experience! Only thing i would change is the fruit options, and maybe make that torte actually more of a quiche! YUM!!! We left the tea room happily cracked out from all that caffeine and VERY full!!!

text: La Colombe is Philadelphia's favorite non-Starbucks roaster, and I just don't get it. That aside, I moonlight as a barista from time to time, and I personally think the beans are nothing to write home about. Quality has definitely gone down over the past few years, likely due to higher quantities of beans being roasted. I find that the brewed coffee leaves a bitter, dry taste in my mouth - not unlike Starbucks. The espresso is better, but still not as great as I would have expected. I'd agree with a previous reviewer as to the beans being roasted way too dark. In fact, the key to LC's success has probably been locally producing a product that's still better, but not much more, than Starbucks. text: Armor Concepts is a company that specializes in door and window security. The majority of their products are designed to strengthen your door jamb and door and make it impossible for a burglar to kick your door in. I found Armor concepts after three houses on my street were robbed within a single week. In each case the thieves kicked the door in and were gone within a few minutes. I decided to do something about my house and was thrilled to find a local business that had exactly what I needed. I purchased their EZ Armor product to strengthen my doors. It is basically a four foot piece of metal that replaces the kick plate for you deadbolt. The biggest difference is that it has eight 3 inch screws holding it in versus the two wimpy 1/2 inch ones that most deadbolts have keeping your door secure. I also installed the Hinge protectors and door protector. I was actually angry when I was replacing the screws holding my door into place. They were all 1/2 inch or smaller. It is no wonder doors get kicked in so easily. There is literally nothing sturdy holding the door in. All of the Armor screws are 3 inches long and actually connect to the framing of the house. The product was fairly easy to install, but I would highly recommend having a power drill handy to make it go much faster. A competent handy man can have one door done in roughly 30 minutes. The location and building are extremely nondescript, there is not even a sign to speak of. It is more of an industrial office than a retail shop. The staff is extremely helpful however and it is still the easiest place to get the product in Nashville. I was very happy with the product and the company providing it. They are a local business and all the products are made here in Nashville. If you have concerns about your security, and you probably should, then this company can be a great help to you peace of mind.

text: As I was going to see Wicked at the Straz Center, I was hoping to be able to reserve a table for dinner at Maestro. It was totally booked so i searched and found Spain! By 6:15, the place was packed. Deciding we did not want to sleep through our performance we stuck with Tapas. I must say that starting with very good Mojitos pointed the party in the right direction. We found it to be a wise and tasty choice. We started with Vieiras Corunesa, large grilled scallops with manchego cheese in a white sauce. The combination created a delicious flavor. Our server, Yesenia, who made us feel like it would be a special night, suggested Pimientos de Piquillo, pimientos stuffed with crab meat and shrimp in a spice pimientos sauce. The sauce gave just the right kick to bring out the fresh shell fish. We had to try the Paella. The slight wait was worth it as all dishes are prepared to order with all ingredients fresh! Having a glass of homemade Sangria complemented that traditional dish perfectly. Ending with a delicious Cappuccino and flan, I could not have had a better pre-theater delight! Every one on the staff made us feel most welcomed. This will be the place I come to for a night at the theater or just to hear good live Spanish guitar and see a live Flamenco show on the weekends. You will not be disappointed. Salut!

text: Devon is just the right kind of seafood restaurant. Lively and clean, busy and bright. You see eating seafood, especially shellfish is a brisk and boisterous affair. You gotta get your fingers into it. Devon is elegant but still brisk. The waitstaff is handsome and professional, and the food is first rate. If you can get a seat, get ready for feast size platters cooked to perfection. The wine list is tremendous, and although I'm not a huge wine fanatic, I know a good Riesling when I taste one, and a good Riesling is de rigeur if you're doing serious shellfish. Well, that's how my mama raised me. The main dining room is in a clever cave-like section that looks rather like a refurbished subway tunnel. That's a good thing, it's very tastefully done and it adds to just the right atmosphere of fun, even though this is a fairly classy joint. Right on Rittenhouse Square, Devon is in the high zoot neighborhood and last time I went by there was a convertible Aston-Martin DB9 parked out front. (Yes it had paddle shifters). So scrub your face and bring your wallet, and your appetite. Now as far as I'm concerned there are just a few signature dishes that tell me how good a seafood restaurant is. The first (and the only one I tried here) is the Lobster Bisque. Devon's gets four stars, and so does the restaurant.

text: It's a simple eatery without the bells and whistles, but you can watch fast, skilled shuckers who serve up plump, fresh fare with a flick of the wrist and smile. The quality is there with the raw, but grilled with a slight char on them they were unforgettable. text: Based on the hundreds of reviews that rave about how great Chifa's food is, I don't I could provide any additional information that would sway you otherwise. What I can provide is this: I never thought that a Garces restaurant could pull off a hybrid of Peruvian and Cantonese cuisines. Stupid me. This true "top chef" knows his spices no matter where they are from in the world. His worldliness transcends his dishes and he shows his skill and knowledge in how he incorporates these fresh and tasty ingredients into every bite-- throwing your taste buds into overdrive. While many of the ingredients were more local Thai than Peruvian or Cantonese, I didn't judge in the least bit. Garces presents extremely clever dishes and combinations that keep you craving for more, which is the one common denominator between all of his restaurants. As a diner, I would prefer Chifa as more of a group dining experience than the intimate setting you would get from Amada or Tinto. Its absolutely a step up from DISTRITO, in terms of a fancier group setting, and it made for a fun atmosphere with my group of friends. If you are a fan of solid food and are craving something different, then do you and your taste buds a favor and get down to Chifa.

text: The first time we walked by Pascucci's we saw a nice sized crowd outside waiting for tables. The second time we walked by, same thing. The third time, we decided we'd try it out. Upon seating, they will give you a basket of one of the most delicious cheesy garlic breads you'll have in your life. I would have eaten the entire thing if not for the need to share with the hubby. So now expectations are running high... Wah, wah, wah... I ordered a Pizza di Lucca with goat cheese, artichoke hearts, olives, peppers and sundried tomatoes. The ingredients sounded so deelish. As my mouth watered in anticipation, I was envisioning a thin crust pizza about to be placed in front of me. No... it looked more like a personal pan pizza from Round Table! And not to discount RT if that's your thing, but this pizza is not what I expected from a seemingly authentic Italian restaurant calling itself Pascucci's! Hubby ordered the Venezia pasta: farfalle with smoked salmon and capers in a lemon-cream sauce. The only thing good about this dish was how it sounded on the menu. It was pretty bad. The salmon was way too salty and the sauce was gummy. Our server was sufficient but didn't come around too often. The big crowds standing outside steered us wrong. text: I've been to the Jerk Hut twice, once inside and once outside. If I had been rating this place just based on the inside experience, I would have given it three stars. However, my outside experience was pretty damned abominable. When I ate inside with my boyfriend and two friends, our experience was fairly pleasant. The place is pretty small and shabby (dare I say a little dirty?), but the service was prompt and the employees friendly. My Jerk Shrimp was not as amazing as I had expected, but still palatable to say the least. I got a pineapple soda to wash it down, and I was happy. The outside experience, on the other hand, was quite the opposite of pleasant. The hostess was a little abrupt with us, since we questioned the $5 per-person "entertainment fee" and $6 PER SIX-PACK "corkage fee". Now please, let me define for you a corkage fee (thank you, Answer.com): A charge exacted at a restaurant for every bottle of liquor served that was not bought on the premises. The Jamaican Jerk Hut does not sell any alcohol, so this is a misleading use of the term "corkage fee"... they aren't losing out on any alcohol sales, since they don't have a liquor license. The only thing they did that was worthy of monetary compensation was provide us with a bucket of ice. That really pissed us off. So even before we sat down to eat and drink OUR OWN BEER, we had already shelled out $21 between three of us. (Good thing we brought another six-pack in our backpack that they didn't notice...) Let me just say that I wouldn't mind paying a $5 cover to see an act worthy of that money. However, instead of hearing authentic Jamaican music, which I was hoping for, there was a white guy with dreads who was pretty much the worst Bob Marley impostor I've ever seen. Fake Jamaican accent and everything. There isn't much that I despise more than white people faking Jamaican accents... or anyone faking any accent, for that matter, and trying seriously to get away with it. Anyway, I digress... I'll just say that the music was not up to par. While we were sitting there trying to endure the terrible music and forget about the through-the-roof prices, we were kind of paying attention to our mostly bland and disappointing food. It seemed like they were mass-preparing meals, except they took three times as long to come out than a mass-prepared meal would. The only thing that I really enjoyed was the coconut shrimp appetizer. The sauce was a little too sweet, but mostly good. The jerk chicken with rice and beans was kind of dry and not as spicy as I would have liked. Very, very disappointing. The fried plantains weren't even good... they were greasy. Yuck. I might give this place a try again, but it will NEVER be outside.
label: NEG

text: Full disclosure, a relative of mine worked here, so I've eaten at Risky Business on numerous occasions, but I think I've had ample opportunity to fully assess this place... A relic of the recent fin-de-siècle, Risky's is an aptly named revamp of the failed "Ventana Grill," a midpriced American that never quite took flight after two attempts in the mid-90s. The new concept seems to have stuck: a family-oriented (in the daytime at least) sports bar, which embodies all of the hedonistic virtues of that prosperous era... a wide-ranging menu (salads to ribs to pizza to burgers to seafood to pasta to steak) that is wide in palate (asian, italian, southwest, mexican and cajun influences), carb heavy (the so-called "angry" mashed potates), and heaping in portion. Desserts are monstrous and unabashedly decadent. I was never truly impressed with the cooking; it seemed to try to please too many people at once, and never really scored well at anything in particular. Often they went a little haywire with the jerk seasoning, which always hurt on the way out. Particularly in these lean, recession hit days, where such extravagance seems out of fashion, it's surprising to note how little has changed at Risky's...even the loud fire-engine-red decor and staff attire (cargo shorts, ankle socks, running shoes) seems dated. The bar really seems to be the primary attraction here...well stocked, with TVs at every angle, and filled with regulars: Air Force types, guests from the resort up the road. But if you truly like that gluttonous, stone in your gut feeling after you eat, don't let me stop you from going here!

text: Having read that St. Louis is a huge bbq town, and then reading that two of the best were Phil's and Mama's Coal Pot, we first made the pilgrimage to Mama's because it was closer to the airport, and then made a mad dash across town to Phil's because Mama's is closed on Sundays. text: It was his jolly and bearded mug that dominated grocery isle before Newman decided to make dressings and sauces. Chef Paul Prudhomme has been and remains one of the original crusaders of New Orleans Cajun cuisine. It was on my very first trip to New Orleans, that I decided that my first taste of Cajun (yes, I've managed to avoid it for a lifetime thus far for some strange reason) would be with Chef Paul and his vaunted Louisiana Kitchen. Thankfully the meal was spectacular. The month-in-advance reservation saved my date and I a lovely table with a few of the New Orleans foot traffic below. There was something extremely casual about this restaurant. It had the shiny silverware, the while linen, and the first class service, but at the same time the table was covered with butcher paper with drawings of cartoon rabbits and turtles who happily ignore their fate of turning into pot pie and soup, respectively. I found this devilishly hilarious. But that was my last moment of humor, because it was Chef Paul who got the last laugh. The food was ridiculous. Crazy. Out of control. Off the fa-jazzy. It was my first time having fried green tomatoes. It was the most enjoyable "losing-virginity" experience ever. I highly recommend it. But it was the shrimp chipotle remoulade that really put it over the edge. Other tastes of the evening included the turtle soup, bronzed swordfish, panned chicken breast, and Chartres Street jumbalava. Had death followed me on the tails of this meal, I would have embraced my place in the afterlife, happy, full, and content.
label: POS

text: I first discovered The Metro while attending Grant MacEwan College over a decade ago. The place has gone through several changes since, but is still as welcoming now as ever. After dinner we did the tour of the wine cellar and kitchen, I like seeing where the food is prepared & marveled at the large saltwater fish tank where our delicious friends from under the sea lived until their demise on someone's plate. We also found out they have their own organic farm where they harvested the veggies we ate, they are self-sustaining, in a manner of speak. Neat, IMO. We finally came to rest in the dessert room. text: I was in town on business and my client recommended we check out West Port Plaza. There's a lot of restaurants there and being in the mood for a steak, I chose Dierdorf and Hart's. It was a positive experience except for one significant caveat that prevents me from giving it anything higher than two stars. Atmosphere here is nice but won't make those casually dressed feel uncomfortable. Service was very attentive and friendly. They have a "table captain" come around and show off some of the cuts of meat, seafood and a few interesting cuts of game. He warned us that they tend to undercook their steaks slightly but I thought to myself, "Well, this is a steakhouse. It can't be that far off." I ordered the bone-in ribeye and asked for it to be cooked medium rare, my usual. Unfortunately it came out completely rare, red all the way through when I cut into it. They had even slathered some house butter on top which totally refused to melt given the low temperature of the steak. There was also a little bit of cartilidge in the meat that wasn't real fun to cut around or chew through. It had good flavor but the temperature issue really ruined it for me. The rest of the food was good, helping to salvage the experience. I highly recommend the calamari; the aioli was unique and very tasty. They also had some gouda mashed potatoes which were excellent. I have to imagine that if I had heeded their advice more seriously and ordered medium that they steak would have been just the way I like it. But as a steakhouse, it kinda blows my mind that they would consistently and significantly undercook their steaks. Correct that one part and it could easily be a 4-star joint.
