text: "You call this a chain?" The more I mature the less interested I am in dining in an establishment that has carbon copies of itself littered practically everywhere across the North American landscape. But such is the life of an American in the 21st century and as homo sapiens nature dictates us to adapt. That being said this is the first tyme in several years I've been literally blown away by a large scale restaurant chain. This place was understated magnificence. The ambiance and overall feel were that of sophistication and the aire that you were truly dining in a fine establishment. Which, unfortunately, was also reflected in the entree pricing. (What other dining chain have you seen that does everything ala carte?). The staff was unbelievably attentive, responsive and overall friendly. It's kind a an ego boost to be referred to as "Mr. H" everytyme they refilled my water glass, or attempted to remove a dish from the table. Which was refreshingly quite frequent. The ambiance was nice and darkened and reeked of old warm charm. All brass and wood, not a formica table or wood bench in the joint. Glancing over at the separated lounge area made me wish I actually imbibed liquor, because of it's lush high back loungers and couches. In hindsight I'm questioning whether they'd look funny at me for going over there and ordering a "virgin" something or other just so I can stretch out in one of those chairs. Exquisite and lovingly prepared are the only adjectives I can come up with at the moment to describe the food I was served here. Now I know I'll be chastised later about this, but I wanna just get it out in the open so there are no illusions. I made a cardinal dining sin (at least in my father's eyes) in ordering my entree. In a place nationally revered for the quality it's steak, I off-color ordered a chicken dinner. (Somewhere in heaven a wizened, white haired, black gentleman just took a drag off of his Salem regular and heaved a sigh like he just lost the Superbowl). "I'm sorry dad". And though I wish I could say it was "horrible" and I "got what I deserve" for carrying out such a heinous foodie crime. I can't because it was spectacular. "Sorry again" The stuffed chicken breast was quite possibly the best poultry dish I've ever had the pleasure of devouring outside of a Thanksgiving dinner. As tender, plump and succulent as a 3 year old's cheek the duo of breasts are served hellishly hot on the establishment's standard 400 degree dish stewing in a mixture of lascivious lemon butter and its own delectable juices. The outside was seasoned with a miscellany of garlic and herbs, while the interior was stuffed with a "secret" specialty cheese that was absolutely fanatabulous! And how many tymes can you get away with using the word "fantabolous" in a description. I'm assuming not very many, and this chicken was so yummy that I've decided to spare one here. The family style mashed potatoes weren't the most spectacular and the appetizer of crab stuffed mushrooms was tasty, but neither were the star of the show so their mentions here are a formality rather than a necessity. The wine list was very impressive, but honestly no loftier than one would expect from a place like this. With a place this good though it's a shame that there has to come a lowpoint and this one signaled the end of my meal. Yes I'm speaking of the dreaded star stealer known far and wide as. Dessert. The first to arrive at the table was the much lauded (at least by the patrons behind us) banana creme pie. Though the menu description of the filling as being "white chocolate banana custard" it came out more like an ice cream soup as soon you perforated the flaky crust. It was as unattractive to me as it sounds, so I returned it and opted for a more traditional dessert. The bread pudding with whiskey sauce which hilariously our server made little "bottle drinking" hand signals to indicate the severity of the liquor used to douse the bread in sauce. Disappointingly the "whiskey" was barely audible over the loud sweet taste of the bread. Sad, but not nearly enough to offset the balance of the beauty of this establishment or the care taken to make commercial fine dining more fine than commercial. As the governor of California once quipped, "I'll be back". :)

text: We came to VRC on a referral from our vet. Our American Bulldog needed knee surgery (two of them, actually). We'd gone through quite a process finding a good vet and getting the knee problem diagnosed. So I carefully researched my options, which included UPenn, a vet in Atlantic City and Redbank, NJ, and a practice in Langhorne. We chose VRC because they were willing to answer questions about pricing before we even came in for an evaluation. VRC performed all of the knee surgery options while other practices performed only some of the surgeries and others performed some at one location and some at another location. With VRC we were able to visit one facility, regardless of the surgery that was best for his condition. VRC was much cheaper than UPenn. This surprises no one, right? VRC was cheaper than the Langhorne practice that does dog knee surgery. Malvern is a lot closer than AC and Redbank. VRC is clean, well-managed, and professional. We were shown to appointment rooms quickly and our vet was on time. I can't give VRC five stars because there was a noticeable change in attitude and service after the surgery. One of the staff actually told me that she didn't have time to answer my two questions and only would answer the one that she thought was more important. We also sometimes had to wait a few days for someone to respond to our calls. I also feel liike an expensive surgery should include follow-up visits, especially since our visits were a couple x-rays and a few minutes with the vet. I agree with Martina M.'s review on this matter but like I said, Langhorne and UPenn are pricier! Our dog had a TPLO, an increasingly common surgery for dogs of all size. Our guy is a big boy and our vet recommended that the surgery be done by a board-certified surgeon (otherwise, she could have fixed it for less). If you have a large dog who needs a TPLO, you should go to VRC.

text: I suppose the facility served its purpose in the sense that yes, it's a budget hotel. The room was fine - we only needed a place to sleep a few hours before heading back out on the town... Aside from the elevator that got stuck a few times on the way up to the fifth floor, nothing facility-wise to complain about... Also know that while advertised as being IN the French Quarter, it's not. A three+ block walk will get you there, but not without being accosted by some pretty aggressive panhandlers. Jazz Fest rates were in the 160.00/night range - pretty steep, all things considered. However, they are getting one star because of this: Sunday morning, we realized that four of our Jazz Fest tickets were gone. After tearing the room apart, to no avail, we went downstairs to the front desk to report the loss to the Asst. General Manager, Eric. At first, he was helpful enough, and came up to the room with the little black box that plugs into the key module on the door. A cursory analysis of the findings indicated that on Saturday afternoon, our room was in fact keyed into twice by a hotel employee's keycard - despite having a Do Not Disturb placard on the door. Our room was left un-touched by housekeeping, as we wished. Later that afternoon, I returned to the hotel to see if Eric had made any progress with the inquiry to the keycard holder, and he said that well, it appears that woman didn't actually have that keycard. He wouldn't look me in the eye as he reported this. Eventually, realizing this was leading nowhere, I got the name of his boss, and we were to take it up with her on Monday morning. She was somewhat concerned, it seemed, with our report, but still dismissive of our claim - the report was now that our room was only keyed into once on Saturday, not twice, but conveniently, the batteries were dead in the little black box. Fortunately, we were able to purchase more Jazz Fest tickets from the Sheraton, but we were still out over 200.00 for the stolen ones. After brunch and touring around some, we came back and found out she had 'closed' the case - assuming we had found our tickets. Ummm, no - we had checked out hours before. We re-opened the case, and now the story was that yes, our room was keyed into, but the handle wasn't turned. That makes a whole lot of sense... or not... The housekeeping log noted the DND sign. We chose the Holiday Inn Express because it was a chain, and they are usually pretty good about security and the likes. We were disappointed by the ever-changing story from hotel management, a complete lack of interest in digging too deep into the issue, and absolutely no semblance of responsibility for the actions of the staff... If you stay here, leave nothing of value behind in the room, as there are no safes available. The hotel management kept saying that the cleaning lady was new to the job and country, didn't speak English, and they couldn't readily communicate with her, and because of that, she didn't even know what Jazz Fest was!!! Also, she was at work on Sunday, so the tickets would have "no value" to her. Right - tickets have no value, except of course their same-as-cash nature.. Take your business elsewhere - support the local merchants and stick with a B&B or private Inn...
label: NEG

text: Hooray for opening day! About a week ago I saw a white van outside Village Whiskey with the Garces Trading Company stamped across the side. This peaked my interest to do a little googling and found that Chef Garces was opening a market place style restaurant in Washington Square West. This gorgeous open market style restaurant was perfect for lunch! A perfect combination of elegant and casual. I made it a point to come opening day to see what the place was all about. The menu offers cheeses and charcuterie (meats), salads, pastas, soups and sandwiches. Everything consistent with Garces' style. They even offer their own coffee line and lovely pastries. Even for an opening day, the service was still incredible. Everything was plated beautifully, and the staff attentive. Technically the place is BYO, but they do have their own wine cellar for you to choose from. Each wine was selected to be paired with the menu. Since we were having an early lunch, I didn't sample the wine selection, but bought a couple bottles to take home. The wines are unavailable in the Wine and Spirits stores throughout Philly and are not available in Philadelphia restaurants. We started with the eggplant antipasti (incredible), then I sampled the Cubano sandwich, served with a side of vinegar picked vegetables. The sandwich was such a treat! A great combination of flavors. We also had coffee and dessert. Coffee was delicious and I had a fresh Bavarian vanilla cake that had a blueberry center. Even my friend who doesn't like desserts loved this cake. This is a great edition to the Garces Restaurant Group, and I highly recommend you check it out :)

text: I am a huge fan of Riverchase. Before every municipality in St. Louis started building super pools, Fenton did it first. Also, the indoor pool is great and has slides and lap lanes, as well as a huge hot tub that is open year round. This place is much more than a pool though. There are a ton of sports teams you can join, both as a child and as an adult to stay fit, they have great work out rooms, and a ton of classes from arts and crafts to aerobics. The dressing rooms are pristine and the staff is incredibly friendly. As neighborhood rec centers go, this is one of the older ones around now, which is sad considering it's only about 10 years old. They have really kept it up, though and it's a very nice place to go and work out. If you live in Fenton, it's a cheap membership and if you don't, well, it's a little more, but maybe you will find it worth it. You can always try to finagle a guest pass out of a friend that does live in Fenton....that's what I always do.

text: After reading about Zahav being a tapas restaurant, I was a bit apprehensive to go there for my birthday dinner. I can now say that I was pleasantly surprised. Unlike most tapas places I've been, Zahav actually has pretty good food. It is true, the serving sizes are not that big, but the secret to leaving full is Laffa (essentially a pocketless pita). For a table of 4 people, they start you off with a tiny bowl containing 3 pickles and 3 olives, and a condiment dish with about 3 teaspoons of spicy condiments: Zatar powder, red pepper paste, and green pepper paste (the latter two were surprisingly hot). Both pickles and spices are refillable for free, so don't be shy. There were 4 of us, and the waitress suggested we order 3 dishes each, which is much like the fixed price menu. Instead, we ordered a small Salatim and Hummus, and 6 dishes. They will tell you that the small is for 2 people, and the large is for 4, but we found the small to be more than enough for 4 people (proviso to follow). You get a tower of 8 "salatim" which they describe as "salads", but they are more like the falafel toppings you would expect from a condiment bar at a falafel place like Maoz. Don't get me wrong, they were good, but the quantity of everything but the hummus was off, and for some reason, they only gave us one laffa for our table of four, and made us wait about 15 minutes for more. Perhaps people don't usually require more, but this is the secret to maximizing the minuscule portions of salatim (~2 tbsp of each item) and eating the very ample portion of ultra rich (read: 50% tahini) hummus at all. We treated it like Indian food, eating everything with the bread. Consumed in this fashion, it was good, and certainly better than eating your pickled carrots straight-up. The other dishes we got were haloumi(fried cheese), cauliflower, balkan pastel, hangar steak, lamb/beef kebab, and the chicken. All of those were well executed and nicely plated. The haloumi was a lot like an Indian fried paneer, and they served it with a nice fig paste/sauce. The cauliflower was also fried with a green yogurt-chutney sauce, and the Balkan Pastel was a cupcake-sized pastry with a moist and tender minced lamb filling. The chicken was served with a minty yogurt sauce that tasted rather Indian to me, and not very exciting. The hangar steak with eggplant, however, was very good, but they only give you 3 tiny chunks. Finally, the dessert was a bit of a disappointment. We got baklava and the chocolate semifreddo. As I expected, $8 only gets you a small square of baklava (~1.5"x1.5") and a dollop of lemon cream. I've eaten a lot of baklava in my day, some actually in the Middle-East, and it is always dripping with honey. Here it was oddly dry, crackly like a pork rind, and everything about it was pretty mediocre. Overall, I really recommend Zahav, but you should know what you're getting into when you go there, as server recommendations can be a bit misleading.

text: Araka is a wonderful restaurant for special occasions, business dinners and entertaining. I went for a business dinner and we dinned in the private room upstairs. We ordered a variety of appetizers: - Araka Pita Spread Platter. The pita chips were not the typical pita bread you would think. They were fluffy fried pita wedges that had a slight sweetness almost like a doughnut. It came with a variety of spreads from olive tapenade, chickpea hummus and sweet bean puree. This was one of my favorite appetizers. I really liked the doughnut like pita wedges, it was a unique twist that delighted my taste buds. - Cheese Flight. It came with 3 different cheese that I can't remember where they were from or what they were called. All I do remember is they were foreign blends and each was a small slice of rich creamy uniqueness. Being from Wisconsin, I would have preferred a simpler cheese plate, like a white cheddar with cranberry or fried cheese curds :D ! - Crispy Semolina Calamari. Now, typically I don't eat calamari because it's generally too chewy and greasy because it's so small that it's mostly fried breading. But this calamari was HUGE and I felt it deserved to be sampled. And OMG, so glad I tried it. It was SO good. If you like Calamari you MUST try this. The pieces are just so large and flavorful, not greasy like most restaurants. - Forest Mushroom Flatbread. The prosciutto added a nice flavor. It was good, but there were other appetizers that wow'd me more. I had the Simple Green Salad with roasted beets. The salad was a hefty portion plated on a long plate. Delightful flavors and colors. For my main entrée I had the Scottish Salmon. It was mostly protein which was a nice balance to the enormous array of appetizers I had just consumed. After everything was said and done dessert was out of the question. However, a decadent martini was calling my name. The Chocolate Covered Raspberry Martini hit the spot and I was literally in heaven. The martini got the biggest WOW at the table when it came. It was like a milkshake in a chocolate swirled martini glass with 3 raspberries floating on top. Overall, the atmosphere is classy, the service was wonderful, and the food is phenomenal. Be prepared to spend a fair amount here, but don't worry you won't go home hungry if you order a 3 course meal. The cocktails are divine, but a little pricey for my budget alone. While the flavor was fine, the quantity of dressing was ridiculous. I was able to stomach about 3 bites before I felt my arteries clogging. My main course was a BBQ Sea Bass. The only thing that saved the manager from getting an earful was the fact that the waitress was too nice for words. text: Into the very same orifice that I use for pie I have been known to insert a libation or few as well. I find that a small tipple of the aqua vitae can be, (and usually is) quite refreshing. I also am very fond of the pictures of dead presidents I collect in my wallet. Although I like to engage in quaffing adult beverages, I really hate trading exorbitant numbers of my pictures of these past patriots for the aforementioned elixirs. And I REALLY hate trading my little paper images for single servings or said hooch, especially in high-priced entrapment locales like the Gaylord Opryland Hotel. Please bear in mind this is not a knock on the Gaylord. They are a business and are not holding a gun at anyone's head. If you don't like the price, don't give them the booze business or better yet, do what I did and buy your liquor off-site ala BYOB. Enter Donelson Liquors. Or to be more precise, enter me into Donelson Liquor. Now, I need you to understand something. This is one of the reviews where I am torn between giving them a one star and a five star, with precious little middle ground. I gave them a four, and I'll explain why. Liquor laws in Tennessee suck. You can buy beer (and I assume wine) just about anywhere, but an establishment selling "hard" liquor is much harder to find, especially in the environs of the racket that is the Opryland, Gaylord and Opry Mills Mall. But again, that's a different post. Suffice it to say you cannot buy a bottle of liquor at anything like a "reasonable" rate anywhere near Oprybiz inc. I don't know what the liquor taxes are in Tennessee. I do not understand the logic that thinks that limiting the places that sell alcohol will limit the number of people with drinking problems. If that were true no one in America would have a cocaine problem. In other states you can get liquor in grocery stores, pharmacies, why heck, I've known a few country hardware stores that carried it as well. This is not the case in Tennessee. It may be that Donelson Liquors knows they have you "over a barrel", (pardon the pun). What I paid for a Tennessee product made in Lynchburg at Donelson Liquors was double what you would pay for it in a grocery store in California. DOUBLE. In Pie-Hole Boy's world, thatsa' lotta' dead presidents. Is that Donelson's problem? Nope. Did I shell out the DPs? You bet. It was still cheaper than drinking at the Gaylord. So here goes: One star, you bastards, for fixing the game against an innocent libertine like myself in my pursuit of "Knowing Jack". Five stars for having a cool neon sign in the window with foot tall letters spelling out B-O-U-R-B-O-N. Sweet. Five stars for having the product to back up the sign in the window. (Folks, these people do have a serious selection of bur-ho-bon.) Same five stars for just simply being there and selling the stuff. Upshot? Four stars. If you go, allow yourself some time to peruse what appears to be a fine selection of whiskeys, in particular the bourbons.

The produce is so fresh, you'd think they'd be crazy not to charge more, but shhhh, let's keep that between you and me. Sometimes their organic apples are just as cheap as their non-organic varieties. Go figured. I can fill up two canvas bags to the brim, full of groceries, and not spend over $20. That's just amazing. And on Wednesdays and Sundays, they offer 10% student discounts. And I think on Tuesdays, they have senior discounts. When was the last time you bought something decent for a dollar? Well get ready for dollar grab bags! The produce in there usually has to be used up pretty quick, because the produce is usually nearing the end of its lifespan, but you can do a whole lot with some dollar apples (like apple pie!) or dollar potatoes. Just remember, don't dilly dally with those cooking plans. Dollar produce changes all the time, so you never know what treasures you might unearth. On one edge of Iovine's, there are dried fruits and nuts and trail mixes and random awesomeness, packed and waiting for some love. You'll find something to munch on, and be happy that you did. And for someone who loves some fungus, well the mushroom kind and not really the nasty unwanted kinds that come to mind, Iovine's has some fresh chanterelles and random fresh fancy mushrooms as well as dried varieties like morels. It's almost a one-stop paradise. If only Iovine's started carrying meat, I wouldn't have to shop anywhere else.

text: My first one-star rating...hopefully my last. :( I went on a Dining Day which meant that it was $15 for a 3-course meal, which sounded like a great deal. I was excited for the variety on the prix-fixe menu, but unfortunately, I got what I paid for. While the calamari was tender, it had breading like an onion ring - way too thick. It was also served with cold marinara sauce, which was straight out of the fridge and an unpleasant temperature to eat. For the entrees, several of us got tuna and no one finished it. The portion was generous, but that wasn't why - it was because no matter how we had ordered it, everything came out well-done, which is a complete waste of sushi-grade tuna. Finally, the bread pudding was served as a large hunk that was too dense and dry without any sauce - the best part was the cinnamon-sprinkled whipped cream, which I'm pretty sure came from a can.

text: Stumbled upon this place today while looking for a new place for a bite to eat. Cool little place at first glance, lots of outdoor seating, cute wine bar, 8 kinds of frozen yogurt with a decent menu, pastries in a case, and small upstairs area for live music. Seems like they might have tried to take on too much... I got a tuna sandwich and an orange juice, while my boyfriend got a BLTA and a coffee, which was Peet's brand. Our options for sides were chips, salad or potato salad (so&so's world famous), we picked the famous potato salad. Our total was $28 which seems a bit pricey, we asked the guy at the register about it after the fact and he said that the orange juice was about $5 (not on the menu) and that the sides of potato salad were an additional $3 charge (ALSO not on the menus). We got our food and were thoroughly disappointed. Potato salad was chunks of potatoes with olives in a mustard looking sauce, looked great but had NO flavor. Tuna salad sandwich was smothered in a yellow mayonnaise and the tuna might as well have been straight out of the can (also NO flavor). As for the BLTA it was not toasted and my boyfriend was quite unhappy with this. The coffee was burned and the orange juice was delicious and fresh.

text: I took a class at Spool last night and was really kind of disappointed. The focus of the class was to make pillow covers for throw pillows. Because of time constraints, we only had time to make one cover. This means that if you do not own a sewing machine, you probably have to come back - preferably on a weekday between 12 and 5p - and spend $10/hr sewing the other cover! Also, if you want to buy the actual pillow insert from Spool, you have to shell out another $16.75. $16.75! for a 18"X18" pillow - come on! So if I want to have everything ready to go by the time I leave the store, I've got to shell out $20 for the class, $$ for the fabric, $16.75 for the pillow, and maybe another $20 to finish the second cover. All that and I don't even get to keep my bobbin!? I think Spool needs to do a bit better. I understand that the fabrics have varying costs, but why not have students pick out their fabric at the time they pay for the class and make life easier? Or require paying half the fee to reserve a spot and then paying the balance and fabric fee at the time of the class.

text: Two words: softcore porn. I would never be able to pick up a girl here because I can't keep my eyes from drifting to the tv screen showing massive globes at all times. And I'm not knocking porn at all, I love it as much as the next guy, but it doesn't belong in a bar in Olde City, regardless of how unattractive the clientelle. FIRST IMPRESSIONS: For some reason, this place is always relatively full, while other places just can't seem to get a turnout...I'm thinking it's got something to do with the porn. Most Yelpers here will wonder why the hell they are here, but they will realize it's probably got more to do with their friends wanting to stick around, which is what always happens to me when I'm there. THE ATMOSPHERE: This place is so cliche Olde City it's sickening...wet couches along the wall, bar on the other side manned by unattentive bartenders who try to get slutty girls to do slutty things on the bar for all to see. The dance floor is always packed, but unless you have a drunken dance partner to accompany you, don't count on being able to go out there and find someone because they are all taken or just total creepsters. Upstairs is Otium, which one letter away from Opium, which is what Otium reminds me of-- an Opium den. THE CLIENTELLE: Hilarious...absolutely the most amusing crowd around, you've got your middle eastern guys trying to be jersey boy italians, whose haircuts and beards make them look like Osama bin Jagerbomb. You've got your fat chicks who love to try and strike up a conversation despite you showing very obvious signs that you're not interested, or in the case of girls, douchebag epitomes that think they're God's gift to Olde City, thank God they only prey on spots like this and stay away from the good ones. You've got your underagers who somehow manage to get in because they know the doorman. It's great. And by great, I mean horrendous. THE DRINKS: Nothing special, typical club drinks, just order your goddamn Vodka Redbull and be happy with it... THE MUSIC: Uninspired DJ plays the same kind of crap you hear at any other club, transitions and continuity between songs is virtually non-existant, like most of the other DJs in Philly's suffering club scene, he might as well have just been playing off his iPod. In fact, I usually get so annoyed by the above mentioned atmosphere and clientelle that I don't want to dance. The dancefloor itself is pretty good, but there are other aspects that take way from it-- for some reason, the area in between the bar and the dancefloor is always crowded, and people feel the need to be especially rude here, it's like paying a toll of patience. THE BOTTOM LINE: Really nothing special, I'm surprised Moda has been around as long as it has, but I don't see much of a future for this place, seeing as how the only thing that sets it apart from the rest of the area's attractions is the porn, and even that isn't appropriate. This place isn't much a disappointment because I never saw much potential, but it's not a place that I'd recommend to anyone I'd seek to please or impress with my knowledge of the city...in fact I'd probably do the opposite to demonstrate that knowledge. Go if you must, but don't expect a great time.

I don't often get the beef or chicken bowls. If I want something like that, I go to Edo Japan. But when I want sushi, I go to Tokyo Express. The Mexican rolls are so good. They are spicy (and even more spicy with my soy sauce/wasabi concoction). I love them. They are really efficient here too. Even when they are busy, everything moves smoothly and everyone works together like a well-oiled machine. Tokyo Express = Yummy!

text: Overall, a huge disappointment. Went for the first time last night, which happened to coincide with the downtown Billy Joel/Elton John show. Got there just as the concert rush was wrapping up and departing. Looked like the staff wasn't ready for the crowd or was taking a breather, as 80% of the vacated tables were uncleared. After asking the staff about dining outside and being told to pick anywhere, we found the one cleared table and sat down, a small party of 3. Waited about 10 minutes before a waiter showed. In the meantime, I noticed a friend getting ready to leave and asked whether it was any good. His review..."The food sucks!, but maybe it was just because it was busy." At that point, still waiting for a server to notice us (patio completely empty now), we were just getting ready to ask for a parking voucher and leave when a waiter appeared. Now that we had their complete attention, things happened relatively quickly. Drinks, menus, apps and while we were halfway through our apps, the entrees appeared. The special was spicy Cajun shrimp pasta which my wife was all over. This is one of the menu items that is a chef's special...change the flavor each day, but $10 for a half order, $15 for a full. Serving size looked right for $10. About the size of a house salad bowl. Problem was, it was virtually tasteless. I mean, at least bring out some Tabasco or Pete's if you're gonna advertise Cajun and bring tasteless noodles. It did come with a good looking pretzel biscuit, which was okay, but overall, Huge thumbs down. Next, my friend ordered the Carolina-style pulled pork, which apparently means they put cole slaw on the sandwich. Friend visiting from Chicago was pretty disgusted. He kicked himself for not going with the standard burger...live and learn. A good indicator should have been the table next to ours, still uncleared, that had an entirely full plate of pulled pork with what appeared to be a single bite out of the sandwich. Hindsight...always 20-20. Now, I wanted a burger, but figured it would be a shame to eat at a "nice" restaurant and order ground beef, so I went with a grilled turkey sandwich...was supposed to be roasted turkey breast with Swiss and mustard. I subbed mash for fries. Sandwich looked okay but it was basically deli turkey heavy on Swiss, grilled flat like a grilled cheese...no mustard. No mustard in sight. Basically very bland. The potatoes, of course, were instant. No butter, no gravy. Just plain bad. Now, I'll critique the apps last, as they really were just an afterthought. Ordered the "deep fried tomatoes" and homemade chips with dip. I don't know what fried red tomatoes are supposed to taste like, but I would have expected something, especially since they were garnished in buffalo mozzarella. Unfortunately, they were just plain awful. No pop, no zing, no wow. I think even ketchup would have done something. Unbelievable. So, on the bright side, the space is phenomenal. I watched Cupples Station come alive over the last 5 years and was dying to see how they had finished J Buck's. It is a really awesome restoration. I guess that explains the prices. I had no doubts that the average entree would be between $25-40 bucks. I just expected something a little more spectacular on the flavor end. Sadly, now that the box is checked, I will not return to J Buck's for food. It is probably an awesome place to go for a drink or drinks after work or before a game, but if you are hungry, save your money and eat at the Eat-Rite instead. You are at least guaranteed full flavor with every bite, which means you get what you paid for. P.S. I don't know whether the menus at the other J Buck's are all the same or not. I hope not, but am not willing to risk it, based on this experience.
label: NEG

text: For the record, I would much prefer to spend my time and money at a local restaurant rather than a chain. But there are times where I do crave some Applebee's, Red Robin or P.F. Chang's. I'm not proud of it, but my therapist said I no longer need to feel shame about my choices in life. When I do get a craving for something homogenous, Elephant Bar would NOT be a place that I'd pick again. After a long day at the West County Mall, both my boyfriend and I decided to grab dinner at Elephant Bar. I'd been there before for happy hour and had their appetizers. Their lettuce wraps and egg rolls are just fine. Nothing special, but for half price during the week, a girl can't be too picky. Dinner at Elephant Bar is a whole other story! Per my boyfriend's request, I ordered the Shrimp Adventure. Keep in mind that anything one orders at a chain with the words "Adventure", "Explosion" or "Ultimate Feast", know that the meal turns out to be nothing of the sort! It was basically shrimp battered and fried in three different ways. With some sad looking sweet potato fries on the side. The lamb shanks that my boyfriend ordered were dry and served with a gelatinous gravy. Blech! Maybe if I had ordered the orange chicken or lettuce wraps, the meal would have gone a little bit better. But we left that night feeling disgusted- both with our food and what we paid for it. A total waste. When deciding on where to eat, we usually joke about going to Elephant Bar because the meal was just so bad.

text: Erawan Thai's interior is cozy. The (potentially faux) flowers, purple napkins, and Enya playing in the background were soothing touches. Erawan, contrary to its name (which means "elephant" in Thai) isn't huge: there's somewhat shy of 20 tables. The lunch special ($9) includes an appetizer (OR soup) and salad. I ordered the pad ka pow ("Holy Basil Supreme" on the menu) with chicken - basil sauteed with fresh chili, bell peppers, and onions, all in a light garlic sauce. I requested it be super spicy ("make it like they do in Thailand!"), and, after assuring her that I was in fact dead inside, she brought it out. Sadly it wasn't terribly spicy - only reasonably so. Someone else also got the pad ka pow (as regular hot), but we couldn't distinguish the difference between our plates. Portions are appropriate for lunch, not huge. Service was fine, our water glasses were refilled quickly. Our server (Chu) disappeared mysteriously when it was time to pay the bill, but she probably was willing to let us sit there and chat. I'd say this place is between 3 and 4 stars - I was pleased and will certainly return!

text: Las Paletas sells popsicles and only popsicles. The ice lollies range from traditional to bizarre and surely there is one to fit everyone's tastes. The pops are made with fresh ingredients daily in the store and are served out of coolers in the front. A chalkboard wall displays the flavors du jour and are erased throughout the day as they disappear. Generally, there are two types of popsicle: creamy and fruity. The creamy is like a fudgesicle if chocolate or a pudding pop. The fruity ones are like traditional popsicles but have bits of fresh fruit in them so you know they are the real deal. When I was there some of the flavors were hot chocolate and chili, mexican caramel, peanut butter, raspberry and lime, honeydew, cantaloupe, tamarind, cucumber with chili, elderflower and more. I tried the cucumber with chili and I did not like it. It was too salty and really spicy. I had a taste of the hot chocolate with chili and it was so hot that it burned all the way down my throat but it was very delicious. I also tried the mexican caramel and that was very good. The only problem I have with the place is the location. It's a small shop located in the ground floor of some loft apartments. There is no place to sit or hang out so a bunch of people just stand on the sidewalk. I wish it was in an area with more pedestrian traffic so you could walk around and enjoy the icy treat. In addition, parking is also a nightmare, much like the rest of Nashville. If you're looking for something different and refreshing, check this place out.

text: I get that buying pre-made food is going to be more expensive, but come on! $4 is an ENTIRE BOX of cereal - the good stuff too, like peanut butter bumpers. Why are you paying that amount for a single bowl? text: This new burger joint just opened. Generally, new restaurants try to open with a big bang. Staff and management are plenty and they are usually full of enthusiasm, focused on customer service and running around just making sure that everything is going as well as possible. For this reason we often choose to wait until the "staff calms down" before going to a newly opened restaurant. But, we were wanting a burger so we decided to just suck it up and go to Teddy's just days after opening... we were mentally prepared for the super happy employees, the over tentative managers and such. Our mental preparation for a zeal-induced staff was not needed. Burgers ranged from $8.00 - $9.50 all burgers are served with fries. If you want something other than fries, you will be charged an additional 1.00. Burgers are 1/2 pound. The size of the burger and the automatic inclusion of fries make a pretty hefty meal.... for a large man. Frankly, offering a smaller burger (maybe a 1/3 pound) or offering the burger only without fries would have suited my 5'4", 125-pound body. The nacho burger was tasty and the meat was a nice medium so it was not dry. My husbands Cajun Burger had some nice flavor but the meat was clearly over cooked and dry as an old shoe. It required multiple gulps of fluid to assure that the bites did not lodge in his airway. The fries had potential, but were mildly warm at best. Seasoned salt was poorly distributed on them, thus one bite little salt the next bite huge amount of salt. We also ordered some chips and salsa which was totally unremarkable - chips and the salsa, I suspect, can be found at the local Gordons Food Service. The environment was tragic. The choices of materials used, the total FAILURE to properly manage sound makes this environment extremely uncomfortable. As we placed our order, we could barely hear the person and she could barely hear us. The ultra industrial ceilings, the TVs blaring, and only 35 people added enough noise into the space that it was near impossible to even have a conversation. Oh! The SWEET relief when we stepped outside to walk to our car. We just sat in our car for a minute just to take a deep breath. I can only imagine what this place sounds like when it is raining outside... I suspect that the owner of this restaurant has high hopes to create several of these "joints" around the Indianapolis area and maybe even offer franchise opportunities. But, right now this place is a total miss with their own goals outlined on their website.... "The company's success will be directly linked to great customer service, generous portions of quality food, affordable pricing and an ability to create an atmosphere that is enjoyable, relaxing, clean and ultimately unforgettable." "Great customer service": If they were "working the tables", they would have known about the problems with our food (which is really shocking for a newly opened restaurant - they usually hit the tables multiple times with multiple people... but not here!) "Generous portions": Yep generous for a 200-pound man, coming in from a hard days work. "Affordable pricing": Nope "Atmosphere that is enjoyable, relaxing": Nope, nope, nope! Not even close,... it would have been more relaxing in the middle of a rodeo. "Ultimately unforgettable": yep, but not in the way that they hope. This place is lacking in a real professional touch. Its felt with the choices of materials, their selection of a very poor location and the lack of understanding of guest comfort and the failure to assure that guests are satisfied with their meal and experience.

text: I have been to this place three times now, each time having a better experience than the last. The first time I visited was just a few weeks after they opened during the summer. We sat on the patio during a lovely, perfect summer evening. Our waitress greeted us promptly and handed us our menus. Their offerings were sparse, but succinct - I knew this ahead of time, per previous reviews. We ordered the margherita pizza and the "four cheese" pizza. A quick 15 minutes later, our pizzas arrived piping hot and looking outstanding. I will be honest, when I first saw them, I was a SMIDGE disappointed - they were a bit smaller than I anticipated, and everything seemed unevenly distributed over the pizza. Upon first bite, however, I knew I was in for a treat. The pizza has that perfect crust, in my opinion - slightly crisp, chewy, and just flexible enough to be folded over and eaten "New York-style." Tangy sauce, fresh mozzarella, and a true wood-fired taste really sent this pizza over the top. Both the margherita and the four-cheese were delicious, and after each piece came the difficult choice of which kind to choose next. Fast forward a few months, to a few weeks ago. We decided to walk down, since it is just a block or so from our house. This time we sat inside at the counter, as it was chilly and crisp outside. We had a good view of the wood-fired oven, and began a nice conversation with the pizza-maker (a big, super friendly Italian guy from NYC). This time we ordered the Italian sausage pizza and the pizza topped with feta cheese, gyro meat, tomatoes, lettuce, and tzatziki sauce. The sausage pizza was delicious, with true spicy Italian-sausage thrown liberally on top. However, the real standout was the "gyro pizza", as we called it. I HIGHLY recommend this pizza! Folded over, it was akin to eating a hot, fresh gyro with crispy chewy crust. Completely to die for. Last visit was a few days ago with my neighbor, and I suggested the "gyro" pizza to split, and we both ordered a salad. The caprese salad was outstanding, and beautifully presented - sliced tomatoes and fresh mozzarella, stacked, drizzled with olive oil and balsamic, topped with fresh basil, and served with a couple of bread points. She apparently enjoyed her caesar salad, as well, because she cleaned her plate... and I swear a frown crossed her face as she took her last bite. A glass of Peroni and a pizza later, I cannot recommend this place highly enough. I challenge you to set aside your notion of what "pizza" is in St. Louis, and expand your palate to include the wood-fired, Italian way.

text: What Patrick said, essentially. One friend describes the sound of bands playing the Cannery thusly: "as though they were playing in the bottom of a stairwell." I moved several times during one performance to see if I had inadvertently found a low spot, but nope - things sounded bad all over. Don't visit this venue if you have anything approaching claustrophobia. Getting a good sightline to the stage involves cramming yourself against a brick wall off to one side, and fighting hordes of people to get back out to the bathroom, the bar, etc. Standing on the other side of the room ensures your view will be blocked by 20 or so hanging pedestal lamps that some genius hung directly over the bar, as though having to peer around the giant wooden columns spaced every dozen feet weren't enough of an irritant. You really have to wonder what's up with this place. The Mercy Lounge is terrific in nearly every way this venue isn't. I will disagree with previous reviewers on one fact: I think their drinks are horrifically expensive (order a gin & tonic and you'll pay $5 for a tiny Dixie cup filled mostly with ice and maybe a finger or so of bottom shelf Aristocrat brand gin). The one bright spot is the friendly and competent staff, none of which will throw attitude and most of whom will thank you for visiting. They're awesome folks; it's not their fault, for the most part, that this venue has such serious issues. Bottom line? This is the worst venue in Nashville. Don't go here unless it's a band you're desperate to see - and even then, stay away, since the terrible sound quality and lack of good sightlines will break your heart.

It's kind of the equivalent to Mexican "Menudo" in that they make this soup from the belly of the beast. The difference, however, is a much more complicated flavor. Lots of vegetables are thrown at this dish making it delicious and good for the soul--so eat up! Masitas de bayun (not sure on the spelling) were my next favorite. The masitas are little corn spheres with a little dose of cheese inside. A really nice combination. More stock items like Sancocho, morcia and empanadas are available and tasty too. text: As mentioned in other reviews, I am a self-identified sushi snob, and have been lucky enough to go to Japan several times, and eat the most toe-curlingly fantastic sushi there. So my sushi bar is set high. Ichiban is the only sushi place in Nashville which I'd describe as excellent, and equivalent the better restaurants in Tokyo and New York City. Its sushi is authentic, fresh, and expertly prepared. Ichiban also offers a wide array of traditional Japanese dishes beyond sushi. If you want a true Japanese cuisine experience, as opposed to Americanized rolls with tons of cream cheese and deep fried crunchy things and random cooked things stuffed in the rolls, then check this place out.
label: POS

text: I love to cook, and eat! So, it just makes sense that I yelp about the coolest kitchen outfitter on the planet. It doesn't matter what you are looking for, if it belongs in a kitchen, you'll find it here. Or at least in the catalogue. Pat, my fav WS crew member, is also from Nashville (!) and brings a certain warmth and southern charm to the Hyde Park Village store. Her sweet smile, eagerness to help and kitchen knowledge make the experience here more than just shopping. In fact, everyone who works here is helpful and happy to see you. I picked up a gift for friends and also scooped up a jar of their soon to be famous Sloppy Joe sauce. Also, this is the ONLY place on earth to buy real vanilla extract, NOT flavoring. Madagascar vanilla beans make this the ultimate in vanilla extracts ~ if you bake, you MUST have this on hand. This place will have you running home to try new recipes with your newly purchased equipment, and serving them with pride on your beautifully set WS table! Life is short and at times a bit tough, so treat yourself, and your family and friends, to the beauty of fine kitchen gadgets and food!
label: POS

text: Not as great as Tiffin, but when you want to gorge yourself on fabulous Indian food for lunch - it hits the spot! It's a great price and the staff is very friendly. The art work is a little crazy, but interesting. If you're near PENN, check it out!
label: POS

text: so our third and final food destination on our little excursion to santa barbara was to have breakfast at tupelo junction cafe which YELPERS seemed to agree -- had a tasty breakfast alternative to the OC and for that reason i had to try it. the decor was the first thing that caught my attention. very earthy. very clean. very updated. very spacious. it felt like i was eating on the patio in the countryside somewhere but i didnt have to worry about bugs or fleas. perfect for me. we ordered the apple beignets which came in high regard, the vanilla french toast, and the crabcakes. of the three -- the crabcakes really impressed. if you like that overly breaded crabcake that most places serve, then this is NOT the crabcake for you. but if you're like me and you wonder why crabcakes dont have more crab in them and wish they did -- then you'll love these. the only other crabcake that i can remember eating that left a lasting impression on me was over at HOUSTONS restaurant but those were flakes of crab inside the cake and it cost like 30 bucks for 2. here for half the price, we had shredded crab meat waiting for us inside the cakes and it was just as tasty with the avocado salsa and poached egg on top. MMMMM.... im a crabcake lover so i definitely could appreciate it. other than that the vanilla french toast was okay. kind rich but it had a good tarty berry sauce to it. the apple beignets were tougher than i thought they would be -- pretty much 4 deep fried oversized donut holes but if you like apple butter then you might like this as well because they had a real nice apple butter sauce to go with it. im sure we could have ordered something else better to come away with a better impression of this place but the crabcakes are reason alone for me to try this place again. oh yeah and the all female staff with their clean cut outfits were pretty easy on the eyes as well. in case, you end up going and seeing a bunch of guys having breakfast there and wondering why they're not over at the locak IHOP instead pigging down pancakes. thats why.
label: POS

text: The best things on the menu are the seafood hot pots. My parents like this place so I've been here a million times. It's got sentimental value and the interior of the restaurant looks exactly like the chinese restaurant in 'Seinfeld' except for the "CARTWRIGHT!"-barking host.
label: POS

text: Performance Bike, we are breaking up for good. Yes, I've always preferred supporting local shops like Therapy or Trophy. And yes, you often have really great prices on things that no other shops carry and that I need right away. But as of today, I vow to do whatever it takes to not spend another dime on your premises. Here's why. The customer service here has never been that great. Checking out always took longer than necessary, the employees were never particularly knowledgeable, and I've rarely if ever seen a woman working there--small annoyances really in the grand scheme of corporate retail. The big stuff was when we tried to get a broken chain replaced while it was still under warranty and the mechanic straight-up lied about calling and talking to SRAM (on Memorial Day Sunday no less) and claimed that they had told him to just fix the chain instead of replacing it. We later verified with SRAM directly that they were closed and would have never said that anyway. The other dealbreaker is that your employees are incredibly flaky about whether they will allow returns/exchanges for items ordered online. One year, my in-laws bought me about $150 worth of clothes online (none of which fit) and the store happily let me exchange them on store credit. Today my husband tried to return a $3 seatpost shim and was thoroughly rebuffed--which was pretty short-sighted, considering that we had walked in to buy about $30 worth of tubes and maybe a helmet. Don't get me wrong, I will probably still order stuff off the national website on occasion and do in-store pick-up. I might even see your sister store in Wilmington every now and then when I don't feel like paying sales tax. But you and me, Philadelphia store, we're through.
label: NEG

text: Above average chain restaurant. Food was above typical chain restaurant food. Expect to wait around for 10-15 most nights. I'm going to rank as one of the top 3 chain restaurants in the area!

text: Benton Park Cafe, located at the corner of Arsenal and Lemp in South City St. Louis, features some of the best breakfast and lunch food in all of South City. In addition to its tasty menu and convenient location, the Benton Park Cafe is open weekend nights from 10 pm-4 am, perfect for drinking coffee and working on that novel that's eluding you at the moment.

text: Inside Harrah's This was on my list (an actual spreadsheet - I'm that serious) of places to get prime rib dinners cheap, and it would do in a pinch, but it was not one of my favorites considering how much better other cheap prime rib dinners were. It is very cool that you can get a $9.99 steak & shrimp skewers meal available 24 hours a day, but it's not cool that neither are really as wonderful as that sounds. They weren't bad, just not delicious. It was still a very filling full-sized meal that came with choice of potato, but when the waitress brought out mashed instead of baked as my man had ordered, she first took a look at what she'd written on her order pad before telling him "you said mashed" before realizing that it was her job to make it right instead of getting into a pissing match (for the record, I heard baked...). Since I was going for the $8.99 prime rib dinner, I called first to make sure of the hours it was available since I'd seen 2PM but wasn't sure. The person I talked to and the one she also talked to in the background had no idea, weren't particularly pleasant, and finally debated and told me 5PM. When we showed up, the chalkboard sign right in front of the phone advised that it was in fact Sun-Thurs 2PM-11PM, so they missed that detail. If they had been a little more friendly, I wouldn't have bothered with this detail. But they weren't, so I did. My meal was fine, but again, it really wasn't all that tasty. At all. In fact, after that prime rib I started to wonder if I really still loved it as much as I always have or if the love had faded. Thank God I did not give up hope and enjoyed others that restored my obsession so that I can do all this prime rib hunting again on next year's trip. I didn't try these, but during the same Mon-Thur 2PM-11PM time frame as the prime rib, you can also get something from their "Asian Pacific Rim Special" for $9.99 with choice of lemon grass marinated pork chops, honey glazed walnut shrimp, General's chicken, Thai marinated swordfish or spicy Mongolian sirloin steak - they give you a few pieces of sushi with each, too. All of these looked really good, but then, so did the prime rib...
label: NEG

text: Mokka is a great little spot for coffee, breakfast or lunch -- much needed in Columbia, which suffers a serious lack of good eating establishments. Beer and wine are offered on select weeknights, but the Kaldi's coffee and the freshly made food make me a regular customer.

text: Fritanga is wonderful. You get great service - The owner Orlando is welcoming and attentive. You also get great food. My husband LOVES the chicken soaked in lemon juice and then fried up. The empanadas are good. He had tamales one day that were good. The pork is good. Everything is good. And you wonder how you can get food this great at such a great price! Don't come here expecting a Mexican restaurant experience. You DO NOT get chips and salsa to appease your appetite until your entree comes. However, that probably just makes you appreciate your entree that much more. The dining room doesn't seat that many people, but that is a good thing. You'd be denied the pleasure of receiving personal service from the owner. This is definitely one of my favorites.

text: Smoky & dim. Probably a good pub to drink in but I wouldn't return for the food. For starters, the chips were okay, but the pasties were pretty unappetizing - a ground meat slurry in pastry. Maybe that's how they do it in Dublin. I guess I was hoping for something more like a traditional Cornish pasty. Entrees were quite average too. Bangers & mash were served with a mustard/horseradish sauce which was not at all complimentary. The guinness stew was meat & veg in a thin salty beef stock. It was served with a cheesy mash which, when stirred into "stew", gave it a bit more body. But it seemed to completely lack the assumed ingredient of guinness, which would presumably give it richness and flavor. And/or cooking time for the flavors to develop. The duck was also pretty so-so, mainly let down by beans which were extremely hard (like, raw). That dish was comped. I wasn't expecting anything fancy, just good solid pub grub, but The Dubliner failed to impress.

I also like the CPK Cobb salad - the half is PLENTY big - not need to get the larger size. Tortilla and Minestrone soups are good, too. Nice.

A few years later and I have added a star. The last few times I was there have been a much quicker experience and same great flavor.

text: Prince Conti had excellent reviews on AARP and was in the heart of the French Quarter, so we booked it. It was not a bad place, probably sufficient when held against other Qtr hotels, but there some things that left me feeling "Meh. I've experienced better." Our room was small, but nicely decorated and clean. It had double beds that were not very comfortable and lacked fitted sheets, so they come undone as you sleep. The kids' bed didn't even have a mattress pad. The bathroom small, but clean. The continental breakfast was woefully uninspired and cheap compared to the fare offered at other hotels on our trip...crossiants that were refrigerated, some fruit. There were no trash cans, you were to put your dirty plates in one of the tubs and paper trash in another. So outside of restocking items as they ran low, no one was staffing it and yet they had a tip jar out. The coffee, however, was excellent. I think the parking was reasonable; it was $25 a day, which was cheaper than what someone else I chatted with in San Antonio paid where he stayed, $36 a day. Quiet, with view of roof and dilapidated buildings next door. You could hear the people behind our beds in the next room, so the walls are thin. I don't remember hearing any noise from above. The beds and the breakfast seriously knock this hotel down in its rating and I think the place is probably more noisy on the weekends (we were in NOLA on a Monday-Tuesday). I'm from Phx where it is HOT and NOLA's summer heat zapped me and seriously effected my ability to enjoy the place. Probably best to visit any other time than Summer.
label: NEG

text: I'll have to help out the neighborhood eatery here as some of the Friday night specials have been outstanding. Last November, I had the New England seafood bowl which was a dozen or so clams and mussels, four humongous shrimp, four equally humongous scallops, parsleyed potatoes, corn on the cob and huge wedges of crispy garlic bread served in a bowl full of rich seafood broth AND... topped off with a half of a lobster for $21. I don't know how they made any money that night but such deals do exist. As for everyday fare, OK I guess.

text: This Hudsons is in a really great area, being located right on the University campus. I came here for a friend's birthday, and I thought it was great place for a get together or even just to hang out and talk. There were small tables and bigger tables for groups with comfy benches on one side. This place was fairly dim and luckily not very busy at the time, so it was easy to hear one another. I also don't remember them playing the music very loud. I did order some food here, and it was your basic deep-fried pub food, but I do remember the vegetable spring rolls being very tasty. The whole menu was really expensive though. I'm not sure if Hudsons does this anymore, but they used to take pictures of their patrons and post them on the website. They took a couple pictures of our group that night, and I did go online to see them. It's kind of a scam though, because if you want to see the pictures, you have to sign-up as a member on the site. I totally got bombarded by emails after that, but at least I got the see the pictures, which were actually pretty cool. I was just glad I wore makeup that day.

text: So frustrating! Cannot figure out where to go for anything --placing order, asking question about the confusing form, paying, getting your fountain drink-- and it is inconcievably crowded all the time, so you will just be wondering around in everyone's way for most of your visit while you try to figure out what the F&#* is going on. The sandwiches are fine. Way too expensive. Totally overhyped --I'm over it!

text: I love this location of Save On Foods, because they have a large natural foods section. A lot of the same products sold here can also be found at the Planet Organic right next door. It's not always cheaper though, but Save On usually has better sales more often. This Save On Foods also has a great bulk section. They have these organic Thompson raisins that are the best raisins I've ever had. They are so sweet and soft, not like most dried out, hard raisins. I also like to get unsalted bulk sunflower seeds, flax seed, and pumpkin seeds. When I really feel like treating myself, I get the chocolate-covered cranberries. These are so amazingly good, but I have to watch how many I buy, because they are not cheap. They are anything but healthy, but I justify by telling myself that it contains fruit. When I feel like being even more unhealthy, I get the bulk Jelly Belly sours. These are so addictive. Watermelon flavour is healthy, isn't it? If you're into organic or super healthy foods, you'll love this Save On Foods. Aside from the pseudo-healthy treats, this place is packed with tons of natural products.
label: POS

text: My wife and I ate at the Jackson on a Monday night, and almost had the whole place to ourselves. A couple was just finishing up when we were seated, and a group of 4 arrived just before we were done. The staff was friendly and attentive, but not overbearing. The food is what will bring us back, just excellent. The portions were right on target and the prices were what you would expect to find. Not too pricey, not cheap. If you would like a nice quiet romantic evening at a fine dining restaurant, I would suggest Jackson. The only thing we didn't care was the neighborhood. It seems the entire street of Magazine shuts down at 6pm, except for the few restaurants. I don't think it is the worst neighborhood, but not the most pleasant either.

text: Armando did the flowers for my wedding in Santa Ynez last weekend and they were exactly what I wanted and absolutely beautiful! The details were impeccable and the combination of colors was perfect for a summer morning wedding. Armando is very responsive and knows how important communication is to a bride-to-be! I would absolutely recommend his services to anyone wanting creative, modern, beautiful wedding flowers.
label: POS

text: Dan and I stopped by Varga for a nice weekday lunch. I knew they started a new "speed lunch" menu. Also, I hadn't been here since summer. During lunch, this spot is pretty slow. Still, the city is in sore need of good bars that serve weekday lunch, so I'm really happy this is open. The beer list, as always, in incredible. They also standardized the beer list: 3.5 for half pints, 6 for goblets or pints, and $25 growler fill. Between us we tried Bell's Hopslam, Great Divide St. Brigid's Porter, Slyfox Odyssey, Great Divide Old Ruffian barleywine, and St. Victorious Doppelbock. They have so many choices that I really love the new offering of half pints. Varga also keeps their beermenus page and twitter meticulously up to date. Dan and I were both craving burger, so we skipped the lunch menu. The burger was good; well topped with bacon, aged cheddar, lettuce and tomato. The burger was also served with fries and house made ketchup and mustard. I enjoyed my meal, but it's not my favorite burger in the city, and the $14 price tag is steep despite the Kobe label. We also split a bowl of spicy gumbo with chirzo and shrimp. This was a good idea because neither of us ate all of our food, and the bowl of soup was $8. Considering the speed lunch includes a bowl of soup and half a sandwich for $9, you almost can't pass up this deal. Bottom Line: I still like Varga a lot. It's a great choice for good lunch and beer in the neighborhood. When the weather gets nice and you can sit outside, that just another reason to love this place.
label: POS

text: Decent cheap Mexican food, served by sullen teen staff who act like they're doing you a favor. Walk across the bridge and eat at Tortuga's in Lambertville. Spend the extra $10 and get a better meal served by friendly people.

The bartenders make the best dirty martinis I've ever had. And they serve 6 mimosas for a flat rate at brunch! My ex is the Restaurant Manager and will always make sure that your experience is a pleasure. All you have to do is speak up if it isn't!

text: My family and I were in Reno from July 5-7, 2009 visiting friends. text: Okay, this is one of my favorite restaurants. I was introduced to the place by a former employee in good standing, come here every other month and go for broke with a big dinner, have been used as a guinea-pig by the chef-owner, and am apparently IP, if not VIP enough to have been given a New Year's Gift of Sake. This is one of the best places for Sushi in the Santa Barbara area. The fish quality is high, and I particularly love the salmon, yellowtail, eggplant, and shitaki nigiri. The beer and wine list is standard for a good sushi restaraunt, so I can't complain that they don't carry Asahi Black. They have a wide assortment of rolls that demonstrate a sort of California-Fushion approach to sushi, using fruit, lobster, vinaigrette's, and other oddments a truly traditional place usually doesn't have. On the other hand, like those traditional places very little cream cheese shows up on the menu. Favorite non-standard roll: Champignon. Several kinds of mushroom, heated, with sweet sauce and a spritz of white truffle oil. If you like Mushroom and Sushi-style food, you will love this. In fairness, I have to admit the waiting staff is a little erratic. Some are excellent, others seem to forget to check in on you, or what it was you asked for last. Since I'm almost always at the bar, this isn't quite as critical. The parking is also limited, as the strip mall it's part of only has a few dozen spots. I usually park at the "extended Ahi parking" along is outer wall. Turn in at the motel next to it instead of at the stripmall itself. Their entrees are also excellent, though a bit pricey. Order something unique if you are going this route. I highly recommend the Gindara, it's a traditional Japanese sea bass dish, and it is warm, miso-sake-sweet, and you can eat it one flake of fish flesh at a time. The Agedashi Tofu is very good here, and the reason why I now try it at every Japanese restaurant I visit. The place is elegant-casual and not really a rowdy place. If you want even quieter, go for a late lunch at 1 or 1:30. The lunch deals are good and the focused attention of the chef and waitstaff doesn't hurt. Ken-san experiments a lot in his cooking, and every few months the specials menu on the chalk board changes around. They are often very unique, and very tasty, so give it a try! (Wasabi Duck Tempura, last time I was there. Mmm.) Ken and his sushi team are very friendly, and it seems like one slot is filled by a Japanese exchange chef- certainly these cheerful guys seem to disappear "back to Japan" about as often as I convince them to start feeding my girlfriend extra salmon.

text: Seeing as there are only 3 reviews on this place, I contemplated not even taking the time to write one, but.....it is SO bad that I just have to. I was in New Orleans for a work convention and my coworkers and I decided we wanted to eat somewhere nice but not too fancy. Somehow we chose Tony Moran's because the menu seemed decent and it was close to our hotel. To enter the restaurant you must first walk through the accompanying bar called The Old Absinthe House. I truly wish at this point we had become lost and given up, but no, we made it to the back and 'voila', Tony Moran's! OK, so the ambiance was nice, candle light and table cloths. I thought we were in for a nice meal. The second our waiter came over and opened his mouth, I knew it was going to be bad. He rambled off the specials and at one point said "We have a very nice baby veal tonight". Cue the giggle from me and someone else at the table. The waiter paused, looking perplexed, and asked if he had said something wrong. When we realized he hadn't been joking, we kindly explained that ALL veil is baby cow so it is oddly redundant to say "baby veal". After reviewing the menu and noticing the typos (come on really?) I settled on the Fettuccine Alfredo and a shrimp cocktail app. My shrimp was actually served hanging off a martini glass, which I found tacky, with some soggy lettuce smothered in generic from-the-bottle cocktail sauce. Yuck! I couldn't even finish it and there were only 4 SMALL shrimp to be had. After the disaster of the appetizer course, our main entrees arrived. (Remember I ordered the Fettuccine Alfredo) As he is setting down my meal the waiter says "Linguine Marinara". Seriously? The sauces aren't even similar, at least TRY to get it right. Anyway, one person had the chicken picatta which was good, but another had the most generic looking 'meatball and sauce'. Yes, MEATBALL, a giant ball-o-meat atop a mound of pasta. My friend next to me ordered the Tuna cooked rare, so naturally it came out well-done. And the strangest part was it is was served on top of pesto AND marinara sauce. It looked like the "chef" had changed his mind half way through plating the thing!! Oh and the grilled veggies were so peppery that she actually coughed while trying to eat them! Tony Moran's claims to be "famous" for their Alfredo, the only thing that should be famous about this is how bad it is. I expected a creamy cheesy sauce blanketing my noodles, taking me to saturated fat heaven. This is NOT what I had. I don't even think what I had could be classified as Alfredo. You know how Fettuccine Alfredo leftovers look the next day? Kind of clumpy? This is what I was served, and for $19!? Ugh, then to top off a terrible meal it took almost 35 min for our waiter to divide up our check and swipe our cards. He apologized so many times through out the meal for random things that we decided Tony Moran's new slogan should be "Sorry about the delay folks!". Please do not be fooled by this place. It is a crappy restaurant posing as upscale dining.
label: NEG

text: I am not entirely sure where to begin with this review. The most obvious problem with El Vez is the atmosphere. If you are sitting anywhere near the bar, plan on having the ass of a half-drunk person as the defining feature in your table. Twice over the course of one meal did the same group knock things off of my table. Because the wait is so long, people flock to the bar to pass the time. At $8 bucks a drink, the mixers are certainly helping the bottom line, but make dining anywhere near the bar impossible. While certainly this is the fault of careless customers, the establishment must accept a fair share of the blame for poor crowd management and floor layout. There were two girls serving as hostess and two doing something at computers. Perhaps that payroll could be better spent on maintaining a division between those drinking at the bar and those eating at tables. Also, if you enjoy talking to the people you came with, well, take notes and have a conversation after leaving. Two people directly across from one another nearly have to shout. Unpleasant to say the least. They push their guacamole and mixed drinks pretty hard. I would too if I was charging $14 for $3 worth of avocado. Was it good? Certainly. Can my grandmother produce the same result with nowhere near the expense? Without a doubt. And there is little doubt that freshly made margaritas are great, but at the price, I can't drink enough to justify why I am yelling at the person across from me. Finally, if you are known for something you shouldn't have to announce it as soon as I sit down, and, it shouldn't be a relatively simple appetizer. You should be known for your entrees. I ordered the the enchilada plate. Not one of the sauces tasted right. In my mind, if you don't get the sauce right, all is lost in the world of enchiladas. The black bean enchilada had a great filing, but the sauce was laughably sweet. The chicken enchilada was okay, if you are able to ignore the almost chef boyardee like tomato aftertaste. I was looking at that sauce, and wanting to taste the delicious, smokey flavor of chile ancho, but it just couldn't fight past the tomato taste. At this point, I was pretty well defeated, ready to call it quits. So I did. I dipped my fork in the shrimp enchilada, the sauce was off putting, though I can't identify why, so I called it a night. For the price and the buzz, I was expecting at least a decent meal. Frankly, the evening was a total let down. If you want mexican food, you are headed to the wrong place. If you want food that is shaped like mexican food, and served in a place decorated by a chicano stereotype, then you are certainly going to enjoy yourself. The food was not terrible, but it was certainly not worthy of the wait, the noise or high prices. You can do much better for yourself in Philly.

text: Added 1 star to review because I felt so badly for the manager, otherwise would've been a 1 star review. Last Saturday night decided to try it out...long overdue that a mexican restaurant is in the area, since the closest mexican place is the Murrietta's north of the Summit. We arrived at 7:45 pm and were promptly seated at a large round table more appropriate for a larger party, especially since there was a table for two right next to it (there were two of us~my husband and myself). The table had not been cleaned off and there was a bowl of salsa verde on the table, I'm guessing from the party before us. The young man who seated us quickly wiped down our table and brought a basket of chips and the same green salsa but left the original bowl on our table. Considering the table hadn't been cleaned prior to our arrival, I'm pretty sure it was a used bowl of salsa-yuck! I ordered a margarita on the rocks and when I tried it I couldn't taste any tequila whatsoever, just a lot of Triple Sec. I asked what kind of tequila was used and was told "Hornitos", which explained why I couldn't taste it-in my opinion that's more of a sipping tequila. For a margarita a better choice may have been Cuervo Gold or something with more of a bite. I ordered the "Enchilada" shredded beef burrito which the menu stated came with shredded beef, beans, rice (which I requested having left off, I don't like rice in burritos), lettuce and cheese, smothered in red sauce and cheese, with sour cream, guacamole and pico de gallo (price: $8.95, A' la carte), and my husband ordered the two taco combo plate with rice and beans. When our food arrived I was surprised that my burrito was cut in half, displaying a skimpy amount of beef and lettuce and although the tortilla was tinted red (apparently from sauce being sparingly applied and then left under a heat lamp),and drizzled with a meager amount of sour cream, it was not what could be called "Enchilada" style. My husbands taco plate was somewhat more appealing, although the tacos were made with one small corn tortilla each so when he tried to pick one up all of the shredded beef filling ended up on his plate. This wouldn't have been a problem if we'd had any silverware or napkins, but the waitress had to be reminded to provide those to us before we could start. The rice was faintly tinted but contained no pieces of tomatoes, onions, peppers or anything else to spice up the flavor and I unfortunately got a grain of rice that was hard and uncooked when I tried a bite. The beans were better but were barely lukewarm and the miniscule crumbles of oaxaca cheese weren't able to redeem them. By this point I had pushed my plate away and when the waitress came over to check on us and asked if I needed a box I told her no thanks. Within five minutes we were approached by the manager who was apologetic and explained that their chef had left at 7:00 pm and the kitchen was being run by the back-up cooks (why would the chef leave a new restaurant at 7:00 pm on a Saturday night?) She told us that the burrito would be removed from our bill and offered to replace it with any other item at no cost, which I declined. She then offered to make the burrito herself and said she would even box it to go, as my husband was almost finished with his meal. I agreed and she went into the kitchen, returning with a burrito that turned out to be much better than the previous one when we sampled it the next day at home. In spite of the sincere and gracious action from the manager, I wouldn't eat here again...the prices are too high for a casual restaurant, the dining area was not large enough to have any measure of privacy and the food was a disappointment. I think if they lowered their prices significantly and turned their restaurant into more of a cafeteria-style restaurant they might have a shot after they get over the glitches that every new restaurant experiences...from now on, I'll make the drive to Murrietta's.
label: NEG
