text: I was having a wonderful night at home with my boyfriend, we made dinner and we watched an episode of mad men, then we decided to go outside to grab a smoke on our deck and that's when things took a huge turn for the worse. With a combination of the rain, me wearing slippers and the slippery deck, I took a huge spill and fell directly on my chin and split it wide open. Needless to say, I needed stitches and my boyfriend and I went from relaxing to preparing for a possible night in the ER. I actually wanted to go to Penn but we didn't know where the ER was, we ended up passing Jefferson so just went there instead. I will probably be sticking with Penn from now on. As soon as I got there and checked in, the nurse took me back to take my blood pressure and temperature and confirm that I needed stitches. That's when the waiting started. The Emergency Room was in crappy condition, there was food trash all over the place from people waiting before us, fast food wrappers, cups, empty chip bags. We also had two homeless people come up to us asking for change for them to get food and drinks out of the vending machines. It took the receptionist yelling at the security guard a few times for him to even consider asking them to leave if they didn't need medical help. We were there for SIX hours, Five before the lady even called me in to take my insurance information. About twenty minutes later I was called back to see a doctor. Things were so disorganized. On top of that, my doctor didn't seem to know where anything was. He was running around, asking multiple people where things were, coming back and apologizing to me for the wait...this happened probably five times. I watched him run around like a chicken with it's head cut off. Kinda acted like it was his first night on the job. He also kept calling me young lady, I honestly don't think he was more then a few years older than me. haha. Anyway, I understand that late nights in ERs are going to be busy, I know it's expected that there will be a wait. I still think six hours is a little insane. The bad rating is because of my so-so experience once I got called in the back. They got two stars instead of one because the doctor did a decent job sewing me up. The worst part was the lidocaine, but that's expected, I hardly felt anything while getting the actual stitches. Overall, I wasn't impressed with their professionalism. I actually wasn't impressed with much of anything. Hopefully their specialized doctors are better because I have an appointment with one in February.

My wife ordered the White Pizza (a strange item on a place that seems to have a much more tropical flair), which I thought was fair but she seemed to like OK. Again complimenting the wait staff, they were amazing. They kept us in drinks without hovering, they brought the cake when we were ready and got us in and out without a hitch - quite a feat with 15 people who were cruising downtown in a limo. text: Hey, if you're feeling the need to lay down some serious bucks on nothing but atmosphere, then you're sure to love the tragic experience known as El Vez. Hey look, there's a goofy bicycle rotating in the center of the restaurant! Check it out! There's a photo booth where you can go in and make nauseated faces after realizing how much you spent and how satisfying the food wasn't! But you say you enjoyed their one of a kind cocktails and margaritas? Get outta town! What they're serving here isn't anything you can't get anywhere else, save for maybe that frozen blood orange margarita, but having tried it, I can safely say you're not missing a thing. So then, be prepared to pay out the wazoo for the "special guacamole" they have here (many different varieties; nothing exciting that I haven't had at other eatieries for a fraction of the price) as well as your entree. What? You don't want to spend between 15 and 25 bucks for each thing? Well then, you have no business being here! Actually, how this place stays open based on getting what you pay for is a mystery. What El Vez serves is nothing exciting, with no major crazy variation on anything that justifies the prices paid. I suppose it's good if you want trendy, "new" Mexican bullshit, but for what it's worth, you can do a lot better by going to one of the more authentic hole in the wall joints in town. It might not be flashy and the music might not be as obnoxiously intrusive, but your wallet and stomach will be much happier, plus you won't have to deal with hipster servers who put on the fake smiles and couldn't care less who they're dealing with. El Vez is cookie cutter nonsense with a colorful high gloss finish, that, unless you're just of that sort of crowd who doesn't care what they waste money on, doesn't leave any positive impression once your visit is over.

text: Govinda's Cafe (Gourmet to Go) is downstairs and the main Govinda Restaurant restaurant is upstairs. Fancy upstairs, casual downstairs. I've heard good things about both.. though I've only been to the cafe, so this review is for Govinda's Cafe (Gourmet to Go): Govinda's Cafe- Gourmet to Go- is a hip, cool Philly cheesesteak joint... there is an atmosphere of fun here. The best part is subtle: it's all vegetarian! Their cafe features vegan and vegetarian soups, sandwiches, and other deeelliccccious items. I can't rave enough about them. They offer soy or regular cheese on their sandwiches, as well as flavored tortilla wraps instead of bread. Tip: go for the soy cheese and wrap on your sandwiches for a tastier edge. I find the chicken versions to be tastier over their other meat soy renditions. The items are grilled fresh on the spot-- and each cook adds their own touch: I find each one has their own "specialty"-- they make one or two items more standout. So one item can be extraordinary one day-- and the next just good. Therefore, you have to know the cooks and their niche too.. to get that extraordinary touch. Their sandwiches are unreal. Most items are large portions-- perhaps even large enough for two for some. Their chicken cheesesteak is so much like the real thing- my favorite. You cannot tell it's not real chicken.. it's so tender! They have a range of sandwiches, each having its own fan base... i.e. tuna, pepper cheesesteak, ham, etc. Some rave over the Subji Wrap, which is more of an Indian style veg wrap. Others rave over their Chicken Salad sandwich- it's really super good. They even have an awesome chicken Mexican quesadilla. It's really an international type grill. Sort your selections and choices as you would in any non-veg place: it's not all necessarily healthy, non-oily, yoga-happy stuff (though some items are). It is a good decent place for good decent grills, which just happens to be veg. The place draws quite a crowd, so do be prepared to wait at times. It's a sure shot winner, each time. .............................................................................................................................. Update several months later: Still fantastic sandwiches.. I go there all the time. One thing though.. I noted recently that the portions (sandwiches) have perhaps got a bit smaller lately (?!).. not too happy about that. Aaah.. inflation.. :( . I recently tried their new platter dishes, which they added.. and definitely prefer their sandwhiches over the platters. I hear they will be adding this/that.. sometime... but I still think their orignal grill stuff is the star. My mouth remains happy as the sandwiches keep getting tastier and tastier. The hostess was brisk and efficient, our server friendly, though it was hard to hear her over the din. text: I ate at Cafe Antonio for the second time today. The food and service, like the first time, was awesome. The ambiance is actually really good. There's a lot of natural light and the tables are far enough apart to ensure a reasonably quiet and private dining experience. The wait staff was very good. I wasn't rushed, and I wasn't made to wait either. The timing between the order-taking and delivery of food was just right. The staff also kept on top of water refills - something that I appreciated, as I always seem to be left waiting for water or other drinks when I eat out. The food is the real star at Cafe Antonio. The menu had a large variety of dishes, all reasonably-priced for the quality and portions. The chefs do a wonderful job with the food. I've only had the pleasure of having a handful of dishes, but all of them were served steaming hot and were packed full of great flavor. Also... BYOB! It's nice to be able to bring your own bottle of wine. You get exactly what you want and you get to save money. Overall, Cafe Antonio is an excellent place to eat. If you like Italian food and live in the area, you owe it to yourself to give them a try.

text: I still for the life of me can't understand why this place does not get better reviews across the board; they are always crowded when I have been and the food is always amazing. Their batter, which is not crumbly or crumby like other places, is a very much like a tempura batter and oh so good. I have not yet tried on single bad thing on the menu, from their fried mushrooms with horseradish sauce, chicken n buttons and Monterrey Chicken breast. Then there is the amazing mac n cheese (only second to Cracker Barrel, still need to try Loveless and Rotier's on that) and their awesome burgers. There is the one dish that is sure to make any lover of Mac n Cheese outright soak themselves in drool... The Ultimate Pasta, which is so good; think mac n cheese on steroids and this is what you get. Also, if you are a fan of Chicken Parmesan and are really hungry, they have the largest serving of Chicken Parm anywhere I have seen. Now while it is not the best in town, it is still very good. Finally, I must say, they have the best Chicken Tortilla soup I have ever had anywhere (even back home in Texas), as it has the perfect amount of cheese, tortilla strips, chicken, corn and seasonings in it. As for there Caesar salad, it is consistently good every time I have had it. I could go on and on about all the tasty menu items there, but there are to many to name. However, I will say that they also have some very good shakes. Now, my only complaint is that I wish they would bring back their coupons! They used to have coupons where, among other things, when buying two entree's you got the lesser of the two (cost wise) for free.

The section concerning American and Japanese propaganda also just goes to show how people have to dehumanize the other side in order to carry out the horrible acts that constitute a war. On that note, I might want to ad that the section concerning the war in the Pacific did have some graphic and disturbing imagery. There were some parents with some young kids which I thought was a little out of place seeing as there were some definitely R rated photos. The museum goes far to convey the insanity and cunning it took to liberate Europe, as well. Having been to Normandy I think that gave a great picture of D-Day. A great place to take a half day and break from the food and drink of New Orleans and get your history groove on.

text: The Green Hills Library is housed in a large new building just off of Hillsboro Pike. If you live nearby, this library would be a great place to come and study, thanks to the many large wooden tables by the windows and comfy reading chairs distributed throughout. Actually, the setup of this library reminds me a lot of the one at the college I went to. They have a great selection of adult fiction and nonfiction books, DVDs, audio books, and a small music section. What really makes the Green Hills Branch unique is the children's section. It's HUGE! Since kids get their own separate room, parents don't have to worry as much if their children make a little noise. There's even a designated "Toddler Computer," which evokes funny images in my head. Speaking of computers, Green Hills has over 30 public computers, so hopefully that means the wait is never long. If you like to own books as well as borrow them from the library, Green Hills has a great biannual book sale for a few days every May and October. Adult books cost $0.50, children's are $0.25, and there's also a decent free section. Once you've picked out your books, you can grab some fruit to munch on at the nearby Green Hills Farmers Market, find a bench at the Sally Brewman Green Hills Park next to the library, and get lost in a good book.

They were doing stuff with blueberries and multiple spirits and god knows what all. It was like Dexter's Lab. The joint itself is very stylish, dark and modern - well not so dark in the spring with daylight savings time as in winter. Theres a giant skylight 40 feet above the bar, but the rest of the place is nicely finished with tables that go way back in the narrow space. Every once in a while, the place gets packed, but it's a reliable after work mix of young suits, the slightly tattooed, and otherwise casually good looking hipsters. There are two flat screens that play not only domestic sports but the English soccer leagues too. The music is top notch - these guys have got style for sure. It's unpretentious and done well. You'd think that would be enough, but the food is great too. Not your ordinary bar food for blue collar Philly, no. They've got a hummus plate with pita and different kinds of olives. My favorite is the lobster quesadillas. They've got a great bisque, and you only need one dish to fill you up. Alfa is really as close to a perfect bar as you can ask for. Not too big, not too small. Great drinks, great food, great service.

text: Cora's is a chain from Quebec that has been making waves on the breakfast scene in other parts of Canada. Although it is located deep on the south side, I made the trek to find out why people are raving about the place. It only took me a few moments looking at the menu to see why. Mountains of fresh fruit adorn waffles, French toast, pancakes, yogurt and granola parfaits, crepes, and more. I ordered a Seven of July, which was crepes and French toast covered in fruit. The French toast was sweet with nutmeg and cinnamon, while the crepes were crispy. I am very partial when it comes to fruit, and I can honestly say that both the variety and freshness were perfect. At the other side of the table, a roast beef panini was ordered. It came with the soup of the say and a side salad. The salad included a glass filled with sticks of carrots, celery, and zucchini, with dip at the bottom. The reaction? One of the best he has ever had. No small compliment. I had coffee (average) and he had a raspberry fruit smoothie (delicious) and we shared a side order of roast potatoes (tender and savory). Prices are average to middle for this kind of food ($10-$12), service is very friendly, and the decor is bright and colourful. It was very busy though, despite it being a weekday afternoon. On weekends, be prepared to wait in line. However, the plates really look like works of art and everything tastes as good as it looks.
label: POS

The complimentary bread is also really good...crispy on the outside and soft & yummy on the inside. text: I hope that no one ever tries to light up in this place. It's a tinder box with all of the wood and lacquer. PEOPLE YOU DON'T KNOW WHAT YOU ARE MISSING. The food was wonderful. The spring rolls, which I base the way my night is going to head, had fresh vegetable filling and the sauce on the side (huge plus). The service aspect can't be gauged because only having 3 tables occupied makes it possible that a 12 year old off the street could at least get the job done. **Note** Our server was good, not great. I hate myself for late night eating. It's just as good cold and reheated. Three funny/odd moments of the night. First, there were more To Go orders than people actually eating in this place. Second, our server told us she only works there one night a week and the Thai place she works at full time does things differently. I didn't have her ellaborate and don't think I want her to either. And third and most commical..... They played the SAME SONG over and over again. I have no idea what it was because it wasn't in English but they had one song on repeat. I felt like I was in Ground Hog Day. Maybe this is why there were so many take out orders.

text: I haven't had a buffet like this since Vegas. I was convinced you couldn't find a better one than there. So so so so wrong! I didn't know what it was for but when I looked over the stations, I noticed signs like "$4 for 6 jumbo shrimp" and "$5 for ribeye steak" at the grilling station or "$2 for an ice cream sundae". It occurred to me that if you wanted those extras, you pay for them. It's a clever way to keep the buffet price at an affordable price. They had plenty to choose from even if you don't want those extras like fresh oysters! I think I had about 4 full plates with 4-5 oysters on them. It was HEAVEN! I have never heard of Guinness beer ICE CREAM and yes, I had a scoop. It was definitely beer and a different experience when it comes to ice cream. The food was very fresh and tasted high-end which goes well with the whole restaurant which was very clean with nice decor. I don't know when I'll ever be back in Tampa because it's a long way from California but Vegas, the Buffet Capital of the world, is a regular vacation spot for me. I don't know if any of the buffets there will measure up but I hope it does! Tip: Get the player's card before you don't already have one. Save yourself $5 per person.

text: Blondie and I were jonesing for steak. And it was Mother's Day. Since we had only moved here less than two weeks ago I didn't know the area eateries that well. Our waiter was helpful but a bit of a snob. He did, however, help Blondie select a Sangiovese Santa wine which she greatly enjoyed. For the entree Blondie ordered the petite filet mignon with lobster bernaise. She likes her steaks well done and that has resulted in some rather chewy meals but her steak tonight was perfectly cooked and actually very tender. High marks for that. I ordered the king size prime rib cooked medium and it was also perfectly cooked. Blondie and I shared a helping of asparagus cooked soft, just like we requested. The main meal was very enjoyable. For dessert we shared a slice of key lime pie, which we both thought was not tangy enough and too sweet. Not bad enough to ruin a meal, just not what we were looking for. Since it was Sunday, the wine was 25% off, which was a nice surprise. All in all a very nice meal and good experience.

text: I went here today for a really nice, relaxing lunch. The decor is pretty subdued and tasteful. There weren't too many people here, which worked to my benefit. So did the cook, who came out at one point and asked who had the spicy lamb, and both of us said yes. He said "It's gonna be good" and smiled. I figured that portended well for our meal. The roast lamb sandwich came out with a side of greens. It was a nice homemade seeded roll stuffed full of lamb, spices and cheese. As promised it was spicy, but not overly so. There was a plethora of flavors in the lamb sandwich. As promised they had a spicy past/sauce in a small bowl. I put it on part of the sandwich. It was marvelous, adding more flavor and heat without being too hot(e.g. habanero hot). I had a dessert that was a like flaky pastry soaked with honey and stuffed with something that reminded me of a cannoli filling. I left with a nice warm glow and a full stomach. I"ll be back.

text: It's funny that there are 29 five-star reviews of this mechanic. I am a former customer of theirs. I will never go back after my last experience with them. I had been going to 11th St. Auto Repair for years, with two different vehicles that I personally owned, and then most recently with a third company-owned vehicle. Every time was the same: prompt, friendly, honest service. Then one day my girlfriend pulled into town in her jeep with Rhode Island tags. The truck was experiencing some issues that had been bungled by a sub-par mechanic in Connecticut. So, thinking, hey, the guys at 11th St are my buddies, been going to them for a long time, they will fix us up. We dropped the truck off with a list of all the things we knew needed to be done, as well as a list of things we wanted them to look at. They looked at the list, then looked at the registration that read Rhode Island. One guy looked at the other, nudged him and said, "he he, Rhode Island." We came back several hours later and NONE of the things we had told them to do had been done, NONE of the things we asked them to look at turned out to be problems, and they had taken the liberty of plastering a Pennsylvania emissions sticker on the windshield, and charged us $95 for the "service." Stunned, we staggered outside and sat in the truck for a moment. I felt foolish, angry and embarrassed. I asked the gf if she wanted me to go back in there and confront them. She said no, it's not worth it, just take your business elsewhere from now on. And we have. F you 11th Street auto repair. You are NOT honest mechanics.

text: First of all I applaud Joe Edwards for his efforts to continue and make Delmar the best street in all of St Louis to visit. Without his vision and efforts the street and U city would be a dilapidated rundown area and not the the engaging, diverse, and profitable place that it has become over the last 30 years. From Blueberry Hill, the Pageant, Tivoli, Bowling Alley and now Eclipse/Moonlight in addition to the Trolley cars coming soon; the man has pursued his wonderful, funky, eclectic vision for U City to it's fullest. That being said, there is no way that this restaurant deserved any of the awards recently won in the Riverfront Times and Sauce magazine. I give the Eclipse high marks for its interior, but the food is very average. I appreciate the efforts of the Chef to bring in some items that you can't find on most StL menus (bone marrow as example) but the food is lacking in layered levels of flavor. The bone marrow was disappointing, the Trout needed some acidity, the Caesar you could get at any Applebees, and most everything was on the cold side. The service was marginal at best. I did think that the Eclipse bar and the Moonrise bar were both being ran by a mixologist with a subtle but loving hand. I wish I would've enjoyed the food more, but much like the other reviewers I will still return to the Moonrise but I will skip the Eclipse and make my way to the bar. I do hope that it improves because I will always support Joe Edwards and his efforts to grow U-City
label: NEG

text: I have a major axe to grind with said establishment and how poorly they handled a snafu from way back when. (If only Yelp had existed back in the day!) It was a typically crowded Saturday night, and parking was of course at a premium. So instead of circling around for parking for 30 minutes, I caved and decided to hand my keys over to the valet. Fast-forward to the end of our meal, where our waiter told us to give him my claim check when we were ready to settle the bill so he could give the valet a heads up to bring our car around. We did so, which would have worked fine, except for the fact that it took a good 20 minutes for our waiter to bring my credit card back so I could sign the bill and leave. This triggered a most frustrating chain of events. Under the assumption that we would be out in a few minutes, the valet brought my car around in a timely manner, but when I didn't show up soon after (because the waiter was moving at a snail's pace), he left my car in the middle of the dark street with the keys in the ignition and the driver's door partially open. WOW - you might as well have put a sign on it that said, "Please steal me." Knowing how New Orleans is, I'm frankly shocked that the car didn't get stolen. But it gets worse: not only was my car abandoned and ready to be stolen at any time, but it was also blocking traffic (darn narrow Warehouse District streets), so I got a parking ticket. As I'm finally leaving the restaurant, someone outside informed me of what just happened with my car, and of course, I'm furious. (I was a broke college student at the time, so a parking ticket was certainly not a welcome added expense for the evening's activities.) The brilliant valet who ditched my car resurfaced and made excuses for why he left it. I soon realized that I was going to have to escalate the matter to management to get any sort of resolution and was irritated enough, so decided to go home, regroup and try to get this resolved the next day. I first started with calling the restaurant, who so adroitly played the blame game and said that it's not their fault (even though it was their waiter who delayed me getting out the door) and that the valets are from another company that I would have to contact. I then reached out to the valet company, who pretty much said they couldn't do anything about what happened. Nice. As a last resort, I tried contesting the parking ticket with the city of New Orleans (It's all about the principle of the situation!), which, in their infinite wisdom, they rejected my claim. Being the tenacious one, I decided to go back to square one and approach the restaurant again, but in person this time. I showed up during a quiet afternoon and politely asked to speak to the manager. He showed up soon after, and listened as I calmly explained what happened. After I finished my story, I was appalled by how he responded, talking to me as if he were calming an upset child and using such platitudes as "oh baby" and " sweetie, I'm so sorry." text: I Love this place... I don't know what else to say. It is the best game in town. The food here is so good. It is a shame that I am in Arizona right now, the land that Chinese food forgot. I am dreaming about the soup! The bowls of soup are HUGE, definitely enough to share for 2-3 people, but I can definitely down one alone. I recommend the roast duck noodle soup with ho fun noodles. Another great starter is the coconut shrimp, and if you like it, BBQ eel. For dinner, I recommend the Chilean Sea Bass. Very large portion in a soy glaze. Another great choice is the Chicken Chow Fun (I lived on this in China, and Sang Kee does it so well and authentic). When in season, I recommend the lobster. You get a 1 1/2 pounder in your choice of sauce. I love the XO sauce with the lobster, its a perfect combination. This place gets busy. Everyone in and out of the Main Line loves it, and on the weekends there is always going to be a wait. During the week you can expect to sit right down or maybe a 15 minute wait. Its always best to call ahead earlier in the day if you're going in on the weekends, or go in if you don't mind a slight wait. text: I actually had a table at the Super Flea for many months. You can even sell your unwanted gold or get a haircut! The hot dogs are cheap and a good bargain but the mini donuts were a bit off in my opinion. There are alot of collectors items for cards, stamps, coins, etc. So take it as you will, there will always be excellent finds and deals there but in my experience it sucks that you can't just sell anything for any price. If I want to sell my movies and games for 5 bucks less than the other guys I should be allowed to! But I guess those guys own half the place so of course the managers are going to look after them to get their rent payment. text: After seeing other bad reviews, I just couldn'tt keep my experience to myself. This place is Atrocious. If that's all you were looking to know, then read no more, but if you are looking to be entertained - then by all means, do read on. This place USED to give the best pedicures. and I USED to be willing to fork over the extra cash for it. No More! Here is some background to preface this review *I live in the city and I wear flip flops Every Day. So my feet get more than their fair share of abuse. *While I bathe and generally make myself presentable to society, I am not what you might consider girlie. I am a very busy woman, and to me these things are nice, but by no means a necessity to life. I am a good human being regardless of the occasionally bushy state of my eyebrows. *The Experience:* Let me now describe for you what I could only call a cursory pedicure that lasted all of 15 minutes (including polish) and that I would not have expected to pay more than $15 ($20 with tip) for; but which ended up costing me a whopping $40. And that I probably could have done my own self for free. This particular day I thought to myself, "self, you are waaaay over due for a pedicure. it would probably be a good idea to treat yourself to the good place, despite the higher price tag." So I walked into Allure, and with a hint of embarrassment, asked for a pedicure. The 10 women who were lounging around doing nothing proceeded to fight over whose turn it was. That should have been my first clue. The woman who led me to the chair seemed nice enough. As with every nail place I have ever been, I warned her that I was ticklish, but that I didn't mind if she didn't mind my hysterical bursts of laughter. All seemed to be going well, and sure enough the minute the pumice stone hit my feet I broke out into fits of loud boisterous laughter which I am known so well for. All of the girls in the salon started to point and giggle (this is totally par for the course and happens everywhere - I am used to it). At this point, the only thing that made me feel slightly uncomfortable was the fact that she kept making what I can only describe as "bedroom eyes" at me which went so far as to include a slight puckering of the lips and sucking in of the cheeks. I thought this strange and it gave me the distinct impression of being hit on (I would have been equally unnerved by had these advances been made by a man or a woman, this scenario isn't exactly primed for romance - I mean, what would you even talk about on the second date?) After 1 or 2 passes of the pumice stone, she placed my foot back in the water and I figured that having seen my feet she realized that they might require some heavy duty artillery. But then the woman did something really quite strange. She rinsed of my feet and started to drain the water. She dried my legs and feet and started to put some lotion on them. She asked me if I shave. I said that I had the day before (there was some stubble, but it wasn't any of her business - I was by no means some wildebeest covered in fur) and jokingly said I didn't feel the need to impress anyone. Her response - raised eyebrows and a guttural sound which I can only classify as chastising in nature. She continued to prep my feet for the polish. I didn't understand what was going on. I kinda tried to tilt my feet to see if I had missed something. But No, the calluses were all present and accounted for. I should have said something then and there. But i think I might have been suffering from a shock related condition. Then, to add insult to injury. She looked up at my face, stitched her brows together, raised her upper lip and asked me when i had last done my eyebrows. I said, Why yes, I am over due, but I can't do it this evening (it was around 5) or my face will be all red. (I have been doing my eyebrows for over 10 years - and owned this face for longer than that - I'd like to think I now how it reacts to things). She continued to insist that this would not happen and that I should have her do them. I chose to drop the subject rather than insult her lest she take it out on the polish she was about to apply. This continued on into an awkward 10 minutes under the dryer not unlike weird silences while on a date you would rather not be on in the first place. text: Ok Ok I know this place is considered crappy but it deserves a review. My daughter turned 11 this week. It was the first year that she didnt really want any toys or dolls, she wanted her ears pierced. me: What do you want for your B-day? A doll? female offspring: no , I want my ears pierced. me (uncomfortable): ha ha sure you dont want any toys? girl I hardly know anymore: no, I want my ears pierced, and some new outfits an mp3 and a cell phone. me(getting desperate): LOOK BARBIES! so I had to face reality that my little girl was growing up. We picked up her best friend and headed to the Granite Run Mall. I got into a slight fender bender on the way there (not my fault of course). My mood was darkening. A few tears escaped my eyes as i watched a mall employee mutilate my daughters ears. Friendlys was not my first choice but as fate was proving that it wasnt my day anyway. the girls wanted to go so we headed for Friendlys. A multitude of emotions tore at me on the way there. Lets just say i wasnt feeling too friendly. The Friendlys experience always starts the same way. No matter how busy or dead they are, they make you wait at the door for a little too long. It almost seems like your visit is an inconvienence, as if you showed up at Aunt Agnes's house uninvited. Sure shed put you up but youll get the attitude. There is also a long wait after being seated for the server to visit. Since im in the biz, I recognize when someone is in the weeds and they often are at Friendlys. Ok, things start looking up from here. Once we were acknowledged, the girl did a fine job. She checked on us, got our refills ,all the things that we should expect but are often lacking. The food works for me. Its not fantastic , but its filling and reliable. I got a Reuben. Ive had better but it was good. I was actually not hungry due to the days tragedies and when the plate was put before me, my appetite started to return, and along with it a better attitude. The girls shared a sampler, which they raved about. My notoriously picky son got his standard Grilled cheese , which met his approval. My wife also got a sampler, which was good (I especially liked the mini cheese sticks). i like the diversity of the menu. Theres really something for everyone. Its all very tasty. The prices were right too. We laughed and joked and had a good time, and isnt that what its all about (not the hokey pokey like we were led to believe as kids). As we all ate our ice cream (YUM!) i reflected on it all. The car could easily (if not cheaply) be repaired, noone was hurt. My daughter is behaving naturally for an 11 year old (and i,naturally for a dad). And Friendlys is not so bad, in fact, quite good. And.....hey wait, did that boy wave at my little girl!? OH HELL NO!

text: Oh...what happened to Crestwood Mall??? This used to be MY mall. I spent what seems like every weekend of my early teen years stalking through this place. I had it positively memorized. They had everything a thirteen year old girl could want....Claire's, American Eagle, Auntie Anne's Pretzels and a movie theater. Now.... Oh my...I have to say, I avoid this mall at all costs. Half of the stores are vacant and it gives the entire mall a very...well to put it lightly, creepy vibe. Dillard's is no longer an anchor store and so the entire East end of the mall is DEAD. The stores that are left seem drab and picked through, as though it's the place where clothes and shoes go to die, and the movie theater...well...it's seen far FAR better days. The seats are dirty and the floors are sticky. The entire theater seems kind of just, grubby. Upside, however, is that it IS the cheapest movie theater in St. Louis playing new releases...so maybe it's not so bad to live with the grime. My best friend's boyfriend doesn't even like it when she goes to this mall alone. I'm not kidding, it's that desolate in there. The Macy's is still alright for a quick run in if you know what you need and it's more or less a wardrobe staple. Otherwise, this mall has really gone down hill. I easily could drop this to one star but I have hope that it will turn around. I mean, it's Crestwood, something has to happen to this place. As it stands, however, it's on it's way to being blighted for sure. Until they fix it, I will keep avoiding it.

text: I was with a party of four who ate here last night, and I can only give this new restaurant the highest praise. It's located on busy Gallatin Road, in Madison, which is where I grew up. I am so proud that this authentic Cuban restaurant has made its home in an older business district that for years has struggled to maintain consistency. This is now the jewel of that strip of worn-out buildings, and it gives me hope that more of Nashville's immigrant population who make their homes in the area will tempt us with their traditional wares. Leaving all that aside, let's talk about the food. Oh wow, the food. We started out with a couple of $3 appetizers. One was a large plate of fried, crispy plantain chips -- with a texture like healthier potato chips -- with a dipping sauce that tasted of olive oil, garlic, lemon and a couple of other subtle tastes we couldn't identify. Magnificent. The star of the entire night was the next appetizer: the Cuban tamale, which was a giant plate with a thick square of masa filled with flecks of pork. Words can't express how good this dish is. Get it. It's large enough for four people to share, and might be the best $3 you will ever spend. The main course. I had the original Cubano sandwich. It is traditional -- roasted pork, ham, cheese, long flat pickles and yellow mustard. The bread is wide, flat, fresh and crispy, with grill marks across the top. Yum. Our Miami-loving friends said it's at least as good as the ones they have had down there. My wife had the ropa vieja. It's a very traditional Cuban dish, and perfectly executed. The meat had obviously been simmered a very long time, because it was juicy, tender, flavorful and falling apart. All of us got the black beans and rice side, as well as chunks of sweet plaintains, which were the best we've ever had - perfectly fried and not at all chalky or pulpy. Our friends had outstanding dishes as well. Virginia had chicken fricasse, which was so tender it was quite literally falling off the bone. Her husband, Andrew, a pescatarian, ordered shrimp in garlic sauce, which was very tasty. I woke up this morning and I finished off the half of the leftover Cubano sandwich I couldn't get through last night. Perfect breakfast. Then I started contemplating how to plan my dinner schedule around this new treasure.
label: POS

text: It's Lenten season. Along with giving up cakes, cupcakes, pastries, etc., I've also made a commitment to eating health-IER. I thought the decor was cool. Didn't really feel the effect of being inside a ship or sub, but nonetheless, the portholes were kinda cool. The restaurant was actually bigger than I had expected, and although the parking lot showed otherwise, there were quite a few groups dining in. So.. I chose an apple gorgonzola salad w/ chicken. I was already thinking that I'd be taking half of it to go. It had lettuce, green apples, candied pecans, gorgonzola cheese, grilled chicken breast and it was lightly dressed with a red onion vinaigrette. The ingredients were fresh, they meshed well together, and the chicken was moist. I truly.madly.deeply enjoyed my salad; my altar boy also said that he could eat it on a regular basis. Unfortunately, we didn't have any leftovers to take home. The kabobs were good too. They each had chunks of chicken breast, red bell pepper, green bell pepper, and onions. The herb rice didn't have much flavor, but the Mornay (cheese/butter/cream/calories!) sauce gave the dish extra flavor. Altar boy found the 2 kabobs too filling for lunch though, which is something to think about if you decide to get kabobs for lunch. Btw, our server, Tammy, was excellent. She was easy-going, attentive, and engaging. She also got us more information on the Mornay sauce even though we didn't ask for it. Amen to Flowing Tide Pub 2!

text: Jack's bbq caters to the tourist trade in Nashville. It was a major disappointment from a food and authentic standpoint. First off you are in a que that takes way too long. by the time you get to the big menu board, you are committed to buy the food because of the amount of time spent in line. While in line, I observed the cashier dumping the mac n cheese and the cream corn from a bag! (*I asked the cashier later if they make these sides or if it is "store bought." She admitted it was a commercial product.) It looked like she was slopping hogs by the way it was poured and served in the commercial warming trays. Disgusting for a "authentic" BBQ joint. All meals are served on a styrofoam plate with plastic utensils. Not very "down home." Also no wet wipes at all. Too much grease to wipe off with just paper. I ordered the "three meat" combo for $13.00. The portion was smallish and plopped on the styrofoam plate. Now, most of this review could be dismissed if the food was good, unfortunately, it wasn't. The ribs: The ribs did not have the membrane removed from the back of the bone. This is a very basic butcher requirement when prepping for pork ribs. Sadly, it was an inedible crispy, greasy membrane that stuck in my teeth. Awful. The smoke flavor was not that apparent. The pork shoulder: The pork shoulder was inedible. It had way too much fat content attached to the meat. I could not get a good bite with the taste of greasy fat in my mouth. Disgusting. Void of smoke flavor as well. The brisket: The brisket was the best of the three. It had a good smokey taste and was not as dry as the other meats. The sauce. I had a choice of two sauces, (poured from a broken communal container.) The "hot sauce" was way to hot and you could not taste whatever you put it on. Void of taste. The other mustard looking sauce had an abundance of vinegar and the vinegar taste was so strong it was inedible. Now, I would understand a few things wrong with every restaurant but Jack's falls way too short and is a money mill for the owner serving pour quality bbq to unsuspecting tourist. This is an honest and unbiased review.

text: I love visiting the St. Louis Coffee Oasis. LOVE. I first ate at the Oasis way back in 2006 after a long day of apartment hunting. I ate a few more times and then kind of forgot about it as I explored what was then my neighborhood instead. Flashforward to 2010 when I'm trying to make up for all the time I've missed by eating at the Oasis once a month. Seriously, what was wrong with me? I'm kicking myself for letting this place slide off my radar for so long. As everyone has said, the owner is beyond fabulous. He often does everything himself -- cooks, serves, brings water, checks up, mans the register, etc. Because of this, some time might pass between his checkups to your table, but honestly, you never really notice. You're too busy going over the extensive menu of yumminess, diving into your delicious meal or listening to him get verbally playful with diners. He's a treat to dine with, and I'm thrilled that he calls me and everyone else in the joint "my friend." I honestly believe he's sincere when he says it. I usually go for the the falafel plate. It's a toasted pita covered with lettuce and onions, covered with hummus, and piled with falafel. Others have remarked that the falafel may be too try for their tastes, but I actually prefer a drier falafel over a moist one. I think the crispy bread-like substance allows the spices and other flavors to shine a bit more. I usually end my meals with an order of baklava (during my latest order, the owner joked, "What's that? 20 pieces of baklava? Coming right up!"). There are three kinds of baklava available with different kinds of nuts. This isn't the drippy, syrupy kind of baklava (though I love that, too) -- this one is flakier and drier, with an inside that sort of reminds me of the crumb topping on Grandma's apple cobbler back in the day. I love it, and I could easily eat more than any girl should. There are other desserts too, but I haven't tried them yet because I keep revisiting the baklava. Prices seem a bit on the high side (My falafal plate is about $8, and my baklava runs about $2.50), but I'm happy to pay it because the atmosphere at the Oasis is so jovial. Moreover, you can sit for as long as you like and enjoy wifi and people watching. The Oasis is smokefree (yay!) and is just a few blocks north of the CWE Metrolink station. Parking? Pshaw. I love taking the train and not worrying about any of that. The #1 bus also runs up and down Euclid.

text: In the past year, Banh Mi had become the latest food fad that everyone seems to enjoy and being in Philly, we benefit from a respectable size of Vietnamese population residing in South Philly. That being said, the best Banh Mi in Philly is in a small store in Chinatown called Q.T. Well, it's not scientific observation of course. All I did is comparing a few bakeries in Chinatown, Ba Le, O Sandwiches and Ziet Cafe in South Philly as well as Sampan around 13th and Walnut, so I'm open to suggestions on places that I should try. But as of now, I'm sticking with Q.T. Two friendly ladies behind the counter made up the Q.T. sandwich team. They make each sandwich to the order to guarantee maximum bread crispiness and freshness. The prices here are slightly more expensive than conventional Chinatown standards and since it's made to order, there is a 5-10 minutes waiting time but it's quite worth it. Like other reviewers have mentioned, each Banh Mi has slightly sweet and sour pickled carrots and cucumbers, fresh cilantro for spice and jalapeno pepper for heat. The non-vegetarian ones are smeared with pate. I usually get the special Banh Mi which contains a combination of three different meats. The bread is toasted and crunchy which compliments the crispy vegetables, the creamy pate and the meat. The storefront can be slightly improved and it'd be great if they can speed up some in the sandwich making department but other than that Q.T. is definitely a welcomed addition to the Philadelphia Banh Mi scene.

text: I have had this sweet little art supply store across the street for some time, but sadly haven't gotten enough time (or purpose, perhaps) to bring more business here. Nestled comfortably beneath West Elm and Lucky Strike, the building's sprawling basement becomes a veritable oasis of creativity. FIRST IMPRESSIONS: As you walk down the stairway into the store space, a slight bird's-eye view allows you to see the shelves packed with every kind of paint, ink, pencil, cray pas, canvas, paper, rule, and book. It's very well-lit, and roomy, so you know you'll have a pleasant perusing experience. THE SELECTION: Comprehensive, to say the least. There's an entire section for framing and poster-board along the east wall, everything from school-level art supplies to stuff for the more serious fine artist. While the selection is pretty wide, there have been a few times that even Blick couldn't meet my need, so don't count on it for those stretch requests that you couldn't find anywhere else. THE PRICING: It's as spendy as anywhere else, you go there, probably spend more than you would have hoped, but there's no denying you'll be satisfied with what you get. I'm not sure if we have Adobe to blame for the rise in art prices, but I remember being able to use my allowance on a big box of crayons, some stencils and a sketchbook, with a little left to spare on some Bubble Yum...if ya know what I mean. THE SERVICE: Good luck getting some service, they're always dealin with someone else whenever I'm there, I haven't been fortunate enough to get anyone's time whenever I've needed something. The employees are likely mostly students at the nearby Art Institute, they know their stuff, but the underlying attitude that I see at most art stores-- bored, underpaid, undermotivated art students just trying to make some drinking money. Not knockin the service really, but it's a funny truth you might now notice when you go. THE BOTTOM LINE: The quality and organization of their supplies are both top-notch, not to mention the place is conveniently located, which is what keeps me coming back, it's certainly not the pricing, however. Recommended, in agreement with most other reviewers, over Utrecht and Pearl.

text: Being from the midwest, traffic in the Philadelphia, Baltimore and Washington area drives me nuts. Outside of the car, they are generally the greatest people you ever want to meet. But put them behind the wheel of a car and you got some of the biggest A-holes to ever hit the road. That being said, when I am visiting this area late fall or early winter, when it seems to be dark all the time, I prefer to stay close to the hotel when in search for a place to eat. I was staying at the Hampton on Baltimore Pike and the closest place I could find was the Hooters near the intersection of Highway 1 and Highway 202. Normally I don't seek out places that feature scantily clad women, but I don't avoid them either. I decided to take my place at the bar and order from there. In front of me was the so-called kitchen were there were three kids preparing all of the meals. There were also about a dozen slightly sleazy but still attractive waitresses roaming around ready to engage in some prick teasing conversation. I decided to keep it light, so I ordered a garden salad with ranch dressing and a half a pound of steamed shrimp. So far as the food goes, the salad was just about at the end of it's shelf life, bagged lettuce and red cabbage just beginning to turn red along with some stale croutons. Dressing itself was some standard restaurant pack. Shrimp kind of reeked of some fishy smell which indicated they were not fresh either. Dipping the shrimp in the provided drawn butter or dousing it with hot sause would kill the taste, but what would be the point of that? But that was not the scary part. I am a corporate food safety person for a food processing company and the Hooters food preparation crew broke almost every rule in the book. I'm not going to waste time listing every detail but one example was that the person cooking most of the food was also trying to unclog a sink. He began by using a hot water hose that had rubber peeling away from the surfaces and rotting threads in trying to clear out the clog...the rotting stuff was right over some fried foods that he was preparing at that time. Finally he got frustrated, took a black brush and started reaming out the drain. He then wiped off the excess water from the brush bristles, went to a cooler to get some raw chicken, put the chicken in a bowl and then threw the black brush on a shelf where bowls used to prepare their famous hot wings are kept. All without changing his gloves or washing his hands. If you want some eye candy, this is the place. If you want to avoid getting sick from food poisoning, this is a place to avoid. The only two things that save this place is that 1. They fry the crap out of most of the items they serve and 2. If someone does get sick, they'll blame the booze.

text: A bad restaurant may go out of business if its food is not good - that's the basic rule of competition. The point of dining is high pleasure, and we all expect a dining time with full of laughter, serious discussion and demands for more of the food. However, when it comes to monopoly, it's a different story: the restaurant doesn't have the threat of failure as a spur for improvement. I'm talking about Aramark Campus Dining in the University Of New Orleans, which has been serving UNO and torturing UNO students for years. Although the food there is cheap, for me and the other diners, very often, a low price cannot compensate for the joyful experience of dining. Located in the University Center (the UC), the Aramark Campus Dining is not alone; there are also Subway, Chick-fi-la, Béne Pizza and Pasta for students to choose different food for the meals. They serve as direct competitors to the university's cafeteria. The University Of New Orleans, envisioning that there would be a big threat of competition for the running of its low quality restaurant, provided it a good guarantee by forcing all students living in the dorm to buy a meal plan. The meal plan for residents starts at $1,135 per semester and ranges from 10 to 16 meals per week. Although the university has been trying to make improvements such as expanding the campus dinning area, the food quality still remains uncompetitive. There is pizza, spaghetti, fried chicken, tacos, turkey, sandwiches, hamburgers, French fries, or some kind of American food, depending on the day you go to eat. Many times you will be served a hamburger with a muffin soaked in artificial butter oil, toasted and assembled with beef, which was cooked in a large quantity at one time. If you are unlucky enough, the beef may be burned and blackened and look like coal that is not so delicious. The French fries there are the worst I have ever eaten in the US. Please don't be frightened when you are faced with a full plate of fried potatoes, full of oil, cold and soft enough to discourage the diner from even tasting them. That's malevolently bad. The variety of foods is poor. For breakfast, the options are unchanging: only sausage, omelet, egg and bacon. Lunch and dinner have different foods, depending on the day you go to the cafeteria; however there are only a few I consider to be "edible". Not only being stressed out by homework, but also being freaked out by the food in the UC makes me even more tired. There is no music for the meal, but only the noise because of people talking too much, especially at lunch. I'm amazed by how crowded the UC is every meal, and it makes me wonder if there are any students that have passed out or have been taken to the emergency room due to the UC food or not. In fact, the restaurant can do some more valuable change to improve the quality of the food, for example, serve different fruits for each meal. Nevertheless, it seems to assume all students have the same preferences for everyday, so the cafeteria always provide the cheapest fruit, cheapest pizzas ... available. I believe that bad food will give us memories of flavors that may later haunt and follow us in our dreams. I live in the dorm, and I'm forced to go the campus dining 10 times a week. After finishing a day full of work, I go to the University Center, saturated by the smell of fatty American food, and I feel that I even have more tiresome work to do: eat the food to survive. Maybe I'm a bit prejudiced with American food since I'm an Asian, but why can I enjoy Burger King, McDonalds and KFC but cannot give any compliment to the UNO Campus dining? The campus dining is supposed to provide relaxation and relief for students, not take their money and abuse them with bad food.
label: NEG

text: Two parts to this review, the station and Amtrak itself. Station: 1.5 stars. Amtrak Train travel in general: 3.5 stars. I really enjoy taking the train now. It is a new thing for me. Flying for years visiting relatives, although fun when I get there, is almost always torture. Squished together, the lines, check in, re-check in, security check, and now pat down/shoes off/power up laptop, take off jewelery etc.. ad nauseam... Amtrak has none of that nonsense. Advice: I always recommend the business class as it is only 20 bucks more, with the same lousy food naturally (hehe) but the seating is more spacious and comfortable with a lower noise volume which makes the comfort level goes up the scale to 100% in comparing to just regular fare. I have tried coach (LOUD and sometimes Greyhound-sque) & I have tried the lowest level of 2 person suite for travel (less leg room,) and I still prefer the business class. Perks: Business class you have 2 foot rests... one in front of you that you can rest your feet on and a leg/foot rest that props up like a lazyboy chair. You can lean back in your chair without disturbing who is behind you. There are 120V electrical plugs (for coach also) for every seat pairing. Pros/Cons: It is a longer way to travel, by train, but not that much longer if you are going to Chicago or Michigan. Sleeping our way to Michigan, rather then driving through the ice and snow is a blessing. Your luggage does not get searched, you can pack liquids and breakables as you choose, you don't have to take off your shoes, in business class you sit in a different (A LOT less crowded) waiting room. For $20 it is beyond worth the cost. Pros: Your luggage is always with you. You don't have to pack like someone might go through your stuff and you don't have to worry about your lip gloss causing an international incident etc.. If you pack something your big suitcase that is your favorite item, you don't have to worry about a luggage handler/sorter/etc.. lifting it off your hands. Carry that hair gel and in your carry on with no worries. This part is a big deal for me. Through many years of flying and the last few years of having to pack everything trying to keep in mind where to pack valuables (on me,) liquids of any sort (sealed in something and pray it doesn't burst in the suitcase.. oh the horrible memory of ruining a beautiful dress from Hair conditioner. :( etc....) .. THANK GOODNESS all I have to do is pack it up and go to take the train! Cons: Your luggage is always with you. Make sure ALL your luggage rolls or your shoulder bag is VERY light. Trust me. Your shoulders/back will NOT like you if you lug your heavy (or soon to feel that way) luggage around everywhere (thinking of Union Station and trading off to go to another hub.) The station itself: I like the location, as it seems a bit removed from the immediate area's traffic. The people who are working the ticket counter have 10 shades of attitude but they get 10 flavors of crazy going through there and not just mine. ;) (Good crazy is ok :p :D ) The fastfood joint is dirty and I couldn't bring myself to eat there. The chairs are horrible and there are no good places to put your luggage nor yourself for that matter. All sorts of characters walking in and out of there. I feel safe enough but I wouldn't have anyone I care about stay there too long waiting for me to pick them up. Always room for improvement. What's up: Take luggage that has wheels. Your shoulders/back/neck will scream at you if you try to carry bags everywhere. Pay the extra 20 bucks for business class for a much better experience. I love trains now. So stress free compared to driving/flying. Don't tarry at the station. Time your rides to be close to pick up time. I have heard many stories of VERY long waits for taxicabs, be warned. As you can call while you are on the train there is no reason to make people wait at the station for you or vise versa. Have fun! :)

text: Prior to going to Bern's I was told it was the best steak house in the world. Those are BIG words and hard to stand up to especially if you eat out a lot. Upon driving up to Bern's, the outside was quite simple. Not sure what I was expecting but with a statement like "best in the world" I was expecting not only a great steak but a rich setting. I pulled under the overhang to drop my car at the valet which was the only parking option and when my husband opened the door the first words out of my mouth were "The Madonna Inn". Then I realized that the people we were with were already inside and I hoped they hadn't heard me. Have you been to the Madonna Inn in SLO, CA? Bern's was a bit old fashioned and gaudy. I saw rooms with metal rental chairs, the kind you see in an old Italian restaurant with red and white checkerboard table cloths and in another room I saw white rod iron chairs that are usually outdoors. I ordered the filet of course because I had to try the steak and this is my favorite cut. With the steak was a small cup of French onion soup which was really good, for my salad I ordered the Macadamia Vanilla Bean Vinaigrette on the side since the waitress didn't recommend it and I got the Maple Dijon also on the side. Good choice because the Mac Vanilla bean dressing was more like dessert vs. dressing. With my steak came veggies that I left alone, a baked potato and Steak Fried onion rings. I could have ate a whole plate of these fried onions. They were thin shoestring onions that were lightly breaded and lightly fried. Don't forget to order some mushrooms on the side and if you like mushrooms, order your own because you won't want to share. Now the steak was very good don't get me wrong but it is not the best steak I've ever had and I wouldn't rate it the best in the world because I have yet to hit all the best possibilities. My favorite steak has a bit more seasoning and a touch of melted butter. A few surprises and treats were the kitchen tour. It was immaculate and beyond reproach. There are a ton of restaurants and probably a few of my favorites that I wouldn't want to know what goes on behind the scenes. This place definitely had something to show off. The second treat was the desert room. There is an actual room you go to, that has individual Booth's surrounded by walls with just a doorway on each end. I have never seen anything like this. It made dessert really special. If you have never been to the desert room, save room next time and have this experience. The atmosphere was wonderful, not to mention the deserts. I had the Creme Brule but since I'm a purest when it comes to this dessert, it wasn't my favorite. I like a crisp sugar topping and this had a sort of cookie crust. Good but not what I expect. But the Macadamia Nut Sundae was to die for and I'm not an ice cream fan so if you are, ORDER IT.

text: My wife and I had "date-night" last evening and chose to try Janos' new restaurant. We have both been fans of Janos for well over 20 years, but that might change unless he can get a handle on this new endeavor. Janos is trying to change that by directing people to the front door on Sixth Ave. Sorry I don't get that. My wife and I entered from the side and it was as thought all the wait staff stopped in their tracks and stared at us like we had committed the ultimate crime. All evening we watched others couples experience the same reaction; and then with heads down walk the walk of shame to their table from the front of the building - too funny. Service was very slow, but we had a lovely server and she made up for the long delays for drinks and dinner. We started out with an appetizer of calamari; we should have stopped there. The calamari was one of the best I have ever eaten. Unfortunately, dinner orders did not hold up as well. I had the Cochinita Pibil, black beans, achiote vinaigrette, caramelized pineapple, jicama salad. The flavor was not as full as one might expect, the pork was not cubed or shredded as traditionally served and my piece of pork was 1/2 fat, very little tasty pork to enjoy. My wife ordered the Orecchiette with white wine, chevre, dried tomatoes, cilantro and found it lacking as well. The only other enjoyable part of the meal, aside from the calamari, was the variety of specialty drinks. My wife loved the selection and if you are into heavily contrived cocktails you'll feel the same. I even found a couple to enjoy. We will give Janos another attempt, but hope that in the interim he finds a better butcher and works on fine tuning the menu so there is greater consistency across dishes.

We had our first night's dinner at Smokin' Gecko's BBQ, which is technically part of the Circus Circus casino. The food was fantastic--love that cornbread with honey butter. We had breakfast and lunch the next day at Flavors! buffet, which is a lot better than most of the buffets I've ever gone to. Only complaint about the food would be the scrambled eggs at breakfast--college dining halls do a better job than they did. We spent a lot of money in the casino (of course), but had a blast losing it all. No complaints about the parking garage, which was narrow, but we were able to find a spot for our Mustang and didn't suffer any dings. Minus one star for the high price for wireless internet--$9.99/day is just ridiculous. For a trip that's closer (and thus cheaper) than Las Vegas, I really don't think you can go wrong with the Silver Legacy.

They honestly seem happy to have you in the store and are excited for you to taste their wares. Can't make up your mind? No problem! They'll give you as many samples as it takes for you to decide (provided you're legitimately going to buy things, of course. Don't abuse the generosity). Moreover, they don't do that weird singing/rhyming thing that other ice cream chains (down the street, ahem) do to "keep people happy." I'm happy enough with B&J's honesty and smiles, thanks. Ben & Jerry's has about 16-20 flavors available. There's plenty to offer everyone with tastes leaning toward chocolate, nuts, caramel or fruit. And while Ben & Jerry's is a chain, the workers (many are area university students) take pride in the store and really make it feel like a local hangout. Ben & Jerry's annual Free Cone Day happened last week. Any free food day has the potential to go from a great idea to a catastrophe in an hour (see Denny's, KFC, etc.). However, this B&J planned properly for the crowds and had plenty of ice cream left even when I arrived at 7 p.m. (some flavors were already out, it's true). text: Hmm, what can I say about West Ed that no one else has said yet? Not much, so I'll just take a bunch of quotes from everybody else's reviews. Just kidding! As a local, I too have a love/hate relationship with this mall, but lately it's been bordering more on the love side of the coin. You gotta go in an easy-going mood. Do not, I repeat DO NOT go when you're stressed, cause you'll probably end up hating this place forever. It's packed, there are lots of people, and most tend to walk slow because they're window-shopping at the same time. So try to clear a little time for yourself when you visit. I used to be one of those people who would bulldoze through the crowds to get where I needed to be, and it took me awhile to figure out it just doesn't work that way. Go with the crowd, don't fight it. You'll be less stressed, and make people less irritated that way. The shops at WEM have been getting better over the years, with the introduction of names like H&M, Hollister, Abercrombie & Fitch, and Coach. There is a good mix of affordable and expensive high-end shops, something for everybody. WEM has several food courts, and the one by Galaxyland is the best because it offers more variety, including Korean and South Asian cuisine. If you've got more time and want more than fast food, Bourbon Street is the place to be. This is one of my favorite places in the mall. Even though they've replaced some of the older restaurants that had more character with typical chain eateries, this corner of WEM has so much going on. Choose from the Old Spaghetti Factory, Moxie's, Tony Roma's, Hudson's, or even Hooters in this special part of West Ed. There's so much to do in this mall, even I haven't tried everything yet. There's the waterpark, Galaxyland fun & rides, mini-golf, sea lion shows, shooting range, movie theatres, bowling, and Fantasyland Hotel, to name a few. They used to have more animals in cages and behind glass throughout the mall, but they've stopped doing that since some of the animals became sick. I'm glad for that, because it was so depressing to see them cooped up in a shopping mall. I mean, a zoo is usually bad enough, but a shopping mall? I wonder how long the poor sea lion is going to last. If you're a first-time visitor to West Ed, I suggest approaching it with an open mind. Don't go expecting the time of your life, but still be open for a fun afternoon. As for me, this is still my favorite mall in the city, because it's got everything in one place.

text: At dinner the other night with some publishing folks who regularly exhibit at the comic & popular culture conventions (ie: Comic-Con), "con-curry" was described as the odor resulting when the elevator doors are opened upon a bevy of character-dressed attendees who've roamed the convention for three days without a change of costume. Not terribly pleasant. Nevertheless, I think I'd prefer to inhale con-curry over the scent of artificial coconut layered on top of the many years of stale cigarette smoke which assaulted me every time I passed through the Circus Circus doors. I dreaded to return here each evening. My room was spared but the scent did permeate every public space of this Hotel. The semi-connected El Dorado and Silver Legacy hotels fare a bit better in the olfactory department, according to the testimony of fellow trade show exhibitors. Outside of Houston, the largest concentration of obese Americans is here at this Hotel. But Reno may beat out Houston in the overall aggregation of unhealthy + ugly people. I guess this isn't entirely Hotel management's fault. But the decor surely is. My room was furnished with two clown paintings, the most offensive (nightmare-inducing dismembered clown head in lower right corner) of which I covered with a poster that I tactically picked up on my second exhibition day of the library trade show. I didn't care for the burgundy and forest green color scheme of my room -- which blossomed to full effect in my polyester bed spread, but at least the room seemed clean everywhere but in the corners. (Hard to tell with the floor, though, because of the busy carpet.) The soaps and lotions were too perfumed but the bath bars were slightly redeemed for being equipped with massage nodules which were a nice touch in the truest sense. My only real room gripes were with the high pitched whine that emanated from some kind of poorly plugged hole in the bathroom wall, and with the absence of bathroom ventilation. (Hey, maybe the plugged hole IS the ventilation system?) I couldn't hear the high pitched whine from the bedroom but, then, I did close the bathroom door at night. Closing the door did not, however, obscure the sound of the pair having sex in the room next to me. I'm for less shared sound in Hotels in general, but overheard sex doesn't always have to be a two-star-deduction kind of sound. Nevertheless, hearing the woman's haggard *speaking* voice made it so; I'm positive I beat the dude she was with to the shower. So props to their morning circus circus antics for succeeding where my wake-up call failed: rousing me after my own late night. Be aware of added fees and required deposits: My room had been booked by my Company, in advance, so in order to place (even local) outgoing calls from my room I was required to leave a $30. deposit. And I was charged a $15. handling fee for the package sent to my attention at the Hotel. *The handling fee for this 32 pound box did not include the handling of it across the street to the free shuttle bus that transported guests to the convention center. This Hotel really did feel like one of the great equalizers, though, on the level of our nation's National Parks. And there's something to say for that. I don't normally enjoy small talk but I kind of enjoyed it here, via passings in the lobby and shared elevators. No such thing as hip here. And if you think you are, don't expect anyone to care or notice.

text: Guilt and lack of review finally overcame me, so I dragged the beautiful wife to Terrace View (at least this time it was 50 below or whatever it was when we tried to go there the first time). Upon walking up, somebody came right up and opened the door. +1 Upon walking in, we were asked if we had reservations. And the place was empty (outside of the employees of course). Ummm, no. But thanks for being open! Not a problem, we were seated, only to discover that their happy hour only runs 3:00pm to 5:00pm. 5:00???? On a Friday? Downtown? Seriously, that's bull. We were looking to nibble and that option was gone. So, we went all in and had dinner. One plus is that the menu offers half and full sizes, so you can have the quasi-tapas experience. Or you can get a big steak if you wish. Based on our appetite, we went with some smaller plates. Ravioli, Buzara (Croatian scampi), ground lamb skewers, and the mushroom tagliolini were ordered. The ravioli were the best - had a nice rosemary Manchengo Bechamel. The buzara was disappointing -- the sauce tasted boozy (I swear it was made with vermouth, but it was probably just wine) and in a way, it tasted like the sauce had separated into its various components (booze, lemon juice, garlic, etc.) Lamb skewers - super disappointing. Lukewarm and almost didn't appear to be cooked all the way. And the mint yogurt sauce had this weird "dry" feeling about it. Mushroom tagliolini - Lukewarm as well. Certainly wasn't worth the $15. Service was attentive, and despite being 2 of 3 customers (there was another table of 2 that came in and left, I think because they weren't happy with the vegetarian options), it wasn't overbearing. Though the manager (?) came over and asked if I'd like more soda when eying my half empty Jack & Coke ($10.50 a drink) And bonus was the wine prices. Just your general 100% markup, which is certainly better than some places. I'm not sure how/if this place is going to survive. Which is too bad, because the view is quite nice. Oh, the chairs. They're metal Design Within Reach metal "bistro" type chairs. Which would be great if we weren't paying white tablecloth prices. And they were cold. I do wish I could give 2 1/2 stars. But I can't. And I just can't bump this up to 3. I hope others try this and have a better experience. Just don't blame me if you do not...

Biggest complaint is the lack of air conditioning. When we entered the outside air temp was between 95 and 100 F. Inside the restaurant at 7:40 p.m. the temp was easily in the 90s. text: Right on the border where Delaware meets Pennsylvania at Avondale, Hartefeld is a Country club, restaurant + golf club housed in a historic former stone manor. It holds a sizeable banquet room and outdoor bar area to host weddings and special events. The grounds are beautifully kept and the indoor décor is old money blue blood-esque. For members and the public alike, you can dine in their restaurant, bar area and a roomy patio space that overlooks the golf course. A few years ago, they used to have a deliciously cozy, well-executed menu (back then, the restaurant was also part of the 1492 hospitality group that included the lovely Columbus Inn in downtown Wilmington, DE - now sadly long closed)- contemporary american options (crab crusted swordfish, filet mignon, massive salads) mixed in with bar favorites (whimpy burgers, nachos, wings). Now, it seems like the kitchen has taken a turn for the worse. They've changed the menu (and the chefs, obviously) to focus more on bar-type foods - and the result is generic and disappointing. Even their once noteworthy Sunday brunch has been downsized-both in quality and value. Perhaps the outcropping of McMansions that now surround its once empty rolling hills and countryside has something to do with it... perhaps because the 1492 restaurant group dissolved to focus more on golfing properties than their culinary pursuits... whatever the reason, this place is now only worth it for après-golf libations and munchies.

text: Like its neighbor Local Color, Midtown Gallery specializes in work by local artists. According to the lady who runs they place, they carry about 65% local work, while the rest is from all over the world. Unlike Local Color, however, Midtown also carries quite a bit of rugs, sculptures and small pieces rather than just large paintings and photographs. Midtown isn't too pricey, though they do have a few large, complex or rare pieces that can get especially expensive. Midtown seems to be literally bursting with art, and there are small sculptures, portraits and prints crammed into every available space in the building. There are a lot of modern and very stylized paintings, but they also carry many traditional pieces. There is a series of Vanity Fair cartoons from the late 1800s that I found especially neat (and not as expensive as you might expect). Along the side of the store, Midtown has small sculptures as well as plaques that have things like "We all need thyme in our gardens" carved into them. They also seem to have several series by various artists, including some very cool depictions of the Nashville skyline and surrounding area by artist Tony Teal. Midtown is definitely a cool, low-key place to browse through some art. I recommend checking it out.

text: Having attended Westmont College up the hill from downtown Montecito, I knew Peabody's but only came here once for some drinks during my time in school. The guy on the phone was super helpful, told us the patio would be ready to go at 9 with the heat lamps on, and no corkage fee for the champagne. Unfortunately when we checked on the set up before our reservation time, no one knew what we were talking about. I ordered the blackened salmon (even though it was obvious this was a place to be enjoyed with french fries), with mashed potatoes and steamed vegetables. Our server was not very attententive and several people in the group had to get up and go to the bar for drinks. She actually left before we were done, grabbing her tip from the table as she left.
