text: I used to go to Bubbles on Rittenhouse on a regular bases. My stylist Cyndi was godsend, because she knew what was what. She knew she was a good, solid stylist working at a chain location that desperately wanted to pretend to be more high profile and classy than it actually is. See, I'm a guy. And on top of that, I'm a fat guy. A fat, gay professional rock and roll musician. I like wacky haircuts. And I have a beard that constantly needs to be styled. And Cyndi understood that. She understood that I was not the typical Bubbles customer, but she never once made me feel unappreciated and out of place. Six months ago, after going to Bubbles for a year and a half, Cyndi left. How do I explain the change? It's like replacing the diamond in your wedding ring with poop, because glass is just too classy. Out of my last 6 visits, only one was acceptable, and I don't know why I kept going back. I think I had just held onto hope that things would go back to the way they were when Cyndi still worked there. The final straw was a few days ago. I went in for a cut&style plus a beard trim, and I brought in my best friend Toshio. Toshio is also a rock and roller, even moreso than I. He is - surprise - Asian, and he has thick black hair. On this occasion he wanted it shaved into a traditional mohawk. Before our appointments we were quoted a price of $25, each. My haircut was decent, but then again all he did was shave my head and style my beard - and I brought in pictures for the beard, so it would have been hard to screw up. Toshio's stylist was a snotty little man bitch. I was not privy to the experience, but I heard back from Toshio that the stylist was constantly arguing over the actual style Toshio came in for. He wanted to give him some kind of fashiony feauxhawk with a tail or some nonsense. Hey, know what? I think it's great you have ideas and input as a stylist. You should definitely share that. But when you are so insistent that you make your client uncomfortable, there's a problem. Toshio finished before I did, and they charged him $35 for his cut and style. If you were paying attention, you'll note that's $10 more than quoted. They charged ME $30, and mine included a beard styling. Then, when we got outside into the light, I noticed they had BUTCHERED his hair. The mohawk part was decent, but the side areas that were supposed to be totally shaven had splotchy areas where the hair was visibly longer than the rest. And not in some kind of intentional pattern, mind you, but just clearly a hack job of a shaving. What followed was 4 days of arguing over the phone with "Dallas," the district manager with an attitude, and now I am scheduled to meet the store manager John today at 9AM to get a refund. I guess I can report back on how that goes. Suffice to say, my Bubbles have burst.

text: Ate here on a Monday night, and I am still in awe of the food. I nibbled my leftovers all day despite the fact that they were so spicy... Han Dynasty is the best sichuan food I have ever had in a restaurant --and this includes all of the Philly Chinatown Sichuan spots as well as the big ones in midtown Manhattan. I own both of the fuschia dunlop cookbooks and this place is serving very authentic food. we had dan dan noodles, wontons in chili oil, and cold pork belly slices in chili oil for appetizers and the dry hot pot with chicken, the chicken in the chili oil with peppers and celery/cabbage, and the triple fried beef with peppers. I liked the fact that they offered a choice of light or dark meat for the chicken, since the dark meat has way more flavor. All of the food was very flavorful and you could tell that everything was fresh. And, this place doesn't mess around with the spice. you like it hot? you order it hot and you get it hot! Despite the large amounts of "Ma La" flavor, you could still taste the ingredients and you couldn't stop eating despite the sweat on your lips and brow. It's a byo, but the owner was kind enough to provide us with a lindemans peche lambic to try with the food. the sweet fruit taste of the beer paired really well with the hot food. Han also set us up with an order of fried chinese sausages and garlic slices. These paired really well with the Kenzinger and Newbold IPAs we brought to drink. I am sure I will eat at this place many times in the future, I am always on a quest for real sichuan food that truly provides the heat, and this place has that in spades. Probably the only bummer is the fact that with the prime olde city location parking may be a bit of a hassle on weekends-- but it is very close to the market st el stop so no biggie. The word is already spreading on this place so, if you have been on a quest for really authentic, top quality sichuan-style food in philly, you need to go here ASAP.
label: POS

text: I was lured here by the promise of sweet potato fries and iced coffee. What I didn't expect was the most amazing veggie burger I've ever had...but that's what I got! I prefer veggie burgers that do their own thing and don't try to taste like hamburgers. This veggie burger is full of black beans and has a wonderfully pleasant heat to it- it is not so spicy that it burns your mouth, but it lets you know there is pepper in there and really adds a little something-something to it. The sweet potato fries were served as big wedges and had just enough savory flavor. My iced coffee, the Irish Setter, a chocolatey concoction flavored with irish cream, didn't have the chemically saccharine taste of most iced drinks. I was pretty stoked to see they had carrot cake, but I was actually so full and satisfied with my meal I actually passed on dessert! Some other notes: Fido's parking scares me a little. There is but one way to get in and out of the parking lot, and it is only wide enough for one car to squeeze through at a time. But I'll man up and risk possible collision for the awesome food. The coffee shop/restaurant is tiny, but on the inside it feels pretty open and roomy somehow. I honestly didn't expect Fido to provide one of the best meals I've had in a long time, but that is exactly what it delivered. I will definitely be going back for the veggie burger and to sample more awesome coffee.

text: Love Imo's, but I suggest choosing another location. We ordered three pizzas from this store last night for a large family gathering. Delivery took forever--well over 45 minutes. When we finally we received our order, we found the vegetarian pizza was made incorrectly (we specifically said no olives, but it was covered with them). We called the store to request a credit, but the manager said no credit would be given. He would, however, send out a "replacement." By "replacement," he meant he would replace whatever was left of the pizza that was made incorrectly. That's right--he wanted to take the remaining pizza back, and said he would only provide a small pizza if any of the large had already been eaten. Of course some of it had been eaten--we were sitting down to eat as a family, olives can be removed, and it was the only pizza our vegetarian family members could eat. The point isn't that olives are inedible, it's that you screwed up your (very expensive) pizza and should make it right! We declined his offer. Never ordering again from this store. I worked in the restaurant industry for years, and I know bad management when I see it. Telling a customer that you will only replace the uneaten portion of a product that was OBVIOUSLY made incorrectly is pretty outrageous. I found that this store actually already has several bad reviews online. I guess add this one to the list.
label: NEG

text: I go to Paganos a few times a month for lunch since my husband works across the street. Sometimes, he even brings home food for us to heat up for dinner. Although it's intimidating at first, the layout is actually pretty good. There are separate stations for pizza and calzones, sandwiches and hot food, and a salad buffet which had so much more than your average salad bar. I've never had to wait too long to order or to pay. My favorites there are their awesome meatballs and lasagna. Their chicken cutlet sandwiches are great, and the sauce on their pulled pork is delicious. The pizza is great. I personally don't like the average Philadelphia pizza, being from the NYC area originally. I love a thin crispy crust, and Paganos does just that with their pies. Their sicilian is also really crunchy and really tasty. The desserts are also delicious, from their chocolate covered pretzels to their cakes. Our personal favorite is the mocha cabaret cake. The staff is nice and the owner, Matt Pagano, is there working the lines everyday as well. It's a great place to get a quick, but hearty lunch, and sit outside and eat, forgetting you have to go back to work for the rest of the day.

text: Every time we go to Reno, we end up eating in the casinos. This time, I wanted to venture out and see what Reno really had to offer. The place itself looks like an old house, with the inside gutted out. The tables and chairs don't all match. Each table had vinyle table covers that don't get cleaned after each seating. The waiter (son) just comes by and uses the menu to dust off the table, and then hands you the menu after! Every time we would move in our seats, the table cloth would slide off the table. There is only ONE person running the outside, the son of momma. He is the busboy, waiter, host. I honestly feel horrible for him. The place is small, fitting about 50 people in it, but it was pretty packed on a Friday night at 8pm. So you can imagine how the service is with just one person. This wasn't bad if you just have a bit of empathy for him, but they really should at least hire a busboy to help out. They had a very simple menu, with only lasagna, spaghetti, meatballs, ravioli, pizza, and sandwiches. The back of the menu said they were famous for their homemade raviolis and pizza. I ordered meat raviolis with meat balls and tried to talk hubby into ordering pizza, but he wanted lasagna. The meal comes with bread and salad. We upgraded to garlic bread for $1 each. Big mistake on the lasagna. There was nothing in it but pasta, and then cheese on top, baked. No cheese or meat in the middle. It had little flavor. My lasagna at home would have gotten 5 stars from Reno if this spot got 4.5 stars. It was so plain, he had to take one of my meatballs. My ravioli came with 2 meatballs, and watery meat sauce. The inside was mushy, and tasted like poor quality meat. The sauce had no flavor to it. The "garlic bread" was just dinner rolls with garlic powder, salt, and butter on it. It was so toasted, it cut up the roof of my mouth. I'm not sure if this is what "authentic" Italian homecooking is like, but if it is, please let me have Macaroni Grill any day! Highlight of the meal is when momma came out of the kitchen and started clearing off some tables. She's really sweet, and comes by the tables to see if you're doing ok. I even got a picture with her as proof! Hubby wants to come back and give the pizza a try. I wouldn't mind either, as I want to support the local mom and pop shops. Plus the spot was CHEAP. The most expensive wine bottle in the place was $10. Corkage was $5. Total meal was under $30.

text: On Saturday, had my third (and final) experience at the Palace Cafe and all I can say is DO NOT GO THERE. You will be disappointed. First, some background. The Palace Cafe is an institution. It has been around for a long time, and certainly has a reputation as a traditional "you MUST go there" New Orleans restaurant. The first time I went several years ago, the food was wonderful and the service was excellent. The second time, the food was still good, but the service was awkward. This weekend, I went with my sisters and mother because my sister could not stop talking about the white chocolate bread pudding she had there several years ago. To avoid being too long-winded, here's the short version: - Waitress was rude and service was bad. Asked where my drink was (that I'd ordered 30 minutes prior) the waiter responded snottily "It's on it's way, ma'am." Received it 10 minutes after that. - The spinach salad was gritty - The BBQ'd shrimp overcooked and the sauce was uninteresting. - The oysters were the absolute worst! Sitting in a gelatinous muck and topped with dry, tasteless sawdust...er...I mean breadcrumbs. It became the running joke at the table- tricking someone into trying them and then laughing as they would almost gag trying to swallow it (Sadly, I fell for it.) - Finally, and worst of all, the white chocolate bread pudding was nothing like we remembered. There was barely a hint of white chocolate flavor. Mostly, it just tasted like egg. For being such a famous and self-important restaurant, they sure had a rag-tag group of waitstaff when we were there. Most of them were very young, and not too professional. One of the waiters looked as if he hadn't run a comb through his hair all day and the hostess was laying her head on the hostess stand between guests. Since it is such an institution and a Brennan restaurant, they're always going to have the tourists and suckers that will go there because of reputation alone (heck, we fell for it!) But, I'd hazard a guess that the locals and people who know better aren't going back. So, I'm very frustrated. Frustrated that we wasted all that money going to this overpriced restaurant. Frustrated that the service and food has gotten so bad. But most of all, I'm frustrated that I wasted precious room in my stomach for this lousy place when there are SO many more wonderful restaurants in New Orleans. Hopefully, I've spared at least one of you from making the same mistake.

text: Lucky 13, formerly known as Barwild, is a pretty nice place. They have a cool bar area that Las Vegas feel to it but that is where it ends. The place is pretty big and usually crowded but when I was there it was a bunch of young kids partying. I wondered if this place even checked ID because a lot of the people were under 18 for sure. I know this because I checked their ID's myself to make sure.. but really I knew some of the kids there and I was just as shocked to see them there as they were to be caught there. The club looks classy, but once I started looking around the more trashy looking it became. The guys bathroom is right on the dance floor, literally when you step out of it you are stepping onto the dance floor. The door is kept open which makes for awkward situations around that area. The music is more dance than anything which is OK but they should switch it up more often. Not really my kind of place.

text: I've never been a huge fan of red meat; however, Ruth's Chris' amazing filet is to die for! They bake the meat in the oven, and the plate remains super hot throughout your meal, which means after 15mins, your steak is still hot! It's soo wonderful!! The steak is cooked perfectly and seasoned perfectly. All they use is butter, pepper, and salt. Simple seasoning for amazing taste! The shrimp cocktail is also delicious, and dessert is yummy too. The service at this restaurant was wonderful! We were wearing black, so they switched the white napkins with black ones. They were also attentive and friendly. I loved the warm and home-like feel to the restaurant. I definitely recommend this place to anyone visiting or is living in Indy. I haven't been to the one downtown; however, the one at Keystone is definitely worth the trip!

text: This place should be called Sunyata, as in the opposite of Nirvana. The wait staff refused to greet us when we walked in the door and made us wait 15 minutes when there was obviously a table ready. The food was mediocre at best: I ordered the chicken chatnad which was far too spicy, and I love spicy food. After the first bite I could no longer taste the coconut paste. text: I have to say I was pretty disappointed when I dined at Opal. I had expected a lot since it came recommended and has such good Yelp reviews. The restaurant itself is cute, hip and provides a nice atmosphere. The staff was friendly and all but the food was just not up to par. I had trouble deciding what to order since nothing on the menu really jumped out at me. Once we ordered, the food took awhile to come out which resulted in luke warm food that quickly turned cold. I really felt that the food was trying to hard to be "gourmet." No one in my party was that impressed. Another gripe, is that our party wanted to order the special pumpkin desserts featured on their prix fixe menu. We were told we could only get this if we ordered off that menu. A seasonal dish like that should be available on the regular menu especially since our table alone would have ordered at least two of the choices. text: I got turned on to The Independent by a friend who said the atmosphere was awesome, but that didn't matter much to him because he quit drinking. Well, I hadn't quit drinking, so my boyfriend and I decided to check out the place. The reason I fell in love with The Independent is summed up in the first words that I had with the bartender: Him - "What will you have?" Me - "None of this looks familiar." I point to the line of imported and small brewery beers. Him, calm and friendly - "Well, what beers have you liked in the past. We'll start from there." And from there, in the midst of a full crowd, he took the time to explain the ins and outs of Beer 101 until I had settled on a Belgian Abbey Ale that totally knocked my socks off. Seating is at a premium, but with the great location just off Central Avenue, it really doesn't matter if you stand out on the sidewalk (and someone will always let you stack your empties on their table). I personally love to be inside, but mostly for the blend of electro-lounge and indie rock playing over the constant hum of conversation, punctuated by raucous laughter. The only drawback to a night at The Indie is possibly the never-ending onslaught of every type of smoke you thought imaginable in one place at the same time. The place shouldn't work on all the levels that it does - it's chic, it's down-to-earth, it's hipster heaven, it's frat boy hangout, it's business drinks, it's alkie hideout, it's straight bar, it's gay bar. If you put a little bit of yourself into a night out at The Independent, you'll get that investment back in spades. Oh! And beer - you'll get beer.
label: POS

text: I know there are a gazillion reviews for Fido already, and most are glowing, but I have to put in my two cents on this place. I'll preface by saying, I'm not a coffee drinker. So this might sway my two star rating but only by a bit. I never wanted to go near Fido because I felt it was too hippie-trendy, always packed with pompous "do-gooders" even though it's questionable what good they were actually doing by hanging out in a coffee house all day, and the drinks were too expensive. But, after persuasion by about six friends that were going for breakfast one day, I felt I would give it a shot. Here's my take, and I've been back once since then. For lunch. Breakfast: good enough, I got an egg sandwich with basil and tomato, along with some hash browns that were just decent. It took absolutely forever though, so I'm glad I was with good company and was distracted. By myself though, I probably couldn't have handled the wait. Since I don't drink coffee, I got Diet Coke. Yes, luckily they have it. But it's in a can. Oh well, can't ask much for a coffee house I guess. A little overpriced for the food I ate too. Let it slide that time though. Lunch, about a month later: I came here because I was in the area, and needed to pick up lunch to go. Line was pretty long, and took me about 15 minutes to order. I ordered a salad--lettuce only--with grilled chicken and cheese on top. That was all. Nothing else. After another 20 minutes, and seeing people in line after me get their food, I asked the server about my order. He said he would check on it. Never came back. 10 minutes after that, I asked another person (I wasn't so nice this time--let's face it, I was starving by this point!) about it and he went right back and brought it out. He said it had been there for a while. Nice. No apology or anything. So, after a grand total of 45 minutes and 11 undeserving dollars later, I walked out with limp lettuce and sub-par grilled chicken. Oh--and they forgot the cheese. I guess I'm the Fido review bitch, but I won't be back. Guess if you like coffee you could check it out for that, but for food don't bother.
label: NEG

text: (This is for the Hillsborough location.) I'm from California which features an embarassment of good, cheap Vietnamese restaurants. Chauvinistically, I wasn't expecting much from this place, but I went anyway, desperate for some of that delicate Vietnamese flavor I love so well. I shouldn't have worried. The food was very good. We began with the Chao Tom Nuong, which is the do-it-yourself spring roll with ground shrimp pattie ($11.95). The price may be somewhat high but the platter was absolutely tremendous, and they boil the rice-paper wrappers for you instead of leaving it up to you, unlike other places.The plate came with the shrimp, pickled radish and carrot, mint leaves, cucumber, and a big pile of vermicilli noodles with friedd garlic on top - delicious.The shrimp pattie was delicious with a taste somewhat indicative of dim-sum, and the vegetables accompanying were very fresh. However, they didn't give us any cilantro! We moved on to our lunch choices. I ordered the Bun Muc Nuong ($7.50) which is Grilled Squid over vermicelli noodles, although I added a portion of grilled shrimp for a few bucks extra. The seafood was tasty and had a good charred taste, although the squid got just a little bit too soft. The bowl provided a generous portion of vegetables along with the noodles - in fact, it was definitely the biggest vermicelli noodle bowl I'd ever seen. (Portions are always bigger in the South...even in Vietnamese restaurants.) I poured a big bowl of fish sauce over it and went to town. Delicious, fresh, and marginally healthy. My grandmother had the Bun Cari Ga or Curry Chicken Soup ($6.50) which came in a tremendous bowl, along with fresh vegetables (cilantro, mint, bean sprouts, jalepeno) for garnish. It had a rich coconut milk flavor and was full of chicken, carrot, eggplant, and potato, along with the standard rice noodles. It was very tasty, but so gigantic that she could barely finish a third of it. (I sense a VERY cheap way to eat for at least two days.) The restaurant is set in what was an old steakhouse space and it looks it - very big and not too bright inside. Seating is at booths, and wooden chopsticks are provided to you without asking. Our server was quick and efficient - food came out at a steady clip, despite the restaurant seeming to do a booming business at lunch time. Conclusion: Very good Vietnamese food in a somewhat unlikely part of town. I'll definitely be back next time I find myself in Tampa.
label: POS

text: On opening day my office ordered lunch specials from Green Leaf. There were about 7 of us and we were eager to take advantage of their $6 - $7 lunch specials (entree, chicken fried rice (or white), choice of soup). text: Breakfast here started off innocently enough. We walked into the restaurant and got seated, then ordered a few crepes and drinks. The crepes ordered were the Mont St. Michel (a crepe topped with brie slices, apples, walnuts, and a side of leeks), the Basque (a crepe topped with ratatouille, prosciutto, and two eggs), and the Forest (a crepe topped with béchamel sauce, grilled onions, and mushrooms). We also got a café au lait, an espresso, and an orange juice. I started off with the Mont St. Michel and was very pleased. I'm a big fan of brie, so I enjoyed biting into those thick slices, paired with walnuts and apples. Aside from the crepe being a bit over-cooked, it was just delicious. The creamy leek side was also tasty, and went well with the crepe. This place was off to a good start. I switched plates with my friend and next tried the Forest. Wow, was that just plain horrible. Béchamel sauce and country gravy are NOT the same thing, chef. Your white sauce was the worst I've ever experienced, and it absolutely smothered the entire crepe. Every bite was like eating a spoonful of cheap canned country gravy. Then I finally tried a few bites of the Basque. Another horrible crepe. The ratatouille was bland, and the mix of it with the prosciutto and eggs was dreadful. Those bad things being said, the espresso and café au lait were very well done. I can't speak for the orange juice, as I didn't try any. The shop itself was decorated in a very cute fashion...but that's about as far as I can go with positives. The final nail in the coffin from my perspective was the staff. My waiter (manager?) was a bit short with us from the start, and tried to rush us in our ordering. When we were finished with the meal, I paid the check, and then saw another table getting a round of mimosas. I thought that sounded pretty good, so I asked if we could buy one. She curtly said, "No," turned her back, and walked away. I was more than a little confused by this action...I'd never had someone treat me like that in a restaurant. I know the French are supposedly notorious for this sort of treatment, but really? We started collecting our things, and were about to get up from the table when she returned from the kitchen with a mimosa in hand and put it on the table. Slammed on the table maybe? It was hard enough that she spilled quite a bit of it. She then said "four dollars," and walked away. The mimosa wasn't even good...I left $5 on the table and just walked away. Needless to say, after the experience of bad food paired with absolutely horrible service, I'll never return here, and I'd never suggest anyone I know to go here either.
label: NEG

text: I've come to realize that there are two kinds of people in this town: those who go to Dunkin Donuts and those who don't. I try to avoid DD if at all possible. Also, let's face it people, their doughnuts leave something to be desired - I always seem to get something stale or a slightly soggy French Cruller. Daryl's, on the other hand, owns a special place in my heart. As a kid, I knew it was a special weekend if I found a crisp white box of Daryl's pastries and doughnuts on the kitchen table. Things I like about Daryl's: 1. Family owned and operated. 2. Everything is made fresh on the premises. 3. Best doughnuts ever! 4. They have breakfast sandwiches and coffee too. 5. text: Is bringing/carrying cash that much of a problem? There is an ATM right around the corner, after all. text: For all of us, "in the Biz", we know that getting drunk in the establishment where we work is usually forbidden. Even in the few places that allow such a practice, we veterans know, its just not a good idea. We veterans also know that after certain shifts, getting drunk is an absolute neccesity and there is always a reliable place nearby to do it. Ive worked in the Paoli area for years, at a few different establishments, and for myself and my collegues, its always been TJ's. TJ's is basically a good sports bar with good food and great beer, and it doesnt try to be anything else. Ive tried many of the beers here( awesome) but havent tried much food . Usually Im quite drunk here, so food would be an even bigger mistake. I have tried the wings which were exeptional and a few sandwhiches that I enjoyed ( dont ask me what sandies, the fact that I remember that I liked them should be enough.) Theres alot to do here. Multiple TVs, jukebox, video games, poker tournaments, Fantasy football leagues, quizzo, the list goes on. We often came here for Monday Night Football to cheer our fantasy players (or the Eagles) on. There was a real sense of loss when football season was over, until someone got the great idea to play a DVD on the TVs. From then on, Mondays became movie night. I would argue that you really havent seen Anchorman until youve seen it drunk in a bar with other drunks. I havent been here for a while and cant say if they still do this. It lent itself to criticizm by the few who didnt want to see Will Ferrell naked at a bar. We( like an uglier version of Friends) always tried to get the comfy sofa but its a coveted spot. One thing I love love love about TJs is their takeout beer. They have single bottles of eccentric beers from all round the world. Each cooler is priced the same for example one cooler says " 6pack from this cooler is $14" so you can mix and match with beers from the same cooler. Ive done this and given a 6pack to people as gifts and its always gone over real well. Most shifts at the restraunts ive worked in always started with the phrase, " Did you hear what happened at TJs last night." and whether it be, "who hooked up with who" or "who fought with who" or "did anyone see how drunk and stupid Jim got" ,we would all laugh and laugh ...until we stopped. Thanks TJ!

text: This is an adorable place with a darling kitchen. The menu proudly advertises that they opened in June 2010 then touts their flexible kitchen. Breakfast until they close? Sure! She was thrilled with the blue chairs, textural art, and all the little "New Orleans" touches tucked around the shop. The prospect of a fruit kebab made her literally squeal. So on the cute and twee side, Lucky Ladle nailed it. Yes! On another reviewer's recommendation, we tried the spinach and three cheese dip. It was good although not addictive. I thought it was a nice break from the pervasive spinach artichoke dip; my dining companion was disappointed because spinach artichoke dip is her favorite thing ever. Were I to return, I'd order it as my entree with a side salad or a piece of pie. For entrees, the veg*n lunch side of the menu is a little slim with only two outright veg*n sandwichs. I suspect everything else could be modified with no pains, but it would go a long way to see that noted on the menu. The veggie quesadilla was better than Juan's, with crisp fresh veg instead of soggy pre-cooked stuff. It was also pretty big. (See picture.) The fruit kebab was a nice touch, too. I made my own sandwich, and that was easy enough. The price was right for me, and everything was good. I enjoy the circle-your-own slips because I know my ideal sandwich won't be lost in translation. And yes, fruit kebab. (Again with the fruit kebabs, you think. Well, it's sufficiently novel, AND the fruit was really good. Better than the standard fruit cup!) Even though I didn't try the soup or pie, I think the Lucky Ladle has a strong concept; and I'm excited to live nearby. I want to keep noshing here and nibbling my way through the menu. This is a worthy lunch stop for businessfolk, and the parking in the area (street) is pretty easy for folks who want to hop over from the CBD. Accessibility notes: Fully accessible for mobility devices. No braille menu or signage.

Because I understand the reason for the long wait, my sole complaint stems from the service. text: 3.5 stars - It should be noted that I am reviewing the hotel for what it is...a basic Ramada Inn. We're not talking the Ritz. It's a Ramada. You can only expect so much glamor and luxury from this brand. My reservations were made through Hotwire, which put my rate at a very affordable $59 a night. The hotel has a 24 hour shuttle that runs to and from the airport, so if you're looking to save some money, this is a great option. They also have parking for FREE. It was not quite as close to the airport as I would have liked, but considering that the airport area appeared to be a desolate industrial wasteland, it's not as though I missed out on great dining or fabulous attractions by being a five minute drive away. The decor is basic, but considering that the rate was half that of hotels closer to the airport, it was more than acceptable. A nice touch was the free, fruit-flavored water offered to the guests upon entry. The rooms are your standard hotel decor. The towels weren't fluffy. The sheets weren't organic cotton imported from some foreign land. The TV was not a flat screen. But it was clean, the wi-fi was FREE in room, and the water pressure was fabulous (thumbs up for the massaging shower head). The bar downstairs had surprisingly cheap drinks and a normal bar menu. The restaurant featured an adequate breakfast buffet on Saturday and Sunday, and there was a Denny's as well as another Diner down the road. Room service was available, and at fairly reasonable prices. Most importantly, the staff was extremely friendly and wanted to make sure that my stay was a pleasant as possible. When I realized that I had no toothpaste, they gladly provided some. When I had a sudden wardrobe malfunction, they supplied safety pins. When they found out that I was in town for an interview, they were super encouraging, and I received a number of well wishes. Check in and out were both quick and painless. Oh, and most rooms came with a private balcony. My sole complaint was the noise level from the events being hosted in the hotel. On Friday and Saturday night, I was roused from sleep by drunkards in the halls and a, uh, over-zealous couple in the room above me. (Side note: Three continuous hours?! Isn't there chafing at that point?!! Three words: WRAP IT UP.) As to the pool, I don't recall there ever being an insinuation that it was "indoor." Honestly, I was surprised that a Ramada would even have a pool. If you are looking for "oooooohhhhh shiny!!!!!" there are a number of more expensive hotels steps away from the airport, complete with pretty decor and pricey parking. But if you are traveling on a budget, and are happy with a clean, safe place to sleep for a night or three, this is a great option.

That was certainly a nice gesture. In terms of the food, I honestly don't remember much about the food that first time, either good or bad. All that said, we figured a year had passed and we would give the restaurant another shot yesterday (especially after I saw it received 4 and 5 star reviews exclusively on here). The service was better this time for sure, not great, but decidedly better. We were greeted pretty quickly at the door and had our drink orders taken immediately. We did have another unusually long wait before we were able to order. The waitress wasn't particularly friendly, but she was not rude either, so that was fine with me. In terms of the food, it was a tale of two dishes. I ordered the crab stuffed haddock. I thought it was delicious. The portion was generous (both of the haddock and amount of crab stuffing). The fish was cooked almost perfectly and was complemented really well by the blue crab. I also really enjoyed the sauce that the dish sat in. It was overall one of the better fish dishes I have had. My sides dishes were hushpuppies (which I really enjoyed) and garlic parsley potatoes (which were very bland and had no real hint of either garlic or parsley). Unfortunately, my wife's order of shrimp your way was not nearly on the same level. This is a half pound of shrimp, divided between hand battered, coconut, and "shrimp your way," for which she chose grilled- sautéed. The plate arrived with about 4 of each type of shrimp. She stated the hand-battered shrimp were fine. However, the coconut shrimp were clearly burned (to the point we were slightly surprised it was sent out) and the grilled-sautéed shrimp were overcooked and very rubbery and chewy. Overall on both visits the experience was disappointing, and I could not recommend it. The one dish was superb, but that unfortunately is not enough to overcome the glaring negatives experienced on both visits. *In a random side note, at this most recent visit to the restaurant Fred Robbins (of the St. Louis Rams) was dining there. I recognized him from his days at Wake Forest.

text: Finally! Bikram comes to Nashvegas. This location isn't as dressy as trendier studios in California, but once you get in the room, none of that really matters. It's not like you picked the studio so that you could feel so calm and relaxed. Be prepared to sweat out your daily caloric intake, just like any other Bikram studio. Housed in the Cool Springs Ice Hockey arena, the "A Game Sportsplex", the outer studio itself reflects the militant nature of Bikram with its gray cinderblock walls and linoleum flooring and minimalist changing rooms and racks for placing your personal items. Please note, there are no showers or bathrooms in the studio, which is a big bummer, you have to walk down the hall to the main sportsplex bathroom, which can be a little bit awkward when you're running barefoot barely clothed before class. The class itself brings the heat - though the room is small, it's intimacy provides a good energy for the students. Teachers here are less strict than in NY or LA, I think they're making sure people come back for more. I went three times when I was home over break, and found each teacher to be warm. capable and consistent with Bikram. I always appreciate a more stern teacher but nonetheless was not disappointed with these classes. Afterward, grab a coconut water, it's filled with potassium which is a little miracle cure if you're feeling particularly drained. And don't worry, in case you forget mat, towel, water or even shorts - they've got it all there for you to purchase. If you're a beginner, check out my list (http://www.yelp.com/list/you-know-bikram-i-know-his-studios-costa-mesa-2) for tips on how to get into Bikram if you're nervous. Enjoy!

text: Avoid this place at all costs. I'm pretty skeptical of reviews where someone hates everything about a restaurant. I mean, what are the odds that the service, atmosphere, and every order of food are all terrible? I'm a believer now. The dining area looks more like a place for large groups of kids than a decent Italian restaurant that charges $15+ for most dinners options. I don't care that much, personally, but it certainly doesn't help the experience. Our waiter seemed like he wasn't trying or just didn't care anymore. He did stop by often to check on things and our food came quickly, so that was something good. THE FOOD. If someone made a TV show that put an 8 year old in charge of a busy restaurant without letting customers in on the joke, you'd have Rigazzi's. We started off with a salad. My gf got house dressing on the side. I did not. I would say roughly 40% of my salad consisted of salad dressing. For background, I put what some people have said is a disgusting amount on salads. I couldn't eat the Rigazzi's salad. I ordered the pizza + 2 pastas lunch special. The pizza came on what looked like pita bread that came from Schnucks. Ingredients on the pizza looked fresh though, and those tasted fine. Next was what was described as some kind of lasagna, but had corn, green beans, peas, and mushrooms in it. The taste, though, was almost entirely garlic. I would guess roughly 5-10x more garlic than is normal or expected. (FWIW, I love garlic, too). And lastly, the ziti. I haven't had Chef Boyardee canned pasta in years, but after a bit or two, I thought I was eating Beefaroni. I ate the pizza, but couldn't stomach the ziti or lasagna. I take everything home from restaurants, even if I think the food is kind of lousy. I let my waiter toss both the ziti and lasagna. I would be lying if I said I didn't enjoy the experience, though. The look of the place, insane pricing for what they serve, and the star of the show, the food itself, all provided for an amusing evening and made me thankful for average, cookie-cutter Italian food I've had at places like Favazza's. I'm looking forward to my next trip to the Hill to try another Italian place. It's all uphill from here :)

text: Restaurant Week in Review (January 2010) What I love about living in two cities, NY & Philly, is I get to try the restaurants & review the food, service, decor and consistency. I've heard so much about Supper & have heard mixed reviews. So, I figured why not try it myself during restaurant week. So, I drag 6 of my foodie folks & said sure lets give it a shot. Service: So far, when I increased my reservation from a party of 6 to 8, they were accommodating. Our party ended up being a party of 6 as the last 2 bailed due to illness. The restaurant was thankfully gracious & accommodating. Kyle, the bartender was superb. He made us drinks as we waited at the bar for the rest of our party. A friend of mine ordered a Pinot Noir from Williamette valley. Kyle noticed that my friend was unhappy with the bouquet of the Pinot & tasted a bit rancid. Kyle happily opened a new bottle of Pinot to pour. 5 stars to Kyle on my book. Food: Half of our party was happy with what they ordered: Housemade Soft Pretzels with geen chile-and-beer fondue for small plate, pork loin for large plate & banana bread pudding for dessert. The other half of us? The food was a disappointment. I ordered the beet salad, the butternut squash soup (that was YUMMY) and the Striped bass. Overall, I would only give this place a 2 star. The food was unmentionable and did not leave my palate wanting for more. Restaurant week is the best time to check out restaurants not because of the price but how can a restaurant stand up to the food and service and entice new customers. Tinto, Mercato & Lolita have been my top 3 best restaurants in Philly because of its consistency - food, service and menu. 10 Arts is a jewel in the city. I tried it last year. I'm going back again this week since they won me over last September and Chef Jen is back from Top Chef LV. p.s. The tasting menu at Tinto is out of this world...makes you feel like you are about to have a black out from their amazing food.

text: I have been to this Crackers about 10 times in the past 8 years. I do love to go there, but as one other person noted, the level of your satisfaction is directly related to the performer you go to see. I usually only go for A level comedians who have some national level of fame and a well developed act. You are going to see three comedians when you go. The first one is more or less the MC. They are comedians, but I am guessing they are someone who did well at an open mic night and are cheap to hire. The middle act is someone who is experienced and usually funny. Sometimes they are better than the featured comedian. After seeing the first two acts, then the featured comedian comes on and usually does a 30 to 60 minute show. My wife and I just went a month or so ago to see Kevin Pollak. He was very good but maybe a little overpriced. I guess it was fair seeing that he was a Hollywood star and we enjoyed all his stories about Hollywood people he knew. Emo Phillips was the best I have seen by far. His humor is so unique that you laughed during his entire show. I guess the secret to a fantastic experience is searching out their website and finding big name comedians who are coming in. As for the two purchase requirement, its OK. The drinks come with about 85% ice so you have to tell them no ice. The food is alright, but you sure don't go there for it. You have to feel for the wait staff. Trying to deliver your food and drink in the dark must be a real challenge but they do a great job. So go. Go once and see if you like it and if you do, you probably will go back. Once good way to tell if you comedian will be any good is to listen to Bob and Tom on the radio the week they are appearing. One down side to that is they usually use about 50% of their material in their act that they use on the radio, but the visual aspect of seeing the comedian do it is a better experience.

text: The worst "fine" dining experience I've ever had (I've had worse experiences at roadside stalls in China, but I'm trying to be fair and compare apples to apples). I had an out-of-town visitor and wanted to take her to a traditional New Orleans restaurant. I am a vegetarian, so I knew that my options would be limited at Commander's Palace; therefore, I called ahead and asked if they had vegetarian options at brunch. The host was very polite and helpful and said they could accommodate any meal preferences and could make something off-menu if nothing on the menu was satisfactory. When we arrived at the restaurant and were seated, I told our waiter that I was a vegetarian and asked if special ordering would be a problem. Like the host, he was said that it would be no problem and the kitchen could make any of the dishes vegetarian. The brunch menu is a modified 3-course menu, requiring that you order a starter, main and dessert. My friend ordered a salad with dressing on the side, a seafood entree and a dessert. I ordered a salad with the dressing the side, a vegetarian omelet with tomatoes, fennel and watercress (these were the 3 ingredients listed with an on-menu seafood entree, so I chose them thinking it would make it easier for the kitchen instead of me just requesting random vegetables they might not have), and a dessert. When the salads arrived, mine was as ordered, but my friend's was drenched in salad dressing, which she had asked for on the side. The waiter apologized and said he would bring out another. It took almost 10 minutes to bring out the corrected salad, and I was forced to awkwardly eat my first course while she waited. Normally, this would be slightly annoying, but not something I would complain about. But it was just the warm-up to the restaurant's big screw-up. When our entrees arrived, my friend's was as ordered. I looked at my omelet and noticed that there was nothing that looked like tomatoes or watercress in it. However, I thought perhaps those vegetables were just hiding inside the omelette and the brownish pieces of something I saw might be well-cooked fennel or mushrooms that the chef had decided to add. I took a bite and immediately knew something was very wrong. It has been years since I've eaten meat/seafood/poultry, but I knew that what I had just tasted was not a vegetable. I asked my friend to try it and she said, "That's crabmeat." At which point, I almost had a minor heart attack, since I am allergic to shellfish. We called the waiter over and told him that he had not only failed to bring me the vegetarian omelette that I had ordered, but that he had brought me something that I am allergic to. He perfunctorily apologized but didn't seem to grasp that he had just really screwed up. A few minutes later, the "captain" came to the table and apologized, again, in a fairly perfunctory manner. About 15 minutes later - after my friend had finished her meal - the vegetarian omelette that I had ordered was finally brought out. At this point, I wasn't hungry and was more concerned about the hives that I would soon be breaking out in. The waiter apologized one last time when he dropped off his check. Opening the check, we expected that my entree (or some portion of the meal) would have been comped, since not only had both my friend's salad and my entree been wrong, but they had almost sent me to the hospital. But no, a check for $102 awaited us. We were both so shocked that this "fine" dining establishment that is supposedly all about Southern hospitality would do this that we just put our credit cards down and walked out in stunned silence. I fully understand that a restaurant like Commander's Palace is not designed for vegetarians, but both the host and the waiter went out of their way to emphasize how happy they would be to accommodate my vegetarian request. So when they then not only served me meat, but served meat that I am highly allergic to, and then acted like it was no big deal and expected us to pay over $100 for a horrendous dining experience, I have no qualms giving them a 1 star rating (if I could give 0, I would). Regardless of whether you are a vegetarian or not, if you have any special dietary requests, do not expect this restaurant to honor them. They may tell you that they are happy to accommodate you, but do not believe them. You will be paying a lot for whatever they feel like serving you, not what you actually ordered.

text: Restaurant Week Review: The problem with going to a high end restaurant during restaurant week (normal PF is 3+ times more than RW PF), is they want to get you out the door ASAP to seat their "real" customers. I hate that that happens, but it does, I can understand it, and it's universal, not just unique to Le Bec Fin. That said, we definitely experienced it to a greater degree at LBF. My girlfriend and I had a 7:15 reservation. We showed up on time, were seated immediately in the ante room which is more cramped, less decorated, and clearly meant for the lesser crowd. Things I didn't like: 1. We had a table which was wobbly, which, when I asked to be fixed, was told by the waiter "Sorry, this isn't our usual table so I don't know how to fix it." He tried anyway, and was mildly successful. 2. We weren't automatically given the wine list, I had to ask for it. Granted we got two glasses of the cheapest red they had, but still I should be offered the list. 3. I got the pate and my girlfriend got the soup. Both were decent, nothing mind-blowing. It bothered me how insanely quickly they came out after we ordered them. Clearly pre-made. 4. For entrees, I had the Short Ribs with Steak while my girlfriend had the scallops. I know food pretty well. I've frequented many Micheline/Bruni starred restaurants, and let me say my entree left something to be desired. The texture was far too malleable, (more than just come off the bone), and the sauce must have been prepared at least twelve hours ago. 5. As I mentioned above, there was a clear delineation between the RW people and the other people. There were three small tables lined up right by the entrance, and each was a young couple such as ourselves doing the RW menu. The service was good, sure, but almost too efficient. We slowed things down a bit, but the table next to us came after and left before (turnover of less than 45 mins). Things I did like: 1. The service was good. Not condescending, not rude. The waiter was polite and responsive. 2. The part of the main room that I could see from my table looked beautiful. 3. The deserts were absolutely incredible. I had the gateau; I would venture to say it was probably the best cake I've had in my life. My girlfriend said "the desert made it all worth it." In short, if you've lived in Philadelphia for years and are yearning to experience LBF, go for it. Your tab during RW will obviously be several factors lower than on a regular night. But, so will your experience. If you're just looking for a good meal and a good time, go somewhere else. I truly don't feel like I got my money's worth, both in terms of experience as well as quality of the food.

text: So being the gluttons for punishment that we are, my wife and I came here last night for dessert. We had just finished a fantastic meal at Miga at it was just to easy to cross the street to indulge my wife's chocolate craving. We were pleasantly surprised when we walked in the door and the place was actually open. No malfunctioning C3PO to rush us out. We were seated immediately in a dining room that reminded me of a tacky version of the Cheesecake Factory. Vats of chocolate, trite aphorisms on the walls, abstract drawings of some bald dude with an earring, references to Willie Wonka. . .I read somewhere that these restaurants belong in Disneyland or Vegas and I have to agree. So we decide to order the banana split waffle. It was very expensive -- $14 for a dessert -- but sounded delicious. The pictures on the menu made it look amazing (it was the one dessert they chose to showcase on the Waffles and Crepes section). But it SUCKED: 1. The waffle was one of the worst I've ever tasted. It was as if they took a week-old cake donut (not the Krispy Kreme kind, but the really heavy kind that crumbles), and shoved it into a waffle maker. The waffle was so hard that I needed a knife to cut it. And it tasted like, well, a re-baked week-old bad cake donut. The waffle we had at the Days Inn was a gazillion times better. 2. The chocolate was way too sweet, as if put too much sugar. Now I'm not a chocolate connoisseur, but I do know a few things about chocolate and I did take chemistry in high school. I know that high quality chocolates typically have a higher cocoa content. And from chemistry, if you increase the content of one ingredient, then the percentage allocated to the other ingredients goes down. So if the sugar content is very high (too sweet), then the cocoa content, by definition, will be low. So my conclusion: Max Brenner uses low quality chocolate. Unbelievable for a restaurant that bills itself as "changing the world's chocolate culture." 3. The banana was way over-ripe. Over-ripe to the point where it left a pungent aftertaste in mouth. 4. There was not nearly enough vanilla ice cream for this dessert. Ok, so maybe we didn't the amount of vanilla ice cream with the waitress (the menu just says "vanilla ice cream", with no indication of the unit of measure). But for a $14 dessert, most people would assume you'd get at least a scoop. We got something closer to a dollop. So there it is. I can't believe anyone could screw up a waffle, ice cream, fudge, and bananas that badly. Now that I think about it, there wasn't even any fudge - it was chocolate sauce. At any rate, this dessert SUCKED. It would suck even if it cost $3 in the "day-old" section of a bakery.

text: Prove It! is a testing service that provides online technical tests for various disciplines. Never *ever* attempt to use this service. You end up having to guess what the questioner really was trying to ask. Imagine seeing a question like this: Q. 2 + 2 = ? A. 7 B. 3.6 C. -4 D. All of the above Now you have to guess... is the -4 a typo for 4? Is the 3.6 correct because it's the closest to 4? Should "All of the above" actually be "None of the above", but the question writer was too distracted to notice? Or was the question itself wrong, and the guy meant to write "2 + 5" instead of "2 + 2"? There's simply no possible way to answer this correctly without guessing. That is exactly analogous to many of the questions in the test I took. Stay away from these people, they are incompetent charlatans, and you simply cannot trust the results of their tests. If you are basing your hiring decisions on the results of these tests, there is a very good chance you are missing out on the really good candidates who will throw their hands up in frustration after they see so many completely impossible to answer questions. It took several minutes get acknowledged by our server, who looked to be running a little ragged. He looked at us from across the room and said, "I'll be there in a minute!" When he finally came over (about 10 minutes), he basically threw a couple menus at us and ran away (he was polite, but didn't spend a spare second at our table that he didn't have to). The special that night was draught beers (I know, blasphemous at the TIN CAN, but it was about half the price of the beer in a can), so after the server came back (about another 15 minutes), we ordered a couple beers. The beers took about ANOTHER 15 minutes to get to us. I had worked up a bit of an appetite in the meantime, and had plenty of time to peruse the menu and decide on something, so when he brought the beers to us, I said, "And we'd like to order food when you get a minute!" Which MEANS...."HEY I'M READY TO EAT PLEASE TAKE THE ORDER DON'T RUN AWAY." To no avail. He looked really uncomfortable and said, "Uhhhhhhh it's gonna be a few minutes." Okay..... Boyfriend and I drank the beers, which were, frankly, disgusting. They needed to refill their beer machine or something. However that works. But they were completely FLAT. Tasted almost stale. Like if you left a half a beer out overnight after a drunken house party and you're still hungover so you think that beer will taste awesome when you sleepily drink from it the next morning but you get a very rude awakening. Awful. I mean, I know they specialize in canned beer, but come on. Server man didn't come back. Yeah, he was busy, but I was definitely annoyed that people that arrived AFTER us seemed to get their drinks and food in a timely matter. I think he must have forgotten about us a couple times. Poor guy seemed very flustered and unorganized. After boyfriend and I bit our tongues and finished the nasty beers, we decided to peace out. It had been close to a half hour and server man didn't come back. I finally WAVED him down, and he looks like he's about to cry he's so overwhelmed as he scurries over, and I asked for the check. He looked very upset and defeated, and apologized. I told him it's okay, but we need to move on. He was the quickest in bringing us the check. Not sure what to think about that? Didn't want to piss us off even more, or "SWEET I can get rid of a table"? As we walked out, I counted the tables he was serving. Twelve. TWELVE. Most of them had 4 or more at their party. Was still annoyed because boyfriend and I were there when it was about 6 tables. If you're too lazy to do the math up there, we were at this place for over an hour and only had one flat, stale beer apiece to show for it. But I felt bad for the guy. He was putting an order in at the computer by the stairs as we passed him, and I said, "Hey, you really need some help up here! You have 12 tables!" He sullenly replied, "I have the patio, too." I want to give this place a chance. So much potential! Maybe I'll be back if I can be convinced it's not always like this.

text: Of course we had to discover this place mere weeks before we're set to move (we live less than two blocks away). I walked in and this already felt like a five-star place to me. Garces Trading Company was like DiBruno Bros condensed into my favorite things: olive oil, balsamic vinegar, cheese, and cured meats...WHEN I WALKED IN. Who can compete with that kind of first impression?! Bonus points: free samples of meat and cheese at their respective counters. We waited for a table, and as it turned out, Mr. Garces himself was having a meeting at the table we were supposed to have! Fine with us; it gave us an opportunity to ask him for a picture. He's such a nice guy...very soft spoken and low-key. He took a quick photo with us and wished us a great meal. And a great meal it was! Definitely didn't disappoint. Our table of 7 got the chef's tasting menu, and while it was fairly similar to Amada, a lot of things stood out on its own. - First course: cured meats, prosciutto, olives, cheese platter, baby artichokes, and breakfast radish. Needless to say, we started off with a bang. The meats were fan-freakin'-tastic, and the prosciutto practically melted in my mouth. I was a little bummed they didn't give us manchego cheese, but the selection given was superb (especially the onion pecan butter...who would have thought?). The baby artichokes were good but the dated walnuts had an interesting taste. Still not sure how I feel about them. They were okay, but I wouldn't specifically seek them out. The breakfast radish with goat butter was surprisingly good as well, and I'm not a huge radish fan. - Second course: spicy lamb sausage, cioppino, roast chicken, and roast lamb. I don't particularly care for lamb, but the preparation on these two dishes were spot on. The heat in the sausage takes you by surprise at first (totally hit me in the back of the throat, haha), but the spice is not overwhelming and definitely adds a nice dimension to what would have otherwise been a normal dish. The lamb and chicken were accompanied by fingerling potatoes and two kinds of sauces, one of them being a roasted red pepper (kind of sweet). The chicken was one of the best preparations I've ever had. YUM! The cioppino blew us all away, however. The broth was TO DIE FOR. Seriously. I wanted to run into the kitchen and jump into the vat. - Third course: ricotta gnudi with wild mushrooms. I was originally going to order this dish if we didn't go with the tasting menu, and I'm kind of glad I got to try it first. It's like gnocchi but bigger, fluffier, and cheesier. Very very yummy, but I don't think I could eat a whole plate of this. Nice ending to our meal. Dessert wasn't included in the tasting menu, but they have a huge selection to choose from. I was kind of disappointed with dessert...I tried both of the macarons they had, and both fell flat, imo. The white chocolate mint one tasted like toothpaste (and had nearly the same consistency), while the salted caramel macaron was unbelievably sweet. Holy moly...they either need to tone down the amount of filling they put, or tone down the sweetness. It overpowered the meal and I was really bummed about that. It still ended on a good note, though. For some reason they gave us an extra cappuccino on the house. :) Still, this place gets five stars because of everything else. I'd definitely come back (although I'd be a little more careful with the desserts). A few tips: - They don't take reservations. They also don't put your name down until most of your party is present, so plan accordingly. - It can get pretty loud. This isn't a fancy schmancy date place, but it's a great place to go with a group of friends. Just be prepared to raise your voice a little and strain to hear your server explain the dishes.

text: Concealed pretty well down a small alley a block from the County Theater Bobby Simones is well worth the search. The restaurant is fairly small and very comfortable and offers a terrific dinner menu and is also a great place to grab lunch or just drinks. Its located only a block and a half south of the court house in Doylestown. You cant go wrong with any of the meat selections, Bobby's does an exceptional job of finding the best meat in the region and I have never eaten a piece that wasnt cooked to perfection. A great dining experience for me is a combination of great food, atmosphere, service and attention to detail. There are plenty of places that do well in 2 or 3 of these areas but most fail to hit the mark on all 4. Bobby's attention of detail is incredible. Here's an example: while having lunch there one day I ordered a Chicken Caesar salad, I happen to like anchovies, many don't. Bobby took pride in telling me that he only serves white anchovies and explaining to me the difference they make. He was right; anyone can make a decent Chicken Caesar, but these really changed the flavor of the salad and made it an experience. There is a private room in the back that they are happy to set up for you if you want to host a party that is quieter than the main part of the restaurant and is just the place for a business or family dinner for 10 or less. Adding Mike Conti to oversee the restaurant has only taken this place up. Mike is the consummate professional and you are pretty much guaranteed a special time when you go. There is seating outside in the summer months and a bar across the alley that are also part of Bobby's but each area seems to offer something different and stands well on its own. If Bobby is there you will know, he is like an old time restaurateur who takes real pride in meeting you personally and making sure that your expectations are surpassed. If not, they will be immediately. Pride goes along way to making this spot one to put on your list of "must go's"

text: I have taken several weeks to not write this review because of my obvious bias: 1) I'm sending my kid here, and 2) I'm also [censored by my baby mama.] That being said, however, after several weeks of critical thought and analysis, I am now ready to give my full report on why The Orchard School is the finest school in Indianapolis. The primary reason is their core values dictate what they do. Their values reflect a forward thinking learning environment that fosters and celebrates individual achievement and experimental learning in a unique and culturally diverse environment. Uniformity and conformity are not found here. A strict disciplinary approach with rigid structure is not here either. Every student is taught with individual needs addressed, not a curriculum of pass/fail or right/wrong. Instead of telling a student the answer, the teachers teach them HOW to solve the problem, HOW to think through to the answer. Usually, these types of pedagogical approaches are not found until well after post secondary education, yet Orchard is applying these principals early education. The results are impressive. The students show maturity well beyond their years. Their ambitions (along with their achievements) would be impressive for most high school students, much less elementary. For example, I had a third grader telling me about how he just updated his resume, and explained his plans for after he completes his college degree, in addition to what he wants to accomplish along the way. The kid had more in the works in his advanced mind than most adults! But consider this: He is not the only one and far from it. All of these kids LOVE their school, love learning, and are disappointed when school breaks come around. Another reason why I love Orchard is it's approach to the community as a whole. One of Orchard's core values is diversity. Purposely, the school wants, and works, towards an multi-ethnic, multi-income, multi-viewed world in their classroom. Inclusivity and celebration of diversity is real at Orchard, not faked or seen as some chore. It is palpable and a true vision of how a multicultural America could be. How does a private, non faith based school make their tuition affordable? Their large network of donors, of course! Even the teacher's give to the Annual Giving Fund. Corporation donations, grants and a large endowment fueled by gifts from interested parties, parents and alumni defray the actual cost of tuition to affordable rates. Yes, Orchard actually charges less in tuition than it actually costs, and offers need based financial assistance, in order to insure that they capture a diverse range of ethnicities, incomes, and backgrounds. And yet, the students there seem very similar: Eager to learn, a deep drive to succeed, and very well mannered in social and professional graces. The last, but certainly not least, reason I love Orchard School are the dedicated to the point of fanatical parents, teachers and alumni. The teachers are incredible in that they are fantastic and patient with each one of their students, but that once they get to Orchard, they do not want to leave. I cannot recall the exact number but the average teacher has been there ten to fifteen years!?!? That is unheard of in private education, much less public school. My child's teacher has been there for over twenty years and that was her first full-time teaching position. Everyone loves her and she could go anywhere she wanted to (especially with her accomplishments) but she loves the school. The school is in her and much as she is in the school, and she is far from the exception! Also, the parents are the main recruitment tool for Orchard. Almost every single Orchard parent was referred by and Orchard parent. Those that were not recruited directly, were recruited indirectly by parents eagerness to put "Open House" signs in their yard. It's hard to find this much fond dedication from alumni of colleges, but parents seem to be even more motivated to spread the fame. Also, alumni also are involved and give back to their school out of their time, talents and treasure. Several parents offer products of theirs as raffle donations, and we are not talking about small freebies, but big ticket items like AUTOMOBILES! That's dedication! In summary, Orchard is the best school I have ever encountered, and I am somewhat jealous that I can afford to send my kid here. I just wish I could be a kid again in her shoes for a little while!

text: I've been to the Swift Half about four times since it opened, so this is a pretty well thought out review. Although I don't have any pictures from my trips, I do have a good amount of insight. Here it comes: I expected this new Good Dog outpost to have excellent food. I went recently with Allie, John, and Rachel and they were all ready for dinner. They ordered mussels, fish and chips, and cucumber sandwiches, respectively. I had a few mussels, and they were decent, but this is clearly not the spot you want to hit for mussels. The fish and chips looked delicious when they were served, but further investigation revealed that they were overly breaded and couldn't keep up with Memphis Taproom. Rachel commented that her small appetizer was good, but also that she could have made something better at home. Needless to say, the food is not a selling point. To be honest, I'm also disappointed with the beer list. In fairness, Swift Half has some good beers on tap. But when a week passes in between visits and not a single tap changes, I'm not inclined to return anytime soon. The beer list is not totally uninspired, with Southampton, Flying Fish, Stoudt's, Brooklyn, even Chimay represented on tap. The bottle list is extensive and well priced. One nice part of the menu is the inclusion of small plates of meat and cheese that could be matched to beer, if you're so inclined. Currently, they have the Six Points Sweet Action on tap, which I raved about ever since the first time I had it at Sidecar. It's not as amazing as my memory made it, but I was glad to see this hard to find beer on tap. It's still excellent, and a nice find for a rare style: American Blonde Ale. Service here is meh. It's not bad, I think it's pretty hit or miss depending on who's working. My favorite thing about this spot, and the reason that I keep coming back, is the outdoor seating. The piazza is a really cool area, and it's great when the Phillies are on the big screen. Inside Swift Half is a normal bar, and I wouldn't eat or drink inside. text: I had to go to the ER this morning, only the third time ever in my life, thank you very much. What can I say, I'm a klutz! The hard and icy snow piled up so high along the streets and parking is pretty crappy, so when you do park along the side and bring your utility vehicle up onto the hard packed snow, do not underestimate your first step out of the truck like I did. Little did I know that under several feet or so of snow was a drain, if I had parked a little further back or forward I would have been fine. Expecting to step onto the hard packed snow, I stepped right out and my left foot and leg went slamming down to the drain grid. At that I then lost my balance and went sideways. I see you laughing, but ouch! It was painful yesterday and last night I could barely sleep it hurt so bad, when I awoke this am. the pain was twice as bad as I tried to apply pressure to the foot. Being the stubborn fool that I am I waited for hubby to leave for work, called my own work and then drove myself to the ER using one foot. Am I your hero? The ER waiting area was empty and I thought joy, joy. Checking in was as quick as a wink and I only waited about ten minutes before being taken back. Yikes why did I come here today? I saw how busy they were and it wasn't even 7:00am, so I said no to a bed that was offered to me and said I was fine in a chair after hearing all beds were full in both the hospital and the ER. During my time there I watched ambulance's bring in patients who were registered right there in the hallways from the stretchers they were brought in on. Some of these patients stayed right there, because there were no rooms left. Maybe they would have moved me along a little faster so they could have had my room, if I had agreed to one. Two hours I waited for a simple foot Xray, it did not even require the ER's time, it was a matter of calling an Xray tech to come and get me. After seeing someone brought in who fell on the ice and get attention right away, I started to get angry, but I started to cry too. I finally said to a Doctor passing by that it has been two hours and no one has seen me and I would like to leave and go elsewhere, since they were so busy. Dr. Jack did not catch his last name, grabbed my wheelchair with fury, swung me around and down corridors in a very rude and malicious way! He was so ignorant in the way he talked to me and handled my wheelchair. Two techs were standing there talking, doing nothing else, had no patients and I was seen right away. They were very nice. Turned out I have torn ligaments and tendons, no broken bones and I'm in a show boot and on crutches for the first time in my life and hopefully the last. They prescribed me heavy duty narcotics, but I'll pass on those. This is the closest hospital to my home, I tend to drive three times as far to go to another hospital, for the couple of times I have had to go. I have heard nothing but horror stories of St. Mary's, but hubby has been admitted here several times and I thought it was okay, not as good as others, but okay. I wonder how they will open up beds in the hospital for the heart attack patients just arriving. Do they go by who could have been released two days a go and their insurance is just being milked? Do they weigh the insurance of the new patients arriving or do they really care about who needs the most care? The way they handled the patients coming in and out was unbelievable. Most were pacing like hello, what is going on here with my care. Instead of standing around for a good half hour talking in huge groups when the shift changes, keep on moving to take the few minutes of care you need to for the many fall victims who came in and the burn victim. Get us in and out to free up your space and time for the seriously ill. I lost two dear friends in this hospital, one was a diabetic who had fallen and was in for injuries and treatment, he ended up with pneumonia and died, another was in after a stroke, he was to be released and go into therapy in two days, he got pneumonia and never did leave. I am not a fan of this hospital. I give kudos to Michelle who fitted me with this awesome blue boot (not) and crutches and taught me how to use the damn things. She was awesome.

text: For $26 all you can eat sushi, this sounds like a reasonable deal. Allow me to reiterate: ...this "SOUNDS" like a reasonable deal. Considering that, this place was basically Bizarro-world. Relatively pricey for all you can eat (you can find cheaper) and the sushi was mediocre... at best (you can [and have] find better). I snowboarded earlier in the day, so I was ready to throw down - STARVING!!!! To be honest, we tried all of it. There was, though, one thing that left an inescapable impression upon me. The chef, though very friendly and well intentioned, offered me Uni. For the uninitiated, Uni is the roe of a sea urchin - my favorite!!!!! So I'm thinking, "OK, this is where this experience makes a turn for the better." I then notice something to my horror. He pulls out this tray, which strongly resembles an ice tray. He then proceeds to extract the Uni from it by twisting the tray, LIKE AN ICE TRAY!!!! OK, what's going on here?!?!? How can this get worse? He takes the extractions and places them in the MICROWAVE!!!!!! Looking around the room, I have two thoughts on my mind: 1) Am I being punk'd? 2) Where's the hidden camera? After the painfully out of place "DING", he plates the Uni and brings it to me. Mind you, at this point, I know this isn't going to go well, but harboring such a "roll with it" type personality, and considering the good intentions (I think) of the chef, I conclude that I'm going to have to actually consume this. How shall I describe this? Have you ever had deep fried ice cream... you know, where the outside is warm and the inside was, well, frozen? Yeah, it was a lot like that. First of all, Uni isn't for everyone, and for those that do enjoy it, we understand why others don't. This though, was an abomination!!!! They would have been better served by saying that they didn't have any! Disgusting!!!!! And I rarely will make that claim!!! I cannot speak for their dinners, but stay away from the "sushi" - stay far away!

text: Oh Lambert. Poor, poor Lambert. My heart breaks for thee. You were once a hub, a nerve center for the most traveled suitcase-carrying businessmen and women in America. The movers and shakers all traveled to and from you, your warm bustling concourses beaming with life. In the 1990's you were the #8 airport in all of America in terms of volume. There was too much congestion and the city bought out surrounding housing and bulldozed them to make way for a bright shiny new runway to support the flight traffic. And then something happened. TWA went belly up. American Airlines cut your hub status. And Anheuser Busch got bought out by some Belgian company. As a metro area, St. Louis stagnated while other cities grew. From 2000 to 2009, you lost half of your travelers. Half. 50 percent. Ouch. It used to be that going to visit you was a hassle. Long lines, long waits, crowded gates. Now it's not a hassle anymore. It's sad. I can breeze right into you at almost any time of day without a problem. What once were busy shops and restaurants are shut down or empty. Everything about you is stuck in the 80's. The decor, the technology, the signage, even some of the people. Sometimes I wonder if you even know what the internet is. I guess it's not all bad. I don't wait very long anymore in your security lines, and check-in is easy. I never have to fight to find a parking spot. There's not a long wait if I want a coffee. And I don't have to wait very long to get my luggage. But a part of me still misses the old you. When you were strong and confident and growing. It pains me to see you weak and frail and collapsing. They built your new runway, finally. It's no longer needed. I think it's used, once in a while at least. But they had to knock down all those houses to build it and spend all that money, instead of giving you the face lift you so desperately need. Sometimes when I visit you I don't know where to go. Your signs are vague and misleading, and I have to double-back or loop around to get myself straightened out. Wait, how do I get on westbound 70 again? Which way to the car rental returns? Why does that exit say airport when it just takes you to an open field? No wonder people don't like visiting you, you make yourself hard to find and harder to leave. I don't know why, but even though you're located in the county, you're owned by the city of St. Louis. It's a sad parallel. What happened to the city in the 50's and 60's (mass exodus) happened to you in the 00's. You're trying to jump start yourself, but nothing really works. As of 2010, your largest carrier will be Southwest Airlines, located in the auxillary (east) terminal, and the main terminal will be a shadow of its former self, losing all hub status. I don't know what to tell you, Lambert. You had your moment of glory and now it's gone. You keep wearing skinny ties and members only jackets and oakley sunglasses, but it's the 10's. It would be funny if it wasn't so sad. These kids today don't remember you back in the day. They only know you as a lonely old man clinging on for life, depressed and confused on how to approach the future. I know you have it in you. You can be great again, but it takes hard work and dedication, and I'm not seeing any of that from you. Don't take this personally, but you're just not the airport you used to be.
