text: I know there are some people who prefer Geno's over Pat's...and for those people, I must say that you are CRAZY. Absolutely CRAZY. And here's why: I've been to Geno's once or twice before, a long time ago and things haven't changed much. When my coworker and I was scheduled for a training up in King of Prussia, well, we couldn't drive past Philly without a stop at a cheesesteak joint. As my coworker has never been to Philly (uh, how?!?!), I decided that if cheesesteak was what he was craving...well then, we have to do the Geno's/Pat's taste-off. We start off at Geno's, and there was no one in line. There was no one in front of me, and no one behind me. No one walking up the street to come to Geno's. So there really wasn't a need for the lady behind the counter to get *quite* as snotty as she was, when we didn't know what "wit" meant. I mean "wit" what (it turns out - it means "with onions")? Obviously, we're new here, and as it's not like we're holding up the line, the attitude wasn't really called for. Eh. Whatever. We were hungry. I *LOVE* cheese wiz, and as that is what the original cheesesteak was made with, well that's what I always order (before you doubt me - look it up. I'm right.). My coworker got his with provolone, because he's weird about eating "plastic cheese". Whatever. He quickly learned to rue his haute palette, as he bit into his cheesesteak - to find that the cheese was stone-cold and un-melted! Have you ever had unmelted cheese on a cheesesteak? It's not exactly gross, but well, it's not tasty either. There is something about warm, melty, oozy cheese that is part of the cheesesteak experience! To add insult to injury, both of our breads were a *wee* bit on the stale side (not "3-day-old stale"...more like "been-left-out-all-day-next-to-the-oven" stale), and I didn't like that the meat wasn't quite as chopped up as I liked. This reminded me why I stopped coming to Geno's after my second or third visit so long ago. On this trip, we ate at 3 cheesesteak places. Here, Pat's (see my review), and Jim's. I have to say, that this was definitely bottom of the list for both of us. Actually, I ranked this cheesesteak to be about on-par with Jerry's. Yes, you read that right - Jerry's. A NOTE: because of the "rivalry" between Pat and Geno's, I find it really hard to write this review without doing a comparison. Normally, I try to avoid comparing one establishment against, another, as each should stand on it's own, however the rivalry between the two is so popular, that it's nearly impossible to eat a cheesesteak from one, without thinking of the other.

text: I really didn't want to give this place one star. I tried to think of reasons to give it even a paltry 2 stars. But I can't. I can't recommend this place to anyone. It failed in nearly every way that a restaurant can. Let me break this down for you. It serves cafeteria-type food to elderly people in a strange atmosphere with a slow, overworked, and absent-minded waitstaff. Let me start out by saying this restaurant wasn't my choice. The only thing I knew about it was that it was a German restaurant in Dutchtown. I don't mean to be overly snobbish (only a little), but when was the last time someone had a really good meal in a German restaurant? Do nice German restaurants even exist? And moreover, what even constitutes German food anymore? America already stole sausages and hamburgers for themselves, so what's the difference between eating at a German place and a baseball game? In the case of the Feasting Fox, I'd rather be at the game. You'd pay about the same, get your food faster, have a better atmosphere, and at least have the chance of seeing someone under the age of 60. Ok, about that atmosphere. This place is kinda like if your grandma had a huge old house and converted it into a restaurant. No, not your cool grandma (the one that owns Winslow's Home), the grandma that never threw anything out and bought everything cheaply. The one that collects weird knickknacks of foxes and old faded landscape paintings. The one that mis-matches china, glasses, and silverware (There were 5 people at my table. There were 4 different types of glasses for soft drinks, and everyone had a different type of plate. I'm not entirely sure this was intentional). You know you're not exactly experiencing fine dining when people are wheeling in oxygen tanks behind them. No offense to all the oxy-tankers out there, but they're not known for their discriminating taste. In short, this place was old. Sometimes it was hard to tell which was older, the restaurant or the patrons, and I'm pretty sure the restaurant is over 100 years old. So anyway, the menu is pretty standard. Chicken, steak, german sausage, salad, and umm...that might be it. We got an appetizer of parmasan cheese puffs, which consisted of cheese whiz on melba toast. It may be the single most offensive dish served to me in quite some time. Seriously, even when I was in college I could whip up better stuff than this. I deliberately tried to find something on the menu that I'm sure they couldn't screw up, because at this point the fear of the restaurant gods had been stricken in me. I chose the herb chicken. It's pretty hard to screw up chicken, I thought. Especially compared to steak or sausage. The waitress said I got the last chicken of the day. I looked at my watch. It was 5:30. I'm assuming they're not expecting any late night diners since their clientele has to hit the sack in time to get up for the Denny's early bird special at 5AM. In retrospect, I wish they had been out of it because I would have gotten a second chance. I got a soup with it, and the waitress said the soup of the day was vegetable. Sounds good, a hard soup to screw up. Here's the problem. The soup of the day wasn't vegetable, it was irish barley, and it was brought to us anyway without asking if it was ok. And, surprise! It tasted like it was from a can. But hey, canned food was better than what awaited me. After about 45 minutes (and several ignored requests to refill our glasses), my entree arrived. The chicken was huge, a full half-chicken. I guess they made up for in volume what lacked in taste, because this thing was bad. It had been badly overcooked and dried out. The skin tasted like paper and peeled off in one long pull. The problem was that all the herbs were in the skin, so I was left with a huge skinless, dry, flavorless chicken. And I had no idea what to do with it. So I boxed it up and took it home, where it still sits in my fridge. At least the mashed potatoes and vegetables that came with it (probably from a mix) were decent. The desserts were alright, but it's kinda hard to screw up dessert, even if you try. Anyone can make a cake or a pie from a mix. Heck, the people at my work do it all the time. Oh, and we ordered ice cream to go with our strudel, which of course never arrived. At least at work people bring in a dipper so you can get your own ice cream if you want it. So when it was all said and done, our simple dinner turned into a 2 hour extravaganza of crap. The food sucked, the atmosphere sucked, and the service sucked. The stuff that tasted the best either was out of a can or made from a mix. There's a reason why people pay more than $10 for an entree, and that's so that they can eat real food that's prepared well. I'm not quite sure how this place has stayed in business for 100 years, but God help us if it manages to drag along for another 100. Time to put the Feasting Fox out to pasture.

text: Been a Great Basin FCU member for 20 years. They closed the branch closest to me so I decided to go here to withdraw money since I had to be in this part of town any way. The bank teller asked for my driver's license so I could make a withdrawal. I saw her run it through some machine. I asked what that was. She said they scan an image of your driver's license they have it on their computers and don't have to ask you for it each time. Not just your driver's license photo. Your entire license image is in their computer system. I explained I wasn't comfortable with this because of identity theft issues. I was one of the people who got a letter from St. Mary's saying my personal data had been breached by an ID thief. She agreed to delete the image. I asked why she didn't ask me if I wanted my driver's license scanned. She said it never occurred to her to ask. Now I understand that banks already have access to lots of information we would consider personal. But the goal here, I believe, is to reduce the risks of thefts, not increase them. Great Basin should tell customers their driver's licenses are going to be copied before they do this. I don't know if they sent this out in information to customers. I never saw this. I wonder how many thousands of Great Basin FCU customers don't know that there's a picture of their driver's license in the credit union computer.

text: Cripes, this place is begging to be closed. I apologize in advance, for this is a long one, but man... I needed to vent. Upon moving to our new 'hood, the husband and I were looking forward to finding our new go-to Thai place. Luckily, there are a few within walking distance and while the majority of reviews for Thai Cafe are pretty 'meh', we thought we'd give it a go anyway. After all, there is ONE radiant review and we were being optimistic... Now, I've eaten in many restaurants and experienced service ranging from crappy to incredibly awesome, but I never, EVER experienced worse service than at Thai Cafe. Absolutely abysmal, atrocious, abhorrent... I've gotten better service at White Castle. Justin and I invited his family to visit our new neighborhood and thought we'd try this place out. We walked in at 7pm on a Saturday to see one occupied table of two, but not a single employee anywhere. We hovered around the hostess stand, admiring the interesting decor (that's where one star comes from). We waited and waited and considered just leaving (as we should have. One table on a Saturday and no one seating customers? Run for your life!!!). FINALLY a very unhappy-looking woman seated us, threw menus at us and stomped off in her flip flops. A million years later, she came back and asked, "What do you want to drink?" A valid question, of course, but it was said with such venom, we were taken aback. My father-in-law asked for his regular, Sapphire and tonic, to which she replied, "We don't got that." He asked for Tanqueray instead. "We don't got that." We could've played that game all night, as she wasn't offering what, in fact, they DID have. I mean, did she want our money or not? Finally, she told us they only had "the cheap stuff." He said he'd take it. Another million years later, she came to tell us they didn't have any tonic. Jeeeeesus, this place is awesome. So my father-in-law looked over the specialty drink menu and asked what was in the elusively-named drinks, when at this point he should have known that answering any of our questions was not anywhere close to this woman's priorities. She had to ask the people in back about the drink ingredients and then had to go back again to see if they actually had those ingredients. At this point, there was still only one other occupied table in the place, which was no longer a shock, especially since I was ready to leave. We finally placed an order for appetizers and our entrees, which took another bazillion years to appear. The appetizers were brought out by a delightfully friendly older woman whom I'd wished had served us the whole night, as I suspect it would've changed this review in its entirety. One of the apps went missing and was never received, the tempura veggies were batter-sodden and the accompanying sauce was an unidentified gelatinous mess, and the satay was so overcooked it was like shoe leather. Maybe it's a good thing the fish balls never appeared... The second star comes from the entrees, which, after the hideous service, drinks and appetizers, were shockingly good. They don't mess around with namby-pamby spice levels here. If you ask for medium spicy, be prepared for some zing. I liked my green curry, Justin enjoyed his duck curry and while I can't remember what everyone else had, the entree portion of our meal briefly settled our grumbling about unprofessional service, lack of water refills and the fact that they did, in fact, have Tanqueray in the bar (my sister-in-law went on a covert mission and peeked at the bottles). During this whole dinner ordeal, a few other parties came in hoping to have dinner, I presume. Two parties waited it out and were finally seated, while two other parties waited, waited, waited and finally just bailed. If you have the patience of a saint, bring your own water bottle to dinner and avoid the appetizers, you will likely enjoy yourself at Thai Cafe. If you have ever dined anywhere else in the world, EVER, you will likely realize that Thai Cafe is perilously close to running off all their business with their absolute lack of service and unremarkable food.

text: My husband took me here tonight for Valentine's Day dinner. I knew nothing about the place in advance except that it's a Marc Vetri restaurant, and he is an amazing chef (though I've yet to make it to Osteria, it's on my list). We were not disappointed. Every dish was fantastic. I stuffed myself silly (small plates? how much can I eat? yeah, right) and hope to save up all day next time for a meal this good. Brief description: this sleek industrial/modern space is really inviting. I love the fact that you can eat at the bar and watch the cooking take place. That is really cool :) The place was noisier than I expected and the tables were very close together, so you were kind of sitting (almost) on your neighbor's lap.... but these are minor details :) Now onto the food..... there is much to choose from, which is nice... I'm a huge eggplant fan, and the highlight of my evening was the eggplant brushetta dish. I have never had eggplant spread that good. My only complaint was that two small slices of garlic toast were not enough to sop up all of this goodness (no fear, there was other delicious bread on the table). If you get nothing else at Amis, get the eggplant bruschetta. A close second are the eggplant "fries" that strangely decorate the rigatoni with swordfish. Delish and addicting. If they sold these fries from a street vendor, I'd be in big trouble.... Other standouts: Roasted potatoes (my husband's favorite), crispy and delicious Baked clams (yummmmm) Turkey cutlet - who would of thought that turkey mascerading as a thinly pounded veal cutlet could taste so good? Simple, but delicious, and nice with the accompanying greens and freshly shaved parmesan. Others: The grilled cauliflower lightly breaded -- ok, but not exceptional. It was too hard for my taste. Beef carpaccio - nothing against, it, just not my thing (hubby loved it) I hope I'm not forgetting anything.... Desserts were good. The menu is extensive and everything looked delicious. We had an "ice cream sundae" with the most delicious amaretto-tasting ice cream I've ever had, sprinkled with walnuts and covered in fudge. My husband had the chocolate ganache cake that was good, but I wasn't a huge fan. I'm coming back for the Belgian waffle with nutella ... had I not had pancakes for breakfast, I definitely would have gotten it. Service was great. Very attentive and helpful. A new favorite -- we'll be back for more.

text: Technically, my rating is 4.5 stars, but Yelp doesn't let you give halves. Sometimes it's difficult being a vegetarian foodie, especially one with a mushroom allergy. At Bayona, it was pretty effortless, starting with making the reservation. Upon calling I had several questions and they were all met with a good, helpful attitude which set a really good tone for the evening. When we arrived the same helpful woman (I recognized her voice) greeted us and seated us in the parlor-type area for drinks while our table was prepared. She had a good knowledge of the wine list and her recommendation for a red (Tempranillo/Cabernet Sauvignon blend) was spot on! Once seated, we were greeted by our server's assistant, who was adorable and charming. He brought a small dish of olives and curried and pickled veggies, which were super tasty. Our main server greeted us next. He has an extremely cheerful demeanor and seemed to genuinely love his job and the food he serves. Right off the bat he gave us a great explanation of the menu (including when something was made with chicken stock WITHOUT ME ASKING!). I let him know that I was a vegetarian with a mushroom allergy and he immediately suggested some ways to modify or combine existing menu items. He also took my dietary restrictions to the Chef de Cuisine and let him come up with some dishes that he would want to make based on what he had in the pantry. I know sometimes chefs can get snippy about modifying their dishes (each component has a purpose, I know!), so I was excited to see what he would come up with. Before I go into what my mom and I ordered, I want to say three words: SWEET POTATO BRIOCHE! Moving on. My mom settled started with the Bayona salad. The portion was unexpectedly large. It was well-dressed (don't you hate when restaurants drown your salad? I do!) and had a slight sweetness that paired well with the shaved parmigiano reggiano. My mom didn't finish her salad (saving room), so I gobbled it right up! For her entrée, she went with the pan-seared pancetta-wrapped halibut, broccoli flan, and shoestring potatoes. After the first bite of halibut the only thing she could say was "outstanding." The broccoli flan was amazing (mom was nice enough to share). Those aren't two words that I would have put together before my trip to Bayona, but it's now something that I am hoping to replicate at home. The only "bad" thing my mom had to say was "I would have been okay with more shoestring potatoes." I began with the Greek salad, which was on the daily specials menu. I was extremely pleased with the proportions of the ingredients in my salad as all too often someone gets carried away with the feta. Not here. You don't always see garbanzo beans on a Greek salad, but I enjoyed the addition. For my entrée, I chose to go with one of the chef's options: gnocchi, sautéed spinach and broccolini, and puréed tomato confit. This dish has converted me from feeling luke-warm about gnocchi into a HUGE FAN. And kudos on not overcooking the spinach. So many people do that I generally refuse to order it. Thanks, Bayona, for not making me regret taking those risks. So where's the reason for the half-star deduction in the rating? I had a pretty good conversation with the server about my mushroom allergy. He repeated it back to me several times and yet my entrée arrived topped with hen of the woods mushrooms. Everyone was extremely apologetic and it was quickly resolved. A new plate was fired up and delivered piping hot, but it's a big pet peeve when my plate is delivered with poison on it. The simply charming aesthetic of the interior and the courtyard charming is a perfect fit for the vibe of the food. I only wish I had been able to tummy-rub the restaurant's cat (I believe his name is Crusty). OH! I almost forgot!! My mom purchased Susan Spicer's cookbook, and we came back for it the following day as they had held it so it could be signed. Unfortunately Susan wasn't going to be in before our flight left so they graciously offered to ship the book to my mom at no charge. Way to go, Bayona staff!

text: Cannery is under the same management as the Mercy Lounge, and many people often try to classify the two spaces as just one venue. Don't listen to those people! While the Mercy Lounge is a spectacular medium-sized venue with great sound and a decent amount of room, Cannery is a poorly designed large venue that will lure you in with its superior acts and then break your heart with sub-par sound and a terribly located stage. There's a somewhat sneaky move that the owners of Mercy/Cannery often pull. They'll book big acts (like the Raconteurs, the Shins or Sharon Jones) for the Mercy Lounge, and when these shows sell out they'll be moved to the Cannery at the last minute. This may not bother some people, and others might not even realize they're being duped. Here's the problem, however: the Cannery Ballroom's stage is wedged awkwardly at the far end of the venue, quite literally facing a corner. They crowd typically tries to cram itself into the narrow area that is in a direct line of site with the stage, and about 10% of them are successful. The remainder of the audience is left to peer at the band from across the bar or a distant corner. The drink prices are the same as at the Mercy Lounge (pretty good), and the staff is the same. Aside from the building itself and the terrible acoustics, it's just like Mercy. I've just genuinely never been to a show at Cannery in which I haven't been behind a pillar, wedged into a corner or wondering why I can't hear the vocals or overheads. I'm afraid I have to skip most of the shows here, no matter how good the band.
label: NEG

text: I was the first person to review Tower Tacos. I feel like it is one of my babies, so it makes me sad to see it's decline. Still, I wanted to give him the benefit of the doubt. I have tried to revisit Tower Tacos several times, in hopes of changing my mind. I tend to give privately owned establishments a little leeway because I know they don't have corporate gurus directing them and they usually put a little more love into the food. Unfortunately, the food is not the same. They serve Mexican food with new ingredients that are of poor quality. I don't know what else to say. Feel free to read my last review for some explanation. It's seasoned pork sauteed with chorizo and pineapple on a soft corn tortilla with red onion and cilantro (usually). Any taqueria on Cherokee will do this taco well. Unfortunately, not Tower Tacos. I don't understand... they used to make these great!! I don't know what the meat was seasoned with and white onion? This is not an eastern European restaurant... That onion completely overpowered any sweetness or flavor that the taco could have had. $23 later and no chips were placed in the bag to go with our guacamole and meal. Twer Tacos needs to get back to the basics. Lose the Russian food, unless you are opening a "Tower Stuffed Peppers" restaurant and focus on good, solid Mexican food with fresh, quality ingredients. This is a street where solid Mexican food exists elsewhere.

text: So, I read the reviews here on yelp, and being a nihon-a-phile (person obsessed with Japan), I had to check this place out asap. My girlfriend and I arrived around 6pm on a Saturday evening, and upon entering the 3 sushi chefs yelled, "Irasshaimase, Hai Doozo", (Please come in! Thank you for coming!). And were escorted to a quaint little table for 2. The waitress immediately served us water, toasted rice green tea, and presented us with the special board featuring a nice selection of, Maki, Nigiri, Sashimi. There were quite a few items that were actually flown over from Japan including Oysters and Red Snapper, which we ordered and loved. The presentations were beautiful, and everything was extremely fresh and delicious. As far as I'm concerned this is the BEST sushi place this side of New York. If you are traveling alone, and you have a decent sized wallet on you, I would suggest sitting at the bar and telling the chef, omakase onegaishimasu "Oh-Ma-Ka-Say, Oh-Na-Gai-She-Mas", The expression is used at sushi restaurants to leave the selection to the chef.

text: First things first: CASH ONLY. Know before you go (we didn't, but luckily there's an ATM across the street). And while I said the prices were moderate, it's easy to drop $100 on dinner if you do appetizer/entree/dessert. On to the food: delicious. We started with carrot soup. It was artfully presented with olive oil drizzled on top. It had a bit of cream and was rich and flavorful. There was a bacon/pork flavor to it. My friend loved that, but I found it overpowered the carrot flavor. I also dislike bacon, so it may have been my prejudice. Next we shared the plato de charcuteria. Manchego cheese with quince paste was a favorite, as was the cured pork tenderloin (paper-thin slices with an incredible texture). There was also serrano ham, chorizo, goat cheese, and some type of very strong blue cheese. Served with grilled bread drizzled with olive oil. For dinner my friend got the black rice with shrimp. I had a taste; it was interesting, but for the life of me I can't identify the flavors. Squid ink, perhaps. My pork tendorloin was delicious, grilled but tender inside. The highlight was the red pepper and mango 'salad' beneath it. It was warm and delicious, sweet and savory. And everything was beautiful to look at, wonderful plating. Finally, we each ordered spicy hot chocolate and a side of churros. The churros were made fresh, not too sweet, a nice complement to the chocolate. The chocolate was so rich and smooth that we used it more like a fondue for the churros. I'd like to go back and try the other chocolates. They even offer a tasting, I understand. Cafe Apamate is a BYOB, so bring your own Spanish wine for a great night out. In all, we ordered far too much food. My friend knew better and got her entree to go. We were surprised at how quickly our bill added up. More than we expected to spend on a casual weeknight with a buddy. But for a special night out it is fine. And next time we'll know to order less food. They also serve mini-tapas, which is certainly 'mini' but reasonable if you just want some light bites. Oh, and the service was friendly and attentive.

All I have to say about this sandwich at this point is...ewwww. Seriously, not just the worst falafel sandwich ever, but one of the worst sandwiches, period. text: One word, perfect. I hate walking into a specialty sandwich shop or cafe, and find myself staring at a bloated, long, and utterly exhausting menu. Who would think a grilled cheese tasted good with apples? But now, after eating one with apples, I can't fathom having another grilled cheese without them. Why do everything okay, when you can do a few things GREAT? This should be the slogan of House, because it certainly is the way they designed their menu. The Jersey Joe, a wonderful panini on artisan rye bread. Crisp, fresh, delicious. The key to any sandwich is the bread, and House make's sure to use only the freshest locally baked bread (From a bakery whose name escapes me at the moment). The tomato soup is freshly made, with real organic tomatoes, served steaming hot. The place is literally a hole in the wall, but very cozy, especially on a cold, wet day. I wouldn't call it House, it's more like Home, because you feel right at home when eating there. The gentleman who served us was extremely gracious and courteous, and I could tell he was very proud of the work they were doing there. Small business pride is something that gets lost in the monstrosity of the big chain restaurants. What else can I say? This place rules.

text: This is one of the better Starbucks around. It's busy and the area is nice also. It's conveniently located across the road from Grant MacEwan University which might make it a lot noisier and tough to find a seat once school is in session. It's a pleasant, spacious location with a good array of indoor and outdoor seating. I've never noticed the parking sign, but you can bet after getting a parking ticket at North Town Mall last week I am looking at the signs more closely. Unfortunately the lot here is managed by Diamond Parking as well. I have only begun to deal with that. Watch for my review of Diamond Parking and North Town Mall. It should be obvious that you should keep an eye on your car for the parking Nazis. If you're going to be longer than two hours, you might want to find a better parking spot. I think I saw some free street parking. Busyness - This is a pretty busy location. It's fairly close to downtown and just across from Grant MacEwan University. I would imagine that it gets even busier once school's back in. Noisiness - There's a nice high ceiling that seems to absorb the noise reasonably well. The music isn't too loud either. Ambience - I've been coming to this Starbucks for a couple of years and I've always liked it. Power - It is available, but the window seats and tables in the centre have an issue. I'd bring an extension cord if you want to use some of the tables in the centre. Free wifi - Available and works well. Being one of those people who keeps a number of tabs open, you might want to login with a browser which you don't use often, otherwise each page becomes a login page, oddly enough. (In Firefox Windows 7 at least.) Staff - Always friendly and helpful. I've rarely had a complaint about a Starbucks employee. Seating - There are 28 seats in this Starbucks, with four armchairs and two good sized tables for laying out a bit of work. I like the square tables they have here. They're at a nice height and are quite roomy, compared to the dinky round cafe tables I normally see at Starbucks. There are four or five tables outside on the spacious patio. It's also bordered by some hedges to give it a bit of privacy. I don't know if they ever use the patio heaters. Security - When I first started coming to this location, there was a homeless camp in the empty lot nearby. It's gone now, but the Starbucks is close to downtown. Not too bad of an area but 107 Ave is close by. Take the usual precautions.

text: I was a little nervous about this place after reading it was a franchise out in California, since I've never heard anything good about bbq in California. Still I wanted to keep an open mind and I do like good bbq, so I went here for lunch. I was seated right away, but it did take some time for my server to get to me, since it was a little crowded and they appeared to be short staffed on the waitress/waiter end. Once my waitress came over, she took my drink and food orders very fast and efficiently. Like the Yelper Kalina I, I too had what tasted like a watered down drink. In my case it was a Sprite. Though on second though, I wonder if someone didn't set the mix/mixer right. Usually those are prepackaged though, unless technology has changed. I ordered the Carolina style pulled pork sandwich with fries and coleslaw. When it comes to bbq there are 4 things you need to do well: Meat, meat, meat, and sides. The meat was tender, but had absolutely no taste. Now if its a Carolina style meat, it should definitely have some taste ie a rub or vinegar/sourness to it. The fries were a mix of sweet potato and regular fries. They were ok, but nothing noteworthy. The guy who brought my order over said "Try this apple cider vinegar with peppers in it on your fries. It's delicious". I did so on a small portion of my fries, and well it tasted like vinegary fries. No real apple or pepper taste. So unless my tastebuds are completely shot that was a waste. The coleslaw tasted like it had been made fairly recently, since it had some crunch to it. However there was no zip to it(needed pepper or something else) and it wasn't creamy enough. It also irritated me that they served the coleslaw on TOP of my meat on the sandwich. I'm not sure if that was intentional or just a plating error. It's possible I missed the description of the sandwich, but thats the first time I ever had coleslaw dumped on top of a barbecue sandwich. And I've eaten my fair share of bbq sandwiches at this point, especially after living down South for graduate school. Service was good. Kalina was right about the servers. If I was 10-15 years younger and single I'd be back almost every day just for them. The space was nice but there is one flaw. The bathrooms are located downstairs with the kitchen/prep area. This wouldn't be a big deal except there is a narrow staircase. So you have to play chicken/who goes first in order to get back up. I did actually see some burnt ribs that could have been Kalina's. I"m glad she sent them back because they looked scorched. I might go back and try something else at some point. The ribs actually looked and smelled good that were upstairs.

text: I hate this club. Passionately. I see people complaining about the parking. Thats nothing compared with the sheer FILTHINESS of this venue! In your least favorite, least expensive clothes in your wardrobe, because your shoes and pants at least will become a disgusting mess. The bathroom - NAUSEATING. I have seen shit on the floor (as in feces, not random garbage)! So along with that is of course the expected pools of urine and the occasional puddle of vomit. Even with ear plugs in, I usually hear ringing in my ears for a good 24 hours after I've left. It is oh-so-hot inside. I would not be surprised if the building lacks any [working] ventilation. This venue has potential - its large, has tons of rooms, and can even accommodate a couple outdoor areas. But its really just a huge mess. The cess-pools they call hot tubs? They need to be gotten rid of. I stay away from here at all costs. Only a very few DJs can drag me here anymore, usually at an event thrown by the Local 13 crew. And I never leave happy. Guess I can't learn my lesson. Local 13 recently brought Paul Van Dyk to a venue in the Navy Yard called the Philadelphia Cruise Terminal. 3000 capacity, better sound, impressively clean (even in the bathrooms!!) -- despite the fact there were only 2 areas here, I know I would be ALOT happier if they started throwing their large annual events (Bang!, Whistle) there. text: I landed in St. Louis at 2 p.m. My friends were at the airport ready for my arrival. I hopped into the car and off we drove into downtown. I was like hey guys where is that arch thing. They were like wait you'll see it soon "Its the gateway to the east or west I think" one of my friends said and I started laughing so hard. So finally we arrived and we drove around and it was pretty empty but I guess people don't do monuments on a Wednesday afternoon. So we could not find parking because we're retarded and finally we stopped and asked like a cop and he was like there is tons of parking see the cobble stone park anywhere. So all of us turned and bam tons of parking!!! haha. So we parked and made our way to the arch the walk requires a little effort not that much but its a lot of stairs. We finally arrived and we fooled around for a bit till we decided to go in and check out the museum and let me tell you it was uninteresting. I guess they have some cool stuff but it was all very bland. Next I was like hey I heard you can go to the top is it true? All of us were unaware that there is a trolley type/escape pod thing that goes to the top for like 15 bucks. OK well my friends were broke and I just didn't want to pay. I was feeling cheap haha but some how one of my friends swindle three free tickets to the top. Let me tell you nothing is better then free stuff. OK so the museum is underground and to catch the escape pod i call it because it looks like one. You have to go down even lower. We finally arrived and you have to watch a super boring video about the gateway arch. Then the pods come OK if your claustrophobic I'm warning you its nothing going to be fun for you at all. So if you feel like you have to go up get the seat that is pretty much alone. You get the most space and it feels normal. If not you're SOL and have to get the cramped sides that have two seats and are super close to each other. The ride to the top is bleak to say the least because you have no view. Except the occasional view of the emergency ladder well that also goes to the top of the arch. So like canned sardines we arrive and pop out of the can. You have to walk up some more stairs and bam you're at the top. 600 and something ft in the air. OMG THE VIEW IS AMAZING!!!!!!!!!!! The place was much empty and we stayed for a bit and took pictures that I will upload soon. St. Louis was an absolute blast. I highly recommend it and the Mississippi river is dirty! I don't understand why Samuel Clemens liked the thing so much.

text: I love the Monon Community Center! If you live in Carmel it is a true bargain. I love the fitness center and find the staff professional and courteous. IIt is also very clean. The outdoor aquatic center can be a bit over crowded on very hot days and weekends (and don't go in mid-afternoon on Tues and Thurs because of the camp kids!). Otherwise, it is a really nice place to hang out, especially if you have children under the age of 14. Other than the lifeguards, I don't see too many older teens there. The indoor aquatic center is a nice break from a dull winter. Oh I should add, if you are a true lap swimmer, use the indoor facility. Rules on how to lap swim are posted and the serious lap swimmers inside adhere to the etiquette. Outside the rules aren't posted. text: One of my friends came down from Moscow for a few days this week, and wanted to meet up for dinner. His one stipulation was that we get something we couldn't get in Moscow. That doesn't narrow it down much but we decided to head for Chef Roland's. I think it was around 8 pm or so, which is apparently after they close during the week (which I didn't know at the time). We rolled into the parking lot and saw chairs stacked on the tables. Disappointed, we started to back out when one of the restaurants employees knocked on the passenger-side window and invited us to come in anyway. Normally I feel like a jerk when I make restaurant staff stay late, but they were so damn inviting that I couldn't say no. Chef Roland came out and sold us on blackened prime rib (for the three friends who were with me) and blackened catfish (for me!). You always start out the meal with a bowl of gumbo or jambalaya. Both are exceptional, but I like the jambalaya a little bit more (it's tomato-based and a touch spicier. Mmmm). The serving sizes are generous and come with numerous sides. The catfish (which I think was a special) was coated in a delightful spice rub and cooked perfectly, and my three friends seemed to enjoy the prime rib immensely. After our meal Chef Roland tried to sell us on dessert (which all sounded amazing) but I always leave that place too full to function, let alone properly enjoy bread pudding with Chef's own whiskey sauce. This place is the perfect place to go on cold nights when all you need is some spicy soul food in your belly. A Star for staying open an hour later just to serve four more people. Chef Roland, you're amazing!

text: My first time at the French Quarter Festival. I'd been to Jazz Fest several years in a row and although I like that, I think I prefer the French Quarter Festival. Highlights (why I prefer it to Jazz Fest): - It's located all around the French Quarter: Bourbon and Royal streets, Jackson Square, by the waterfront. and the Mint Building. It's fun that it's in the actual downtown and that it's spread out a bit. - Unlike Jazz Fest which is a big open fairground area, on hot days, you also can also find shade in several areas and a breeze by the water. - Only local bands can play it. I like that it's more New Orleans focused than Jazz Fest which can have everything from Stevie Wonder to Jimmy Buffet to LL Cool J. Lots of brass and zydeco here: more voices and sounds you can't hear just anywhere. - Lots of musical stages all around so you can easily sample a bunch of different bands. - You can walk there from your hotel (Jazz Fest is a cab ride). - If you want to do other things than the festival, there are all the normal Quarter things to do there was well: get a daiquiri, shop, sit down in a bar, etc. - Lots of food booths! Awesome food too represented by several local restaurants. My faves were the sausage pepper and onion sandwich (like an open calzone almost), crawfish sausage, shrimp etoufee, and best bbq turkey leg I've ever had. Yum yum yum! - Food is good prices too: most stuff is $5 and have generous portions and great quality. - Admission is free :-) - It's sponsored by Coca-Cola: my cola of choice. You have to see my Sunnyvale collection of Coke collectibles. ;-) And because it had Coke booths, Vitamin water--my favorite hydration beverage of choice--was readily available on those hot days. Lowlights (my flip side to highlights): - The Mint Building area was way too cramped: very small shallow area with iron gates keeping everyone in. - It's craziest on Sunday: longer lines for food and harder to get around I loved it and would definitely go back again. :-) Jazz Fest is fun when you want to see a bunch of popular bands or your favorite performer is on the bill, but if you want to taste more of the local flavor, I'd come to the French Quarter Festival.

The pizza was oily and small for the price that we had to pay. The beer was good but was foamy and almost diluted. Overall, it was just a disastrous experience. I don't know what they are doing when they open this place because their customer service is really poor and the offerings, while look promising, does not match all the hype, not even close. There are better places on campus that offers better customer service and cheaper alcoholic and food options. text: I heard Newman's Natural Carpet Cleaning ad on the radio, and thought, "No way can they do what they advertise." My carpet had been professionally cleaned five weeks ago, looked dull, stained and dead, and I just thought I would have to "bite the bullet" and get new carpeting throughout the house.....very expensive to say the least. When I heard the ad, I thought I would call for an estimate (free!). The owner came out (this is a family run business), and told me he could do wonders with my carpet, explained that the technique he and his wife used was all natural, and gave me a fair estimate. The husband wife team showed up on time, and went to business cleaning the carpet which ended up being brought back to life, all stains gone, no chemical smell and it was dry in about an hour. text: When it comes to Mexican food you don't usually have to high of expectations. Mostly, it's nice to have hot food with some spiciness, free chips and salsa and a decent margarita. All that and keep the plates under $10. On all those fronts Amigo Joe's succeeds. The food was hot, moderately spicy, the chips and salsa were free and they had a decent margarita. The Margarita had just barely enough salt and looked as though the glass had been sloshed around quite a bit before arriving at the table as it was a bit sticky as well. The Salsa was a highlight. Fresh cilantro and onion was visible when poured into the dipping bowl. The chips were pretty average, nothing to write home about. The entree's left a lot to be desired. I tried the Carne Asada with didn't taste like Carne Asada at all. It was steak, but it was tough and had very little flavor. I also tried a couple of the dishes around me and the only thing that seemed to have any real flavor was the Steak Chimichangas. Overall, I'd go back if others were insistent. It's not a bad place, just nothing really stood out enough to make me want to seek it out another time. And with endless amounts of good cheap mexican in town, it's hard to justify going for a very basic cheap meal at this place when there are other better options. I would also like to say that I was unimpressed with the service. The waitress just seemed like she was in a rush and barely took the time to listen to our order. It reflected later when one of us was brought the wrong dish. Not a huge deal, but just a bit of a turn off.

text: I'm a graduate student at the University, so there are many times when we hop down University Avenue cruising for places to grab lunch. Frog and Firkin is often that place we wander to only when we've exhausted all the other options on the strip. It's ok. Just ok. The food is at best mediocre. There aren't many choices, and most of those choices are pretty much the same things with different toppings. The wings are alright, the burgers are ok. That should give it a three-star rating in my opinion, but every time I've been there (probably a dozen or so) the service has been frankly abysmal. The waiters and waitresses are pretty much never the same people any time I've been there, and it makes sense because they are so close to the University they probably get a pretty high turnover of staff. If turnover isn't to blame for the lackluster service, then the hiring staff needs to be a little more discerning with who they hire and HOW they train them. The seating outside should be a fantastic option with misters for the hotter months of the year, except the blaring music is frankly annoying. You're lured into the place by the promise of eating an outside lunch with friends only to spend 35 minutes listening to loud, crappy music for a restaurant. My last experience there had a light jazz cover of a Paula Abdul song blaring for 10 minutes that literally made me sick to my stomach before the meal arrived. I asked the waitress to please turn the music down because we couldn't hear each other talk, and she did, but it was turned up probably 3 minutes later by someone else. Isolated light jazz aside, the music is too loud 90% of the time that I've been there. With a theme like "Frog and Furkin," it would seem that you'd get a more publike experience, but it just comes off Junior/Senior University student hangout. Not bad thing in general, just it is was it is. OK.

text: The best thing I had at A La Maison was a delicious bottle of Pinot Noir. That's a pity, considering the restaurant is BYOB. French restaurants are rather rare outside of downtown, so I was delighted to come back from a four month absence to find A La Maison had opened up in my old stomping grounds of Ardmore. I'm a huge fan of French Bistro food, as I worked in one for several years. I brought my wife to A La Maison Friday night, which took some persuasion as my wife doesn't share my love of French food. She just doesn't understand what all the fuss was about. I assured her that she would have a revelation once she had it at a good bistro. Unfortunately, A La Maison is not a good bistro. The decor is sparse but passable, done on a budget but reasonably tasteful. The wait staff was friendly but unpolished. They would benefit from acting slightly more formal and brushing up a bit on their knowledge of the menu. The menu was essentially standard bistro fare, except for an interesting looking smoked salmon tian. I ordered that as an appetizer, only to be told that they were out of it. (At 6:45 on a Friday?) Okay, I'm not that picky, so I went with the pate, to be followed by the nightly special of steak Diane. My wife ordered the house salad as an appetizer and the roasted salmon Dijonnaise as a main course. The pate came with a spot of mustard, some cornichons, and toasted baguette slices. The baguette slices were hard as rocks, so I used the house bread instead. The pate itself was reasonably tasty but not memorable in any way. My wife's house salad was imposingly large, with a light-tasting vinaigrette, palm hearts, pine nuts, and a few other knick-knacks. Like the pate, it was unremarkable, even a little bland. The more glaring problems began with the main course. My wife's salmon was expertly cooked, but it was under-seasoned, and the sauce was sparse and wimpy tasting to boot. It came with sauteed Swiss chard. Technically there was nothing wrong with the Swiss chard, except for the fact that apparently nothing had been done to it other than throwing it in a pan. No shallots, no wine, no vinegar, and no spice of any kind. Hey, Swiss chard is a nice vegetable, but you should at least TRY to do something with it! Similar problems plagued my steak Diane. I had been told it was tenderloin, but I was dismayed that I received the top of the head from the tenderloin, which is the least tasty part. For $28, I would expect a better cut. Just like the salmon, the sauce was sparse and underwhelming. The accompanying mashed potatoes could have come from any diner in Philly, and the spinach was a clone of the Swiss chard, i.e. badly in need of something else to give it a kick. In fact, that was the problem with the entire meal. Nothing had a kick to it. The things that make French food so special, the rich stocks, gobs of butter and cream, wine, fresh herbs, pungent shallots, all seemed to be missing or used extremely sparingly. This isn't rocket science, guys! It's just as easy to make a knock-out batch of creamy mashed potatoes as it is to make a bland batch. The final verdict? As much as I wanted to like A La Maison, I had to agree with my wife's judgment: Not Worth The Calories.
label: NEG

text: On this rainy and overall yucky morning, I had a Seinfeld moment and found parking right outside of the restaurant. How good is that? A good omen for a good breakfast. I was a little surprised that the place had that old school coffee shop character with all that hipster patronage, but it felt warm and a bit frenetic. It was 3/4 full at around 9am. I got the Huevos Rancheros with good guacamole, and an intriguingly smokey and spicy, but nicely light red bean topping which I preferred to the usual heavy and indistinct refried bean glop. I think there were bits of chorizo in the mix. The blue fried corn tortilla was light and crispy and kept its crunch throughout the meal. Only thing I didn't like was that the fried eggs came over hard. Usually like it over easy. Need to ask next time. The home fries were terrific, chunks of piping hot, crisp on the outside and almost sweet on the inside taters. This is the best that America has to offer, I swear. The La Colombe coffee was good and fresh. Service was friendly yet uninstrusive. As I left with my left overs, my car was still out front, with 10 minutes to spare on the meter. Good quick service with exemplary food. Very un-Seinfeld-like.

text: I was taken aback when going into Maggianos last weekend. Much fancier than I expected and felt totally underdressed. The menu is extensive but the waitress told us all meals were meant to be split or would be extra large portioned. I would have preferred normal portions for a cheaper price but I like taking home leftovers so whatever. The food was tasty, but if you want the real Italian experience I would recommend the Hill. One of my favorite things when going for Italian is dipping bread in Olive Oil with Parmesan cheese. The bread came out crispy on the edges and warm and soft in the inside. Dipped in the olive oil, it was a delicious combo. We also ordered an appetizer mussels, diablo style, which came in a garlic tomato sauce. The mussels were good but nothing extraordinary. I would pass next time. Stopped early on the appetizers and bread to save room for my massive entree, the mushroom and veal ravioli. They came 5 large raviolis to half order and were covered in a white creamy sauce with sundried tomatoes. The ravioli was ok, I was looking for more flavor in the filling, kind of bland overall and so I made sure to include the sauce in every bite. My friend ordered the chicken tortellini special which he claimed was really good. We split an order of the side spinach. Just the right texture and seasoned wonderfully, I liked the spinach better than my entree. I know I need to try more on the menu, but I'm not sure I would bother to come back. So many other places to try. The desserts I saw made my mouth water so if anything coming back for coffee and dessert might be an option!

text: This was such a bad experience that I am writing about it years after the actual event! The summer of 2003, I was working in Washington, D.C. and my mother's health was failing on the west coast. She was from Louisiana and, declining with Alzheimer's, talked a lot about wanting to go back and visit. I saved up and we were able to make the trip as a family. Of course, a nice dinner out in the French Quarter was a big part of the trip to New Orleans. I chose this restaurant because my mother thought she knew the family name from Lake Charles and my father remembered that they had dined at this location shortly after they first met. When I waited tables, rule number one was always to take special care of the timing with tables with the elderly and small children. Not only had this staff apparently never thought of such a rule, they seemed intent on ignoring us BECAUSE we had someone elderly with us. After 45 minutes I had to go find a manager to please, please have someone come take our order. I explained that it was getting difficult to keep the party there, my mother's condition and that it actually seemed we were being ignored. I was very nice about it and was begging them to help me since this dinner was an event more than a meal. When the server arrived, he was apparently bent out of shape at having been sent to the table. Another 25 minutes later, when our food arrived, I sincerely believe a salt shaker had been dumped in my dish. text: I was on the plane coming to New Orleans, and struck up a conversation with a friendly gentleman sitting next to me. There was one thing he told my boyfriend and me to do when we got to the city, and that was "go to Mother's." And we did. I was there with two other people, and we went for lunch (I've heard that breakfast is a much different story). We ordered at the counter, I ordered the Turkey Ferdi, and the two guys I was with ordered similar Po-Boys. As we waited for our food, we admired the hundreds of autographed pictures on the walls, and thought to ourselves that this place must really be something if all these famous people came here... When the server came to our table for the first time, she delivered one sandwich, which we would soon learn was the first of many strange errors in our time there. My friend Andy touched the sandwich and decided that this can't be what he ordered (it was soggy and didn't have any gravy on it), the waitress came back, asked if he touched it, and when he said yes, rolled her eyes, huffed, grabbed the sandwich and walked away. Is that all, you ask? Not so much. The waitress then came back with two sandwiches, AND a cup of gumbo and some crawfish etouffee. Remember when I said we just ordered three sandwiches? Yeah. Anyway, we told her that we didn't order these things, and she told us not to worry about it (despite signs saying not to tip the servers, she told us to tip them anyway, and we could keep the side dishes), then walked away and came back with the other sandwich. We decided to try the etouffee and gumbo first, and after each of us had taken two bites of each, ANOTHER waitress came to our table, informed us that we hadn't ordered these items, and took them away. This seemed spiteful, and a total waste of good food, but nonetheless, we had our Po-Boys to dive into, so oh well. These Po-Boys were not what any of us were expecting, given the raving recommendation from plane guy - the meat was dry and the bread was definitely soggy - but we were hungry and ate them anyway. I don't often give something a thumbs down after one experience, but everything that occurred was so backward, that I probably won't go back. Sorry, plane guy, Mother's gets a thumbs down from me. On a higher note, the crawfish etouffee was very good, if not amazing. Woo hoo.

text: Amid the morass of mindless delis now proliferating across the stripmalls of America, two stand out: Which Wich? and Penn Station. Penn Station may be a franchise chain, but (this location at least) feels like a neighborhood deli, perhaps more in the manner of its homebase Dayton, Ohio than Penn Station, NYC. I've never been to a sandwich shop in "Penn Station" but there definitely is more of a "stop looking at me", "hurry up and order" shouting-in-the-kitchen "Yankee" feel to it -- much more than Jersey Mike's, which pales in comparison on both counts of quality and price. It's kind of an appropriate analogy with New York vs. New Jersey. Penn Station's crown jewel is its homemade, handcut french fries and similarly hand-squeezed lemonade: a heavenly duet to satisfy any snacktime craving. For a bigger appetite, the cheesesteaks are great (and the official cheesesteak of the Cincinnati Reds), as is pretty much any sandwich I've had there. Still hungry? Finish up with a fresh-baked chocolate chunk cookie! Advantages: Fresh fries, lemonade, greasy sandwiches, malt vinegar on the condiment bar, neighborly feel Drawbacks: television always on, sometimes surly and/or inattentive service. text: We were visiting friends in Oldsmar who had heard nice things about this place, so we decided to try it. The atmosphere is very warm - lots of dark wood and stone - and the service was attentive and friendly. We weren't as impressed with the food. We decided to share two appetizers. The cheddar-spinach dip was bland and the tortilla chips served with it tasted stale. The guacamole was prepared at the table, so we knew it was fresh, but it lacked zip, and the portion was too small for the $11.00 price tag. My husband ordered his flat iron grill medium-rare. The first one they served was well-done and the second one was practically raw. They finally got it right the third time. He enjoyed the sweet potato fries more than the steak. The glaze on my spit-roasted pork tasted like it had too much bourbon it, and it overpowered the flavor of the meat, but the sweet potato mash was delicious. One of our friends ordered chicken breast stuffed with spinach, goat cheese, artichokes, and sun-dried tomatoes and raved about it. Our other friend was very disappointed with his salmon, which he said was on the dry side. The server suggested we share a couple of orders of tumbleweeds, which are crispy onion straws served with a spicy dipping sauce. They weren't greasy and we all agreed they were excellent. We shared two desserts, fried banana caramel cheesecake, which wasn't as tasty as it sounded, served with vanilla ice cream, and apple-walnut pie, served with cinnamon ice cream, which was okay but nothing special. Our friends mentioned our disappointment to the people who recommended the place, and they said they had been here twice for lunch and enjoyed the burgers and wraps very much. We might try it for lunch the next time we're in the area, but based on our experience we would never make a special trip here.

text: Don't believe the hype. I had been waiting for quite a while to try this place after reading the good reviews here and elsewhere. Both my friend and I are vegetarian, so I was excited that it featured several items sans-meat. Oh, but what a disappointment. I ordered the yuka fries, which arrived cold and slowly. The chipotle sauce was good but the two thimble-sized cups of it were not enough. My rice and beans were very bland and boring. And not even authentic Mexican cheese. Just about five shreds of what looked like American cheese. Seriously, almost no cheese at all. And the beans tasted as if they were right out of a can. My friend got the squash dish, and it looked so unappetizing that when she offered a bite, I declined. Very small portion at that. The prices here are outrageous, definitely priced for tourists. The food was also delivered at different times. The tortillas were not homemade and were more like what I call "Wonderbread" tortillas. White and floury. My friend's mom's soup looked ok but the vegetable garnish looked limp and unappetizing--unripe tomato, wilted greens, bleh. I was actually embarrassed to have wasted their money and appetites here, even though they acted as if they liked it to be polite. There were leftovers and we didn't even take them home. And I love and respect food and almost never let it go to waste, even if it's not so good. Do yourself a favor. For real Mexican, make the drive to Tampa's taco bus. Casa Tina isn't even on par with some of the worst Tex-Mex chains. On the up side, cute decor and nice servers. The salsa was good, chips tasted old and cold, probably from last night's dinner service.

text: Aint State Parks great? First, they are free to get in. Second, Pennsylvania has some great hiking trails Third, The things that do cost money are very affordable Never go to a commercial campsite. They charge sometimes 3 or 4 times more than the State Parks do and the staties are offering the same amenities in a cleaner , safer environment.. Ive singled out Marsh Creek here because weve been going to it frequently this summer. All of the State parks have their plusses and minuses, the plusses of Marsh Creek are the water activities. As you come up park drive you will see the beautiful, sprawling Marsh Creek Lake. Unfortunately, there is no swimming here but you are welcome to bring a boat or rent one of the many watercrafts at the marina. No swimming in the lake but that brings me to the main reason we come here.....the ool notice there is no "P" in it. Lets keep it that way! Seriously, the pool is great. There is a $7 per person fee on weekdays ( maybe more on weekends) If you compare that to the many exclusive and discriminatory swim clubs around, its pretty reasonable. For a public pool, its very well maintained, both in the pool and out. There is something there called the "sprayground", which is a fountain area which is fun for the kids. The pool is well guarded by as many as 6 lifeguards at all times. They have the requisite snack bar ( but they allow you to bring your own food to picnic if you wish). The bathrooms are clean with a shower/changing area included. My only complaint is that there is no extra baby pool separate from the main pool and I get a little skeeved seeing the diapered ones in the same pool as me but when its in the high 90s, I get over it. This place is perfect for us middle class folk, who cant afford to become members of a swim club and are tired of making their kids swim in the creek. So support our State Parks people! Sometimes your tax dollars go towards something worthwhile.

We would have a new room with a working toilet and everything would be fine. .....but it was not to be. We were meeting friends for dinner so we had to leave. When we returned, the same front desk person knocked on our door and told us maintenance had snaked the toilet so it was working now. I wish maintenance had done that after our first call. We thanked him and gave him back the keys to the second room. I was told to talk the front desk the next morning about the situation. The next morning I talked to a new desk clerk about the nonworking toilet and he said he knew about it and the owner had heard and we were told we were required to vacate the premises immediately that morning and we were never going to be allowed to stay there again. I was in shock. We have been staying at hotels on a regular basis, including many Best Western's, with no problems. And during our prior stay at this hotel the front desk person said our file said "really nice people" and how we must have made a great impression. Now, because we were frustrated that we were in a room without a working toilet, we were told we were required to leave. It didn't make sense. We still had two nights on our reservation. This new clerk told us that last night's front desk person relayed to the owner that I had demanded to be compensated for two nights when all I did was ask as a suggestion in frustration. The desk clerk was apologetic and made excuses for the owner telling us he was under stress because of the renovations and also how the main computer system had gone down that night. We asked to talk to both the hotel manager and the hotel owner but we were told neither could be reached and the situation wouldn't change even if they could be reached. There was apparently no way to get this miscommunication undone. He was sympathetic and he did comp us $30 which we appreciated, but there was no way we could connect to the two decision makers, the hotel manager and the hotel owner to get the situation fixed. This is not the way you treat a customer. No one talked to us except the front desk person who was accusing us of demanding something we only asked for in frustration and as a suggestion. Plus, shouldn't a hotel do something more when your toilet doesn't work? The broken toilet wasn't the only problem. The cold water at the faucet only turned off at a precise point that took a while to find. The shower had very low water pressure. And, the next morning, the toilet wouldn't flush again. Plus, we heard another customer complain about how a hotel staff person walked in on them in their room really early in the morning. In the end, the owner did us a favor. We found Pacifica Suites. It is closer to our Goleta destination. The toilets work and work and work!! The rooms are much cleaner. The breakfast is better. The people are nicer. And we are very happy to give them our business - we have many trips we will be making each year to Goleta. Do yourself a favor and don't stay at the Best Western South Coast Inn.

text: The Second Mile Center is a series of second hand stores on one block. They sell everything under the sun, and they have the space to do it. The clothing store is especially huge, but it's not so overwhelming because all the offerings are spaced out in aisles and aisles of racks. The property is a big square with a very high ceiling, so it feels spacious, which is nice. When it comes to quantity, Second Mile takes first prize. When it comes to quality, Second Mile is much lower on the thrift store list. They have a lot of junk in my humble opinion; however, as the owner of Toviah Thrift told me last year, just because I wouldn't buy something doesn't mean that nobody would. There certainly do exist thrifters who aren't concerned with trends, and I'm sure Second Mile gets plenty of those shoppers. While Second Mile has a lot of low quality items, it also has its share of gems. The ratio of crap to gems here is the same ratio as at Toviah Thrift; Second Mile is just a much larger, more organized property. Like TT, SM also had some religious affiliation. Definitely stop by--they have everything under the sun and it's all oh-so-wallet-friendly. Racks and racks of shoes, dresses, blazers, handbags, AND this place has sales from time to time. A thrift store holding a clearance sale? Yes, they do. Once my mom and I came here on Xmas eve and they entire inventory was being sold at half off. Pretty crazy. This block is positively magical when the weather is warm. Tons of trees, lovely Victorians in the area, not too much traffic. With the SM folks on the block, it's the type of place where you'd want to sit down and just chill for a while. There's just something about South 45th Street. When you visit, cross the street to visit the used furniture store with furniture that talks to you. Someone here tags the items with papers that - well, talk to you! Sometimes it's a story, sometimes it's general commentary, sometimes it's a snazzy one-liner. Even if you have no need for gorgeous vintage items that could never fit in your apt, come visit them to see what they have to say.

text: I sooooo wanted this to be good... I live only a few blocks away and wanted nothing more than to have this style of food within an accessible walk from home. I won't dedicate this whole review to bashing the food and just note that the atmosphere was great and had a very cozy and unique vibe going for it. But the food... The peking duck buns were dry as was the peking duck. Buns should be moist and warm and these were cold and dry. The hoisen was so thick, sweet and viscous though that it totally covered the dryness of both the buns and the duck (not in a good way). You could have substituted anything in place of the buns and the duck and gotten the same flavor when mixed with this hoisen. I didn't see the pork belly soup on the menu online when recently checking and maybe for a good reason. Pork belly is one of my favorite food groups. It's on a pedestal with decadent rich foods like foie gras and sweetbreads. This pork belly reminded me more of jello jigglers. One big cube of gelatinous fat, and the meat was even dry, a miraculous acheivement surrounded by all that unrendered fat and served inside of a liquid! Not to mention that we found a piece of the metal dish scrub pad wires in ours, which is as understandable as findng a hair in your food, it[s just something that inevitably happens in restaruants, it was just insult to injury. The braised beef brisket noodle soup was the highlight because the beef was good. But alas the noodles were not stirred during the boil and were mostly still stuck together lending an unappealing undercooked noodle that was inedible (not al dente, undercooked). We didn't try dessert. We couldn't justify paying for it at this rate. Both my wife and I work in restaurants and know that kitchens have their bad nights and that mistakes sneak under the radar which is why we understand the scrub pad wire which would have never stopped us from coming back. However when you see that the pork is not cooked properly and you still put it in the soup, and when you can obviously see that the noodles were not stirred and therefore not cooked properly and yet you still served it, it shows us that you just didn't care. We will consider a revisit, however not until we hear from many that this restaurant has changed it's course.

text: Biggest let down ever on the biggest bar night in STL. It seems like whenever I walk into this place it is a big disappointment. I was told that this would be the place for the night last Wednesday. Aside from the dreadful weather I thought getting there about 6:30pm to start my Thanksgiving bender would be early enough. After a $25 cab ride (mistake number 1) to the location I approach the inside and flag down a waitress to see if I can put my name down on a list for a table since I'll be having about 8-10 people following me here shortly. She explains that's not how it works and that I'm on my own basically to fight the rest of the yuppie bar crowd for a spot. Dumped next into the bar area from the door I'm immediately swarmed by bald 40-somethings in bad sweaters and miller lites trying to reclaim their college livers while their trophy wives and 20 something kids look on at how much of a fool dad looks around all his friends. If I had an alarm for "GET OUT NOW" it was blaring as loud as the tornado sirens were later in the evening (mistake number 2). Bartender sees me, immediately takes my order, grab my drink and start scouting tables large or large enough for my fellow drinkers. Spot a table, center of the restaurant, beautiful TV with the Blues game just about to start ANNNNND reserved. Ok, I can't put my name down but someone was able to call ahead and reserve a table? I thought I put on my best Kirkwood resident impression but apparently not. Drink is halfway down, time to head back to the bar. 3 or 4 guys, not bar backs but guys who apparently work there stand at the receiving area chatting as I try to flag down the bartender again. One of the "guys" takes my drink order and gets it for me. Wow it is weak and a diet, not looking good. So looking for tables has now turned into who is finishing their meals? Found two prospects right next to the bathrooms, great! Room to stand, can still watch the game, friends still haven't arrived and I can grab a table before they get here and be a hero and hopefully salvage some of this terrible evening. Waiting patiently for the the first table I spot a blond who is on to me. Standing at the edge of the table as the couple moves to get up I swear I've never seen someone run as fast as this woman did in heels to cut me off. That's ok, I got the next one which, was probably the better option towards the back since there was lighter traffic around there. Friends arrive, waitress was epic and took great care of our group the rest of the night we were there. Booze was flowing, life was good. Gets to be about 8:00pm when I was told that group for the reserved table was supposed to arrive and 8:30 rolls around and they finally show up. Thought it was funny because this group was all under 21 and the waitress who was serving them was none to pleased to be serving iced tee and water all night. I was a bit annoyed I lost prime bar position for a booth too small for my group. All in all, this place is way too crowded and small to handle the amount of people that were in there that night. text: Curiosity always niggles when a new restaurant opens in the small borough of West Chester, especially when it opens within a space that was previously occupied by one of my favorite cool-blue jazzy spots in town, Vincent's. Boyfriend Mike and I watched with increasing interest as the renovations went on, and finally decided to mosey on over the other night... Well, it was one of the most disappointing dinners I've had in recent memory, almost verging into 'Kitchen Nightmares' territory. It pains me to see such a great space wasted on such an inadequate enterprise. Upon perusing the menu, we settled on burgers, because...well... who can resist ordering something called an Inferno Burger? For variety's sake, I got the Bison Au Poivre burger (13 dollars). Coupl'a apps (mussels and lobster mac & cheese) to round out the order. The wait, for there being two other occupied tables in the upstairs dining area, was pretty arduous, especially considering that they seemed to have the sound-system set loudly on some all-Dave Matthews, all the time channel. The appetizers were fine...the mussels were decent and the mac and cheese creamy and generously sized.... it was more flavored with the essence of lobster rather than teeming with meaty bits of it, though. However, the burgers were a supreme disappointment for many reasons: In fact, I'm not really sure what the worst offence to taste and decency was, there were so many. *A shred of wax paper stuck to the bottom of the dry, dense bun on Mike's burger (!!!). *The fact that he specifically asked for the lettuce, tomato and onion not to appear on the burger....and lo & behold there arrived a heaping pile of anemic iceburg ribbons, a watery tomato slice and onions on the top bun. ("Oh yeah, I *asked* him to take them off, sorry", the waitress said later. Darling dear, then why did you originally present the food as it was, and then scurry off? Silly waitress.) *We had to wait for 5 minutes or so to entice Chatty Cathy* away from the table across the way she was jabbering on with, just to ask for catsup. *The burgers themselves were mediocre at best. I sort of liked the peppery charred outer "crust" of sorts on mine, but the meat inside was drier than I would've expected. Let's put it this way: it was NOT worthy of it's 13 dollar pricetag. But my boyfriend got the worse plate of food...the consistency of the burger was that of your worst TJI-Applebees-Ruby Tuesday's fare. A charred-black outer crust enclosed dismayingly dry, flavorless meat. Even stuffed with cheese, it couldn't muster up even the hint of moisture. The only saving grace is that Side Bar has (for West Chester) a decent selection of drafts and bottles, as well as a goodly number of drink specials throughout the week. If only we had just come for drinks...! sigh. *not her real name

text: 707 Restaurant The 707 Restaurant - located as its name suggests - at 707 Chestnut was picked by my son for a dinner on a recent visit to Philadelphia. I asked him if it was named for the aircraft (Boeing 707) and as our visit was to prove, there was some semblance of association in that the quality of the food was reminiscent of old time airline fare but far more expensive. But if you like overpriced food in a plastic trendy setting, it just may be your cup of tea. We, four of us, started with the Cheese of the day. text: The Masonic Temple is a gloriously kitschy attraction that rivals the Mütter and Eastern State in weirdness, and it's hiding in plain sight, right across the street from City Hall. Built in the 1860s as the grand lodge for the state of Pennsylvania's many masonic lodges, the Temple is filled with a repetitive series of meeting rooms that each pay homage to the stonemason's craft: there's a Morrocan Room, a Renaissance Room, a Corinthian Room, an Ionic Room, and a positively psychedelic Egyptian Room. Some of these rooms have stone and tile details, and the main hallway is mainly marble,though many of the theme rooms feature painted plaster. The Masonic Temple is an architectural candyland, offering a bizarro tour of how elite 19th-century Americans viewed other cultures, and a peek into the mysterious, kinda-creepy, kinda-laughable world of the Masons. You do have to take a tour (I think full admission is $8), as they won't let you wander. My guide was a funny and likeable mason who seemed more interested in chatting up one of the women on the tour than telling us about the building. But he was refreshingly frank when asked about the Masons and their history, and he had some good one-liners. I'm not sure I'd join his club, but it was fun to visit.

text: Tropicana Field is Major League Baseball at its worst. I have to believe it's the single worst major league baseball park in the whole country. In fact, the last time I went to the Yankees/Rays game here, I sat 4 rows behind home plate. My seat was one of 5 seats in that row, and my fellow Yankee fans and I couldn't stop talking about how much we'd have to pay for similar seats at Yankee Stadium. * It's huge, which means there are plenty of concessions and things to do. * It's a home of the Tampa Bay Rays, the biggest surprise in Major League Baseball in 2008. Now, I have to call 'em like I see 'em: * It's a dome, so . . . 'nuf said. Baseball in the dome is weird enough, without a depressing gray roof to look at. Just ask the outfielders who can't see the balls hit high in the "air." Besides, any ballpark with ground rules like this one: "A batted ball that hits the catwalk, lights or suspended objects and remains on or in the catwalk, lights or suspended objects in fair territory is a fair ball and it shall be called a double" should be torn down immediately. * It's never sold out, which means you can always hear that heckler from behind home plate. Mr. Szasz (pronounced "sass," fittingly) became world famous for his unique heckling antics. It's fun to read about him in Sports Illustrated, but at the ballpark it's just plain annoying. * It's huge, which means it's even more depressing, gray and hollow than one can imagine. * It's a home of the Tampa Bay Rays, still the worst franchise in the history of Major League Baseball despite their 2008 success of historic proportions. This place deserves only one star, if that. But they're awarded an additional star for housing a Tampa MLB franchise that is NOT the Giants. For those of you who forgot (or didn't know), my hometown San Francisco Giants back in 1993 were a few days away from relocating to Tampa. I would not have liked that.
