text: Hands down the best BBQ in St. Louis. I'm from West Tennessee and fairly picky about my BBQ. I've eaten it all over the country (in fact we once made a cross country road trip stopping at every BBQ place we could find). I'd say the ribs at Pappy's are the best that I have ever had anywhere! The pulled pork and brisket rank very near the top. Sides are generally tasty, though I like mayo based slaw and this ain't. Get the sweet potato fries. Be prepared for long lines at lunch that move fairly quickly. It is just that good.
label: POS

text: Well, they're open on Christmas day, which is credit to their business model since every tourist in the French Quarter needed somewhere to eat in the afternoon before going about the rest of their Christmas--myself and my husband included. Any place that has a plate of their food either shellacked or plastic wrapped outside to entice people inside is not a place you go for good food. Since my husband and I don't like tomato juice, we did not sample their Bloody Marys--just beer and water for us. I will say that the green bean on top of the Bloody Marys and the spicy olive juice mixed in looked good, but the tomato juice part was provided by a jug of mix. I had a plate of their mushy jambalaya and my husband had the red beans and rice with grilled andouille which was actually not so bad. Service was a little slow despite having lots of wait staff on, but the place was busy. Our waiter, perfectly nice, waited to run our card until he helped the bartender stock some of their Bloody Mary ingredients..strange considering he had already picked up our card with the bill. Why not just run it right away?
label: NEG

text: Skip the tasting menus if you want to find value. The foie gras 3 ways is good enough. Its hard to go wrong with foie. Venison sausage and white bean cassoulet was good, but unimpressive. Venison is a lean meat, so they could have done something to keep the sausage feeling moist. The cassoulet was a little mushier than I'd want, but very well seasoned. It was topped with panko/pork cracklin mix, but the cracklin was wasted. Good execution, but poor dish design. Sugar and spice duckling was nicely seasoned, but didn't come out as warm as it should have. This is supposedly the signature dish at August, so I'd try it again. We went for a late service, so maybe the kitchen was just being lazy. I suspect this dish could be awesome. The duck came with a canelle of marscapone grits, and a dab of quince jam. The marscapone grits were perfect. Gnocchi with truffle and crab was delicious. The homemade gnocchi was light and excellently crafted. The sauce was rich but not overbearing. The crab seems to have been thrown on because people think crab is expensive and good, but added no value to the dish. Crab in the presence of really rich truffle and cream ended up being just a texture in the mix. Again, I'd say good execution, poor dish design. Pork belly slices on a garlic custard pastry served in an oyster and bacon broth. Too much going on in this dish. Let me preface this with the fact that I LOVE fat. I never shy away from eating fat, but it has to be done well. The pork belly slices were just fat, not no taste or texture. They were served with a rich oyster broth with oysters and bacon on a buttery pastry. It was too many rich elements on the plate for the fat to be just untreated fat. That said, the oyster and bacon soup was outstanding. The bacon pieces were house smoked, in the top 5 bacons I've ever had. Separate that component out and that dish would be awesome. Excellent food, but its always a little disappointing to have a good meal that could clearly be so much more.
label: POS

text: Come here to take gorgeous pics on the river -- and then leave. It's the touristy-est of tourist traps. This is New Orleans' version of Chicago's Navy Pier -- but not quite as cool as Navy Pier. Overpriced shops and kiosks, awful food court -- but the views of the river, wow.

text: This is, by far, the best place to workout in Tucson if you are A) a real person and B) get a little wet at the thought of being able to watch your own personal cable TV while you do your cardio. For $20/month, with no contracts, and a modest sign-up fee, the price can't be beaten. There are plenty of cardio machines (five rows of ellipticals, three rows of treadmills, two rows of stair machines, and two rows of bikes). Even at peak hours, it's easy to hop on a machine. About 1/3 of those machines have the aforementioned TVs. I'm convinced that being able to watch baseball games, lame VH1 reality TV, and cable news is the main reason I've been able to lose weight. The "real person" factor is another big selling point of Gold's. Sure, there's a dude with a mullet, a 1980s sweat suit, and the mien of Chuck Norris who I always see there. There are also at least a few guys who work out there that more than likely shoot bovine growth hormone directly in to their scrotums. The vast majority of the people I see at Gold's are just regular folks, though. This is no hoity-toity, huge weight-pumping, scary, judgmental gym. The people are friendly and leave you alone. The only reason Gold's doesn't get the full five stars from me is that the machines seem to break a lot and take a long time to be repaired. Plus, the place has been in a perpetual state of renovation since I joined in February of '08. Something is always out of order or being torn down and redone - never in such a way that there is ever significant inconvenience, but it's still worth noting.
label: POS

text: Came yesterday with my boyfriend and 2 friends and I left somewhat disappointed. I ordered some green mussel appetizer and a bowl of vegetable noodle soup. The mussel appetizer came out and it was dry and overcooked. You could clearly tell that they mussels were simply steamed and then had a chili-tomato sauce poured over it. Unflavorful and dry. The noodle soup I had specified to be vegetarian, but yet it still came out in a beef broth. It wasn't until we spoke to somebody higher-up (the servers are hispanic and don't seem to understand English) came out and offered to remake it. I said that it was alright, they didn't have to, but the boyfriend insisted on it. So they made me another one but it was just unflavorful and anyway, by that time everyone had finished eating.. at the very least, they do put a whole lot of vegetables on there unlike other vegetable noodle soups I've had elsewhere. Yet I guess in a noodle soup, it really is the broth that makes all the difference, and this one was simply just soy sauce in water (and that is what the chef said). I can understand if they don't specialize in vegetable noodle soup, but if you're going to offer it, at least make it decently. Otherwise, don't offer one.. Still, I do appreciate that the chef (or, whoever that was) remade it for me. It's the effort that counts, I guess. It was my first time here, and it wasn't the worst place I've gone to. It's just that everything else I sampled here off my boyfriend's order like the salt baked squid was just normal like any other place in Chinatown too. So, that coupled with a wrong order and an unappetizing starter gives it just 2 stars. I won't hurry to come back here anytime soon.

text: Assholes. Okay... so I, and about 125 other family members go to Santa Barbara for my sister's wedding. A crap load of us stayed at this hotel... you'd think since they're getting a lot of business from my immediate family alone, we'd have been treated just a little bit better. On the second day of our stay, we come back to our hotel and find a bunch of random stuff that wasn't ours, in our fridge! After freaking out, I described what I found to the front desk and they stared at me with a blank look on their faces, "Well, what do you want us to do about it?" Um... HELLO!!! Someone was in our room! I ended up speaking to security because they were too scared to contact management, and he was convinced I was making all this up to get a discount and called me a liar!!! I was totally enraged! I told him I felt unsafe if someone else had access to our room and that I wanted to either get another room or get a refund and move to another hotel... he didn't get it. After 2-1/2 hours of going back and forth, he finally came upstairs and then realized I wasn't lying... reluctantly apologized... brought the food down and the stupid boys at the front desk put 2 and 2 together... the housekeeping was to transfer this all from one room to another... and accidentally put stuff in our room instead... but of course we didn't know this at the time so we thought our space was totally invaded and didn't feel safe thinking someone else was in our room!!! So although it was a very simple mistake, it caused a lot of drama, frustration, screaming... oh and we missed the dinner with the bride... and couldn't find a place to eat for dinner where the kitchen was still open until about midnight!! Finally spoke to the manager the next day and of course, he was only going to say sorry and let it be... but I made sure he got our side of the story and he agreed to compensate us for our trouble... so we got $120 back and a late check out. Bleh. And if that dramarama wasn't bad enough... my other sister's room at the hotel was an oven... a/c didn't work and they said maintenance couldn't do anything about it. The pillows... well you might as well have been using a piece of paper under your head... And if you got home passed 11pm... you were shit outta luck for parking. This place was clean... but wow, they suck ass. Never again!

text: To say that I know and love Persian food is an understatement. The first thing that I look for when I move or take a long vacation is a good Persian restaurant. I had high hopes for this place based on the reviews here and elsewhere. For those who like authentic traditional Persian fare, you will be disappointed. The kabobs are good and well cooked, however the saffron rice is too oily and buttery. For me, buttery tasting saffron rice is an absolute deal breaker, and ruins the meal. It should be light and fluffy, not oily. The other traditional persian offerings (ghormeh sabzi, fesenjan, Kashk-O-Bademjan) all were bland, too oily and disappointing, This restaurant seems to cater to an "americanized" palate. It is not bad, just not truely traditional. I could go on, but you get the idea. I gave this place several chances and each time it disappointed. It is also inconsistent. Go for the kabobs, skip the rest. I will not be back.

The sauce- THE SAUCE. It is the right mix of sweet and tangy but holds it own. The last big plus is the cheese, it melts the way that cheese on a pizza should melt, it's not goopy and it doesn't taste weird when you pick it off the pizza to eat it by its self. I have always had it delivered so I cannot say what it's like to actually sit and eat there but if they can deliver it without any issues I would assume it would be the same.

text: It's hard for me to understand the rave reviews about this place. I think the food quality is decent, but it sure isn't GREAT. I think it's not really a great value, and seems kind of like an amateur operation. Their ordering process seems a bit inefficient. You order and pay at the register, then shuffle over to the employees who are actually cooking the meat and assembling the pitas. Where they then ask you what you just ordered. You're asking me? I ordered it over there--ask the guy who took my money 20 seconds ago. It just screams 'amateur' is all. Hell, even Subway can figure this one out. Why can't you? Food quality, not bad. They have a decent selection of fillings that apparently can just be mixed and matched. And by that, I mean there is NO STANDARD to what goes in what. If I order a gyros pita, should I have to ask for tzatziki and feta cheese? Answer: no. That's what comes standard with gyros. Here, you DO have to ask. Same thing with the spicy chicken pita (I forget the name) but wouldn't you assume that I want.... spicy sauce? Is this concept THAT HARD for this place? I only come here when I have a BOGO coupon (that's Buy one get one free, but the word FREE is implied so the trailing F is unnecessary--it's BOGO and not BOGOF). 7 bucks and change for two pitas seems like the right price point. 7 and change for ONE? Not so much. So after you finish shopping at Whole Foods, drive your Prius on down to Pita Pit and order an alfalfa sprout pita. And don't forget to ask for alfalfa sprouts in that, otherwise, amazingly enough, they won't be included. Oh, and if you ARE driving a Prius, could you please make sure you know how to turn your car off when your accelerator sticks and your brakes fail? Otherwise Darwin's gonna getcha. "The driver couldn't figure out how to turn off the car as it was accelerating, then the car hit a wall and burst into flames". If you're too stupid to turn off your car, thanks for at least cleansing the gene pool by driving a Toyota and killing yourself.

Old Nelson is a little bit expensive, which is why I only go here once a week or bi-weekly. Their salads are huge and if you get dressing on the side, you can maybe make them last a day. They also have cold cases with greek yogurt and hummus, which are both healthy additions to lunch. I don't know what kind of mayo they use on their sandwiches but it is by far the best mayo I have ever tasted.

text: $11.00 for FROZEN YOGURT!!! OVERPRICED and doesn't do a thing for your taste buds. It makes Coldstone Creamery look like the deal of the century. Not only that you have no clue how much it weighs til right before you pay! Are you kidding me? And if you want a smoothie add another $1.00! Ha, that is absurd, it costs an extra $1.00 to throw in a blender? So i did an experiment. Two of my friends do like this place however they stand alone. I've heard many a conversation about people that got a huge sticker shock at the register. text: Cafeteria food at its finest. I know that sounds a bit odd, since the word connotes all the mystery meat and scoop of strange mashed potatoes memories of our high school times, but I think there is some kind of Hoosier or midwestern tradition of piling in the van and entering these kinds of establishments --after church on Sunday, say, or a gathering. What an array of food! All of it freshly made, so there's nothing here that's industrialized. Those spuds are real spuds in the mashed potatoes, so no fear that this stuff came out of a box. You grab your tray, and your utensils and after you have passed the dessert station first (yes!) you park yourself next to the entree station. See the whole roast beef? The fried chicken? text: My wife and I were in town for a golf trip to Sandpiper and we stopped at The Habit on Sunday evening on the way home to O.C. as it was so highly rated. This is a burger stand with only outdoor seating at small tables. You order from one window, pick up from another winder, and help yourself to the soda dispenser that is cut out from what used to be another window on the side of the building. We both ordered the #1 combo, the standard burger with fries and a drink. We added cheese to the burgers and substituted onion rings for one order as they were also so highly recommended. The food came out and I will say that everything was piping HOT, I had to let the burger cool down for a few minutes before eating. The burgers come wrapped in paper and the cheese was oozing off the sides of the burger. I so wanted the first bite to be out of this world as almost all the reviewers had noted but it was just OK. The meat patty was a good size and while I prefer medium rare, they only cook their burgers medium. The burger was closer to medium well done with no traces of any pick flavorful meat, it was overcooked and too dry for my taste. Also there was no fat dripping down your hands that to me is one of the telling signs of a great burger. It had a slight charbroiled taste but nothing any more special than a Carl's Jr. burger. We ordered grilled onions but it looked like they only saw the grill for a short period of time as they were still raw when we bit into them. The lettuce was shredded but the sauce was not that special. On to the fries, nothing to shout about - fairly average. Then onto the onion rings, again nothing to shout about - they tasted like your normal onion rings that come out of the freezer. I will say the location in Goleta is a college town and there were some co-eds clad in cut off shorts that enhanced the ambiance. But that did not make the food taste any better. After we finished eating I looked at my wife and asked her what she thought and she said it was OK, nothing special or memorable. To say that we were underwhelmed is an understatement. I would say the burgers and fries at both In & Out and Islands are FAR superior to The Habit. Perhaps I caught the place on and off night but unfortunately I have to say O V E R R A T E D!! I would rate The Habit a 3 but I am giving it a 2 because of the expectations placed by all the other reviewers. I am dumbfounded that this is the highest rated Yelp restaurant in Goleta.
label: NEG

text: I went in for a late breakfast on one Saturday morning since I have heard nothing but good things about this place so I decided why not. The location was not in my favorite part of town. It's like you don't exist because they won't get a portion of the tip. After my waiter had gone to check on my order, another waiter saw me and actually checked to make sure that I had everything that I needed. I was almost blown away. I ordered the Smoked Salmon Eggs Benedict with the breakfast potatoes. No mimosas for me that morning. I didn't particularly enjoy the salmon that was on top but that's just my personal issue with salmon sometimes but after removing that it was almost perfect but those potatoes were to die for. I want to head back to this place with some close friends on a Sunday for the jazz. I liked it. I'll be headed back.

The waitress asks how everything is and I tell her it tastes great but funny there is no chicken in the soup. She checks with the cook and he says they put it through a food processor to "enhance the flavor" I then notice chicken granules like sand at the bottom as if a wonton broke open. She says thats just the Noshville way. I replied "Sweetheart, I dont mean to be rude but can I tell you why there is no chicken in the soup? Because chicken costs money. text: Summary: Pretty darn good pizza. I ventured out for lunch today with co-worker Damon. We had no idea where we were headed, but ended up in Soulard. Speciality pizzas ($25 - $27) include the Boss (pepperoni, sausage, mushroom, onion, bell pepper, black olive and garlic), The Garden State (bell pepper, spinach, mushroom, onion and tomato), The Soprano (pepperoni, italian sausage, meatballs, ham and bacon), Old Blue Eyes (ricotta, garlic, mozzarella, parmesan, and topped with EVOO), The Good Fella (extra steak, bell pepper, onions, mushroom and EVOO), and the Jersey Style (smoked ham, tomato, onion, hot peppers and garlic). I suggest 1) Going here on a empty stomach-- not empty as in you have 1/4 tank left in your car, but when you're running on EMPTY, hungry. Unless we're talking about pizza, foods generally are best fresh, so why not waste your money and eat as much as fresh food as you can instead of having it microwaved and soggy! 2) Stop eating when you're full and take the rest home. You can always have leftover food the next day or so. As I've been eating healthier, I come to appreciate those dainty places that don't serve greasy food. text: This is the big kahuna of the Russian restaurants of Philadelphia. Don't be deceived by the restaurant designation, the place, like most bigger Russian restaurants, is more of a dance hall with lots of tables to serve patrons with tons of mass produced food from mostly prix-fixe menu. I will start with the good that encompasses my reason for going there regularly (several times each year) for over 10 years. The place is very big, it will seat hundreds of patrons in relative comfort, it has a big stage, powerful sound system, large dance floor, resident band, BYOB, and a good overall layout. This makes it great for weddings, birthday parties and other major events. Since Golden Gate has been around for a longer time and has had more or less stable ownership and workforce, the waiters tend to know their duties, restaurant at full capacity will generate handsome tips. There are very few walk-ins, most business is done by reservations for larger groups with menu setup well in advance. I have not scheduled parties there, but many of my friends have, so I am somewhat of a regular guest who never gets to actually order as prix-fixe "banquet" decision has been made for me well in advance. Now the bad, or the reason why I don't like to schedule events in GG. It is too big. Just too many people at the same time for an enjoyable dining experience. There is next to no intimacy within the table, only few obstructions to view for most of the dining area, some parts are raised up in order for patrons to be better seen. Moreover some tables are mere inches away from large dance floor that does fill up to its gills at times. Band is way too loud and somewhat obnoxious. Talking to person 3 feet away from you is often problematic. If you want to talk in between dishes, best bets are either to go into hallway or even outside. 99% of the songs played are repeating every night, sometimes several times each night. Most of songs are covers and remixes of Russian, European and Italian pop music, mixed in with something slow sang by request, so don't be surprised to hear singing in three or four different languages within mere 10 minutes. And to make it all stand out, few things are sang in a way that would want to make you hear that performance again. Food is mass produced. Menu will have some of the greatest delicacies of European food, seafood, sushi, caviar, foie gras, etc., but don't expect that it will be prepared by several chefs trained in France for many years, for all purposes GG cooks are nameless creatures hidden deep within the kitchen. So if you want to spend big money on foie gras, lobster or sushi, lookup a specialty restaurant in center city or in well off suburbs, GG is not the place for it. Last concern is the regular patrons. You will see all kinds of people on almost every night. Every age group from teens and sweet 16s to elderly celebrating quadruple bypasses and 50th wedding anniversaries. One thing for sure, everyone dresses to impress and everyone dresses about the same. While elderly are a problem only on dance floor and sometimes with long addresses to birthday boys and girls (including self-made poetry), the under-aged crowd is a different problem. There is no drinking control there, its 100% BYOB, so expect wildly drunk teenagers. There is no dress code there either, so expect very slutty looking girls. When there are lots of booze, teenagers and slutty girls... there are fights, but they end fast. Lastly dress code for most others. Men in suits, women in black dresses, other colors make it look like a reenactment of Pleasantville. End result, its doable, it is still a great place for a huge party, but for majority of dining out with handful of friends, this is just not the spot.
label: NEG

text: I've been to parks all over Nashville, and it's possible that none of them are individually as good Charlie Daniels Park in Mt. Juliet. Sure, if taken together, the Nashville Parks offer a whole lot more, but they're spread across a county. Charlie Daniels has all the neat features of Centennial Park without the problems. It feels like a community feature rather than a destination point for tourists, it has a football field for the high school. It has an indoor community center with an indoor basketball arena. But those are there for organized activity. For the family, there's an excellent "Planet Playground" for both under three and larger children. They have several tennis courts, and wisely turned a couple of them into a small skate park. They have an outdoor basketball court, a sand volleyball court, several covered pavilions with picnic tables and grills, and an outdoor stage "amphitheater." Every now and then, you find something new, like the pirate ship or the jogging track. There's a lot to like about the park, and if your family is there and you need to kill an hour, it's a nice place to go.
label: POS

text: I really was excited about visiting you, Johnny Apples, after passing by many times and reading your on line menu. I really wanted to love you, I came in with a very hungry belly and a heart filled with anticipation. Our server was so sweet, as I twist my finger into my dimple. She was a petite, cutesy blond with sunglasses adorning her head. She was sugar & spice and everything nice, but dumber than a box of rocks! She could not answer one question, without running to the kitchen or manager. There is no drink menu or tents, but they will make just about anything you have in mind. Their house Chardonnay is a California Barefoot, which I love and has won several Gold medals. With four choices of where we could dine, be it the Pub, which also features it's own menu, as well as the dining room menu, a patio, a deck or in one of the beautiful dining rooms, we opted for the latter. We started off with their signature Crab Bisque which was a delectable bowl of some of the best bisque I have ever had and perfectly laced with sherry. We each ordered own own half dozen of Clams Casino, which were loaded with bacon, green pepper, onions and tough diced clams. They would have been good, if the clams were tender. I had originally ordered Oysters Rockefeller, but they were out. My plate came out with a nice sized strand of dark hair. I was brave, removed it, did not complain and ate most of my clams. Next we shared Seafood Spring Rolls, which were in house made and filled with shrimp, scallops, crab, bok choy, cabbage, carrots and seasonings. These were very good and served with a wasabi sauce and a teriyaki glaze. Our meals came with your choice of soup or salad and a potato & veggie or pasta. The salads were nice and decorated with shaved carrots, which I love. The dressings are homemade, but they forgot to put the blue cheese in mine. Hubby had an incredible Dijon, honey dressing, not at all sweet. Once again, I had a hair on my plate, still not saying one word, I dove in. Hubby had the large cut of Prime Rib, which would have been a small cut anywhere else. He ordered it rare to medium rare. It came out as a very fatty cut of ice cold medium well beef. He said the flavor was very good, but it was roasted yesterday and leftover to serve. Guys have a prime rib sandwich special when this happens, do not serve old overcooked cold meat to your guests. I had inquired if they had Bearnaise sauce, before making my choice. When she returned from the kitchen to explain they did in fact have it, I ordered the Filet Mignon. This is funny now, I am laughing, when my Filet came out with a pitcher of a beautiful Bearnaise sauce on the side, the steak was swimming in a rich brown gravy. Hello, my medium rare to medium steak with Bearnaise sauce is medium well and swimming in brown gravy? Something is so wrong with this picture. I chose pasta and it was hard and dry. We finally spoke up! They did take the entrees off the check, but they also lost two potential return guests. Hair is one thing, but you had better get my entree right! Built in 1724, photos of the many era's, for this three story building are posted on the walls. The first photos depict horse drawn wagons, in front of a huge building with a covered porch. I like to believe it was a Saloon downstairs and a hotel filled with tired guests. Once inside you picture a renovated mansion. The set up of the well dressed tables in the various dining rooms, which ultimately connect to one another, with the main dining room hosting a beautiful stone fireplace. The decor is grand with blown glass lamps hanging from the ceilings and matching lights adorning the green walls. The antique molding stands out, as well as the grand stairway leading to another floor. The large outside patio has umbrella covered tables and fresh herbs growing in the large pots. The "Pub" is a very large and inviting room, with tables and a grand sized bar. Johnny Apples, also offers catering http://www.johnnyapples.com/johnny_apples_menu_catering.htm, Banquets and Brunch, lunch & dinner buffets. In addition to all of this, the lower floor features Holland Pizza, which they own and offers anything from pizza, pasta's & sandwiches to wings. Do take note that the menu items on line for Johnny's is different from their new menu, prices have also been lowered. Summing up this review, is my note to the proprietor's of Johnny Apples. You have so much going for you with your location, a beautiful building, which features a pub, patio, deck and gorgeous dining rooms. Your menu selection is well diversified for Continental cuisine. Your food is too hit or miss. Bring in a good chef or train your cooks. Wear hair nets! You will sell more booze and make more money if you promote a selection of cocktails, beer and wine. Become more than the local watering hole. Bottom line, you have a potential gold mine here, but for now, it is not panning out!

text: In that last 10 years, I have adopted animals from a private shelter, a humane society in Pennsylvania and two different ASPCAs. Tampa's Humane Society is by far the cleanest and best organized I've seen. The shelter building does not have an overpowering "animal" smell (so they must be doing a great job cleaning up after all the animals) and its well marked so you can find the type of animal you are looking for. The staff is very friendly and knowledgeable as well. So, all that being said, we decided to adopt 2 cats from here after our own cat passed away. I've always had shelter cats so I expected the usual issues: fleas, worms, possibly a cold. I expected to have to bring them back to be spayed/neutered or have it done at my own expense. I also expected to pay about $80-90 per cat. I was shocked when I saw the medical record on the cats. They each had all their shots (one was a small kitten, so she still needed some boosters, but nothing more), they had been dewormed, treated with flea/tick/heartworm preventative, well fed, socialized and MOST importantly BOTH were spayed (that saved me about $150 a cat). The adoption fee was $50 per cat, but they were running a special and we got both for $50. I took them to my own vet the following day and they were in excellent health overall. I later took a stray that had wandered into our yard over to the feral cat clinic to be spayed and get her shots (then released back into our yard). It was $25 and the spay/neuter facility was very clean as well and felt like a regular vet office.

text: One of my good friends from college has made it her life's mission to get everyone she knows to move to the City of Brotherly Love, and I have to say, she and Philly are making a very good case, particularly West Philly. Everyone lives in these gorgeous old houses with original woodwork and like 9 bedrooms, and they paid what what would MAYBE get you a 600 sq-ft studio here in NY. Maybe. There are all kinds of cool bars and restaurants within walking distance (v important to potential NY ex-pats), and on my most recent visit, we walked to Local 44. Local 44 is the kind of bar everyone wants to be able to walk to. It's laid-back but not divey, and feels like somewhere you'd go knowing that some of your friends and/or neighbors were bound to show up, too. They've got an intimidatingly well-thought out selection of local beers and micro-brews on tap, each listed alongside its alcohol content for those of you who make decisions based on buzz potential. What's not intimidating are the prices--almost all beers were $4 or $5! This...this I like. To wash down my $4 beer, we picked out a couple of snacks from the menu--shrimp tacos and corn dogs (very hip in NY right now, too). Holy moly, these shrimp tacos were some of the absolute best I've had EVER, and this isn't even a Mexican joint! The corn tortillas were warm and fresh (possibly hand made?), the shrimp nice and juicy, and everything was drizzled with a spicy cilantro cream that had a genuine kick. The $5 corn dog plate went above and beyond what any corn dog plate could even aspire to be--EIGHT plump fritters, with crispy, sweet cornbread on the outside and super-juicy dog bites on the inside. Elettaria, are you and your sad, lone corn dog snack listening? If I do make the big move to the 6th borough, it won't be for a year or two, and will depend on me getting a fancy professor job in the neuroscience department at Penn, Haverford, Swarthmore, etc. In the meantime, I have two things to ask of you West Philadelphians: 1. Please keep patronizing Local 44 so it's still in business when I get there. 2. If you happen to know anyone in the neuroscience department at Penn, Haverford, Swarthmore, etc, shoot me a PM, yes? Kthxbye.

text: This review is for the catering only - we have eaten at this restaurant many times and love the food. My (now) husband and I decided to hire Ono to cater our wedding, as we had our first date there. The first problem (which I'm sure others won't have) is that the catering manager changed three times between the time we booked the catering and our wedding. We met several times at the restaurant with the catering manager(s), and thought we had everything worked out perfectly. We chose our menu and worked out all the details and the only thing we had left to decide was what we wanted to drink. The wedding was for 125-150 people and we were quoted $500 for beer and wine. We questioned this figure, as it seemed quite low, but were assured that this was the average price for a wedding of this size. Nine weeks before the wedding, we decided on specific beer and wines we wanted and asked for the specific quote. Three weeks before the wedding, despite numerous requests we had yet to have a firm price (this was during the transition to the third catering manager, it seems). Finally, two weeks before the wedding we got the quote - $1200. Really? We were told this was due to the wines we had chosen ($200/case), as well as the fact that we wanted 2 kegs (one domestic and one microbrew). When we called to see if they could work with us to get the price down, we were bluntly told that 'those are our prices' and there was no offer to help. A second call revealed that we could switch to house wines ($100/case) and either get 2 domestic kegs, or 1 domestic and 1/2 keg of microbrew and that would put us closer to $800. So that was what we decided. We were in fact charged $130 and $160 for the cases of wine (white and red, respectively). This beverage pricing issue was our main complaint. One of the appetizers we had ordered for the wedding was not actually served (regular tomato bruschetta was substituted for shrimp and pineapple bruschetta). The staff at the wedding did do a very nice job. They were friendly, helpful, courteous and overall kept things flowing smoothly. One other thing that surprised us: the bar staff started packing up at 9:45 (the reception was planned to go until midnight). When we asked what was going on, they told us that their contract stated they were done at 10. A detail that, apparently, they were keeping to themselves.

The ribs and pulled pork are fantastic -- there's nothing else in St. Louis that comes close to matching it. The pulled chicken is the juiciest chicken I've ever had, and as much as I wish they'd add mac n' cheese or corn bread as a side dish, the sweet potato fries are pretty good. They serve their meats without sauce (cause they've got nothing to hide, apparently), but it's fun to alternate bites between the sweet, original, and hot sauces waiting for you at your table. The menu is a little confusing (students can get the lunch menu any time of day, which they don't advertise), but you'll have plenty of time to study it. Everyone at the restaurant is super nice and helpful, too, and there's usually someone walking up and down the line asking if anyone has questions. Would've been more fun if there wern't so many douchy drunk frat dudes crowding the area. Still pissed I missed out on earth wind and fire! Started to feel sick from the heat and lack of sleep. Blood sugar must have been messin me up. hahah. But hey what can you do? The fairgrounds are huge. Oh and a major plus, while you are walkin down the street people outside are selling homemade bbq and cheap beer. I still remember the smell of it to this day. I didn't get a chance to try their food because we were in a hurry to get to the festival, but I sure as hell bought a more than couple of their 2 dollar beers. Not sure if I'm diggin this years line up too much, but I will probably go again. I love New Orleans, and thats just another excuse for me to go 3 years in a row.

I ate way too much that night but could nit stop because it was just that good and I didn't know when the next time I'd be back. text: This review is for the restaurant only. Who serves a tall drink of water without a straw? Who serves mashed potates without gravy? Because the heap of potatoes isn't dry enough by itself. Who makes a chocolate milkshake without topping it with whipped cream? Such a tragedy. Service was S.L.O.W. With the restaurant only a quarter full, we had to wait through a Madonna song (3 minutes) until the hostess stopped laughing with her co-workers in the kitchen before coming up front to seat us. She surveyed the nearly empty floor before sighing and saying, "I guess you can have that booth." We were hungry and ready to order NOW. But we had to sit through at least three more One Hit Wonders from the 1980s before the waiter finally deigned to make an appearance. Once the food finally came out, he never once came back to check if we needed more water, to clear half-empty plates, or ask if wanted any of our leftovers wrapped up. The food itself was classic diner fare, nothing special, but don't hold your breath waiting for wait staff to blow you away with their attention.

I've given them plenty of chances...for both lunch and dinner, on weekdays and weekends, and the result is always the same. The slow service is just the tip of the iceberg. They've gotten orders completely wrong when they aren't even busy. I'm saying not even close... chicken when you order eggplant wrong. For a time, their grinders had shrunk to downright small, however last time I visited they were a good size again so gold star for you guys. One time, I swung by for dinner with some visiting northerners, and they were closed at 6:30...when the door clearly said 8. No note on the door, no nothing. Not how you should run a business. text: I haven't been to Terror Behind the Walls but I have to give aces to the normal during the day audio tour of Eastern State. Narrated by Steve Buscemi (that's almost worth the money right there), it gives you a chance to really explore the prison on your own terms. The first part of the tour is the suggested path with 12 stops. I really found it very interesting. I feel like I really got a sense of the prison itself and what the original architects were going for. They didn't go into super engineering level detail but enough for you to want to know more. The people who designed that place were a bunch of mean mofos. I got the impression that you'd probably go nuts if you were incarcerated there in its original form. The tour also demonstrates how the prison changed over the years in order to handle the influx of criminals. It's funny to walk around near Fairmount because right smack in the middle of a seemingly nice neighborhood is this huge prison. It's kind of awesome. The prison itself has 40 something separate stops that you can dial up on your audio device and learn more about. There is no time limit and you can go in whatever order you want. The punishment rooms in particular looked rather menacing. They're pretty much are a steel slatted bed chained to the wall with the express purpose of administering pain. Now all they need is ice-cream.

text: I purchased the Living Social deal for Tranquility Skin & Massage Studio back on October 21, 2010. After calling and never having a person answer and leaving four voice messages and receiving no word back, I filed a complaint with Living Social on November 15, 2010. I heard back from Living Social on December 1st, during which time I had finally been contacted back from Tranquility and decided not to proceed with my complaint. After two generic phone tag messages I received one that said, "Please leave a date and time you would like to come in" and I thought ok, good, if they're not going to answer the phone for whatever reason, at least now we're getting somewhere. I left a message with Saturday, December 11th as my preferred date at any time and received a message back that there was a 12:30 opening but since there might be a snow storm (?) they may or may not book me...being from upstate NY I find it extremely strange to not schedule someone cause of predicted snow 5 days in the future. P.s. It's not snowing today. Anyway, I called back and left a message to confirm the 12:30. Then I received a message from someone at a different phone number saying the 12:30 was not available but a 3:00 was and to call them back at this new number. I called that number and got a busy signal. Then I called Tranquility back and left a message that I would take the 3:00 pm. I never heard back. So this morning, the day of the massage I called to see if I was indeed scheduled for 3:00, I was told that I was. Then not five minutes later got a voicemail from the person at the other number saying that since they never heard from me that I'm not actually scheduled for today and to call her back about times next weekend (I'm relocating to the east coast next Saturday). This other persons voicemail said that they had just entered a new partnership with Tranquility...apparently not a symbiotic partnership. It has been 10 weeks since I originally purchased and started trying to book my massage. I will be proceeding with my complaint through Living Social and I will edit my review if I receive a refund; I do not recommend this business to anyone in the future. I joked with my friend that I needed a massage from the stress of trying to book with this company. Go to The Wellness Space in Broad Ripple instead, they're wonderful, courteous, and provide prompt responses.

text: I'm not sure what the hype about Fountain is. First, the touted romantic fountain-esque table with the view is probably limited to one or two tables at the restaurant. Other than that, the restaurant has in fact a very dawdy, old-school decor within. After having read all that I did re Fountain, some even to the extent mentioning it to be one of the best restaurants in Philly, I was excited to dine here. However, such excitement slowly dissipated. I went for the 3-course lunch and had the - Halibut: which was asian-inspired with bok choy etc. Sad to say, the fish was rather dry and not prepared at a level that I would have expected it to be. - Beef: Waitress mentioned that the chef typically serves this medium-rare but what I got presented was a piece of meat that was more medium-well, if not well-done in some parts. Needless to say, I did not enjoy my meat as much as I would have a rarer piece. However, while I did make the overcooked condition of my meat known, I did not require to have it redone. I did however, like the fact that the chef incorporated quinoa pilaf into this dish and thought of it as refreshing, in contrast to the old-fashioned decor the place reeked of. - Banana Chocolate Mousse: very disappointing. Probably my fault since I'm not a mousse fan. I guess I got lured by the banana chocolate or seeming banana chocolate mix. What I got presented was a chocolate mousse dome with some caramelized banana on the side... and not some banana infused chocolate mousse cake as I had initially imagined. While I was initially regretting the decision about having gone with the 3-course, fixed dessert menu after having seen another waiter push out the dessert cart... the excitement about the cart dwindled after I saw the desserts offered. Very old-school, and not at all exciting. The saving grace of the meal was the host/ manager whose excellent service right from greeting me to seating me, to his professional conduct coming by each table to explain to the guests that the blinking fire light was in fact only a maintenance issue and to the very end when he graciously handed me my madeleines to go and even got me a to-go bag... all this while mindful of the fact that I was to leave the restaurant at 2pm impressed me greatly. In my many fine-dining experiences in Philly, I have become accustomed to 2nd-grade wait service but this level of service in truly exceptional and commendable.

text: The ultimate dive bar. Literally. It was ranked as one of the Top 20 Dive Bars in America by one of the 'guy mags' (can't remember if it was FHM or whatever). Regardless of what the self-proclaimed experts in the national media say, the Cat is definitely the coolest, smokiest, grimiest bar in Ripple, and it has been servin up great greats for a hot second. The Cat tends to draw a rock n roll crowd, some authentic, some complete poseurs. The music definitely corresponds, with the jukebox generally being loaded with the heavier side of rock, especially on weekend nights. I don't really hit the Cat as much as I used to, but it's mainly just a matter of being busy with gigs and not getting out to regular spots as much as I did when I first moved to Indy. However, despite a minor remodel and an ensuing onslaught of haterism ("I liked it better the old way, now I'm too cool to go there"), the Cat is pretty much the same old place. All the people who are too cool for school now never made it a better bar, anyway. The Cat was, and still is, great for its bartenders, its drinks, its smokiness, its quasi-pool-hall-ness, and its semi-secret location located off Broad Ripple Avenue on, of course, an alley. This is THE BEST place to grab that last drink in Ripple before you head home. While, thankfully, it deflects most of the clones who go to the avenue clubs, it does get crowded at night, so you best be good to the bartenders if you want to get any attention! Believe it or not, their cheeseburgers are awesome, and they even have a steak dinner special on Thursday nights. Give it a try! Opens at 7am. So...nevermind.

text: "Meh" would basically sum up the Joe's experience for me. I grew up on the coast of southern Maine, so I can be a bit of a prat about good seafood. Living in the desert has proven to be a challenge, when it comes to my periodic undersea urges, for obvious reasons. Nevertheless, I had some money to burn and decided to take the fam' to Joes. Meh, meh, and more meh. We started with some shrimp that was fine, if a bit bland, and only barely cooked through, and moved on to a crab variety pot. The dungeness crab tasted as though it had been in a deep-freeze for the better part of the past decade, and the Alaskan sweet crab wasn't much better. At least this stuff seemed well-cooked. When it came to the sides, well-cooked was a bit of an understatement. The corn was steamed to the point that the kernels were falling apart, and the potato's starch and skin were only tenuously holding it together. I will say this: the portions were ample. My girlfriend and I were able to split the shrimp app and crab pot (for one) easily between us. We usually don't get desserts when we eat out, but decided to splurge this time and order the praline brownie sundae (or whatever ludicrous, vaguely nautical name they gave it). I wish we hadn't. The brownie was like something I could buy from the counter of a 7-11, the vanilla ice cream was so-so, and there was but a lonely teaspoon of caramel at the bottom of the glass. I could have made it at home while blindfolded and drunk, and probably for a quarter of the price. All-in-all, Joe's reminds me why I generally loathe chain restaurants. You pay through the nose for the "experience" of the place, and then cross your fingers and hope the food is A) cooked well-enough and B)doesn't give you a coronary before the end of the meal. At Joe's, the "experience" is tortoise-slow wait service and the pleasure of listening to the waiters angrily belt out AM-gold favorites of the '70s. Have you ever been to a dive bar on a Friday at 1:30am? The singing is a little bit like that, only minus the alcohol, and devoid of any real mirth. Joe's is one of those places that blows its financial wad on making you feel like you've come to a wacky, irreverent land of crab, where the staff is kooky and anything could happen. The problem is that everything seems forced and choreographed, and you can't help but be pained, given how hard their corporate machine seems to be trying. If the super classy "I got crabs at Joe's" t-shirts aren't enough, the self-consciously kitschy bibs may put you over the top. This is coupled by the fact that the actual food, which is their ostensible stock-in-trade, is relatively miserable. Quick side bar here: the waiter asked me if I wanted him to put on my bib for me, and I figured he had to be making some kind of grotesque joke, so I laughed him off. Then, I saw no fewer than four other people, over the course of our meal, request said privilege. Really? Is that the premium one pays for, nowadays: the honor of flushing one's self-respect down the crapper and being infantilized in public? As Yakoff Smirnoff would say, "What a country!" Joe's is, quite clearly, a product of an over-stimulated, over-fed culture, in which mediocrity is passable, as long as its loud and expensive enough. I think I'll pass from now on.

text: We did the River-to-River 7-hour walking tour. We live near Philadelphia but hadn't spent much time exploring the city before, until our daughter gave us this tour as my wife's birthday present. The tour was a real eye-opener, showing us the extraordinary diversity of Philadelphia. Our guide, Paige, had just finished her masters' degree in history at University of Pennsylvania and was enthusiastic and highly knowledgeable. The tour didn't go to the usual places--the Liberty Bell, Independence Hall, and so on. The idea was that most tourists already know those places or can find them on their own. Instead, we explored the historic back alleys, the huge wall murals, and the lunch delicacies of the Reading Terminal Market. We now know so many fascinating places in Philadelphia--I can't wait to go back and explore more. Suggestion: Come prepared for walking - good walking shoes and a positive attitude!

text: If you have a designated driver and want to get drunk, or want to eat whatever "Teppanyaki" is, then perhaps Sakura is for you. If you want Japanese food, however, this just isn't the place. I've been to Sakura a couple of times at the behest of friends. I don't eat "Teppanyaki" because I don't consider it to be Japanese food, so I had to make my determination from other parts of the menu. The last time I visited, I had a hankerin' (yen?) for some Tonkatsu, a breaded, fried pork cutlet that yes, also isn't really Japanese but since it has been regularly eaten in Japan for hundreds of years it is close enough. Much to my disappointment, it was not on the menu. How could it not be on the menu? Few non-seafood things are as common as Tonkatsu. A former boss of mine was a Narita airport protester back in the day, and when he was arrested and thrown in jail for weeks without being charged or allowed to see an attorney the upside was that the prison ran its own pig farm. He told me that the best Tonkatsu he ever had was when he was in prison. He might even be compelled to go punch out a cop just to have it again. And Sakura doesn't have it on the menu? Ok, so no Tonkatsu. I decide to order the chirashi-zushi, a sushi dish where strips of fish and shellfish are artfully arranged atop a bowl of sushi rice. This has become my standard means of judging sushi when not at the sushi bar itself. Typically chirashi-zushi is served in one of those lacquered stacking bowls and when created by a talented person is a marvelous work of art. Most people pick up the bowl and use direct shoveling maneuvers with their chopsticks when working down to the bottom. But my chirashi was served in something like a broad, shallow western soup bowl with a wide brim. How was I supposed to eat this, with a spoon? The contents was average, but the presentation was all wrong. I was befuddled.

text: This restaurant is located in the Ritz plaza in Voorhees. New to South Jersey, I was desperate to have some good Indian food, so my fellow Indian friend and I decided to give it a try on a Friday night. Luckily, we didn't have to wait for a table, but it did get packed during dinner, with others waiting to dine. When we walked in, we were pleased with the attention to decor and service. There are bamboo blinds you can let down between booths to add privacy, a thoughtful touch. I have to say though, I was pretty disappointed with the food. I left completely unsatisfied, and with the burning feeling of raw spices in my stomach to boot. Now I'm half Indian, half Pakistani, and I know my food (and I LOVE spices), but something here just didn't jive with my palate. This place has gotten great reviews from a lot of people, so maybe I was wrong to order the veggie thali, but I can't say I've ever felt so indifferent towards my order. I will say though that the Dal Makhani was good. My friend ordered the non-veg thali and she was disappointed too, but I will say that her standards are higher. I have not, however, felt the desire to go back to this restaurant. It's shame really, because it is so nice inside and the service is great. The chef even came over to check on us, welcome us and ask our opinion about. I felt bad, and told him I enjoyed the food (well, I did like the rice and dal...), but made sure to leave my honest opinion on the comment card that came with the check. I actually would be willing to try another dish at this restaurant - maybe they do better with the meat? But I can't eat anything except the lamb because everything else isn't halal. For ambience, this isn't a bad place. But I didn't feel happy leaving.
label: NEG

text: Talk about sticking out like a sore thumb! I never actually thought that I would be one of those women who would find some enjoyment in entering a horse race betting establishment where the average age of patrons is somewhere between the age of 70 and 6 feet under. However, a small vice in me always wondered what actually happened inside those walls...Yea, I've heard stories and I am sure you have too. And upon entering, my preconceived ideas were right on target. A co-worker and I enter through the doors and were greeted by a 70-something platinum blonde woman whose main job I guess was to be a " greeter" similar to the ones employed by Walmart. From there, we entered a wall made of smoke so much so that I couldn't see actually where I was going...(simple exaggeration...but you know what I mean). Wall to wall blue collar workers with their eyes fixated on one of 20 televisions aglow with a separate horse race on each...all around us. Then utter confusion and panic set in...what do we do? how do we bet? why are all these people looking at us? do they have a women's bathroom? do they actually serve food here? what is the director's room and how do you gain entrance? what is a trifecta? Ahhh so many questions I felt dizzy. We made our way up to the counter where a nice woman helped us figure this all out. We had to buy a $3.25 program just so we could actually see the details of each of the races for the day. Then she tried to give us the cliff notes version of horse betting...Yes, that's right...we didn't remember any of it...and ended up betting based on how funny the horse's name was or what color shirt the jockey was wearing... you know typical chick thinking. After 4 races, I actually netted $5.00 after winning one race when BIZARRO WORLD came in first (I took away $55 from that race). But the longer I stayed, the more I understood how people can get hooked on it. Suffice it to say, I don't think that I will make it one of my hobbies but I did utterly enjoy the ability to people watch in this joint.

Here it's always enough that it's flavorful but not dominating. -Salads in a breadbowl! Love it. Yes, Slice is going to cost you more than most Philly pizza places, but it's going to be that much more delicious. J&J is fine if it's late and you just want something in your stomach. text: Just had lunch at Lola and I have to say I'm pretty disappointed - after all these great Yelp reviews I was expecting more. It's Thursday and the place was deserted when my friend and I got there just before noon. Only two other people came in while we were dining. The waitress was pleasant and gave us plenty of time to decide, and there looks like a ton of great things on their menu. It's pretty hot & humid so I decided against the lobster corn dog w/mac & cheese, which was what really intrigued me. Instead, I got a sandwich - the Medusa: spinach & feta spread, muenster, mozzarella, white cheddar and roasted tomato on sourdough. Plus a side of frittes. My friend ordered Antoinette: strip steak, gruyere, onions & mushrooms. "Roasted tomatoes" says something to me other than "sliced romas," which is what was on the sandwich. It pretty much tasted like a grilled cheese & tomato. Which isn't bad, but I was thinking there'd be more green on it from the spinach spread. It was way too cheesy for my taste, though it was definitely a tasty grilled cheese sandwich. The fries were warm when they came out but cooled quickly; my beef with any restaurant that serves fries is that they should be served in a cone like Belgians do, so they stay hot. Not Lola's fault that we're not in Europe, I suppose, though a good idea should be cross-cultural. They were definitely homemade and had the slightly greasy consistency of really good homemade fries. Quite tasty. The bread was fresh and grilled just right - very tasty bread. Jay's sandwich was a big disappointment: The meat was tough and one piece of it was half gristle! No one wants to dismantle a sandwich to cut off the gristle & then reassemble. Blech. Why serve that? It wasn't that it was bad, but for the price & all the good reviews the place has gotten I just expected more. If someone suggests Lola in the future, I'll go and try something different - maybe a crepe, since that's why Jay loves the place and that's what he usually gets. But I won't be craving it between now & then.
label: NEG

text: The neighborhood here isn't all that fancy, but I'd say it's worth going out of your way for it you want the older grand-style Chinese restaurant. The dining area is larger than what the parking lot leads you to believe. So if the small parking lot in front is full, park in front of the closed business next door, which essentially could be the same parking lot. Please do not think the restaurant is over-crowded/full just because their own lot is full, so be sure to go in and check. Decor is old grand style, very busy with lots of stuff, including a large Buddha statue. Tabletops are glass over the old style Zodiac place mats over a tablecloth. They offer carry-out and dine-in, no buffet. Very large menu, with the "per person" group dinners, and entrees. Beer, wine, and liquor are served. There was at least one of those large round tables with the lazy-susan in the middle. The men's room didn't quite live up to the decor up front, but they were very busy, so I cut them some slack in the rating. I'm probably being generous by a half point on Cleanliness and Ambience. But overall, both exceeded my expectations. Food is served on a serving plate, not the plate you eat off of, with large serving spoons, to facilitate sharing. Rice came in a separate covered stainless steel bowl. Portion size seemed large. The fried rice seemed Southern China/Cantonese/Hong Kong style. I had the black (shitake) mushrooms and vegetables entree. It was served over a ring of thin orange slices. Delicious. I ate most of the orange slices. The vegetables were very fresh, and cooked with just the right amount of crispness left in them. The fortune cookie was also served with a couple of fresh orange slices. Hostess and waitress were very professional, efficient and quick. A couple of the waitresses were really cute. Soda and water glasses refilled at just the right times. Papa-san worked the dining room and helped bus tables.

text: I have now been to Le Bec three times, once for lunch, once for dessert and once for afternoon tea. Both times lived up to my fond imaginings (Le Bec has been one of the places I've been wanting to go for years now). For lunch I had a beautifully and simply dressed salad, followed by duck with lentils. The duck was perfect, with crispy skin and tender meat. The lentils convinced me that I do, in fact, like lentils. For dessert that day I had a lemon curd tart that was tart and exactly what I was looking for. My dessert only experience had been at Le Bar Lyonnais, but I am rating it together since they are in the same building! I had the cheesecake, which I have to say was the best cheesecake I've ever tasted. The afternoon tea is a new thing, possibly December only. If so, get yourself there ASAP. We had a quiet leisurely tea that was perfectly relaxing after a stressful weekend of gift wrangling (is it my imagination or does holiday shopping just get worse every year???). We each had our own pots of tea, which was perfectly brewed. Our attentive server never let the cups get empty. She was fabulous. For the tea itself, we had finger sandwiches (fig and prosciutto were the best), raspberry scones with an AMAZING cassis jelly, and an assortment of little cakes (including a lovely coffee macaroon). Service was excellent and accommodating, and we had a lovely time. I highly recommend the tea to all!

text: When I heard about an authentic German restaurant in St. Louis, I was excited to try it, but after the experience, I'm sure this is a "one & done" situation for me. St. Louis Gast Haus is located in a really cool building. When we walked in and saw the long, narrow detailed bar, I was excited. Then we were seated in an adjoining room that has an interesting mural painted on the wall and German folk music playing in the background. It immediately made me think of beer tents in Munich during Oktoberfest, but as the night continued, I couldn't wait for some peace & quiet. I'm sure any German person in America during the 4th of July, hearing "Stars & Stripes Forever" over & over, would have the same feeling. The decor in the restaurant was interesting, but looked like it came from a personal collection or estate sale. Perhaps I'm not educated in the background of German cuisine, but the food seemed to be prepared more like a homey meal, rather than the restaurant type of preparation & presentation. Overall, I can say the family who owns the restaurant is probably trying very hard, but it's doubtful that I'll return to dine. If I did, it would probably be to the bar before a Blues' game!

text: This is not Home Depot. Instead, my girlfriend and I have christened thee: Confrontational Home Depot or, for short, CoHoDo. Most the time we go to CoHoDo, we get treated to the hallmarks of bad service, stupid logistics, poor layout and overall lousiness that a big box retail establishment is known for in the city of brotherly shove (see Kmart at the Gallery for the pinnacle of this). The Confrontational part, though, is the little cherry on top. We have seen numerous fights, screaming matches, and parking lot altercations that allows you to realize that getting out of there alive and unscathed is a miracle in an of itself.
label: NEG

text: Way to trick me, Wonderland. I saw you from the outside with your Beatles decal in the window and thought you might be a place worthy of checking out, but I walked in to realize you were a smoke shop! Though you do have a pretty vast selection of hookahs and bongs, as well as some other cool but random stuff downstairs, the former is sure is not what I expected to see when I came in. Honestly, you belong on Telegraph Avenue in Berkeley than on Walnut Street in Philly. I'm sure you'd get much more traffic there.
label: NEG

text: So yes the Lopez family has been around for a while pawning off their version of mexican as "authentic" to gringos who don't know better. For me, I'll try elsewhere. Their salsa is so mild, so bland it might as well be tomato sauce. Dishes all taste the same, taco, burrito, enchilada, you name it, it all tastes the same but in a different package. The best thing ( and I mean that sarcastically) about this place is how they leave the back door to the kitchen open with no screen on it so little bugs and critters can crawl or swarm in at anytime and join you on your plate for dinner. Want authentic? Try elsewhere. Want taco bell in a sit down atmosphere, try here.
label: NEG

text: The fried chicken was recommended. However found it to be on the salty side for my taste. I did enjoy the fried dill pickles. Service was good. Our server gave us the heads up that there was a large party coming in so that we could get our order in and avoid a long wait for our food.
label: NEG

text: I honestly cannot believe there are only 4 reviews. Eegee's is a Tucson institution and one of the places I HAVE to visit when I'm in town. What are the best items on the menu? Pizza Fries, Veggie Grinder (which comes without mayo standard!), whatever the flavor of the month Eegee is - it will be good, as well as the Pina Colada Eegee. The flavor of the month Eegee switches out monthly and each month is better than the last (over the years I've had them all). For those not wanting a Pina Colada, the other always there flavors are Strawberry and Lemon. You can do a half-and-half Eegee and enjoy two flavors, and a Lemon Ice T-Eegee is really refreshing during the summertime. Note: a small Eegee is actually really big! Yes, the stores need a makeover, but the standard yellow benches are part of its charm.
label: POS

text: I really like this place but the food is not up to par. The idea and location is great. Mid-city needs a breakfast/lunch spot that's fresh and organic but this place is not it. This week there was only one item on the menu that was vegetarian and it wasn't very good. The juices are pulpy and are not made with organic fruit and veggies. The staff and the restaurant are awesome but the food is really lacking. I came home after eating lunch and was hungry an hour later because my sandwich was just blah. My husband ate a sandwich that was basically just bread, there was hardly anything on it. They need to really step it up.
label: NEG

text: Hello, new favorite lunch place. Great food, great service, GREAT prices... we loved each and every little bit of this fantastic cafe/restaurant. I can't wait to come back! I expressed to a gentleman how much I loved their balsamic salad dressing, asking if they would sell me some. He said no, but what does he do? Come back with several "to go" containers of it, no charge. THANK YOU!!!
label: POS

text: This is a beautiful space - the dark wood, floor to ceiling shelves of food seemed so warm and inviting when you've stumbled in out of a blizzard. My first visit was during the recent snowstorm and I couldn't have walked into a more convenient and joy-inducing place during what looked to be a totally destroyed weekend. After rummaging around in the food section (Trader Joe's had been cleaned out so we tied up all of our loose ends here!), we ventured into the west wing - i.e. the beer coolers. (They had Smuttynose. I was sold. ) My friend and I gathered up our foodies and our beeries and brought them to the cashier. After informing me that I had made the wrong choices in beer and redirecting me to an option that he was sure I'd be happy with, we finally cashed out and jumped back into the snow. After the long trek home, bearing a new snow shovel, rock salt, several bags of groceries, several scary movies, and a bag of beer, we were tired, cranky, and in need of tacos and beer. Friend-from-Food&Friends, Your beer choice made me weep. Yes, I was excessively pleased. If I were a boy-kissing type of girl, I would come over there and plant a big wet one on your beardy face. Since I'm not, I will praise you from afar and possibly, stop in from time to time to fake smile and laugh. You made my blizzard. Love always, Liza
label: POS

text: Ok, kiddies! It's time for a pop quiz! Was my naked veggie burrito: A) cold and unsatisfying B) bland C) did it give me horrible indigestion for the rest of the night? D) all of the above Answer: D I won't be going back.
label: NEG

text: Yeah. I'm a hater. Well, "hater" may be a bit strong, as I've got no real quarrel with Ted Drewes. But I just don't really get what all the fuss is about. As the little Yelp ratings guide suggests, I've experienced better. No, I'm not from St. Louis, so I guess I don't have the hard-wired Pavlovian attraction to this place. Fighting to find a parking space and then standing in the parking lot eating this "concrete" just doesn't strike me as the end-all and be-all of summer treats. And, frankly, it's just not as good as a good cup (or cone) of regular old ice cream. Ted Drewes isn't bad. It's nice once or twice a summer if it's not too crowded. I just don't think it's much to write home about, either.
label: NEG

text: The sea kayaking Santa Barbara coastal trip was an amazing experience! Our guides, Amy and Jen, were patient and great. They were really well informed and made sure everyone was having a good time. The whole day was planned out really well, including the picnic on the secluded beach. A wonderful company to go on adventures with!
label: POS

text: On the surface, this restaurant looks fantastic. Inviting, inventive menu and interesting decor. And then, your meal happens. First, the service, as listed here previously is abyssmal. Waiters were so "busy" that they were exceedingly unprofessional. Pretending not to hear requests from patrons, hurrily slamming down plates, and flat out ignoring new tables because they were "oversat". (I put oversat in quotes, because I was a waiter for 5 years, and I would have never been in the weeds like these clowns were with such few tables.) One couple got up and stormed out when they were not even acknowledged for over 30 minutes. We watched as they complained to the host, who promptly did NOTHING about it. Ridiculous. If anyone is a full or partial owner of this restaurant and is reading this, you need to clean house in your front-of-the-house staff. Our food came and while, acceptable, it was very underwhelming. The sweet potato fries, although wonderfully presented, were paired -with an average tasting banana-guava sauce that was so runny that it wouldn't even stay on the fries. Just silly. I also ordered the "boneless" jerk chicken breast, which was neither a) boneless b) breast meat (or if it was it was Grade Q) or c) jerk. Imagine taking a chicken breast that was 60% cartilage, cooking it without seasoning, and painting it red. That was what ended up on my plate. The ONLY reason that I am not giving this restaurant 1 star is that the menu LOOKS so good. I hope to GOD the management makes some changes soon,
label: NEG

text: Loved it when it was at Penn and just as good in center city. I think they are best salads in the city. Recommend the soy ginger dressing and the seeded rolls.... Sandwiches are pretty good too, but the salad is what to get here.
label: POS

text: I live in Philly and work in Cherry Hill, so it was hard trying to find a good mexican place to get a burrito. I had high hopes for the food factory, hoping that it would cure my cravings for a nice, big burrito. I ordered the chicken burrito and I was extremely disappointed. I have never seen a flat burrito, but they managed to do it. As for the taste, it was alright, but nothing compared to say el fuego, or the joint. As for now I guess I'll have to keep searching the area.

text: I'm sure a lot of people are going to hate on El Rodeo for being both a chain and a step down from the top-tier Mexican restaurants in Indy. I, however, love El Rodeo. First of all, the chips and salsa are awesome. Seriously. I haven't found better salsa anywhere in town. The queso dip is really good, too. Second, the menu is very extensive. You won't be short on selection here. The food isn't life-changing or anything, but I think it's really good. Finally, the bar offers absolutely ginormous margaritas for a decent price. Also featured at this location: mediocre-at-best portrait of a horse with a very disproportionate rope hanging on a barn wall behind it. Be sure to check this out.

text: Not worth the price! When you walk in, there are signs and awards of how they are the best burger in Manhattan. Not only is it just a so so burger, they really brought the Manhattan price with them. Yes, everything is computerized and organized, and they have flat screens everywhere, but that's not what I'm personally looking for when I want to enjoy a good grease burger!
