text: In 48 hours I flew into Tampa, flew out to Key West, then flew back to Tampa. It was late, I was hungry, and I was disappointed I couldn't find a decent BBQ place in Tampa. So I just drove down the street from my hotel and found.....Sonny's BBQ It's a chain but has been around for 40 years. So as I scanned the menu....I spot the Super Combo...a little bit of everything....for $12.99....SOLD. And here is how it went.... 1. Ribs: Much like Rudy's in Albuquerque, the rib meat pulled off the bone but was not overcooked. Silverskin still attached, the ribs had the chew, smoky flavor and pulled from the bone clean. I was happy. 4 stars 2. Pulled pork: This pork was clearly roasted not steamed and mushy. However it was a little dry. It was ok but not great. 3 stars 3. BBQ chicken: Moist and tender... hint of being BBQ'ed...but not too bad overall. Sauce not overpowering and complimenting the chicken. 4 stars 4. BBQ Beef: Like the pork, really nothing special here....edible but just plain beef. It's ok. 3 stars 5. Corn bread. Pretty good cornbread...tastes homemade rather than a standard restaurant mix taste. Good crunchy crust. 4 stars 6. Sweet potato: Baked in some butter in foil......locked in flavor ....good taste. I really liked it. 4 stars 7. BBQ Beans: Good beans but nothing special. 3 stars Overall 4 stars because it was the best BBQ place I have found so far in Tampa and it's a great value for the amount of food served. text: This place is pretty rad (if you're into brewing and GOOD, rare beer). We opted to try and use a "local" shop for our second-ever brewing experience, and the Reno Homebrewer did not disappoint. Hidden away in the "industrial" section of Reno, next to artsy tile shops and random "new, artsy" condos, the Reno Homebrewer exists. Shelves of hops, malts, sugars, mesh bags, carboys, etc etc line the (rather small) shop. A decent selection of dried fruit and spices exists in the center of the store. On one side, you can find the wine essentials across from a 'fridge stocked with rare beer that I've only seen here. A bar sits in the front of the shop (a place to enjoy those rare beers), where they also ring up your brewing purchases. We wanted a relatively easy brew session and we wanted to follow a store recipe, so we opted to check out the recipes printed out in the back of the store to "build" a Nut Brown Ale. Basically, the recipes line the shelf and then it's up to YOU to walk around the store gathering the essentials. (It's easy-enough, though. Everything is marked remarkably well.) The price was absolutely right and on-par with anything I've seen on More Beer or Midwest Brewing's websites....but you don't have to pay shipping if you buy in-person! The store help was also exceptional. Both workers were super-friendly and not-at-all judgemental, snobby, or anything that might make a new brewer self-conscious about important questions. We bought everything we needed and splurged on a liquid yeast over a dry. We bought a new mesh bag, some new metal caps, and a $10 bottle of Alaskan's 2009 Baltic Porter Ale. Our total came out to about $50 with all of the ingredients we needed, as well as the "extras." (There is a surcharge of about $3 or so to use the credit-card machine. I felt this was a bit steep.) We found out that you can get $2 back if you return the container that the malt extract comes in (clean, of course). I only took off one star because, well, this place is pretty dirty. There was dust pretty much everywhere. I realize that you sterilize your equipment before using it, anyway, but I would expect a brew store to be a bit cleaner. I also didn't like the steep credit card surcharge or the rather high pricing for the bottled beer (Dogfish Head was about $4.25 PER BOTTLE. You can get a 4-pack for almost double that price - even in Tahoe. I'd only buy beer here if you're looking for something super-rare.....the equivalent of seeking out a fine wine for a special occasion; for this, the Reno Homebrewer rocks.) All-in-all, I think this is definitely our new spot for brew equipment and ingredients. It's more fun to pick out your brew stuff in-person and the staff is really nice. I'll be recommending this place to anyone who asks about brewing beer.

text: I have pretty specific criteria when it comes to evaluating a sports bar: 1. It must show or be able to show my team's games. (Full Disclosure: I am a Red Sox, Celtics, and Patriots fan). 2. It must have enough TVs to put on your game, regardless of what else is going on in the sports world. That Titans game may be in overtime, but I'm sure you could find some random TV in the corner for a Lions fan, right? 3. It must show a wide variety of other games. I enjoy sports in general, and I like to see other games. I mean, I could go to Sox bar to high-five and bro-hug other patrons all night long, but it's more fun to have a diverse collection of fans. 4. It must have at least one "go-to" food item. 5. It must have a decent beer selection. Sam's fulfills all of these criteria, and then some. They have all the sports packages, and will gladly put on your game if you ask nicely. During the football season, the manager labels the TVs so you know what matchups you'll be able to see and when you'll be able to see them. I've only been to a couple other bars that do this, and it's amazing. You can position yourself optimally for a day of sports viewing/drinking without having to bother a waiter or waitress. In addition, they have a good beer selection and decent bar food. The chicken fingers are the gold standard. I could seriously drink the honey mustard. But the chorizo dip, southwest egg rolls, and pizza are all good for what they are. On top of all this, Sam's isn't some chain mega-bar. The service doesn't wear flair or sing songs (although they do wear referee uniforms and are unnecessarily inattentive and gruff). They have a nice "patio" area and do activities like trivia and karaoke. There is also ample parking in an otherwise very crowded Hillsboro Village area. Sam's is a great sports bar - definitely the best I've found so far in Nashville.

text: Anyone who knows what over priced, over done and over hyped clothing stores and fashion look like will no doubt find evidence of it at any Blue Bee store (Blue Bee Jeans, Blue Beetle, Blue Bee shoes, ect.) It is all too glittery, too "look at me, I'm wearing the same overpriced, low waist jeans my pre-pubescent daughter wore yesterday to grade school." 50 year olds and 12 year olds should not share the same wardrobe. I will argue that if you are looking for anti-sweatshop made standard tee shirts, hoodies and (some) jeans, (and are ready and willing to pay for this,) you will find them in a variety of shades and styles in Blue Bee stores. But I stress again, ignore the staff because they will ALWAYS find it necessary to sweetly remark that everything looks "super hot" or "sooooooooo, like, cute on you, omg," when you really just look like another poser or the next innocent fashion victim. Side note: Blue Bee is famous for having bi-annual, entire store sales that last 3 or more days, with discounts ranging from 50-80%, that many poor suckers will set a 5am alarm for and continue to stalk and camp outside the store until it opens. No hurt feelings intended, but the victims are usually Montecito mothers with nothing else to do but waste their time buying their undeserving, spoiled, teenage daughters new wardrobes every other weekend. You know, something to occupy all there free time. Anyone with half a brain would realize that in order to mark down an entire season's worth of clothing at such outstanding discounts the store has initially overpriced every thing you see more than what is retail norm. So it's really a big joke. Clothing stores only mark down stock that is not selling well and that could become another financial burden if not sold at all. When a store discounts clothes at such rates it usually means they are going out business, unless, like Blue Bee of course, they can still make a growing profit on all those suckers out there and even afford to do it every single passing season. So, please, take caution remember that you (your husband, your parents or maybe even your great grandparents) worked too hard for you to allow yourself to waste your cash in a place that doesn't even appreciate what it is worth.

text: I really wanted to love this place since it's so close to my work, but I had a very bad experience that ended with a $420 dress irreparably incorrectly altered. I took it in on a Friday, tried the dress on with the shoes I'd be wearing, the guy pinned it to where it should go, and he told me to come back Tuesday to try it on again, since he wanted to sew the hem where it would go but wanted me to try it on before he cut the material. text: Koken Art Factory is tucked away behind Jefferson and Gravois in Benton Park. It doubles as an artist/event space. It's an old warehouse and besides the main bar area, has not been renovated. But that's what makes it an ideal place to host grassroots events. As long as you don't blow the place up or set it on fire (not sure if it even meets fire code standards), whomever wants to use the space has the freedom to do whatever s/he wants! The space is sectioned off into different rooms or areas so there could be multiple things going on at the same time. I've been there for live art shows, concerts and a mini-rave. If you want to get a taste of what one could possibly put on at Koken, I'd recommend hitting the Riff Raff's Halloween Art Show. They make great use of the space with a "Jack the Ripper" feel to the place. Also, PBR occasionally hosts events there as well and they like to have a variety of entertainment for their patrons. For the right event, Koken would be a great venue. If you were interested in using the space, then I would suggest going there to see the place first. I've always been a vodka guy, an apparent sin when it comes to mixologists. But give me a vodka and coke and I'm a happy guy. With that in mind, you can understand my trepidation going to a bar like Franklin which seemingly is all about the throwback old-school heavy-handed cocktails from yesteryear. All uneasiness however was put to rest when I sat at the bar and struck up a conversation with one of the many excellent true bartenders working there. Not knowing exactly what it was that I would like on the menu I simply told him the kinds of things I normally drink and the kinds of things I normally don't like and he proceeded to concoct a drink which was delicious, strong, and not even on the menu. I truly think that there's something for everyone at this bar and it's simply a matter of finding those drinks that suit your taste. The most frequent problem that I have when I bring friends here is that they order something off the menu that from the way it reads would sound delicious, but which they quickly realize is far outside their comfort zone. They're immediately dissatisfied having spent $10-$12 on a drink that they don't even like. As it is a pricey place, and those are never the best places to experiment blindly on a tight budget, I'd offer the simple suggestion that if it is your first time going there, or if you're like me and not a big cocktail drinker, sit at the bar and just talk to the bartender and have him make something for you. Interestingly enough I find that they can better gauge my taste-buds than even I can. You won't be disappointed and, like me, you'll find yourself looking forward to the next time you can come back and get another!

text: While I used to be a loyal patron of FQP, I now begrudgingly have to give it the honor of my first Yelp review (and not a pleasant one!) My experience here started off good and has been decreasing exponentially upon every visit. Most recently, I stopped in for a quick one-hour lunch... I was greeted by no airconditioning, which (in the summertime), is painful and a hamster-cage-esque stench. They DID put in enough high-powered fans to blow my check, take-home boxes, and food around, though. Our waitress couldn't have been more than 14 years old. The owner clearly hired her daughter so she didn't have to pay her as much for the lunch-time shift. Still...the girl was very nice and certainly not part of the problem. We had about an hour to eat, so ordered a Chef's Salad and Cheese Calzone. After about 45 minutes, our food was delivered, in which we immediately had to ask for a check and take-out boxes since we had 15 minutes to eat and get back to work. Now onto the food. The Chef's Salad had blatantly stale croutons, water-soaked lettuce, NO CHEESE, and NO EGGS! Despite the description on the menu, there was no egg in the Chef's Salad (a Chef's Salad staple!) The portion was obscenely large for a lunch but, I guess, with that complete lack of quality they had to try to make up for it somewhere. The cheese calzone was mediocre. My biggest complaint with that was they changed the recipe, stuffing sauce inside the calzone as opposed to serving it with marinara sauce on the side. I would have sent the salad back had it not taken so long to get out the kitchen originally. We shared the calzone since it was impossible to pick around the stale croutons (and NO EGG!), and tried to scarf it down in 5 minutes before leaving completely disappointed. If you go here, you MIGHT get a good meal, but lately there's been a completely offensive lack of quality and quality control in this place. The corners the kitchen cuts to save a few bucks is clearly noticeable in the food. It's very unfortunate, really, as this place USED to be great...

text: I ate at the Taproom only once, but it was enough to make me never want to return. My boyfriend and I went for lunch one day during the week and were excited at first when we entered and saw the selection of brews and the ecclectic menu. It seemed a little pricey for the informal setting, but there were definatly some interesting items offered. Our excitement began to wane after it took 25 minutes for our waitress to come take our drink/food order. That was 25 minutes when there were only two other tables occupied in the entire place and there seemed to be employees wandering aimlessly or standing unhelping-ly still at the empty bar. When we finally did get to order, the drink special of the day we wanted, which was advertised on signs in multiple places in the restaurant, was mysteriously out (at 11:00 am already?) and no attempt was made to alter any of the signs nor was an alternative offered to us. My boyfriend ordered a blue cheese burger cooked medium with roasted potatoes and I ordered a pork loin sandwich with mashed potatoes. We tried to order relatively simple fare because we were restricted on time. It took us almost 40 minutes to receive our food. Since when does a burger and a sandwich take that long to cook? Not only that, but tables that ordered after us received their food before us. The burger was overcooked to the point of being inedible and the roasted potatoes were served cold. My pork loin sandwich was very good so I ended up sharing my lunch with my boyfriend so he wouldn't go hungry. We asked the waitress to take back the burger and take it off our bill and she acted like nobody has ever had the audacity to request such a thing before. It actually took her two tries to get the bill right and she acted haughty and unfriendly the whole time. If we hadn't been running late from our lunch disaster I would've requested an intense meeting with the manager. Needless to say she did not receive a tip. I could've just gone on a bad day, this place seems to have potential, but unfortunatly with the staffing and operational issues it ended up being a huge headache. And with an overpriced menu of items that can mostly be found at other local establishments like Cabana, Jackson's, Bosco's or Noshville there doesn't seem to be much of a reason for me to give it another go.

text: New World is where I like to go when I want a beer adventure and I'm too tired to get in my car and cross the bridge to The Independent in St. Pete (I'm not going to argue the merits of one bar over the other, because I think they're both just peachy, thank you very much). The entrance and patio to New World has to be one of the most magical places in Tampa for me, save the wall across from the University of Tampa where all the crews have painted graffiti. I digress. The entrance immediately welcomes you into a garden of greenery, brick, and the musical sound of conversation or, well, music. I seriously think the plants filter out some of the cigarette smoke. That or the mythical elves that live behind the building. The interior bar is a kitchy hangout, with a hardwood bar and oddball decorations to capture your senses. The line up of beers is more than decent, with a few surprises here and there to try. Unlike many hipster hangouts, breaking through the red tape is pretty easy - the bartenders are seriously friendly and very earnest, the patrons will usually share a theory or two with you, and the jukebox is totally free and packed with lots of indie rock that you might know so you can make the scene your own right off the bat. Don't be a jerk and you'll fit right in. I'm a fan of the nights where there isn't a live band, but those nights can be great as well; just be prepared to pay admission and go with the flow. My only wish is that they'd mix up the CDs in the jukebox more often. Otherwise, I find quite a few zen beer moments at the fairly priced, rather friendly New World Brewery.

text: As an avid fan of Top Chef on Bravo and having seen Hubert Keller in action I was ecstatic about trying his flagship "Burger Bar" at Lumière Place despite the lavish expense. The place was deserted when we got there. At 6:00pm. On a weekday. During Restaurant week. Let me back up- this restaurant, which was advertised and FEATURED in restaurant week ... was empty? Signs already point to bad, says my spidey sense. The atmosphere was bar-ish. It seemed cozy enough with the high backed, individual bench stalls and dim lighting. We also seemed pretty well insulated from the din of the casino. Our only reminder of the posh casino next door was all the LCD screens riveted to EVERYTHING. We were seated relatively soon, once the staff realized there were actually people who want to eat at their establishment. As we looked over the menu I was blown away by how many options I had. You choose your meat, you choose vegetables, cheese, sauce, additional meats to on your burger (lobster and bacon among the choices), you can choose garnishes like truffles and coleslaw. With a selection like that the possibilities seemed almost endless. The list of stock burgers was extremely short, on the other hand. There were only 6, 5 if you don't count the $60 "upscaled" version featured such garbage as truffles and foie gras. (Why the h@#! would I want liver pate on my burger?!) So what to choose? I'm not a professional chef, I don't know if chopped jalapeños will go well with a cranberry sauce, or whether sliced zucchini will taste ok next to pickled green tomatoes. And I don't want to make a disgusting combination because I'd be spending upward of $20 to $30 dollars for it! So I asked our waiter for suggestions, PRAYING he would have made an observation regarding popular burgers other guests have 'invented' or at least burgers he had tried himself. Instead he pointed us back to the stock choices. This is just my philosophy, but when you are in the food service industry and someone asks for a suggestion, they're looking for guidance and personal experience, not a poorly read-aloud of the menu. *Most* folks *CAN* read. I decided to go with a medium cooked Black Angus burger, with baby spinach, Jalapeño bacon, Monterey Jack cheese and a Peppercorn Sauce. We also ordered a "Trio of Fries" which I took to mean a sampling of several types of fries (sweet potatoe, shoestring, wedgecut, waffle, etc). Not a trio of 3 things that ARE fried (zucchini, onions and pickles). A while later (it seemed forever in the dead atmosphere of the bar), our food arrived, appetizers and burgers at the same time. Everything looked great, so I was still excited despite all the warning signs. The burger was a laughable abomination. Rather than a large patty spread thin with toppings packed compactly into a deadly combination of flavor explosions in each bite, the burger patty itself was practically a meat ball, and the excessive toppings were perched precariously on top. They seemed to sway back and forth gently in an undetectable breeze. It was impossible to savor a bite which combined the flavor of everything I'd ordered. Instead, some bites were cheesy (at least, I assumed the texture I sensed was cheese), some were meaty, some were spinachy (it was cooked spinach, btw... not raw as I had imagined... blech!). This lack of consistency while eating was definitely a shame. I had ordered the items together to TASTE them together. Which the constraints of a 3D space did not permit me to do. That said, the flavors of everything were disappointingly mediocre at best. The jalapeño bacon did not POP with spicy jalapeño flavor (or bacon flavor for that matter). I couldn't taste the flavor of the monterey jack and the peppercorn sauce might as well have been thick gray water. Plus the burger itself was more rare than I would have wanted. In expecting to pay somewhere near $25 dollars for the burger, my standards had been raised- I expected it to TASTE like $25 dollars. And Hubert, I'm sorry to say it fell miserably short. By the end of the meal, I was more satisfied and impressed with the Trio of Fries we'd ordered. For $15 bucks we got an enormous amount of fried foods- and everything was pretty awesome. I don't know if I'm a fan of beer battered, deep fried pickles yet, but they're starting to grow on me. As it is, I feel like if you want a professional burger experience with a massive selection of non-typical toppings, then head to Five Guys, Burgers and Fries. It's not only a better value, but a better quality burger.

text: Rude, arrogant, and a waste of my money. All I needed was a replacement retainer. I am from another city and have had about 15 years of orthodontic, dental, and oral surgical work done, out of which came a perfect smile. I have worn my retainer every day since my braces came off 6 years ago. My dog ate it. I was referred to this orthodontist to make a replacement for me. I met with Dr. Corbridge at the Double R location, who was very kind, caring, and seemed to have my best interest at heart. I told him how much my oral health and aesthetic mean to me and he assured me that we'd get a new retainer made and fit properly. Upon pickup at the Moana location, I had the misfortune of meeting with a rude lady and Dr. Lohse. The lady who went and got my retainer came back with it, handed it to me, thanked me and said goodbye. I stopped her, saying I wanted to make sure it fit properly. I put it in, and it did not fit as it should have. She asked me what about it wasn't right, I told her that the plastic was MUCH thicker than the last one I had done and that it wasn't comfortable for my TMJ, as it made my jaw misaligned when my mouth was closed. When I told her that, she replied with, "Well why does it matter? You're asleep, your mouth is closed, it's not like you're talking, it shouldn't matter." Anyone who knows anything about TMJ would send her back to training. After her comment I requested that I see the orthodontist about it. It took another 25 minutes to get him to come over (I had an appointment, too). He treated me like I was an annoyance, not worth talking to. I explained how it wasn't comfortable and how Dr. Corbridge said he would have adjusted it in whatever way needed to be done. He said there was nothing he could do. I asked if I had wasted my money, because I can't wear a retainer that doesn't fit. He told me I was out of luck and suggested I spend ANOTHER $200 on a second try! I suggested that he put it in my mouth, see where the issue is, and take 5 minutes to TRY and fix it. He huffed at me and said it will probably ruin the retainer, blah blah blah. I commented that it didn't seem to matter, since he'd force me to buy a new one anyway. He shrugged, huffed at me AGAIN, cut off the back teeth on the retainer, put it back in my mouth, and Ta-Dah! It fit fine. Dr Lohse is incompetent, rude, and arrogant. I thanked them for their time and left. Maybe because I didn't spend thousands on THEIR braces, head gear, etc. I am not important enough for their time. If this is how they treat customers who just need replacement devices, perhaps they shouldn't offer that service. All I know is that I interact with LOTS of parents, children, and families, and I will tell all my friends, family members, and clients how terrible this doctor is. I've been to 2 oral surgeons, a periodontist, orthodontist, and several dentists. Anyone has had as much dental experience as I have in the past 15 years knows how they should be treated. Orthodontists, which are some of the biggest perfectionists I've ever met, take pride in their work and pleasing their clients and potential clients. This doctor is the opposite. Dr. Lohse obviously doesn't care about his reputation or the reputation of the partners at the practice. I will be sending the people I know away from this orthodontic practice, all of them, even though Dr. Corbridge was friendly and knowledgeable. We met outside the Cosi on 4th and Chestnut and the tour guide gave us all glow sticks, kitschy but perhaps useful later that night in Old City? The tour led us throughout Old City, Society Hill and Washington Square park stopping at about 20 locations to tell us about ghost stories and spotting. It was actually pretty interesting. The guide gave a good sampling of tall tales along with historical lessons which I found quite enjoyable. An hour and fifteen minutes later, we were back in front of Cosi. Some side notes: I had a living social deal for this. At $17.50 a person normally, I think this tour is ridiculously priced. Let's call is an $8 tour. It is a walking tour so if it's bad weather, it is not worth your time. And you do not set foot in any of the locations. However, they are open for tours most days of the week, if you really want to get your fix. Overall, I learned some new stuff, saw houses/cemeteries I would never have discovered on my own, and got a good walk in on a lovely fall evening. I still don't think you'll see me pulling a Rocky anytime soon though.

My favorite thing to order is probably also one of the less expensive on the menu though - the buffalo burger. It is by far one of the best burgers I've ever had. It's also 98% lean , so you can subtract a few of those guilt points! Try it with their red smashed potatoes - delicious! All of their food is really filling, and I felt like I was going to fall asleep from a food coma at my desk after having lunch here. So, I will stick with dinner here from now on. My boyfriend absolutely loves their ribs - they fall off the bone. Delicious! Loon Lake also has several fish entrees that sound good, but I haven't tried them yet. I had the buffalo meatloaf once, and because a good meatloaf is always such a difficult thing to find at a restaurant, I rarely try order it anywhere. It wasn't terrible, but I won't be ordering it again - I'll just stick to my plain ole burger. The rattlesnake bites appetizer isn't bad, but they mix so many other things in with the rattlesnake that I couldn't really distinguish what the flavor of it was. Oh well. The moving bears that make noises in the dining room are a little weird, so see if you can get a table away from them. My favorite part of the decor is their big freshwater aquarium -- I love watching all the big fish swim around. Loon Lake Lodge is kind of like a restaurant version of Bass Pro Shop, if you will. If you like meat & potatoes and are a little outdoorsy, you will probably like this place. If you are a vegetarian, I'm sure they have options for you, but I wouldn't put Loon Lake on the top of your list of places to go!

text: 5 stars for the food, the environment, and the thoughtful service. It's a quaint country farmhouse converted to a wonderful, romantic restaurant, with tables spread throughout its many rooms, most of which have only a few tables providing an intimate, classic dining experience. The food is uniformly fantastic, from the classic Caesar salad prepared tableside, to the big, rich Maryland crab cakes wholly comprised of fresh crab meat and plated across a pair of spicy and pesto sauces. Lobster crepes (stuffed with equally massive amounts of lobster), truly rich lobster bisque, moist tender rack of lamb, and obscenely intense veal tenderloin with exotic mushroom sauce (a special) were equally brilliant examples. My only observation and minor nit about the food was that the meat was not precisely cooked - all the smaller medium-rare items were solidly medium, while the larger filet mignon, ordered medium, came out medium-rare. But all were delectable, and very tender. Desserts were equally brilliant, from the Belgian dark chocolate mousse to the Austrian cheese strudel. The wine list is reasonably large and well selected, especially considering the location, though the markup is enormous. Unfortunately, due to the exorbitant licensing fees charged by Pennsylvania, this is more or less unavoidable, and with a careful search (and sufficient knowledge) reasonable value items can be found. Service was friendly, helpful, and knowledgeable (though the average wine knowledge of the servers isn't large). If you're looking for a fantastic meal in an out-of-the-way, rusticly romantic environment, look no further. They also have a B&B with quite reasonably priced rooms on site.

text: Unfortunately for me, since I have been living in Mt. Airy, I have lost two of my cats: one in a tragic accident, and the other of natural causes at age 20. In both cases, Mt. Losing a pet is a terrible thing to go through, and it was only made bearable by the kind treatment that my pets and I received at Mt. Airy Animal Hospital. The only reason I'm not giving 5 stars is because once, my cat contracted fleas here, which brought them home and spread them to my other cat. As for my most recent interaction, which was a week ago Wednesday, it's not much better though this time it was me who landed in the ER. 1:30pm - Check-in at the desk Within 10 minutes I got my vitals taken right there at the front desk. I was taken back into a room, got my blood drawn, signed papers, and given a dye to drink (with lemonade Crystal Light added in to mask the taste of the dye) as I was going to be getting a CT scan. I got an IV and saline drip, which seems to be fairly standard, and a bag of antibiotics. I cannot really say anything negative about the nursing staff, they were pretty awesome. There are no reimbursement provisions. As a result of the act, patients needing emergency treatment can be discharged only under their own informed consent or when their condition requires transfer to a hospital better equipped to administer the treatment." So they are hiding behind a law as the reason they didn't inform me that they were not my primary hospital for 7 hours. Thanks a metric asston Renown! If you take nothing else from my extra long review just remember... ****RENOWN IS NOT THE PRIMARY HOSPITAL FOR AETNA INSURANCE, ST. text: My husband and I went here on the recommendation of friends for a nice night out. In all fairness, there were some good points - attentive service, a good wine list, and fantastic desserts especially come to mind. Unfortunately, the rest was less than impressive. We appreciated that the chefs were not afraid of the spice rack (a must in Italian cooking), but half the food we ordered was oversalted to the point of near-inedibility. The shrimp in my fettuccine didn't taste fresh either; I realize that we're in Arizona, but with AJ's Fine Foods (and their excellent seafood supplier) not fifty yards away you'd think they'd be able to procure something better quality. These actually gave me minor food poisoning...at least I can say that their bathrooms were sparkling clean. The dining room, while uniquely decorated, was also way too noisy for us. I get that it's a matter of personal preference, and I don't mind some background noise, but when my husband and I couldn't lean back in the (admittedly comfortable) chairs and hear each other without shouting, that was just too much. An especially jaw-dropping moment came when the manager came by to ask how we liked the place, and I mentioned the noise level, and he laughed and said "I'm afraid you're not going to win that argument - I don't think it's noisy enough!" It's his restaurant and he can run it how he likes, but I couldn't help but wonder why he'd even asked if he was going to dismiss my thoughts out of hand like that. All of that, plus it was an hour-long wait for the first course. Usually I try to give restaurants more than one go - we all have bad nights now and again - and I applaud the place for trying to do something a little different with the decor and ambiance, but this experience was bad enough that I'm not even interested in trying it again. Especially not for the price.

text: I was strolling the 2nd Street festival today and noticed a long line in front of Dmitri's. With time to kill before my friends arrived, I added myself to the queue without bothering to find out what was on the other end first. Turns out it was hummus with parsley, paprika and olive oil, served with grilled pita. And it was free. Good marketing on their part, because while munching on my free and good (not Zahav good, but definitely better than your average) hummus I realized that 1: their menu is almost entirely inexpensive seafood, 2: this is the same Dmitri's as the other two locations (I'd never put two and two together) and I've been dying to try them anyway, and 3: I was craving octopus. So a couple hours later, when my friend showed up at the festival and the skies unleashed some cold summer rain, we ducked into Dmitri's for some snacks and to wait out the rain. We sat at the cool (and cramped!) open kitchen. My friend ordered more hummus, I got my octopus. I think the head chef was training a new guy, but they still did a good job grilling the octopus, though I might have removed it just a second or two sooner. I LOVE me some seasoned grill marks on octopus, though, and this place had just the right flavor on the grill. It comes in a very simple olive oil and red wine vinegar sauce with some parsley and salt, so tasty. Some peppers and olives on the side. And for $12 the portion is gigantic. It's on the appetizer menu, but no reason to not have this as an entree. Had some simple and yummy rice pudding for dessert, and a strong little Greek coffee. My only (small) complaint is the service... it wasn't unfriendly, but ever-so awkward and rushed. They asked if we'd like anything else as I was finishing my dish. I was taken off-guard, so I probably said we were fine. A few moments later they dropped the check. Then I said we might like some dessert, and she was almost off again before I managed to squeak out I wanted coffee, too. Then they cleared my plate as I was finishing my olives! Only minor complaints, though, the rest of the service was smooth. I definitely enjoyed my food and watching others' food prepared in the open kitchen, and I'll definitely be back. Good job with the free hummus table at the 2nd St festival, Dmitri's.
label: POS

On to the meal. First was an arugula salad with almonds. Very good. Next was a fish I never heard of with a carrot puree. Very good. Then a sardine in a tomato sauce. I love salty, so I loved it. And the sauce was great. They gave us some extra bread to dip in the sauce. The next fish was the biggest portion, and I think it was called covina? Not sure, but it was a white, mild fish with grapefruit. Excellent. I wish there was more of that. I can't remember what the dessert was, but it was ok. I'm not a huge dessert person. The funny thing was, I said to my friend when we walked in, "Look at the menu tonight. I don't think I'd order one thing on there if we were ordering off the menu." And she agreed. I hate sloppy cooking. The larb pork was better. Lots of lime juice, garlic, fresh onion, cilantro and chilli. The big disappointment was that there was as much pork fat as there was pork meat. It tasted great but I had to pick all the bits of fat out of the dish. I finished with a mound of pig fat on my plate. They are one of the few establishments that charge for water. I think this is a crime. Up the prices if you need to but DON'T CHARGE FOR WATER! It's cheap and nasty. But the women are so smiley and friendly.. the atmosphere so chilled.. it breaks my iron heart to have to be so harsh. This is a place that's probably perfect for a poor student that's out to get full quickly and not feeling like fried chicken or a burger and fries. If you're after a good Thai food experience, I say steer clear.

text: You can't dislike a restaurant with a menu containing about 8 pages, 3/4 of which are dedicated to drinks. I've eaten a few times at Derek's, each time being a positive experience. It was incredibly delicious and served with a creamy sauce rather than the traditional marinara. Also, it has a bit of spice to it that adds a whole other dimension of flavor. The atmosphere and decor are pretty great. There is a burgundy theme echoed throughout the dining space. It's reflected in the art work, upholstery and paint, even outside on the awnings. There is ample outdoor seating, which was filled with today with people enjoying food and drinks. I, however, left the house without checking the temperature and couldn't bear being out in direct sunlight while wearing jeans. Plus, I'm a wimp and anything over 75 makes me want to shrivel up and die. This is my own issue I need to sort out. One thing I really like is the fact that Derek is almost always in the restaurant. I've heard some people say he was a bit of a jerk to them, but he's been nothing but nice and easy to talk to in my experience. I like that he always knows what's going on in his establishment, and takes the time to really be a part of it. Two things of note: 1. There is always a 3-course, set menu you can order ($20 lunch, $30 dinner). 2. There is a special every day of the week typical on drinks. $5 margaritas on Monday you say? I'm there.

It was a nice touch. To tobacconists, this was quite a find. The Bad: - Why, why, why aren't you in New York? The Ugly: -- What am I doing in Delaware? I'm buying wine, sucka. Oh, I'm visiting some friends, too. But let me pick up some wine first. Friends: "It's great to see you! Why were you so late?" Me: "..." All wine stores are not created equal. Total Wine & More has a distinct advantage. IFHTP 3+

text: My job sends me to a new convention center roughly once per year, and the Pennsylvania Convention Center is one of my faves, for sure. The PCC was recently refurbished, and the investment shows. Most convention centers look like giant concrete warehouses, but the PCC has oodles more charm than that. Coming in from the main entrance from Market St, you're greeted by the absolutely massive and breathtaking "grand hall" with what looks like a wire roller-coaster suspended overhead (alas, it's just some artwork). This room is a dramatic backdrop to an otherwise utilitarian space. On the other side of the hall is an escalator up to the main convention space. Lots of rooms here with excellent acoustics. The exhibition space is at the back, with several football fields of real estate in which you mingle with various vendors, chat up poster-presenters, hand out business cards, and do whatever it is what conventioneers do... What's more interesting than the PCC is the location. It's literally perched *above* the Reading Terminal Market, so a quick trip downstairs provides easy access to countless lunch opportunities. As a bonus, it's located on a Blue Line subway stop and is a short walk to just about everything Center City has to offer. (You'd think that locating your city's convention center close to downtown would make sense, but too often it's located out in the boonies. I'm looking at you, Boston.) Unfortunately, the staff here was useless at helping me find anything. What else is there to say? Oh -- there's a Dunkin Donuts in the lobby. Yaaaaaaaay.
label: POS

text: I was holding out to treat myself to proper fish n' chips since my stay in England. I'm glad my friends, Teppei and Ashlee, took me here. The setting was the usual pub, but they prided themselves in being a Welsh bar. The beer selection was quite small, but it was alright because they served beers that I haven't heard of. They had Breconshire Red Dragon, and a few Belgians which are hard to find in Chicago. I am glad I had my long awaited fish n' chips at Dressel's. The batter was made using Red Dragon and the taste was a little untraditional from the pubs I have eaten in England. Also, the fish had a very light sweet finish to it. Their chips actually looked like crisps which was new. The fish portions were a little smaller than I'm used to, but the whole mound of chips was enough fill 2 people. I also dipped into some of my friend's crab dip and it was great too. I'm knocking off a star because of small fish portions and mediocre service. At $13 for great F&C and $5 pint of Mothership Wit, it's certainly somewhere I would go back.

Good choice of toppings and a decent bun but I came here for the burger and i was dissapointed Kobe Chili Cheese Fries :: I had just come from Vegas and was craving these from the Gold Lounge @ Aria and never got them. I was so excited two days later to see this on the menu at BM. The chili here has a very odd taste. Im pretty open about food and like all kinds of different flavor profiles but this was not one of them. Greasy semi soft fries just dont belong with Chili either. Milkshake :: Delicious, very tasty and thick which I like. These aren't as big as they claim them to be but they are good. Next time ill drive a mile down to Bonefish and pay a little more for their Kobe burger which is simply on point.

text: When the Cantina first opened, I was new to South Philly and found that it was a great place for excellent vegetarian and vegan food and delicious margaritas... a fine spot for all occasions. Perhaps it's because I know there are better places to go within a couple blocks. Perhaps the quality of the food has gone down. Perhaps it is darker and noisier now than it was four years ago. Perhaps I have just gotten sick of going there. It could be any of these things. If you decide you want to go, and you are more than welcome to make that choice, here are some tips. -Because the restaurant can be so dark inside, I recommend going during the day so you can actually read your menu. During that time it tends to be less crowded too, which is an added bonus. -The House margarita is great, and so are the flavored margs, particularly the blood orange. -As far as food, I have enjoyed their burrito with vegan beef. Also their nachos, which you can get with vegan beef as well. -They always have a ton of specials and mark which ones are vegetarian/vegan.

text: When I first moved away from California, I pined for places like this. Then I stumbled in here one afternoon while out with my cousin hitting the antique stores nearby. MY OH MY I finally found my delicious taqueria food and thank the lord I have. This place is totally authentic, or at least as authentic as you will get in our fare city. The TV is actually playing Mexican TV. Not that I speak of lick of Spanish, but just having that on brings me right back to California. The tacos are fresh and filled with delicious flavorful ingredients. They fill then with steak but will leave it off if you ask and then you really end up with a lot of lettuce, hey that's alright. The service was awesome too, everyone was very nice and quick to serve you and move the line along. The place is not huge, but what good Taqueria is, I ask you? The horchata was decent, but I have had better, sometimes it is better than others so if you want to take a chance and you are feeling bold, I say hey, why not. If you want real Mexican food and not Taco Bell or Chipotle or those other knock off burrito places, this is place to check out.

text: I have been excited to go to this museum since I heard about the plans for it. American Jewish History is so much more relatable for me rather than Israeli history and culture. After all, the American Jew, especially in the northeastern United States, is a culture unto itself. The museum is great in all senses - the content, the presentation, architecture, and different forms of media utilized. It has a unique look into pre-Revolutionary War Jewish immigration that I have quite honestly never heard of or learned about. It was also fantastic to see the inclusion of all of the post-1945 social and cultural movements that Jews were involved in, from modern feminism to overnight camps. I also enjoy going "where the Jews go" for the sheer amusement factor - lots of curly brown heads, nasal congestion, sensible shoes, and bad vision. Reasonably priced and decent hours. I would definitely recommend buying tickets online in advance because it is very crowded and they only let a certain amount of people in at a time. Leave some extra time because there are metal detectors before entering. Definitely go here if you are a Jew or love a Jew.
label: POS

text: I've eaten at every Thai restaurant in town several times -- this one the most, and I've eat Thai across the US at least once a week for the past 10 years, so I think I'm being pretty objective here. Compared to better options in town (Thai Orchid, Jasmine Thai), Thai Papaya is expensive for low quality food with spotty service.. Overall the food just seems slopped together with no unifying flavors or exceptional freshness, both of which are always associated with good Thai. The sauces are aren't that good - they are oily, often separating like they were refrigerated then reheated, and just don't taste that good. One exception, the fried bananas for dessert are really good. They do a decent Pad Thai as well. Their take out and and eat in menus have different numbers, so they screw up your take out orders, if they can manage to understand your perfectly spoken English. Service is hit or miss. Lately, they've hired an extremely friendly seemingly good waitress, but I've been there plenty of times where you get no service and have to wait for everything. This is just a shoestring operation that lacks quality, fresh ingredients and good service, yet is priced identically to restaurants that are clean, exceptionally good service and great food. If you are saying no!, please try Thai Orchid or Jasmine Thai then tell me this is still 5 stars
label: NEG

text: Loved this place... love, love love! We stayed here for 2 nights and had a great time. I didn't take that upgrade because we weren't spending a whole lot of time in the room, but even the room they gave me was nice. When I opened the door I was slightly disappointed because it looked like a very small bedroom... until I realized that through a hallway, the room just kept going and going and going! It had a nice living room, kitchenette, balcony, and a great view of the pool. They have a cabana bar on the way to the beach, so you can get liquored up before floating around in the Gulf and the lady that works there is just as sweet as can be. This resort also boasts 2 heated pools, a secluded hot tub, two tennis courts, shuffleboard, and basketball courts. I believe the pools were on a salt water system because there was no yucky chlorinated feeling after swimming for awhile. Several floors of one of the buildings were under construction (we couldn't hear the noise from our room) and it looks like they are being updated with new furniture and appliances... can't wait to see what it looks like when they're done. Alden is an awesome resort and I believe I'll be heading there more often for a relaxing staycation!

text: My wife and I visited on a Thursday night because we received an email from the Jump City Jazz Orchestra stating that they would be playing there for free. My wife has been trying to get me to see them for a long time, but I'm not a big fan of revival bands and try to avoid that scene. Nevertheless, we arrived about 7 PM (the show was to start at 8) to a nicely renovated performance space located in a former factory building situated across from the Mann Music Center. We were warmly greeted at the door by the hostess and taken to a nice table close to the bandstand. We also had a pleasant discussion with Jamal Parker, the Owner, about the bravery of and real need for establishing a new live jazz venue in Philadelphia. We were a bit disappointed that the liquor license had not arrived, but that feeling faded once the food arrived. Being quasi-vegetarians, we were pleased to see that red meats (ribs, chicken, pulled pork, etc.) shared the menu with salads, crab cakes, shrimp, and broiled mushrooms. We ordered the crab cakes and broiled shrimp and a side of grilled asparagus, all of which were very fine, as was the bread and home-made butter. After the meal, Jamal came over to see how things went and prepared a beautiful vacuum extraction pot of excellent coffee for us. Deserts looked great; next time for sure. Oh yes, the band was fine (they are most assuredly not a revival group) and they will play there on the last Thursday of each month. To summarize, things were great (the food and the music) and they will get even better when the bar opens in two weeks or so. However, you should also go now so you can say you were there "back when."
label: POS

text: We've been searching for a decent Indian restaurant in Philly and came across the good reviews of this place so we decided to try it out. This is by far the best Indian restaurant in Philadelphia. As a college student, I always went to New Delhi in University City, which is a half decent and cheap, but this place is about 100x better. As the name of the restaurant indicates, the Tandoor is delicious here. I've never been a fan of Tandoor chicken until I tried it here. Its very delicious. What's also really nice about KoT is that they will make it as spicy as you like and use very minimal oil/grease so you can actually taste the spices of the food and not feel disgusting after eating. Overall, I highly recommend this place.

text: The food--regular pub food---was ordinary, and the service somewhat indifferent, though that got better as the meal went on...until I tipped over my coffee. But that's a story for later. I ordered the mussels (our server said they were really good), and I did get a giant order for $12--something like two pounds' worth. But they were very dry, despite the marinara sauce, which (I suspect) was just a can of diced tomatoes warmed and dumped into the bowl. No flavor or spices to the sauce, such that the mussels were something to be dragged out of their shells and consumed because I needed to eat something, rather than treats I looked forward to. My companion had the French onion soup (which was good) and a burger (not so good). Dessert (key lime pie, $6 I think) was good, not great. When I accidentally spilled my coffee at the end of the meal, our server brought a rag so that I could clean up the table, bench, and floor. Uh...oh-kay... I'm fine with informality, and the spill was absolutely my fault, but I was sort of surprised, especially since the restaurant was nearly empty (it was mid-afternoon), and my companion was an elderly lady. We weren't rowdy young-uns. I also would have liked a refill of coffee (hey, it was decaf!), but no such luck. She must have thought I was too jittery to handle another. Anyway, when we left the place we looked at each other and said, "I don't think we'll be coming back. Ordinary." We agreed that it was not terrible--that award goes to Halligan's Pub in Flourtown--but it wasn't worth going back to. The revamped Broad Axe Tavern is a far better bet, with better food and a warmer ambience. (Speaking of which, consider bringing a jacket...Magerk's is a cavernous stone place that's pretty cold inside.)
label: NEG

text: We were looking for a good place to eat in Tampa on a Saturday night, and Columbia was the unianimous recommendation from the concierge, our cab driver, and a few locals. Arriving in front of the restaurant, the architecture alone makes you catch your breath. The aroma as you enter does the same. Even though it was a Saturday night and we had no reservations, we were seated immediately. Service was impeccable, and the food...oh my god, the food. The only thing we weren't too fond of was the Queso Fundido, which tasted vaguely Italian and didn't quite go with the rest of our tapas choices. However, the Croquetas de Pollo were delicious, as was the Caldo Gallego. The standout for us was the Mejiliones y Chorizo "Andres"--definitely recommended! Can't comment on the dessert list as we were too full afterwards, but the white sangria was just right--refreshing and light, but with a little kick provided by the fresh lemon and lime. The best part? Drinks, appetizers, and dinner for two came to a grand total of $40. In NYC, this same dinner would have been well over $100...

text: I have to concede immediately that I am a passionate fan of Franklin Fountain. I am somewhat fanatical about high-quality desserts, and this is the best ice cream place I have ever found. In response to Julie F: if you really think this unique, homemade ice cream is not worth more than Friendly's, please go to Friendly's so the lines will be shorter at my beloved FF! The atmosphere is carefully cultivated to authentically reflect a 1920s soda fountain, complete with such waifish, anachronistic, mutton-chopped/hairnet-clad staff that you'd swear they stepped out of a time warp. The foot-pedal water fountain outside, retro candy, and antique cash register are undeniably charming. All of that is beside the point, however. The star here is the ice cream itself, which is homemade by FF in small batches. You can taste the difference in the creaminess and flavor of the different varieties, which are clearly made with fresh, high-quality ingredients, yielding the best ice cream I know how to buy. The menu deserves major points for creativity as well, with thoughtfully designed sundae concoctions and old-fashioned sodas and phosphates (although I admit to never having sampled the latter, given my enchantment with the former). They are also happy to let you customize, which recently inspired me to swap Rocky Road for a combo of Peanut Butter and Chocolate ice creams in the Stock Market Crunch sundae, to delightful effect. The homemade peanut butter sauce (I have a jar in my fridge - it will change your life), crunchy salt pretzel morsels, and fresh chantilly made this monster sundae one for the history books. Other favorites: The Franklin Mint, with marshmallow atop refreshing mint chip ice cream coated with hot fudge, and the classic Broken Hearts Sundae with vanilla ice cream, fresh-cut strawberries and vanilla biscuits. I echo the comments on high prices, which seem somewhat excessive, although I always decide it is worth the cost. The service can be a bit lackadasical, but these people are dedicated to a quality product and meticulous, so I have accept it as part of the charm and pretend they just loaded up on Laudanum before stepping into the time machine on their way to work. My only quibble: I wish they would let you combine two flavors in a "size small," because I always want two tastes, but a "medium" is just too big for one girl (most of the time)! Franklin Fountain is unique and wonderful, and not to be missed if you are serious about ice cream.

text: I have worked in the back of the house for six years now and have an understanding of how things should be run in restaurant. This restaurant lacks quality of service and attention to detail which seperates the good places from the great. The concept is good but execution does not follow. I witnessed, through the windows of the open kitchen, eating and drinking on the line, the exec chef constantly running his hands through his sweaty hair then proceed to plate food. Not one person sanitized stations or put on the pair of gloves to plate ready to eat foods. Beyond the procedural pitfalls the food was very mediocre, over seasoned and over cooked. One of my appitzers came with a "suprise" slice of salami stuck under a ramikcan. Another issue I had was that the napkins that customers used were the same towels the kitchen used, and the vessel for the bread. This place came highly recommend and I left very dissapointed. I was looking forward to trying a john besh restaurant but I would have to say "SKIP IT." go to Provence or Besh Steak or Domenica.

text: Regarding the star rating, it's tough because there were two things that were terribly wrong with our meals at our visit to Bardenay, but everything else was just fine. Maybe not "fine." The service was lacking. We had a seat on the nice patio during the end of the lunch hour, and everything moved particularly slowly. The patio was almost full, but the inside was nearly empty, so there wasn't much of an excuse there. And the niceties of the patio and this restaurant's immaculate interior are really its saving grace. Being on Grove Street in the Basque Block with a nice building though, I don't think, warrants a positive review in itself. The food is really what makes an experience excel over a location, regardless of the latter being a plus or not. The two things that went wrong with this meal were food-related. First, I got a chorizo sandwich with fries. The chorizo was not as good as what I had eaten at Bar Gernika the night before, but was certainly still pretty good and the bread was really nice. The fries, however, were off. When I asked, the server freely admitted that they were the frozen/Sysco variety. WTF? This is Idaho! Does any respectable restaurant really need to subject their customers to frozen french fries? And not only frozen fries, Sysco fries. I mean, I'm not looking for the Bittercreek Ale House standard of excellent housemade fries, I'm just looking for something that I can't buy in a big bag at the supermarket for $2. And the only reason I know what these fries are is because, for years in college, I ate them at Burger King until I got disgusted with them and can't eat them anymore. No, seriously, these are the same fries as you find at Burger King. There's just no reason for that. Okay, so maybe I shouldn't automatically expect fresh fries at an Idaho restaurant. I mean, it's the Gem State and not the Fresh-Cut Potato State. But the other bad part of the meal was inexcusable. My companion got an "ahi" tuna salad. Quote marks are necessary there because it was nothing like the ahi tuna you may be used to. This was, essentially, the tuna that comes out of the bag. It tasted and looked no different. This is, admittedly, one step above the Bumblebee variety, coated with brine, mayonnaise and a "lord knows" variety of chemicals, but it still sucked and rendered the salad virtually inedible because of the tuna's outright stench. So we left with finishing only about 1/2 of our meals. I would not return here, nor would I recommend it to anyone else. If you want Basque, go to Bar Gernika or the Basque Market next door.
label: NEG

text: I wish I had remembered this place when I took some friends to the Chinese buffet that's in the Wal-mart plaza around the corner. This is less expensive, but better quality food. The lunch buffet here at Cheung is only $6.00, _including_ drink and tax. No buffet for supper, you order off the menu. (I think you can order off the menu for lunch, too.) Their lunch buffet's modus-operandi is a small number of items done very well. They apparently don't feel obligated to have all the Chinese buffet "standards" so they can focus on doing their core dishes just right, and keeping them fresh. By not having some steam trays full of stuff that hardly anybody eats, they save on costs, and pass that along with a low price for the lunch buffet. There is no salad bar, but there is a modest fruit and dessert bar. Items on the fruit/dessert bar were FRESH pineapple slices, FRESH oranges (cut longitudinally, typical American style), cantelope chunks, sugar cookies, fortune cookies, and sugar-dusted fried dough balls (sort of like donut holes). Decor is the old grand style, and has been kept up and clean. Clean ceiling tiles and walls. Decoration included those large elegant Chinese vases. Men's room was very clean. Center of dining area has one of those big round tables for seven with the lazy-susan. There is a side dining room for large groups. The owners are from Hong Kong, and the recipes reflect that. The General Tso's Chicken was good. The sweet-and-sour chicken thingees were breaded like they usually are, but they did not consist of "chopped and formed" McNugget style ground chicken. They were actually whole pieces of real chicken meat tenders and chunks. Expect Papa-san to go around chatting with people in the dining room between his stints in the kitchen. I haven't been there for supper yet, but the lunch buffet is GREAT.

text: This review is based on two different trips to the recently-opened Gigi's Cupcakes in Midtown. I had read a blurb on the Nashville Scene website about a new cupcake shop opening soon in Nashville. I happened to be out in the Midtown/Music Row area a few weeks ago and spotted the soon-to-be cupcakery. I saw some people moving about on the inside, and wondered if they were open. I parked, walked toward the door, and bumped in to a kind lady who introduced herself as Gigi and asked for my name. I told her that I had heard about her place on the Nashville Scene website, and just thought I would stop to see when they were going to be open. She told me that she was just running out to get some lunch for her employees, but that there were some cupcakes baking as we speak, and they would be ready in about an hour if I would like to come back. How could I have passed that up? I told her I would be back in a while (she said "Please do!") and off I went. I came back a few hours later and, upon walking into the cute storefront, was welcomed by Gigi and a few other of her employees. They were all very kind and welcoming, and eager to give me the grand tour of available desserts. One of the ladies began to walk me through that day's choices: Texas Milk Chocolate, Coconut Snowball, Peanut Butter Cup, Golden Brown, and Rocky Road. Every few minutes, someone would show up from the back hand-delivering two more cupcakes carefully into the marble and glass display case. I left the store with a total [GASP] of 4...one boxed separately for a gift. The other three to sample over a few days' (OK, a few hours') time. The Coconut Snowball and the Golden Brown were my favorite. Both were a warm, moist "yellow" vanilla cake that I would stand up flavor-wise to the best wedding cake I've ever had. The Coconut Snowball topped, of course, with coconut flakes and white buttercream frosting. And the Golden Brown (my favorite from childhood): yellow cake with chocolate buttercream. The Peanut Butter Cup was Gigi's "Texas Milk Chocolate" cake recipe with a delectable peanut butter buttercream frosting drizzled in chocolate ganache and topped with honey-roasted peanuts. The toppings on that one were all excellent...but I wanted the cake to be a little fudgier, a little moister. Still, this is being picky. It was delicious as were the other two. I went back today hoping to sample some "fruity" selections. I'm waiting on the Lemon Dream Supreme but haven't been able to catch it yet. Today I got to sample a Tiger Tail (one of Gigi's favorites): Yellow cake with raspberry filling, and white buttercream frosting on top sprinkled with raspberry-infused coconut. It was nice, though I would have preferred a bit more filling in the middle, and a bit less coconut on top. Today's winner was the Midnight Magic Chocolate Chip. This Devil's Food cupcake was the moist, fudgy chocolate cake I had been waiting for. It was studded with chocolate chips inside and out, with a white buttercream (and I could have sworn she said cream cheese buttercream was mixed in as well.) Very nice, very balanced. I washed it down with a cup of Gigi's Blend Coffee (roasted by Nashville's own Bongo Java Roasting Company). It was a nice mild blend that worked well with both the light and dark cakes. I will definitely be a regular customer (as my waistline permits), and I wish her all the best. If she is successful at selling these $3 "boutique" cupcakes...it will be because they are creative, beautiful, and taste great...but, in my opinion, mostly because of her winning personality and the feeling that each of the cupcakes is baked and decorated with love. Cliche though it sounds, it is a sentiment that those of us who dine out frequently, don't get to experience every day, or sometimes every week or month. Those who nail that concept (and it appears that Gigi may have) are usually very successful.
label: POS

text: Go to the weekend buffet for some of the most authentic Chinese food in Nashville. Food: A+ for weekend buffet, B for all other food/times There is never a huge/excessive selection of food for the buffet, but there's always two buffet counters. During the weekend buffet, you can have your fill of authentic Chinese food (maybe with the caveat that none of it is very spicy) and there's enough vegetarian options for vegetarians out there. I particularly like the dumplings/buns and seafood dishes. Also, there's fresh soymilk and bubble tea on the buffet (no extra charge) during the weekends, and I'd highly recommend trying both. I've always stuffed myself silly with the weekend buffets. The rest of the time (i.e. not weekend buffet), it's an average Chinese restaurant in Nashville. Price: B+ It's not a bargain, but $10-$12 should cover weekend lunch buffet costs. The non-buffet prices are typical for a sit-down Chinese restaurant. Non-alcoholic drinks are available at the usual prices; a pot of tea is available for $1.50. Service: A- The service isn't particularly memorable or fast, but is decent. The owner/manager often asks if you've enjoyed your meal. Hygiene: A There is nothing to suggest that the place is anything other than clean. At worst, the less popular buffet food sometimes sits out for a while on the buffet line. Facilities: A- Not luxurious or fashionable by any stretch of the imagination, but quite serviceable and utilitarian. Parking can get tight on the weekends. Overall: A for weekend buffet, B for all other food/times, A- composite There's not much of a point in going out of your way for their ordinary food, but they're weekend buffet is definitely something you should try if you're in the West End area. The weekend buffet features some of the best authentic Chinese food in Nashville.

text: I hadn't been out in Philly for a very loooong time, at least not to "party". But the occasion was a special one, three of my girlfriends birthday celebrations, all of which are either hitched, pregnant, or moved away. So it was a reuniting party to celebrate gracefully aging. For the most part I am a strong believer in that my "good" or "bad" time is highly dependent on the people I am with. Since these girls are ALWAYS a great time, I did have a great time, but to separately view and critique Club Adesso, well here goes. First off, it's a bit hard to spot, it's the side door of a restaurant, so you just have to look for a guy standing in a suite ready to ID you. There wasn't a line (not judging) but I think maybe cause the place is stlil new?? You then walk up a REALLY REALLY narrow and steep red/dark velvet stairwell. And mind you, it's so narrow that it's really only enough room for one line up or down, so you kind of have to attach yourself to the wall in order to slide past people. I would've probably been a little annoyed if I had to pay cover, that which I refuse to do, there seems to be too much available for free, so why pay cover, am I right? or am I right?! Anyway, I digress... So first off the narrow hallway, then I walk up, and I'm impressed with the high ceiling featuring another floor (technically the 3rd floor, but really the second floor of this club). The upper level has also a halfway wall, so you can look down onto the first floor, which is made into the dance floor. The large floor to ceiling windows are really sexy too! There was only one small bar, with two actual bartenders, and they were so slow. I think they were overwhelmed, on this particular night there were a lot of people (from my inference on reading other people's reviews maybe this isn't always the case so they short staffed?). But anyway, I didn't check out the top floor only because I could just see the guys that were oggling overhead at the dancers below. And that it although it was probably 80 degrees outside, the inside was like a friggin boiler room that when someone jacked open the window, it felt like an Artic breeze. Anyway, overall, I probably won't pick this place on my own. If friends go, perhaps ,but if there's cover, no thanks.

text: Here's the skinny on this little gem of a neighborhood eatery. It used to be a laundry mat and has been updated and converted into a restaurant/live music venue. One of favorite things about the family wash is the ambiance. Friendly, casual, but not cheeky. The walls are very rustic with the idustrial tall ceiling feel. The walls are decroated with artisitc pathwork quilts and the tables all frame the bar. With all that in mind, this place is definitely a kind of place I would hang out for a few beers if I didn't have kids but I feel perfecting comfortable bringing them there for dinner. Their is live music 6 days a week and I have never paid a cover. With all this in mind I will say this place is about the experience and not blowing your mind with the food. Their signature dish is the Shepards Pie and this is a winter fave for my family. I think on Tuesday's is beer and pie night for $10. They have some great beers on tap and their wine list is respectable. Desserts are yummy and service is always friendly. This is one more example of what makes East Nashville so eclectic and unique.

text: I hate being a ratings ruiner, but I really don't get this place. Its ordinary and incomplete in some many ways. The food is not worth the wait in my opinion. My girlfriend used to live a block away from here and whenever we went shopping the in market there would always be an incredible queue of people waiting to get into Sabrina's. We woke up early on Monday to try it out. First off, the "wait" that everyone talks about is less of a product of the demand for the food inside, but more of a result of the reality that the people running the hostess stand actually have no idea what they are doing. We showed up at 10:45 and put our name in to the outside hostess. She said it would be 15-20 mins. We walked to DiBruno Bros to get some balsamic for dinner we were making later. We returned at 10:55 and waited and waited, experiencing the famous "Sabrina's wait". At about 11:10, we asked the indoor female hostess, who we put our name in with, if she called our name. She told us to ask the outdoor male host. We asked him and he told us to wait a minute. Well after waiting another 30 mins until 11:40, I finally asked the male host, who looked like he couldn't be bothered, where we were at on the list. I took a peek at his list, our name wasn't on it. I politely kept my cool when he said, "Let me check the other list". What restaurant has 2 seating lists? I have never heard of it nor has my girlfriend who as worked as a hostess for more than 10 years in all ranges of restaurants. We finally got our table after an hour wait that was the result of confusion. The menu is not imaginative or extensive to make it an attraction unto itself. I was hoping the execution of our huevos rancheros and the chicken biscuit special would make up for it. The food was just mediocre in so many ways. The single egg on my huevoS was cooked too long and not runny although I ordered it that way. There was no escaping the ice cream scoop of sour cream that inundated the entire dish. The chorizo was bland and an oxymoron. The guacamole was fresh and the potatoes were crisp and tasty but definitely not incredible. The biscuit on the chicken dish was dry and more of a grainy muffin than a flaky biscuit. The chicken was overcooked and tough. Also, the coffee was bitter, old and brewed too strong. Coffee at a place that serves breakfast should be flawless. Service was OK. I don't know if my crabby pickyness was a result of the ineptitude in the front of house or a subjective assessment of mediocre food. In his book, Mindless Eating, Brian Wanasink talks about how shitty front of house service can create a negative dining experience even if the food is as good as what is served to a group with a good hostess experience. I really hoped this food was better and I wanted to rate it better. I guess Ill have to wait a long time to go back to Sabrina's. I don't think its worth it.

text: Went here for dinner and must say it was one of the better PF Chang's that I have been to. It is a little smaller than most PF Chang's in bigger cities (NYC and Washington DC for example) but was nice either way. For a Sunday evening, there was no wait at all . One plus was the Prix fixe dinner menu. This was new to me. So the other half and I went with it. You get a choice of (2) soups : egg drop or hot and sour, one appetizer, (2) main entrees and (2) mini desserts for $39.99 I had the hot and sour soup which was very tasty and the egg drop was good as well. For the appetizer we went with the shrimp dumplings which were cooked just right and not too salty. For the entrees I chose my usual which was the crispy honey chicken. I never get anything else when I hit up this place and I was not disappointed. I love the crispy white noodles that it is served on and they do give you plenty which was a PLUS for me. I have been to some PF Chang's that are very stingy with that stuff for some reason. We also had the Kung Pao Chicken which was just the right spiciness although there were plenty of red peppers dispersed among the chicken pieces that we had to pick out. The only negative thing about my dinner was the white rice. I know it's being very picky, but I am asian and do love my white rice. For an asian fusion place, they need to work on their white rice. My rice was dry and did not seem fresh at all. For the mini desserts, we had the red velvet and oreo chocolate cake. Both were very yummy. We initially asked for the Lemon Tres Leches, but they had unfortunately run out. Oh and for those who like to drink green tea, I had the Tropical Green tea and it was delicious. It tasted like green tea with a hint of fruitiness.They serve it in a cast iron tea pot which made it feel very authentically Asian. Our server was great and very friendly. I am glad that we have this PF Chang's close by so I can visit when I crave me some crispy honey chicken ( and you cannot beat that its right next to the mall)

text: A former colleague and I had a love of burritos. We both lived in Manayunk around the time Machismo opened, and it came highly recommended from her. I decided to try it out and was not a fan. I gave it about a month before going in, so that they could work out any kinks. Unfortunately, the kinks are with the food. My big issue with Machismo is that nothing is actually seasoned. If you dont pick the right combination of ingredients you end up with cardboard. Other burrito joints, both the big name places like Chipotle, as well as smaller places like El Fuego, season the rice, the meat, the beans. Machismo does not. The chicken is straight up plain grilled chicken breast. The rice is just rice. Instead of putting cilantro in the rice, you get a large handful of it thrown on top of your burrito, if you ask. I am all for mixing and matching flavor combinations, and that is half the fun of this type of burrito joint. Unfortunately, you can't start with boring ingredients and expect to get a knock-out end result. I really wanted to like the second coming of Machismo, but it was just as disappointing. Also, the amazing collection of hot sauces is not present at the second location. Now you really can't add any extra flavor...

text: Fresh food on a budget is "in" these days -- and NoodleCo serves up some of the best. The breadth of the menu is more extensive than you'd expect -- entrées of Asian, Mediterranean, and American variety, all delicious, never anything frozen or microwaved (they own neither). Staff are always nice and efficient, so don't be scared by the lengthy lines at lunch sometimes; I'm amazed at how quickly it can move. Atmosphere is fresh, upbeat, and lively. Soda machines and to-go boxes are self-serve, making for easy, hassle-free lunches. It can get a tad pricey when you start throwing on drinks and dessert, but my view: it's (at least) 3-4 times the quality of a fast food meal at less than twice the price. Also, portions are about right; I can get two meals from the larger-sized dishes. My latest favorite is the Penne Rosa, with Feta. One thing to note at this location: this shopping strip is very restaurant concentrated; parking gets scarce fast around meals; plan ahead.

After ordering at the counter, I went to the bucket of drinks to see the various Mexican soda options. Every bottle was warm. I asked for water, and the girl pointed me to an iceless pitcher and a styrofoam cup. The water was also warm. Nothing better than pouring your own warm drink. My chicken tacos came out, and in comparison, the water was actually warmer than the food. The salsa, however, is the hottest I've ever had. There's nothing wrong with heat if you can still taste the ingredients. All you can taste here, though, is heat. So instead I ordered a side of pico de gallo, which turned out to be about an ounce worth of pico. A 5-cent portion for $2. It didn't matter anyway since they never brought me any bloody chips! The chicken tacos would've been more aptly named "cilantro tacos." I couldn't even eat the tortilla shells since they had the texture of being microwaved 10x. They were as rubbery as...a big, thick piece of rubber (I'm at a loss for analogies, okay?!). The chicken was flavorless, bland and luke warm. I'm really digging deep for something positive to say about this place, and all I can come up with is: the girl at the register was pleasant. That's all I got. It's not enough to get me to come back. Nice knowin' you, Taco Riendo.

text: By chance my fiance and I walked past percy street bbq and after reading some press on it decided to give it a shot. I liked the decor. During this time we ate our sides which were good. The collared greens and potato salad were gone fast, but the mac and cheese was a little bit off. It tasted gritty. I understand that they are supposed to be smoked but the dry rub they put on it was overpowering. It tasted very peppery. The bbq sauce they gave us to put on the ribs was very spicy. text: I love, LOVE karaoke... but Wanna B's leave a lot to be desired.
