text: I just needed a room overnight for a crazy roadtrip from Chicago to New Orleans. I just had to get out of the cold and celebrate the solstice in the Crescent City. I have to say their website caught my eye and that was basically the reason I booked the room. After all, their website says it was 'the best designed hotel in north america' and that it was 'hip, chic, stylish.' Ok, the lobby is pretty nice and the bar has re-opened. The staff seemed nice enough. The location, although not great, is good enough. It's a few blocks from the French Quarter but an easy walk and around the corner there is daily parking for $12.50. So far so good. Then we walked into the room. The room was small but adequate. It had a funky musty smell, though. It would have been nice to open the windows but no, they don't open, not even a crack. Oh well, after a few minutes I knew I wouldn't notice that smell anymore. I don't know how long this place has been open but I think they're resting on their laurels. The furniture and door frame had little nicks as did the bathroom door. I mean this place looks like it has, as a friend of mine would say, 'been rid hard and put away wet.' Not that that affects your stay but it just has a rundown feeling. Even the knobs on the furniture, which looks like it came from Ikea, were slightly askew. All in all I felt like I was staying at someone's home who didn't really care about housekeeping although he (or she) might wear the latest clothes. More gross was the bathroom. This was also tiny and with a shower stall (no bath) since that was all they could fit in. The shower was real tile, not the usual fiberglass shell you see in most hotels. The problem was that no one regularly cleaned the grout in the shower and consequently there was a lot of mildew in there. More and more this felt like some wannabe swinger's bachelor pad. Oh yeah, the water pressure was extremely weak and not particularly hot, either. I feared it would be a mistake to order room service but it was just a late night dessert so how bad could it be? Bad. You'd be better off trekking back out than trying room service. One more thing, there were only two elevators and one was out of service. That's just another sign to me that this place really doesn't spend much time on maintenance. It just goes to show that one can be lured in by flashing lights and superficial style but that's no substitute for attention to detail. (This goes for people, too, incidentally). I would definitely not recommend this place to anyone I cared about.

text: We have been waiting for Zavino to open and finally made it there tonight. The pizzas brought me back to my favorite trattoria in Rome. The crust is just perfect -- thin, yet with a nice chewy texture; it is delicious! Chef Steve Gonzalez perfected the Italian style pizza crust and topped it with really fresh ingredients. We tried 2 pizzas: Kennett, a white pizza named for its locally grown mushrooms, and Sopressata. I really liked the Sopressata. For appetizers, we had 'Baby Jesus'; I know . . . we ate 'Baby Jesus', I'm sorry . . . It's a salami that tastes like mild prosciutto. For desert, we had chocolate cake and a well brewed french press coffee which hit the mark. All that food for 2 people came to less than $40! We had a great meal. Besides the food, Steve got other important things right . . . His stay in Italy must have made him part Italian. He walks around and talks to his customers just like the chefs there do. Over there, I always felt like the chef was welcoming me into his home, and Steve seems to be trying to create that same experience. The restaurant is also open very late: Sun-Wed till 11pm, Thu-Sat till 2am. That, again, is very Italian. Hitting the pizzeria after 9pm, usually after a long happy hour, for late supper before going home is a great way to cure the happy hour pangs and prevent hang overs. Zavino is bring that lifestyle to Philly! I really love this place. Congrats Steve!

text: I used to say that I'd become a vegetarian the day they gave tofu the exact consistency and flavor of dry-aged steak. In the years since, and in my waxing love affair with farmer's markets and the verdant crunch of fresh produce, I have realized that I love fresh fruits and vegetables because they are fresh fruits and vegetables. I like bacon because it is bacon, and bread because it is bread. This indirectly highlights my main issue with Leafy Greens, and with the entire substitute cuisine lifestyle in general. Ultimately, this is a matter of keeping it real. The food at Leafy Greens is three things: 1. Delicious 2. Really, really good for you 3. Expensive The food at Leafy Greens is not this: 1. The food it claims to be. Maybe I am picking nits. Maybe you can read the above list of what the food is, or the descriptions that will follow, and be satisfied, but I found that, if I closed my eyes and thought 'this is a stuffed pepper,' before I put the bite of pepper stuffed with nut paste into my mouth, then I would be disappointed. Likewise, if I tasted the Mediterranean 'pizza' with the expectation of pizza, it fell short. The zucchini spaghetti with raw tomato sauce was insubstantial if compared to spaghetti spaghetti with savory slow roasted tomato sauce and garlic and basil, but as a standalone dish, it was great. In summary, each of the things I tried at Leafy Greens, the Thai curry soup of almond milk and carrots, the peanut butter and chocolate ice cream of frozen pureed bananas, the mango cobbler, the apricot tart, the pizza, the pasta, etc, were all delicious so long as I didn't hold them to the standard of the thing they claimed to be. Does that make sense? This is not rabbit food. I don't think a rabbit would even know what to do with this food. This is raw food, with the word raw carved into stone and festooned with moss and bugs. I recommend this, but prefer meat that is meat and veggies that are proud of themselves. Also, if you do go there and it's a nice day out, take your food, walk down the driveway, and have a picnic by the little brook. Then you can really start communing with nature.

text: With the recent popularity of the book and film, The DaVinci Code, and interest in the Knights Templars and similar topics, it was inevitable that interest in Freemasonry, would spike . It is impossible to speak about the Masons without the discussion becoming at best political and at worst adversarial. Two things about which there can be no dispute is one, they are fiercely patriarchal and two, they are even more fiercely secretive. That out of the way we can concentrate on the magnificent edifice in the direct geographical center of the city across from City Hall, The Masonic Temple of Pennsylvania. It is arguably the most magnificent building in Philadelphia. There are 7 great rooms inside connected by ostentatiously beautiful corridors and staircases. Each room has a motif; Gothic, Ionic, Egyptian, Norman, Renassaince, Corinthian and Oriental which has woven into its design elements of the Alhambra. The walls are hung with remarkable paintings and the halls lined with extraordinary statuary, many seemingly sculpted from marble are actually carved wood. Tours are worth the $8.00, cash, and the guidelines for touring are strict. But there should be at least a few oohs and aahs.

When we checked in, we were well aware of the Teen Volleyball Tournament taking place in Reno, so we were prepared for it to be a little louder than usual. Like most lower end hotels, we could hear every single time one of these little darlings raced screaming up and down the hallway and every time someone so much as closed a door, which continued well into the night. We didn't complain because there didn't really seem to be a point, but the noises that traveled under our door and the paper thin walls were definitely a drawback - even without the tournament, we would have been able to hear footsteps and conversation outside semi clearly. So the price - $150/night. Honestly, it should have been more like $75/night. There was a little gym downstairs, which I did use, only to find 3 out of the 5 pieces of equipment broken. So overall, if you're in a pinch, this is a clean hotel, but I'm a huge fan of getting what you pay for, and I wish I could have stayed in a casino rather than this place.

text: Craft Wine is a great new wine store that has opened in Reno in the mid-town area. The owner is Ty Martin and it opened on Martin Street, but apparently that's just a coincidence. If you like wines by importers like Kermit Lynch, Louis/Dressner, De Maison and Neal Rosenthal, then this is your kind of store. I like those producers because if I have to pay more than $30 for a bottle of wine I feel some serious pain. These are the kind of importers who bring in quality wines that are affordable. I took a picture of an example of three wines in this range. The A. et P. de Villaine Les Clous is actually something like $32. This is a first rate Burgundy that is affordable. Through his association with Domaine Romanee Conti, de Villaine makes probably the most expensive wine in the world, costing several thousand dollars a bottle. His name is on the wine actually made by his nephew and it's imported by Kermit Lynch. Tasty stuff and it's priced like most California chardonnay. Lapierre Morgon is a great Cru Beaujolais. It would go great with a holiday turkey. It's in the mid $20 range. The Savoie is a tasty white wine for $16 that matches food so much better than the overripe, oaky California chardonnay. People who have been to Kermit Lynch's retail store in Berkeley will recognize the lay out. He has wine in boxes on tables instead of using fancy racks. Ty says he's also going to get in wines from Puzelat, the revered Loire hipster winemaker, and Sicilian winemaker Arianna Occhipinti, who seems to be on her way to cult status. These wines are hard to get in San Francisco. Whether Ty can keep them in Reno is another matter. He also has a walk-in refrigerator with a bazillion beers from all over the world. The good news is I found a source for a Finnish beer I like, Nogne. The bad news is that it's $7.50 per pint-size bottle. The refrigerator is pretty chilly and I get the feeling I'll be carefully inspecting his beer selection in August. Ty is putting good wine in the store. The question is whether it's wine the people in the Reno area want to buy. Reno is Rombauer country and they're not necessarily looking for all these imported wines. Ty also carries some domestic wines. Some other wine stores carry wines from these importers, although not in the concentration that Ty does.

text: Yum! Yum! Dim Sum! I feel somehow cheated that I've never discovered this place in the past! To think of all the meals I could have eaten here over the last few years! However I tend to be suspicious of so called awards like that. We were promptly seated and immediately someone rolled up a cart with a variety of plates on it such as kimchee, seaweed salad and roasted green beans. We tried all three of those dishes and they were all nice with the green beans being exceptionally good. Before I could even taste all three dishes, more carts started coming. I was thinking to myself "wow! this is my kinda place!". Each cart was loaded with a selection of delicious dishes. One cart was full of different types of dumplings, potstickers and steamed buns. Other carts offered dishes such as roasted duck, beef dishes and fried chicken feet. I immediately pointed for the chicken feet which were battered, fried and coated in a tasty sauce. The roasted duck was also highlight as were the dumplings. My understanding is that Lulu's does the cart thing on Saturday and Sunday for brunch. You basically pick out any plate that you want to try and they note it on your check and tally it up at the cash register. For the two of us, we paid about $35 for 9 plates of food and green tea. A bit pricey, but we did eat a lot. I'm going with 5 stars for this place for the fun experience and great food.

text: Geno who is really Joe started with $6.00 in his pocket when he first opened his business. His wife and son named their first born son Geno who now works with his father. I'll start with first impressions: My daughter desperately needed to use the restroom and Pat's told her to go over to the park adjacent from them! We did and there was no restroom! Geno's was right there, so we asked them and they slipped her into the back and left her piddle. She came out saying wow this place is so clean! Now we get to friendliness, cleanliness and decor. Pat's is old and dirty and has not spent one dime of their profits to stand out in these three fields. Geno's on the other hand has put a lot into these areas. Now for the cheesesteaks: Even though we were all headed to Pat's, my daughter and I were so impressed with Geno's that we ordered our steak and fries there. The other five in our party stayed at Pat's. My daughter and I took our order from Geno's over to Pat's to eat with the others ( tacky for sure and I would have rather ate at Geno's because of the cleanliness and decor). First of all to order a sandwich and fries at Geno's, you must order them and pay for them separately at 2 different windows, I can see where this works for them at busy times, but we were the only ones there. The meat at Geno's is much, much better than at Pat's. Everyone, but my stubborn son in law agreed. The bread is better at Pat's. The onions are raw at Geno's and sauteed at Pat's. With a grilled sandwich I would have preferred the sauteed, but I did order a cheesesteak hoagie, so that may be the reason. Pat's uses more cheese. I had provolone. text: Oh FEAST, I really wanted to like you. Why did you have to let me down? You could have been bland, or boring, like so many other "nice" restaurants. Instead, you had to reach for the stars, and try "new" combinations to make your food seem interesting. Sadly, your food was mostly OK and occasionally terrible. The WORST: One dish we tried was a pan-seared sea bass with "pomegranate syrup", grits, and broccolini. All the solid items, the bass, the grits, and the broccolini were sitting in this pool of "syrup." Exotic nectar this was not, my hungry friend! No, this was a cup of Juicy Juice that had been reduced down to a still very thin 1/2 cup of bright red, sickeningly sweet, noxious liquid. No one in their right mind would find this edible, not even on a dessert (and I LIKE sweet things). I don't know what went on in the kitchen, but someone without any taste buds was obviously calling all the shots. The BEST: Flavors aside, everything was cooked well. The fish was cooked well. The broccolini was cooked perfectly, best I've ever had. Pasta was appropriately toothy. Peas were fresh and just blanched. This place also has a terrific wine list, selection, and pricing. The DISAPPOINTING: Feast has some serious flavor/balance issues. A salad with pesto dressing and gnocchi had a dressing with overpoweringly strong vinegar, enough to make you cough. Meanwhile, the twice-cooked pork lacked salt, heat, and flavor. The sea bass... Oh god, don't remind me, let's not go there. The pappardelle with artichokes and pancetta was too heavy on the pesto, which even overpowered pancetta (why would you ever want to drown out the flavors of fried bacon??). The RECOMMENDATION: Come for an interesting and very well priced wine list. Just, if you have to eat, avoid anything with "syrup."

text: I have only had my brows waxed once. It was a little painful, but easier than I thought it'd be. I went to a nail salon and had it done for $5. In and out. Easy peasy. So I decided to splurge to see why Terme charged nearly four times as much. I made an appointment and arrived 15 minutes before my scheduled time. They had me fill out some forms. I explained how I'm on Differin Gel as well as birth control and I take a multivitamin every day. I explained my skincare routine; Clinique's 3 Step twice a day and Clinique's Exfoliating Scrub at least twice a week. I was taken back to a room and asked to get comfortable on the chair. She started with my eyebrows, which were less painful than the $5 place. Especially when it came to tweezing. Then she asked about my lip, and I corrected her and told her I'd like my chin done. I showed her my areas of concern. There were also some small areas on my neck that I told her I had difficulty seeing. The conversation was nice and I was pleased with my visit, until I got home. It was an hour later when I finally able to wash my face. I used the first step of my Clinique system, which is an oil free wash. My chin started to flare up in pain, so I skipped the toner and put some Clinique gel moisturizer on my entire face. My chin and a small area above my eyebrow felt like it was on fire. I looked closer and it appears to be a burn. I went to work the next day and my coworkers agreed that it looked like I'd been burned. After my shift was over, I went back to Terme. I had a few people look at me, including the head of the estheticians. I waited until Jennecka was available, and I was taken back to the room I had been in the day before. She examined the area and explained that the Nufree couldn't have burned me. Nufree attaches to the oils in the hair and doesn't disrupt your skin. She explained that unlike most waxes, it's a soy based product and so gentle that you can swim or even put makeup on directly afterward. She also showed me a pamphlet that explained how it never reaches a temperature higher than 98 degrees. She apologized profusely and gave me some face wash and lotion samples. I was also given a full refund. It wasn't until Monday, 4 days later, that the area on my chin started to peel away. I contacted an estheticians friend, who I had been in contact with since I had been waxed, and asked what could have happened. She told me to get some Vitamin E oil and put it on my chin. Turns out, the burn that I thought I had, was leftover residue from my waxing.

text: Can I go through this review without typing "doggone it" and hating myself for days? Doubtful. Self-loathing is my art form. Hot Dogs are Johnnie's Dog's art form. When I arrived in the area after hitching a ride on 6 trains, 3 buses, 2 pick up trucks and one monster truck...I was told that there is a hot dog place better than any other for miles and miles around. It was a pale imitation. If I waited on line for that I would have gone double postal. I went back two more times. I tried the Corndog and the Texas Tommy. One, it is a chain, and normally i don't mind but for things like Hot Dogs chains don't work. See Nathans. Two, there is no chili cheese corn dog, a HORRIBLE oversight for a true hot dog lover. Three, the price. Great hot dog joints are cheap. This place is not. It should not be more than 5 dollars for two people to eat at a great hot dog joint and this place is more like 10 bucks. Everything is a dollar more than it should be and for that kind of money you can find better food deals and quite frankly better hot dogs. text: This is a wonderful little campground situated on a sloping piece of land off Paradise Road. Beautiful old Coast Live Oaks are everywhere in the park. The ground cover is mostly grass or dirt. The campground is very small, I think there are only 14 sites. Each site is a good distance from the next and they are all a pretty good size. You definitely don't feel like you're sharing sites with your neighbor. The smaller size can mean that it's quieter than the larger campgrounds. $15/night is a great deal, too. There's only one bathroom building with four individual bathrooms, but it's centrally located and not far from any of the sites. Like Jason K. said, there are no showers or sinks. The spigots near each site are nice, with a circular gravel filled drainage catcher, so your feet don't get wet when you're rinsing dishes, hands, etc. We went in March, so it was very green there. I'm not sure what it's like in the summer/fall, but I imagine it's still very beautiful. There's a grassy area where you could play frisbee or catch. Watch for gopher holes, though! Because it's National Forest land, dogs are allowed, but technically should be leashed. The only drawback that I could see was that it's sort of near the road and you do get some road noise, but Paradise is not a frequently travelled road, anyway, so it's not bad at all. The hosts are super nice and very friendly (tend to be talkative). This is the first campground you come to on Paradise Road. We heard that it tends to fill up last because most people pass it by because it's first and they want to go farther in. We drove through the rest of the campgrounds on Paradise Road and concluded that this one is actually the prettiest. The others are more open and seem less "cozy". It's ideal for small groups - if you're with a bunch of people, go to Paradise or Upper Oso campgrounds.

text: Event: Green Day 8/3/10 The concert itself was excellent - Green Day always is. But I'm here to review the venue for those who can't find info elsewhere . . . We came over from PA, and arrived at 4 to tailgate for a 7pm show. There were many others who had already arrived, so the lots must have opened at 3 or earlier. We parked in Lot 1, by the Will Call window to the stadium. The $25 parking fee is a ridiculous rip off, and I would consider taking the ferry next time. I had 4 straight teens with me (16 & 17 y.o.) who had never tailgated. It was a great experience. We hauled an EZ Up tent with us, but you are not permitted to use them there. We grilled dinner and played games in the lot. The Camden police cruised through several times while we were there, and it felt quite safe. There was a lot of drinking going on, but none near us (I picked a quiet spot) and no one was out of control. Getting out of the lots is insane. There was one gate each for the two lots, and they combine to dump onto one little exit road. You would think they purposely do this to slow things down - - and slow it is. Allow at least an hour to get out of there for a big event. The venue itself was fine, but the will-call lines were miles long. We had lawn seats and, once in, found that the entire bottom center of the hill was all dirt! The dirt was completely covered with grass seed - ewwww. Thank goodness we had a blanket to sit on, because it was gross. Had it been raining . . . it would have been a huge mess. Note to the facilities guys: ZOYSIA GRASS PLUGS this fall and lots of 'em - hello??!! We were allowed to bring in 1 water bottle each, but had to remove the lids (potential projectiles). We did so to avoid the outrageously expensive food and drink prices at the Center. Worked out fine, we had our desert and snacks in the parking lot after the show, giving it time to calm down a bit before we left. Still had to wait in lines to get out, but not as bad. Footnote - We had killed my car battery prior to the show by listening to music a bit too long. When I came out, I waited less than 2 mins. before a police cruiser came along. I flagged them down and asked for help - they were as nice as can be. They sent another officer to find me in the parking lot, and he brought me a hot box so I could jump myself. Elapsed time from exiting the stadium to receiving help -- 6 minutes! Thank so much Camden Police - you were awesome. All in all, the venue has work to do on the inside, LOTS of work to do about their parking vendor(s) and traffic situation, and doesn't come close to competing with the Philly venues.

text: OK. The two stars are one each for the dogs my fiance adopted from this SPCA. He loved Briscoe quite a bit, and we both love Tala like WHOA, and this SPCA is the reason both of them were able to live long, healthy, happy lives. Or, in Tala's case, is still living a long, healthy, happy life. What I'm trying to say is that I appreciate what the SPCA is doing; however, I don't think they're going about it the right way. I am forever grateful to them for rescuing my Tala and letting Steve adopt her so that she could grace my life with her presence, I just think that there are some improvements that need to be made. When we decided to adopt another dog, I was a little nervous about this place after all the horror stories I read about it online. True to expectations, it was extremely crowded and disorganized the couple times we visited. However, I realize they are understaffed and I appreciate the efforts of the volunteers. The problem came on our final visit, when we had found a dog we wanted to introduce to Tala. Our meeting with the dog, Lucky, had gone great. She was a ball of energy and her foster mom warned us that she didn't immediately take to all other dogs. However, unless she truly disliked the dog, she just needed some time to warm up. Due to SPCA regulations, Lucky's foster mom wasn't allowed to introduce the two dogs by herself, so we asked an SPCA worker to come out and run the meeting. Again, we had to deal with the extremely overworked staff, none of whom was eager to help us or even ask us what we needed. When a staff member finally agreed to help us, it was reluctantly, and she clearly had other things to do and wasn't that invested in the meeting. As soon as our dog got within sight of Lucky, Lucky started barking, and the SPCA worker said (this is a direct quote), "Oh, this will NEVER work. This dog will NEVER like your dog. They will NEVER get along." Yup, that's right, within two nanoseconds and before the dogs even had a chance to get within sniffing distance, she had written us off. Her comments continued in the same vein as our dog got closer. (Our dog, by the way, was behaving just fine. For that matter, so was Lucky -- she was just overly interested/excited, not aggressive.) Not once did she allow Lucky to get close to our dog, which just frustrated her more and more and made her continue to bark and strain at the (choke chain) leash. Anyone with a brain should have been able to understand that these are two DOGS meeting. Yes, there might be some barking at first. They want to sniff each other and check each other out, and they're just going to get frustrated when you don't let them. But this SPCA worker was not at all interested in giving it time. Within approximately two minutes of coming outside, she had made up her mind. She told us that "You need a less active dog for your dog since she's older, this dog might end up hurting your dog." First of all, I think I know my dog a little better than you do lady, and she might be older but she's nothing if not active. Second of all, if you'd taken the time to talk to me for ONE MINUTE, you'd find out that I work from home and am here all day to oversee the dogs and make sure they get acquainted properly. But why take the time to discuss the situation with us when you can just give up, relinquish the leash back to the foster mom, and go inside without a backward glance? Of course, after she left, Lucky calmed down quite a bit as the tension faded. I called her foster mom the next day and asked for her opinion. She told me that is just how Lucky seems to respond to all dogs, that is even how she responded to the foster mom's current dog and it just took them some time to get to know one another and now they get along great. She said that when Lucky meets a dog she absolutely dislikes, she'll bare her teeth, which she didn't do to Tala. Her foster mom was open to doing another meeting, and said she'd get in touch with the manager of the SPCA to see if she'd run the meet and greet personally this time, since she was more familiar with Lucky's situation and disposition. Then I didn't hear from the foster mom all week. When I finally e-mailed her, she seemed to have lost interest in helping us out. The whole thing was just very depressing. Policies and attitudes like the ones they seem to have at the SPCA will turn people off from adopting. These dogs are going to get put down if they don't find a home -- wouldn't you think the SPCA would have more of a vested interest in spending the time to try and get them placed?

text: The performance was amateur hour at best and one guy's personal nightmare at its worst. There were some really good moments, and some really BAD ones. I have no problem with trying out material on an audience, but enough with the masterbation, child pedophilia, date rape, and nun p*ssy jokes. We drove all the way uptown, the least you can do is memorize your jokes. It was an "interesting" performance, but definitely a comedy of errors. Their website says they've been voted best comedy spot and they teach a kids' camp. Scary if there isn't anything better in NOLA. P.S. No A/C and it was like 100 degrees. I hope my ticket money goes for an A/C unit!
label: NEG

text: I'm sorry but this place REALLY does not deserve to get all the hype it's getting! Lured by the "most booked" listing on opentable, I decided to wander off my tried and tested dining spots to make way for Distrito. I guess all this place has to offer is the decor. The food pales in comparison and what's even more infuriating is crappy food being exhorbitantly priced. My lunch alone cost me slightly below $50 and I was served a shrimp ceviche that really was just shrimp cocktail (bleah!) . At least the fish tacos fared better but at $14, it didn't come cheap. Since servings were tiny and taste truly mediocre, I decided to order on - although I should have gone with my instinct rather than my hunger pangs and gone somewhere else at that point. However, I spotted the fried plantains and tres leche dessert, both which I love and figured no one effs these dishes up.... after all one is a side dish. But OMG the fried plantains ended up being some crap served with weird sauce accompaniment and queso blanco. When the dish was set before me I was thinking WTF is that and what is the white stuff on the bananas.... whipped cream? The combination tasted awful. And the tres leche, was basically some lousy sponge cake with milk all over. VERY DISAPPOINTING MEAL. The only saving grace about this place was the decor - I don't usually go snapping pics in restos, but since I felt shortchanged by the food, I snapped away.
label: NEG

text: Given the buzz, I was expecting more. I still think the best deep dish in St. Louis is Black Thorn near Tower Grove park. However, Black Thorn is so family unfriendly Pi is a better choice if you have kids or actually care about service. The prosciutto bites were good but not outstanding. We had two kinds of pizza - the topping on our create your own (bacon, sausage and mushrooms) were mostly hidden by the tomatoes on top. It was good, but a plain old cheese pizza would have been the same. We also had the "western addition" which is really good. It has spinach, mushrooms, ricotta, garlic, and some other stuff.
label: POS

text: Just tried the Atlantic- salmon + fresh salsa + lettuce + tomato in a roll, toasted. Incredible- the salmon was cooked just right, and the flavors worked perfectly together. Can't wait to try the Lebanon, which the guy working there also recommended.
label: POS

text: Why would you go to Himmel Park over Reid Park if you are in the middle of Tucson? Himmel Park is a great place to have a picnic; the trash cans are emptied regularly and it is dog-friendly. You can play volleyball, soccer, frisbee, or basketball here. There is also a community pool. Himmel Park has a library on the northeast corner of the park. Himmel Park is on a large square patch of grass. In the early morning or in the evening, some people are doing "boot camp classes." That would be cool to see people doing tai chi. If you like grass and picnicking, Himmel is an excellent location you should check out.
label: POS

text: I arranged for our company to have our "team building" outing here back in February. They rates were good, the staff was very friendly & accommodating to our large crowd, even when we arrived almost an hour later than planned. The place was clean and they do have lots of lanes available. They have a few small private rooms to have parties in, and I think you can arrange catering through them.
label: POS

text: Here's a review from an out-of-towner who ended up going here twice. I got the experience of a lull in the afternoon (practically had the place to myself), and during the Saturday night rush. Both times were great. During the day, I had the Beet Salad and it was delicious. Plus, the waitress was really nice and it was pretty darn affordable considering how much food I got. It was also quiet and a nice place to take a break from sight-seeing, do a little reading up on the city, maybe write a postcard or two. The big wood tables are very inviting and the decor was an interesting mix of old and new. Dug it. When I went back at night it was as if the place had completely transformed. Naturally, the only difference was that there was a night crowd and the music was blaring. It was still fun, the bartenders still attentive and friendly, the beer selection decent, and the atmosphere good. I think I prefer it a little quieter, but it seemed like a great place to hang out if you had a group of friends and table to call your own.
label: POS

text: Question, where do you send a thrift shopper who doesn't like to dig? Answer, Second Time Around in Philly. There are a few different reasons I'd send my friends here. The lighting is bright enough for you to see what they've got on the clothing racks. The racks themselves aren't stacked to the gills, but rather moderately filled with well-chosen items. The labels are color-coded; the colors relate to whether an item is new or has been in the store a little while, and is on sale. You may be able to get up to 50% off the ticket price based on the color of that tag. This is my first time around at Second Time, and I plan to make it my lunch-time jaunt for future thrift excursions. This time around, I got a cute Lily print dress for 50% off, and a very sculpted Theory button-down shirt which was new, so I paid full consignment price. This is definitely consignment, not thrift, so you're going to pay a little more. Don't be discouraged by the idea that the prices may be a little higher than you are used to if you're a thrifter. I felt right at home in this store because the sales person was both friendly and a little artsy. This is my kind of place.
label: POS

text: I was a new customer and called these guys on the coldest day of the year. They came to my house within two hours and had my furnace repaired within an hour. I've several older furnaces and a/c units that need to be upgraded, and I will definitely call Harster. They are the best.
label: POS

text: Good diner food. Chicken with gravy, mashed potatoes, nice steamed veggies for $15. Chicken livermore not as good as I remember it. Its good, solid comfort food.
label: NEG

text: Farmhaus was fantastic! The atmosphere, and the staff are wonderful!! We shared the sweet potato nachos, mushroom salad, bacon wrapped meatloaf, and trigger fish. All four dishes were amazing, and the wine list is pretty wonderful too! The server was knowledgeable and engaging (checked in with us just enough, and kept our glasses full). The menu is sponsored by a letter and number each day (thank you Sesame Street!) and you can purchase brews for the kitchen crew for $2. It was vibrant and fun. I can't wait to go back!
label: POS

text: A good solid breakfast place. The hollandaise is good, breakfast special with corned beef hash patties and asparagus was excellent. Liked but didn't love their cornbread and pulled pork benny. But with no wait at noon for a great brunch on a holiday monday... I would definitely come back and try that awesome looking bagel and lox.
label: POS

text: This used to be in my top10 - and fell way off the list a few years back. Sadly, it isn't coming back. What happened to this place? The 'old saloon salad' that I looked forward to before my entree- was big enough for 2 filled with everything, is now a few pieces of lettuce, cherry tomatoes and a few croutons. How sad. I miss my old fave.
label: NEG

text: YUCK!!!! I thought I struck gold when I saw the room rate was $70 for a two room suite. Wish I had checked Yelp first. The carpets in the rooms was beyond disgusting. The decor was outdated, dusty and gross. We had our two year old with us and there were actual dangerour areas we had to safeguard. I thought my pal's cockroach infested beer stained college apartment was disgusting - this actually beat it! The buffet included bisquits, bread, cereal, waffles, greasy sausage, microwaved eggs, and some apples and green oranges. Perhaps they picked the oranges from the trees on the premises? Our heater did not work and ofcourse we were there when it was cold! We froze during the night. We asked housekeeping for another pillow and blanket. The woman that showed up was on her cell phone gossiping and literally soved the items into my arms before storming off. I complained to the front desk girl about everything mentioned above and she offered me a $10 coupon on my next stay. I politely informed her we would never be back. She shrugged her shoulders and smiled. My feeling is she must hear about this all the time.
label: NEG

text: Ok, this was my first experience with Vietnamese food so take this review with a grain of salt. The restaurant had a nice feel to it, good layout, plenty of light, lovely decor. The wait staff was extremely attentive; my water glass was never empty. The menu was somewhat large and confusing for me so I ended up going with the BBQ platter based on other yelpers' reviews. When it arrived, not long after we ordered it, I was blown away by the presentation. The food looked beautiful! Although I can honestly say I'm not positive what to call most of what was on the platter, I did recognize the spring rolls and lettuce wraps right away (those also ended up being my two favorite things). I wasn't crazy about everything on the platter, but enjoyed the new experience. Also, the sweet and sour type sauce and peanut sauce were both very delicious. Thank you yelp reviewers for helping me make my first Vietnamese dining experience a positive one.
label: POS

text: I had heard a lot about this restaurant and was excited to get some drinks with some friends there. I was dissapointed by the rude waiters and waitresses who seemed overwhelmed by our group of five...They didn't want us to sit in the pathway (fire hazard) so we scooted back so that we would be out of the way. When a table cleared that would put us completely out of the path, they made a stink and said the table had to be in an exact position so that it wouldn't wobble. It appeared that everything we did was a problem. They were not friendly at all!!! When we ordered a cheese and meat and crackers appetizer it took about 45 minutes, which is ridiculous, considering nothing had to be cooked! The drinks were about 10-12$ but it was as if us just ordering drinks was a problem and accounted for some of the rudeness... I would go back for dinner but was told the only veggy option, the stuffed bell pepper, was dry and uncooked.
label: NEG

text: Let me start by saying that i LOVE BBQ. I could eat Ribs any day of the week. But, I probably would never order them from Percy street BBQ. They were practically flavorless, although cooked to an appropriate temperature. My friend and I both ordered the double down, had the ribs, chicken, and brisket (the brisket being the absolute winner). I love eating crispy chicken skin, and I couldn't even stomach a few bites of the chicken; it had a very rubbery consistency. I was intrigued by the Root Beer Chili, and was sadly disappointed (not to mention it was luke warm at the very most). Beer choices were good, but I didn't want to eat at Percy Street because of the alcohol. Dessert, however, made the experience. The Pecan Pie was heavenly! Banana Pudding was really thick, but tasty nonetheless. Service, however, was awful. Our server was aloof and inattentive. Upon entering the restaurant, we were greeted rather awkwardly by a manager. I can justify a sort of absent minded server when a restaurant is busy, but i can't when there are literally two other tables seated in the restaurant who are on dessert. There are a bunch of simple things that should be done during service that weren't. And from working in a restaurant, i understand how those little things can either make or break an experience. I was disappointed in the food and service enough that I don't have the desire to return for seconds. And i never say no to seconds when it comes to BBQ.
label: NEG

text: The stadium itself is very nice and new, bathrooms are clean. My problem is with the facilities for elderly or physically challenged individuals. The dome's guest services are severely lacking. My in-law's are both elderly and have difficulty getting around. They asked the usher if there was an elevator they could take to get to our level because they have problems with the escalator...they aren't very steady on their feet. They were told that they had to use the escalator like everyone else. The usher on our level was kind enough to find them alternate seating, though it wasn't an open area for wheelchairs or walkers. They still had to squeeze in through an aisle, tough when you are diabetic and have no sensation in your feet. We asked about getting wheelchairs for them but guess what? They don't have wheelchairs! Maybe I'm just spoiled by U.S. Cellular Field's guest services. Just ask, within minutes, an usher arrives with a wheelchair and your entire party is whisked up to your level on the elevator. Because my father-in-law could not climb the stairs to our seats, we were directed to a chained off area especially for the handicapped. At the end of the game, the usher magically appeared and wheeled dad back to our van. THAT is service...oh, wait, that's another review.
label: NEG

text: I appreciate the B-line. Their menu features pasta, mexican, and burgers and everything is done well. My favorite item is the veggie quesadilla. It's filled to the brim with sauteed vegetables and gooey cheese. Pretty delicious. The dessert case is very tempting, and I've tried the signature cheesecake before. Definitely worth every bite. Good beer selection, with constant new additions and rotations. And Tuesday is half-off a bottle of wine night. Dinner and half of a bottle of wine for less than fifteen dollars? Yes, please.
label: POS

text: Best Damn Catfish I've Ever Had !!!!!!!!!! I have been here at least ten times when I visit the Nolia. Blackened catfish with jambalaya and sauteed vegetables is the Bomb. I can't get enough of this place. Definitely worth stopping by if you hit up Bourbon St. It may be a hole in the wall but so are most establishments on Bourbon. I'd rather eat swell in a comfy spot than look pretty and eat at some tourist trap BS joint that N.O. is full of just like any other city.
label: POS

text: OK, so the location is fantastic and the hotel itself is quaint...you'll be within walking distance of Bourbon Street, the French Market, and Riverwalk but the hotel is not that good. Honorable mention must be given to Andre who stored our bags for us and gave us good tips as far as where to eat, Andre was a true professional and had a great demeanor all of the time, we truly felt welcomed. The rest of the staff was OK...no towels during the day (they were being washed???)...I have never stayed in a place where you do not have towels. The room had no window, the TV was ancient (apparently the plasma or LCD they had had long since broken as the bracket was still on the wall). The room did not have storage space for our clothes so we were stuck living out of our suitcases, the door was hard to open and close (we had to slam it each time so that it would shut properly), and the safe did not work as confirmed by the front desk. We stayed in room 304, take my advice, if you plan on staying here DO NOT accept this room.
label: NEG

text: Ascetically, this spot is a great addition to Fairmount Ave; its large, beautiful, and has great TV setup (big, flat screen TVs). And they love them some Hoegaarden at this spot (as do I ... yummmm, Belgium White). Which means, for a group or a good amount of breathing space most nights, I'm happy to have the Urban Saloon here. But the food is just not good. And that's really a shame, because I want this place to be good. Its bland, and seemed reheated. The service is so slow, that the food would have to be very much delicious to compensate. O well. I'll go there for my drinks and leave the food for somewhere else.
label: NEG

text: This buffet is awful. Half the stuff is cold and has a crust from sitting out for so long. The fried appetizers are a joke... last time (and I mean it, that will be the LAST time) my potato croquettes were so rubbery I couldn't even bite through them. Plus all the dishes are bland, with none of the spice or nuance you expect from Indian cusine. And insult to injury, instead of using paneer in the vege dishes, they use tofu. Don't get me wrong, I love tofu when cooked properly, but this was just flavorless, pathetic lumps thrown into the mix.... well, "flavorless" apart from the slightly chemical-y taste of packaged tofu. Bleah! Basically the only good thing I can say is that the service is prompt... probably because the place is usually empty.
label: NEG

Even the dinners (my friend got beef and broccoli) were mediocre at best--and of course way overpriced.

text: I love me the chocolate balls of goodness! Staff at this location is really nice and friendly! The closest one to me in Colorado is over an hour away. So whenever I find one I'm all over it. This donuts were still fresh at 11am, although i did relieve them of the last 25 chocolate munchkins. And they were not making any more that day! Oh my! The location was clean, well laid out, and near my location - not sure if it is central, but good for me! Visit them and say hello!

text: This was a good place to get a quick bite and ice cream. Lines were a little long, but tolerable. The floors could've used a little cleaning though! :T

text: This place is just terrible. My wife has already written a review so there is not a whole lot I can add. As she said we ordered from here in the past and it was okay, but last night was awful. First off I paid 34 dollars for food that was worse than the stuff that is sold from the carts in center city. (I would have paid less at the carts) Second, the woman who took my order on the phone was completely rude and seemed as if taking my order was a burden. I ordered Garlic Chicken and my wife ordered Shrimp with Tofu. My wife loves Tofu and figured her order would be a safe bet. My wife's food was bathed in sauce as was mine the food lacked any flavor other than that of the sauce that probably came from an industrial sized Kikkomen container. The spare ribs were tasteless and for the most part meatless. The shrimp toast was soaked with so much deep fryer grease that I probably should take an extra Crestor just to counteract the effects. I am actually not sure if the people who run this place are actually Chinese. I have read some where else that it is an American run Chinese restaurant but I cannot confirm this. (This reminds me of that scene in Rush Hour 2 with Don Cheadle) However if this is the case it would explain why the food is so poor. All in all if we decide on Chinese food late at night I think I will take a pass on JC and have a Peanut Butter and Jelly sandwich instead.
label: NEG

text: I went last Saturday night after hearing from friends rave about the freshness of the food here. It was early and only a couple of tables were filled, but while we were there, they were doing a brisk takeout business. I had the teriyaki salmon with vegetables and it was delicious, the salmon with a nice crisp crust and tender inside. The vegetables, a julienne mix of eggplant, carrots, peppers, and others were coked just right. It comes with a side of white rice. My husband had the Tempura Shrimp. It came with an ample serving of shrimp and several tempura vegetables, such as eggplant, sweet potato, squash and green pepper. It came with a side of rice as well. The tempura batter was light, and the shrimp and vegetables were top notch. A choice of soup accompanied the entrees, either hot and sour or clear. We had the clear soup , which was an excellent home made chicken broth with scallions and mushrooms. The room is elegantly simple and the tables are separated by a bamboo screen and drawn back curtains, so it makes for an intimate setting. Our waiter was extremely attentive and friendly. We will back soon to try the sushi. An excellent spot in Palm Harbor!
label: POS

text: What kind of diner needs cops on duty just for it? That's it, Broad Street Diner. But really, Broad Street Diner is gone? That's such a shame. Okay, actually it should have been condemned years ago but now that it's gone I kinda sorta miss it. Not that anybody should have eaten the food there. I can only imagine what that stuff does to your innards. Also, why wouldn't we want to go to a diner where we might just get shot?
label: NEG

text: You don't know summer in Tucson until you've tried Eegees. Native to Tucson, Eegees was originally sold in a street cart until the owners became so successful they started opening chains. Proof that no matter how small the town, a good product and a drive to succeed can take you to the top. I also heard recently that they're branching out to Phoenix soon. Get ready Phoenix for Eegees deliciousness! I don't know who discovered this amazing frozen "slush" treat, but they should be nominated for the Nobel food prize. To know Eegees is to love Eegees. On those sweltering 108 degree days, Eegees is your best friend! On a regular basis they have lemon, strawberry, and piña colada flavor available and they also serve the flavor of the month which varies between "Tangerine Breeze", "Jungle Juice", "Cherry Cider", "Orange Dream" and so on... I personally am a fan of the strawberry / piña colda combination. If you're having a BBQ, you can also add liquor to these fine drinks and have a wildly fruity time! They also serve food, though my interest in the company lies strictly in their drinks. They have sub sandwiches which they refer to as "grinders" and some really fatty side orders that'll clog your arteries. The bacon ranch fries, salty soft pretzels & hot dogs to name a few. The buildings themselves look very outdated, but don't let that deter you. The drinks are well worth it. The drive through's are fairly quick too. A must try if you're ever in Tucson!
label: POS

text: They were really nice there. I just didn't care for the haircut I got. From the outside it looks like the place is super trendy and hip and stuff, but i felt like i looked like my mom walking out of the salon. And I know it's my own fault for not asking them to fix it, but I have a "pleasing others" issue and I think the hairdresser could've done a better job. I felt like there was too much "theory" and "feeling" and not enough cutting and styling. Not my cup of tea.

text: I may have gone here at an off time (it was a Sunday night), but the place seemed pretty dirty and the food was quite poor. It looks like a run down Hooters, and if you're looking for Hooters - you might as well make the trip to Union Staion or another location.

text: One of the few fast food restaurants I can trust to get my food right. I go here every other week or so. Good service inside and out.

text: I use Framers Workroom for all my framing. I am an artist and photographer. I have been using them for years and have never been disappointed, I also have had antique prints framed there and my one of a kind, falling apart pieces were treated with the up most respect to the integrity of the piece. I highly recommend the Framers workroom for all types of framing.
label: POS

text: I can't believe I've lived a block away from Mizu for over a year and just discovered it! It's moderately priced for sushi (two rolls, shrimp dumplings and seaweed salad came to $34) and the portion sizes are generous. We had the American Dream (shrimp tempura, avocado & eel), which was huge and had the perfect amount of crunch and sauce. There was avocado both inside and on top of the roll - Mizu definitely doesn't skimp on ingredients. We also had the Rainbow Roll, which was good and as expected. I really enjoyed the seaweed salad and thought the portion was really generous. The shrimp dumplings were also yummy and came steamed, an extra plus. Though the restaurant is small, it wasn't the tiny hole in the wall I was expecting from reading the other yelp reviews. It's an actual restaurant, with about 6 tables and window seating. We went around 8:00 on a Saturday night and it was about half full when we got there. I'll definitely be frequenting this place often! Crossing my fingers for lunch specials. =)
label: POS

text: Avoid Sushi Pier 2, Come here to the original Sushi Pier! It's worth the drive from the strip! Excellent service and they don't stuff your sushi with rice but with a lot of fish instead! Their talented chefs will take orders as you please and hand them to you as soon as they are done and you can keep ordering. Have never felt so pleased for a $15 all you can eat lunch. I may go back to Reno just for this place again.
label: POS

text: Boscos Nashville Brewing Company is snuggled in a brand new shopping complex in Cool Springs. Boscos reminds me of all the Gordon Biersch Brewing Company restaurants in Los Angeles. There really isn't anything special or differentiating about this place. You'll find the local brews with a Tennessee twist to them plus the typical "gourmet" bar foods. I personally ordered the seared Ahi Tuna and thought it was satisfying but nothing great. You can also find pizzas and burgers with unique toppings. Prices are a little on the pricier side, but you should expect to pay a little more for the pseudo-gourmet food. The crowd that night spanned from the Tennessee cougars to some college kids that were on their summer break. Go Trojans! Fight On!
label: NEG

text: Amazing coffee for half the price you pay at Starbucks. Staff is always friendly and never pretentious like some other local coffee shops (*cough*javajungle*cough*). Everything I've tried on the menu is great and their bagels are really, really good. Great for a lite breakfast and coffee to start the day.
label: POS

text: Me and my wife used to go to this place quite often(2+ times/week) few years back for their different types of kabobs and their good menu. The food was decent and the Manager nice. It all stopped when we took their coupon from that current year's entertainment guide and they said they don't accept it knowing pretty well we are frequent visitors and the coupon was actually printed in that guide! After some discussion, they said they will accept it and when they brought the bill, the prices of our items were all jacked up to compensate for the coupon! Not sure how they could shamelessly do it since the actual prices were clearly listed in the menu! It's been 4 years since this happened and we never went back. 10 years back they could have gotten away with it, but there is no dearth of good Indian restaurants in the Western Suburbs. Horrible customer service. And don't let anyone tell you this was done by the old management. It was the new management-old management was worse than this!!
label: NEG

text: Since it's on the block of the hotel I stay in when travelling to Philly, I've given Mixx a try four times. Each time I leaving thinking, "that can't have been a good night for them", but tonight confirmed that it's chronic. I've taken work colleagues there and they had similar responses, so I know I'm not being picky. Let me start by saying the wait staff is wonderfully friendly and attentive and honestly deserve to work in a better restaurant. Your drink will never go below three sips and they will do everything they can to enhance your dining experience. Unfortunately the food isn't as appealing. The salad is typically smothered in ginger dressing and tastes like it was assembled that morning and kept in a too-cold refrigerator all day. Every roll that I've tried tastes oddly watery and bland, regardless of the ingredients. "Spicy" tuna and salmon rolls have no flavor, let alone any "spicy." One saving point for Mixx is that the sushi is served in nicely large portions and tastes relatively fresh. If you go, stick with normal sushi and don't bother experimenting with the roll menu.
label: NEG

text: My friend introduced me to this place, and I loved it! It's a 50's style Cajun/New Orleans diner, with lots of chrome and vinyl furnishings. The service is great, very friendly ppl ... our waiter started talking to us about music, for some reason. But he was still cool. They start you off with these awesome buttermilk biscuits that are so light and fluffy, they melt in your mouth. And the green jelly they serve it with may look a bit toxic, but trust me -- it's soooo good ... you'd be crazy not to try it. The green jelly is actually a sweet jalapeno jam; not spicy, but sweet and tangy with a subtle kick to the taste buds. Oh yeah, gimme s'more! I had the catfish, and it was oh-so-good too. I'd tell you what my friend had, but I can't remember ... I think I was too busy stuffing my face with catfish. The fish was tender and juicy, and just spicy enough with black pepper that I could enjoy both taste and texture. Our bill was also pretty decent, coming to about $16 to $18 for each of us. A fair price for a well-cooked catfish, I would think. I can't wait to go back and have some of that jalapeno jelly! I should also note: they don't allow kids here, adults only.
label: POS

text: I went here to buy an InterMetro shelving unit here last week after looking on line for one that would fit next to my refrigerator. The staff was extremely helpful - it was the sort of service I would only expect to get at a high end independent retailer. The gentleman at the register insisted on helping me load the shelving and other purchases in my car. The staff throughout the store was knowledgeable and enthusiastic about their products. I forced myself to behave and not buy a million little containers that I didn't need. The Container Store in Cherry Hill is right in front of the mall next to the Crate & Barrel if you are wondering where 2000 Rt. 38 puts you.
label: POS

text: I like Monk's but have found that it has not kept up in the consistency department. It seems they are only interested in collecting as much money as they can and then cashing out. A place for serious beer drinkers and professional pub crawlers. Food is passable, but there are better places to go. Last time I was here - the place was a fire trap and it was dirty. I go when forced by my friends.

text: Just to say that I would move to philladelphia just to be close to this restaurant!. When I use to study at edison Highschool I use to go here with my sister like every 2 weeks and i absolutly loved it!.... For my birthday all i wanted as a gift was to go to this place. im dying to go back to philly just to go to this restaurant. The enviroment is great. The service is super! And was the place it self is so traditional. It makes me feel like if i just took a flight to colombia it self. text: We really liked Rangoon and we want to thank those of you with suggestions here on what to order. We ordered 1.The Jungle Chicken 2. Asian tea leaf salad 3. Rangoon house noodles 4.thousand layer bread and curry potato dip 5.coconut rice Our friend who is a Burmese food virgin ordered the crab dumplings and some other dish that we did not try. We ordered these based on the reviews so thanks! We are writing this review for those of you who like to try Burmese in different cities. We have had Burmese in NYC for years. Both at Village Mingala now closed and also Cafe Mingala which is still open. We have also been to Mynamar in Falls church Va. We want to go back before we review that one but did upload the only photo there. I want to address a few of the reviews saying Rangoon was better than the Burmese we had here. I would not give it a blanket statement saying it is better. But I would say that the menu at Rangoon was so full and their selection was far greater than any Burmese place we have been to. It is also light years cleaner than any place in NY for Burmese. Although our Burmese restaurants are not in China town I wanted to also point out that Rangoon was much cleaner than any restaurant in any one of our four China towns here in NYC. Some of the menu items were better than here and visa versa. We will go back for sure when in Philly again. However I would not drive 2 hours to Philly just to go. We will however drive 5 hours to Falls church VA. to go to their Burmese place because it was much more flavorful than any we have been to but their menu is very limited. Rangoon's strongest pluses were the variety in the menu and clean restaurant and very considerate service. The Jungle chicken was great. None of the other Burmese places we have been to have anything like it as far as I know. For those who have not tried it it is a chicken dish with green curry but the predominant flavor is lime. It is really delicious. The Asian tea salad was not as good as the salads we have here at our Burmese place because it did not have that special zing it was missing the citrus, could not even find the tea leaves and it had too many peanuts. It was more like a Thai salad than Burmese. The coconut rice was almost a tie it was great but still not quite as coconuty as the coconut rice here in NYC and as you see in our review of Village Mingala the rice is the only thing we mention. The thousand layer bread was good. At the other Burmese places we have been they have thousand layer "pancake" which is much thicker and more caloric so I liked the one at Rangoon because it was light almost like an Indian naan. We loved the Jungle chicken but the highlight of the meal was probably the potato curry dip that came with the thousand layer bread. It was much more flavorful than the curry dip we have tried here! The seasoning was distinctly Burmese. The Rangoon house noodles were okay but much better in Falls church Va at Mynamar. All in all it was great meal. I would suggest Rangoon to anyone! They are a great place to try Burmese if you never had it and if you have like us the variety is so great that you could go back many times and not try everything on the menu.

text: We were in Santa Barbara for the weekend to celebrate my wife's birthday. We arrived around 2P and walked around the pier and a bit on State Street. Then off to check into our motel and get settled. As we had brought our laptop I decided to check Yelp for a good place to eat dinner that night. Right away at the top of the list came up the The Palace Grill with 71 reviews and 4 1/2 stars. I looked at a few reviews and clicked on the link to their website. Everything checked out and I was quite enthused about going there for dinner that evening. We arrived about 5:45 and was seated immediately. The hostess was really friendly and everything was off to a good start. Next our waitress arrived, again another sweet and friendly person. We got our drinks and the buss boy brought us a basket of muffins and butter. There was quite a variety and all very, very good. It was now time to order and I decided on the house specialty, stuffed blackened filet mignon, and my wife got divers scallops. I added a bowl of seafood gumbo and my wife got a Creole Caesar salad. Oh, let's not forget that if you want their famous bread pudding for desert, you have to order it at the same time you order your meal. They have to prepare it and then bake it, all taking about 30 minutes. The soup and salad came promptly. I was looking forward to the gumbo as I am a fan of soups and spicy food . It looked good and I was ready to dig in. As I spooned through the soup looking for signs of shrimp and crayfish I saw none. But what was in abundance was pieces of Ahi tuna and loads of rice. There was also a bit of oil or grease that collected on the top so I mixed it around. Now, I'm not really a big fan of tuna in such a soup, and would prefer to have only shrimp and crayfish, that's just me, but I was going to let my taste buds decide. I tried the first spoonful and to me it was not at all what I expected. It was very bland and tasteless and had no kick to it at all, and as I said there was no shrimp or crayfish in sight, just tuna and rice. I was not impressed at all. Campbell's soup makes a thick and chunky variety called Grilled Chicken Sausage Gumbo that has the Palace's gumbo beat hands down! As for my wife's salad... she said it was OK, but nothing special. I also noticed her moving some big un-edible pieces of romaine hearts to the side of her dish. While waiting for our main course to come I was checking out the decor of the room. There are playing cards stuck on the ceiling, really! There is also a huge painting on the west wall of a black trumpet player dressed in a white suit. Not bad, it added to the room and gave it a feel of down south. But what I didn't expect to see next to the painting crawling down the wall was a cockroach, and on the shelf below it several other dead ones. May wife saw the look of surprise on my face and had a look. I almost wish she hadn't because no one wants to see such a thing. In fact, the young women sitting at the table next to the wall called one of the waitresses over and showed her the dead cockroaches. She promptly got a wet cloth and whisked them away. But still.... this was not a good sign and sort of set the mood for dinner. After about 20 minutes I was wondering if our dinner was ever coming. At that point our waitress came by and said our food would be out shortly. It really made me wonder if she had put the order in promptly or just forgot. I say this because the people next to us got their food about the same time as we did, and they arrived 10 minutes after us .Oh well, that's life. The food came and I dug in. It was nicely presenter and looked good, but didn't have much flavor. The stuffed filet was cold and tasteless. When I think of something blackened it brings forth memories of robust flavors and heat, but this had none. The scoop of mashed potatoes and fresh vegetables looked nice, but lacked flavor just like the filet. As for my wife's scallops... they were extremely salty and had an odd grilled flavor to them. Again, not a good experience. The owner's wife stopped by the table to chat a while. She was so nice I didn't have in me to tell her what I really thought of the dinner. I just told here everything was fine and left it at that. I know, I probably should have.... but I didn't. I hate any confrontation, that's just me. Well, we finally made it to desert and for what it's worth it was probably the only half way decent part of the meal. The waitress brought the bread pudding out and separated the center with two spoons and pored the whiskey cream sauce all over it. As the pudding was a bit dry on it's own, the sauce moistened it up nicely and made it quite tasty. I enjoyed it. All in all I was disappointed with our dinner. When you go out and spend well over 100 dollars for a meal you expect it to be good. I can understand an unlucky experience with the meal, but one live cockroach crawling around and two dead ones visible is inexcusable!

text: If you're a fan of the show Jersey Shore, and have been wondering to yourself, "But how can I experience the decadence enjoyed by the classy stars of this flash in the pan MTV show?" but feel limited because you live in Tampa, wonder no more: Just go to Aja. There's precious few adjectives that can adequately describe this place. "Awful" springs to mind quite quickly. And that is followed by "cheesy". Trite, cliche, gaudy, and embarrassing.... I think that sums it up perfectly. Look, maybe you wear Ed Hardy. That's your choice in life; far be it from me to come between you and your rhinestone shirt. Maybe you're a girl with orange skin and something to prove to daddy, or maybe you're a man with flared jeans and a waxed chest. Maybe Aja is the place for you. As this review is probably proving, it was not the place for me or my friends. We'd been coaxed into going, and were supposed to receive bottle service & "VIP" seating as per management for a party. The price we paid was to cover two bottles plus mixers. They brought out only one bottle, and snootily said it was "a $300 bottle of alcohol" that they were "giving" to us for "just" $100. Guys. Guys. It's Absolut. IT IS ABSOLUT. You can walk into ABC Liquor and pick yourself up a bottle for like, $21. We all know the mark-up on liquor in restaurants and bars is near-criminal but MAN. Come on. I was more irritated our money did not buy what was indicated. It was totally misrepresented. And as for the VIP seating, I don't think some fug white vinyl *benches* that just anyone can sit on or bump into you while YOU'RE sitting on them constitute as VIP anything. I was elbowed by people trying to force their way onto the seat behind me, hair was flung against my bare arm, and pretty regularly jostled by the crowd of people trying to squeeze by to the bar. As for the music, it would appear time travel is indeed possible, because the powers that be at Aja evidently built a time machine, and went back in time to 1998 to find a DJ spinning the latest in techno, and brought him to the present. If that's your thing, be forewarned it's eardrum-shatteringly loud. Our "VIP" benches were nestled directly below a booming speaker. No one could speak and the next morning no one could hear. True, I am but a visitor to Tampa, and am more familiar with bar scenes in Orlando. I don't know what else Channelside may offer, but if you're looking for a never-ending parade of douchery, Aja is the place for you. Pull out that wallet and get ready to be ripped off!

text: I will start off being completely honest...I went to Latitude 26 ONLY because I heard you could get a free margarita with the purchase of an entree for mentioning YELP. I thought, this alone gives me reason to check it out. Upon entering the place I could not believe that this was a Mexican restaurant or that it used to be Chuys. It was totally gutted out and much more roomy, with a definite loft style appeal. I fell in love with the decor immediately. I loved the fact the I could go out for some yummy Tex. Mex. and not feel like a box of crayons exploded around me! As far as the food goes, it was good...I am not too picky when it comes to Mexican. Menu was not huge, but I still had trouble deciding! Salsa was perfect, kinda chunky but not too spicy. I had the grilled chicken fluatas which were dee-lish! BUT, the best part of the meal was the margaritas. I can only name ONE other place in all of STL that I know uses fresh fruit juice. This is what will keep me coming back for more. I love a good margarita and it is so hard to find a place that knows how to make them with out sour mix. They hit the nail on the head with these drinks and I fell in love. I was more than impressed and my whole table of four had nothing but great things to say! I also very much liked the personal response I received on Twitter thanking me for my visit...you can't get better service than that!
label: POS

text: DEAR YELP ADMIN - why can I not have a falling star option or ZERO star option, etc. ? text: Some of the best freshly baked cookies around. Warm, gooey, and hefty. They sell by the pound which is unfortunate. For about 10.99 a pound if I last remember, you think you were buying walnuts, but the cookies are so hefty, so it comes out to about $2 per cookie. Still definitely worth it.

text: A large group of friends and I went to Mad Mex after our board exam. We were looking forward to tasty drinks and food after a very stressful few weeks. To our dismay, our server was surly from the moment he saw us. We ordered plenty of alcoholic beverages, appetizers, and food, yet our server still remained antagonistic. He was so terrible that I wanted to argue the 18% automatic gratuity with the manager. Some friends begged me not to make a scene, but I was livid about paying for the terrible service. Even worse, four of us were sick with fatigue and diarrhea for 2-3 days after our lunch. I wonder if our server did something to our food or drinks. We will never eat here again and have encouraged others to avoid this place. Terrible service and mediocre food. Spend your money elsewhere.

text: Yikes. I'm going to have to be honest here - Taco Bell is like Spago compared to this place. I wanted so bad to like Los Gallos - it's only blocks from my house. Not to mention it had no taste what so ever. I went for the second time tonight, giving them the benefit of the doubt by thinking that perhaps, the chile verde burrito was something they hadn't quite gotten right yet. No way. I got the trip tip burrito. Simple. Beans, rice and tri-tip. However, again, the meat was completely bland. I think Angie B. may have been onto somthing - this place may be ok if you just stick to the rice and beans, because the meat is totally tasteless. text: * 5 stars for being 1/2 block from my house; luckily I'd come here for coffee even if I wasn't so close. * 5 stars for not being Starbucks and having local flavor. * 5 stars for both their light and dark roast coffee. My morning productivity thanks you. * 5 stars for curating local art and supporting local artists - it's no small feat to think outside the cash flow needs of the immediate business. * 5 stars for having several different newspapers at the bar every morning and playing great music through a sweet stereo. Philly needs more businesses like Chapterhouse.

text: So...everyone knows about Chick-Fil-A and what they have to offer. However, I had the great opportunity to try their BRAND NEW SPICY CHICKEN SANDWICH today!!! It is awesome! The chicken sandwich is made the same as the original also with the option of lettuce and tomato. They are also offering pepper jack cheese with the sandwich. I opted for the plain sandwich with pickles. The chicken was tender (as usual), and the spiciness was perfect. It was not too spicy where you had to reach for water, but not a little bit where you are wondering if you ordered the wrong sandwich. The spicy part of the sandwich is actually in their chicken breading instead of a sauce on the bun. I tasted hints of Tabasco and different kinds of spices. It was really good, and I can't wait for it to hit the regular menu next week (June 7th)!
label: POS

text: Sad to say, I wasted a meal in New Orleans. Friday night at 7:30 and my wife and I were the only diners. There was one waitress who spent the night talking about how good PF Chang is. We had the Cool Menu...one appetizer, one entree and one desert for $35 each. The Alligator Ravioli was very good, if not a bit cold. They did not have the advertised fish that was on the special...they were "out" yet we were the only ones there. My steak was flavorful, but 2 temperatures overdone. It was not worth the effort to have them cook me another one. With no one else in the restaurant, I knew I was dealing with an indifferent kitchen rather than incompetent one. Server forgot to put in drink orders and they were "out" of the creme broule desert that was on the cool menu. We had bread pudding and it tasted like it was made last week. Nothing I hate worse than wasting a meal in New Orleans. I am no novice, but I have been to a ton of the big spots. I was told I had to try this place and am unhappy I did not look a bit harder for something new (to me)
label: NEG

text: I ordered the Schnitzel Platter (chicken) with french fries and a side of Moroccan Cigars (potato and meat) via Campusfood for delivery. Food came in about 30 minutes which was nice. The Moroccan Cigars seemed like they would be good if you had them in the restaurant, but by the time I got them they were cold, greasy, and somewhat bland. The Schnitzel Platter had very, very dry chicken like it had either been microwaved or spent too long under a heat lamp. They were even too dry for the creamy hummus to make up for. The chicken was breaded in what looks like spices but tastes like... well I couldn't taste it. I would agree with Candace about the "ehhh" fries for sure. I'd like to give this place a real visit to try the food without the downfalls of delivery, but be forewarned if you plan to have it delivered yourself.

text: I really wanted to like Liluma....however it was a disappointing experience. My husband took me here for our anniversary dinner because I had always wanted to try for dinner. We live in CWE and love the outdoor patio. We made reservations for 8pm, however when we showed up, the reservations were only for inside, not out. So we decided to wait the 15 minutes to sit outside. We sat at the bar, which is barely a bar, it is basically an area that is in the way of all the waiters, we were constantly moving out of the way or getting bumped. We also sat here for 15-20 minutes with no one actually at the bar serving us. The staff kept looking at us, but did not offer to get us a drink until the last 5 minutes, very rude! When we were sat, I looked over the menu and thought the 4 course tasting menu looked great, that way I could try so many different things. The first thing the waiter told us was, "i wouldn't order the tasting menu, it will take at least 1.5 hours to get" okay, well there went that idea. We were served bread to begin with, but told they had no oil or butter to serve with it? We each ordered a salad, the chopped and the beet, both were okay, nothing great. The main course we ordered scallops and trout. Again, pretty average, but nothing spectacular. The only good thing about this place was the large glasses of wine and the patio.

text: I love this place for four reasons. One is that it's on the water and it has a nice tropical vibe. Two is because you get to see drunk wealthy senior citizens hit on other ones. Three is because they have their own beer (Ozona Red) and it is tasty and cheap. And four is because the food is darn good. I usually get the ribeye sandwich, which is alwyas perfectly cooked. Comes with blue cheese, red pepper, an donion straws on a fresh hoagie. The ahi and salmon apps are good. I've never ordered an official entree here, as it tends to get a bit pricy. But, I would if I came for a nice dinner and not just for happy hour after work. The live music is almost always good and there is tons of non-valet parking in the blue marina nextdoor. This place will be jam packed on most nights, so plan accordingly.
