text: This restaurant dubs itself as a charcoal house and a saloon. When you enter Kid Shelleen's, you quickly realize that neither of those labels apply. Yes, the restaurant boasts a kitchen and a bar, but that's it. You've got to love a place that tries to label itself with nifty titles to draw in a crowd. Kids' (as the locals refer to it) doesn't have a problem bringing in the crowds. It's a mix of suburbanites, golf club types, young trolley square residents. Most of them gather around the bar that takes up most of the indoor dining room. Menu is your generic American offerings - with your usual suspects for appetizers (nachos, wings, crab dip, etc.), salads, sandwiches, and main courses (Steak, penne pasta with shrimp). Portions are generous, execution is lackluster. They offer brunch on Sundays, have weekly specials - my favorite being "No Whining Wednesdays" - with half-price bottles of wine. Service is super attentive all around from host, bar to server. Roomy outdoor patio saves the restaurant.
label: NEG

Yes that is one quarter for one martini, and you can get a nice filling, yummy dish to accompany THEM for lunch for under $20. Also they will give you a little brochure with a little bit of a walking tour of the Garden District and are well placed to explore the nearby photo worthy cemetaries. Definitely worth stopping by.

text: Whoa . . . . . . . I had NO idea a thin-crust pepperoni pizza could taste so good . . . so right . . . so sinful . . . I mean . . . . I actually walked out of this place feeling guilty. Someone, somewhere around this big Earth, somebody was getting messed over while I was having the time of my life eating Imo's. We have one of these about 10 minutes from my crib here in KS but I always wanted to try one that was in the Lou (or in this case, in the STL metro area). We first had the toasted ravioli. As i'm usually not impressed with such fare, I do understand the Lou is proud of this stuff and since we did not have it on our last visit I wanted to get it over with. As expected, it was good tasting, but not anything I would ever crave. The pizza however . . . . it's such a perfect device for destroying insulin levels. And because it's thin-crust, it really disappears quickly. My wife and I had the 14' basic pepperoni. I was AMAZED at how delicious it was. The crust was perfect. Not too crispy, not too soggy. The sauce had this ever so sweet flavor to it. And the cheese. . . . . . ohhh the cheese . . . . . . I'm not even going to go there. The absolute right amount for the amount of dough it sat on. We decimated the pie in about 9 minutes. Five stars for being incredible. And if the one in Overland Park is anything near as good as this, it is sure to be the new "black" when it comes to our home delivery orders.
label: POS

The reservation book is displayed prominently at the door with a column for "who invited you" as if you have to "know someone" to get a reservation. text: Philadelphia Located within the Reading Terminal Market, lines can be long during peak lunch time hours and unbearable if there happens to be a convention being held right next door. With that said, Carmen's has some very tasty sandwiches ("hoagies") and a large part of the taste factor is the fresh baked bread they use. I believe the bread cartons I saw said "Locasio". And yes, while in Philly, I'm going to order a cheesesteak hoagie. Skip the whiz and get the provolone. It'll set you back a little more than $8, more if you ask for additional condiments. Read the large menu on the wall for their price list. The women in front of me said yes to every option the owner rattled off yet was surprised when her fully loaded cheesesteak cost $12. The sandwich was far better tasting than than Geno's or Pat's and certainly better than any cheesesteak from any vendor pushcart located throughout Philly. The bread is a big factor in that. Are there better tasting places to eat in the food court? Yes, there are a few, but those lines are even more ridiculous. The line at Carmen's moves fairly quick. Cheers! N.
label: POS

text: I really don't get all the 4 and 5 star reviews. Usually I associate that with either uneducated palates and/or someone giving it props because they are liquored up. In this case, it looks like liquored up wins. The pizza here is mediocre and greasy. The pepperoni slice was dripping oil and I had to blot it with a napkin. The cheese slice was ok, but the tomato sauce was bland. Both slices were fairly decent sized. The price was the only selling point. That and it was open late. The place does attract an interesting crowd to be sure. However, I"m not going to a pizza place for characters, but for food. If you are sober and its before 10pm go to NYPD, Milano's or Rustica. Your tastebuds will thank you.

text: Okay, so a few nights ago, my parents ask "Hey Jim, why don't you take us to one of those good spots in the city for dinner? Maybe Aunt Carolyn would like to come along too". It was a Wednesday night, and I had nothing better to do, so I figured why not? They wanted to go to the usual places they go down here...either Soho pizza or Campo's. They're both great, but they get old after a dozen or two times. Also, if I was going to be dining with my parents & slightly-less-than-normal aunt, I would need a place capable of continuously supplying me with beer....lots of beer. Finally, I had a chance to try the Race St. Cafe! I've been wanting to get there for a while...seemed like such a cool place. Well, it was the perfect idea. From the minute I walked into this place, I knew I was going to like it. Easy going, nice people, cool atmosphere, and...lots & lots of beer. Dad & I quickly ordered...Oktoberfest for me, and I think a #9 for him (at first he was thinking Coors light...but after a seriously disappointing grin from me, he changed his mind). The menu was adequately sized...not huge, but very good, with great variety, and well-priced. Perfect for this place! All in all, the meal was great. I'll definitely go back soon, hopefully without the parents. This is one of the few bars in the city that I know of that are perfectly fine to go to alone (if necessary). Being that many of my friends are reluctant to go out in the city (or even leave their damn house)....this is a big plus. It's nice to escape the ridiculousness that Old City can be sometimes. Race Street Cafe does a nice job of being different, and different is always GOOD.
label: POS

text: After lurking on Yelp for ages, I finally decided to contribute. We've (my wife and I) been here many times over the years. We even had our wedding rehearsal dinner here back in 2005. This is the most authentic place we've found in the Reno area for Chinese food. BTW, I'm Chinese, so I know what good Chinese food is. They were good back in the day (2005ish) but then the food quality went down hill, so we stopped going for a couple years. Looks like they got it back together again! We always start with the Seafood Tofu soup which we like a lot. I recommend trying it! I like it on the spicy side, so I always ask for some white pepper (it's not on the tables). The waiter (Sing) knows us and always brings the white pepper for me w/o me asking now. That's the kind of service we like! Also recommend the steamed whole fish, salt & spicy shrimp, and salt & spicy spare ribs. The staff is always friendly and attentive. This is back in our Reno restaurant rotation! If you're looking for a fancy shmancy fusion type place, this ain't it...but if you want some good Chinese food (especially in the Reno area) this will do the trick!
label: POS

text: I don't know about you, but sometime I like to get up on a Saturday, sit in traffic, and end up in front of high pressure sales people. I bought some furniture from Tony Diamond when I first moved to South Jersey. I was all giddy and excited when my "adult" furniture showed. The guys put it together and slipped them a nice piece of change on the way out. So an hour or so later it looked like the table was scratched so I storm over to it only to find it was a piece of packing tape.....how relieve I was- until I noticed the entire back corner was smashed and the two DB's that put it together put that corner in by the wall hoping I wouldn't notice. This was Sunday so Monday I call customer service all ticked off and, to their credit, they said a new table would be brought out. Well two weeks later they show up with the new table....the guy opens the box and started laughing. The one in the box is cracked in half!!!!!!!! It took a good six weeks, but I finally got my table. Flash forward about a year and I'm feeling rammy so I decide to price out some bedroom sets. I get to the store and the salespeople jump of me. Using my awesome ninja skills I fight them off. 10 mins later one catches me by surprise and I accidentally asked for a price...next thing you know I'm sitting at a desk and she's trying to get to me sign an invoice. I explained I just wanted a price and the C-Bag gets all snatchy with me, than comes back with the sales manager for the "hard sell". After being worked on for a couple mins I excused myself and left. 5 mins later they're calling me on the phone trying to lure me back in. They have some good prices, but you better wear two sets of undies because they're gonna try and stick it in.
label: NEG

text: First off, the pictures uploaded by the business on Yelp are not accurate at all. What we got were way mininature-rized versions of the rolls (see pic). Being on a busy studying schedule, we thought it would be a good idea to order delivery and the idea of delivery sushi sounded very appealing. Sadly, I was very disappointed. I ordered and waited over an hour for them to come, even though they are only 7 blocks away (yea, I know I'm lazy). We even had to call them again. We got four rolls for about $40 dollars so I just basically spent $20 bucks on a bad dinner. What we ordered: 1) Apple Roll ($13.25, WTH?!) : OK I don't know what I was thinking when I ordered this. I guess the sound of apple in a sushi roll sounded interesting. What we got however, was a different story. A small sushi roll with a very thin piece of salmon and tuna on the outside, and a tiny piece of yellow tail in the inside. What made up the core of the roll? LOTS of apples. I couldn't even taste the fish. SO hmm I guess I paid 13 bucks for mostly apple slivers. 2) Love for Tuna ($10): There is no love here. I am in disbelief how tiny this roll is for being $10. It was the same size as the non-specialty rolls and at twice the price. To make matters worse, I decided to just eat a piece of the Tuna separate from the roll. Talk about not fresh. It was dry and grainy... SAY WHAT? Dry and grainy tuna?? YEA.... 3) Tex-Mex ($8.50): Again, sounded very appealing and fun with having jalapeno. Again, teeny tiny, and the chicken inside.... SO DRY AGAIN! UGH! 4) Spicy Tuna ($5.50): This one was okay, more spiciness would've been better. And the rice wasn't fresh either! Overall, everything was bland and boring. Most flavorful thing I had during this meal? The ginger. WILL NOT be returning. I've had better sushi at grocery stores than this. I'd give it one star but the lunch I had there once was okay so it redeems a star for that.
label: NEG

text: I followed Maria when she left Saturn club -- and I'd continue to follow her if she moved her salon to the moon. I love Maria, both for her talent as a stylist/colorist and just as an awesome chica. I estimate that she's been doing my hair for about 10 years -- and in that time I've made her come up with some crazy styles and colors. I've had her make me bleach blond, blue haired, raven-locked, short and spiky, bobbed, and everything in between. I walk in with a crazy idea, we work together to make it go, and it always comes up aces. (Have a look at my userpic to see our most recent experiment in black and bright blue! ) Even the miracle-worker Maria aside, the atmosphere at Deluxe is fantastic. From the hip mod-style decor to the Vargas pinup girls in the bathroom, the place is just chic to the core. I can't swear that you'll love it there... everyone's different... but I sure can swear I do. Rock on, Deluxe. Rock on.
label: POS

text: This is an easy place to love. text: Let's start off by clearly stating that I have a profound weakness for 'crab shacks'. When eating seafood, I am not enthralled by fancy service, swanky ambience, or linen tablecloths. For us, it's all about the food, so if you're eating shellfish, crustaceans, or any other sea creatures where freshness is paramount, then it's all about location, location, location. The closer to the source, the better. So it will be no surprise that we're big fans of the SB Shellfish Company, or as it's referred to in our household, the Shack. We live just a few blocks away, so we usually just bike up the pier and when possible, grab a table at the bar overlooking the open kitchen, or outside on the harbor side of the Shack (that way we can sit outside, and have a beer too). The menu's not all high-end. Lots of fried combo's (all good). The real treat though is gobbling down a plate of oysters, maybe a small cup of NE chowder, followed by any one of their seasonal specials. The tanks are always filled with live crabs, lobsters, etc --so freshness is never an issue. The open kitchen is a joy to watch, and the food is fast and honest. When it comes to casual non-sushi seafood in Santa Barbara, there is no competition. The Shack is the place to enjoy a beer, some tasty treats, soak up the sea breeze, and watch all the sail boats trafficking in and out of the harbor. A perfect afternoon.
label: POS

text: My wife and I stopped into this place on a lark. We'd never had Bosnian food before and we were driving by, saw the sign and thought we'd give it a try. We were pleasantly surprised. It was quite early and the place was empty when we walked in, but there were three huge tables set up for groups of 12 or more which all filled up as we ate our meal. We ordered the cevap (sausage) and something else that they described as a "Bosnian" hamburger. They brought out a nice "fatouch" type salad before our entrees arrived. It was crisp and lemony and lovely. The entrees were so massive that we were a bit taken aback. My "Bosnian hamburger" was like a half-size football. It was spicy and delicious. Both entrees were served on the thick Bosnian pita bread called "lepina." We had never had this before but it was quite nice. It's quite thick and handmade and it absorbs all of the juice and fat from the meat. Best handled with a fork and knife. We managed to eat about 1/3 of our food and they cheerfully packed the rest of it up for us to take home. I'd describe this food as a sort of cross between Turkish and Hungarian food. A bit heavy for everyday but quite tasty. They didn't seem to have any wine but we saw other tables bringing their own wine in and they seemed happy to accommodate that. Our bill was $20-25 for dinner (which ended up being our lunch the next day as well). If we went back, we'd probably split one entree and bring a bottle of Petite Syrah.
label: POS

text: I ate here twice while on a week-long vacation to Tucson. It is out of the way, on Kinney Road on the west side of the Tucson Mountains. It is just south of Tucson Mountain Park, Old Tucson Studios, the Sonoran Desert Museum, and Saguaro National Park West, so if you're headed that way, its a great, authentic Mexican meal. The food is very fresh and the portions are huge. I had the cheese crisp for my first dinner, with chicken, onions, mild green chiles, and lots of cheese. These traditional Tucson flour tortilla crisps can be greasy, but not here. It was very mild (gringo food), with obviously very fresh ingredients, and served super hot and melty. I ordered the small and it was the size of a small pizza. The second meal I had the Three Color Burro with shredded beef, which was also very mild. It is a very large burrito stuffed with well-seasoned freshly cooked shredded beef which was a little salty but delicious. The burrito was smothered with green sauce, red sauce, and sour cream sauce, hence, "Three Color". It was served with rice and beans. Very good, but I could only eat half! I highly recommend this place, but if you're looking for something spicy, ask your server, because what I ordered was not spicy at all!

text: I've been reading all these negative reviews of GiGi's and I can't believe my eyes. It was one of the BEST cupcake I've ever had in my life (and I like cupcakes!). Everything about it was delectable, but the frosting, in particular, was especially noteworthy. It was soft and creamy--not too sugary--almost buttery, and it had a distinct chocolate flavor. It wasn't at all fudgy, which I loved about that because I get completely overwhelmed by all of those fudgy frostings. This chocolate was reminiscent of a Texas sheet cake--perfect for a southern bakery. I definitely won't deduct any stars for too much frosting because that's just absurd. The cupcake was huge and the abundant frosting was much needed because I ended up sharing the cupcake. Usually, when I share a piece of cake, my hog bf ends up whoring up the frosting for himself! They are a little pricey and that's their only negative. If you want to wash that cake down with a glass of milk, be prepared to dish out another $3. I guess I can't vouch for the other flavors because I haven't tried them, but the Midnight Magic is definitely worth the stop in.
